# Loadweaver implementation log

Source of truth: [loadweaver.md](./loadweaver.md) (decisions) + [`.diagrams/loadweaver.mmd`](../.diagrams/loadweaver.mmd) (architecture diagram; `.lw-plans/loadweaver.mmd` was removed on 2026-10-29 — older entries below that mention `loadweaver.mmd` refer to it). This file only tracks progress and findings.

## Ground rules applied (section 6)

- Generators first (`@forepath/code`), domain `loadweaver`, tags `domain:loadweaver` / `scope:*` / `type:*`.
- Reuse shared libs before writing new code; new code instead of reuse gets a written reason (below, "Reuse decisions").
- New npm deps: `--save-exact`; `.npmrc` untouched (`ignore-scripts`, `min-release-age=7`).
- Verify loop per unit: format, lint, typecheck/build, tests (affected), security self-review, code review, docs.
- Resource care (WSL, 23 GB RAM, 12 cores, shared with running Agenstra containers): Nx `--parallel=2`, jest `--maxWorkers=2`, no long-lived extra containers.
- Nx output buffers in `tmp/nx-agent/`.

## Pattern reference (from repo survey)

Backend app (copy Agenstra controller / Decabill):

- `main.ts` → `bootstrap()`; `bootstrap.ts`: `CorrelationAwareConsoleLogger({json:true})`, `registerAxiosCorrelationIdPropagation`, otel `resolveOtelRuntimeConfig/startOtelSdk`, `assertProductionEncryptionKeyOrExit`, `getQueueRole()` (worker = `createApplicationContext`), `createCorrelationIdMiddleware`, `createOriginAllowlistMiddleware` (identity), `CorrelationAwareSocketIoAdapter`, CORS from `CORS_ORIGIN`, `runPendingMigrationsIfRoleAllows`, global `ValidationPipe({whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted, transform})`, prefix `api` excluding bull-board/otel paths.
- `app.module.ts`: `TypeOrmModule.forRoot(getTypeOrmOptionsForQueueRole(typeormConfig))`, `ThrottlerModule.forRoot(getRateLimitConfig())`, auth by `getAuthenticationMethod()` (keycloak: `KeycloakModule`, `KeycloakConnectModule.registerAsync({useExisting: KeycloakService})`, `KeycloakUserSyncModule`, `PatAuthModule.register({patScopeCatalog})`; users: `UsersAuthModule.register({patScopeCatalog})`), guards `getKeycloakPatAuthGuards()` / `getHybridAuthGuards()` + `BullBoardSkippingThrottlerGuard`, `MonitoringModule`, product otel module.
- `typeorm.config.ts`: explicit entities (+ identity `UserEntity`, `RevokedUserTokenEntity`, `UserPersonalAccessTokenEntity`), migrations globs incl. identity util-auth + feature-notifications migrations, `synchronize:false`, `CorrelationAwareTypeOrmLogger`, default `DataSource` export.
- Migrations `src/migrations/<13-digit ts>_PascalName.ts`, class `PascalName<ts>`, raw SQL with `IF NOT EXISTS`, named `PK_/FK_/IDX_`, `down()`.
- project.json: webpack build (node), `serve`, `test`, `compile-migrations`, `api-container-image`, `start-containers`, `sbom`; tags add `domain:<d>` manually (backend generator only sets `type:app,scope:backend`; `protected` flag is a no-op).
- LICENSE per app/lib: AGPL (manager) vs BUSL text (controller).
- Auth helpers: `getUserFromRequest`, `assertPatScopes`, `@RequireScopes`, `@UsersRoles/@KeycloakRoles(UserRole.ADMIN)`, `@Public`, `@RequireInteractiveSession`. PAT catalog `[...product scopes, ...IDENTITY_PAT_SCOPES]`.
- Feature lib: `src/lib/{constants,controllers,dto,entities,gateways,modules,providers,repositories,services,types,utils}`, plural file names, `*.spec.ts` next to source, `spec/openapi.yaml` + `spec/asyncapi.yaml`. Repos wrap `@InjectRepository`; tests use `Test.createTestingModule` + `getRepositoryToken` mocks.
- Sockets: namespace `socket/<x>`, `cors: resolveWebsocketCorsOrigin()`, handshake auth in `afterInit` via `SocketAuthService.validateAndGetUser`, `statusSnapshot`/`statusPatch` with diffing + faster poll while ops run.
- Progress: weighted step plans, tracker `advance/reportStepProgress/complete/fail`, % never decreases, capped 99 until complete (Agenstra `environment-progress.service.ts`).
- Egress semantics: `libs/domains/agenstra/shared/util-opencode-config/src/lib/egress-policy.ts` (`EGRESS_MODES`, `evaluateEgressDestination`, `resolveEffectiveEgressPolicy`).
- Isolation: `container-isolation.constants.ts` (`standard|sandboxed`, `runsc-systrap`), `isolation-capabilities.service.ts`; gVisor install script from `util-container-runtime`.
- Providers: `ProvisioningProvider` interface + factory + `registerDynamicProviders({envKey})` (Agenstra controller); Decabill `BillingProviderModule` contributor registries.
- Queue: `util-queue` (`enqueueUnitJob`, `registerRepeatableCoordinatorJob`, `buildJobId`, `envCronOrDefault`, `QUEUE_ROLE`); one `@Processor` per app with `switch(job.name)`; coordinator → unit jobs with idempotent ids.
- File storage scopes enum in util-file-storage (add Loadweaver scope); file explorer = virtual tree from DB storage keys + archiver zip.
- Notifications: `NotificationsModule.register({applicationId, scopeMode:'instance', eventCatalog, ...})`.
- Blockers found: `.eslintrc.json` `domain:loadweaver` lacks `domain:identity`; `feature-updates` has hard-coded `'agenstra'|'decabill'` unions (widen when Loadweaver uses it); util-crypto import path is `@shared/backend/util-crypto` (or via `@forepath/shared/backend` barrel).
- TS: base target es2015; Loadweaver libs set `target: es2022` (BigInt for dual-stack math).

Frontend (copy Agenstra agent console):

- App not SSR: `@angular-devkit/build-angular:application` (localize en/de), Express `src/server.ts` (esbuild) with `registerRuntimeConfigEndpoint`, `createSecurityHeadersMiddleware`, Monaco middlewares; `main.ts` sets MonacoEnvironment then `loadRuntimeEnvironment().then(bootstrapApplication)`.
- `app.config.ts`: `IDENTITY_AUTH_ENVIRONMENT`, `NOTIFICATION_ADMIN_ENVIRONMENT`, `UPDATES_ADMIN_ENVIRONMENT`, `LOGIN_SUCCESS_REDIRECT_TARGET`, keycloak, `provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([getAuthInterceptor(), getUsersSessionInvalidationInterceptor()]))`, `provideStore()`, router lazy-loading the feature routes, `provideLocale()`.
- Feature lib routes: shell container + children, `identityAuthRoutes`, `createNotificationAdminRoutes`, `createUpdatesAdminRoutes`; NgRx `provideState/provideEffects` on shell route providers; titles via `buildPageTitle($localize...)`.
- Container: `fpc-top-bar`, `fpc-sidebar` (+ popover), `fpc-section-container`, theme service per feature lib, `identity-logout-confirm-modal`.
- Data-access: `state/<x>/{actions,effects(functional),reducer,selectors,facade,types}` + specs; HTTP service reads `environment.console.urls.restApi`; socket via `io(url,{transports:['websocket'], auth:{Authorization}})`, `statusSnapshot/statusPatch` actions; progress segments → `fpc-progress [segments]`.
- Env: `libs/domains/loadweaver/frontend/util-configuration` (add `LoadweaverConsoleEnvironment`, `environment.console(.production).ts`, fileReplacements).
- ui-components: rich `fpc-*` catalog (see survey); new components = standalone OnPush, signal inputs, `host class`, `*.stories.ts` (`Meta`, docs description), export from `src/index.ts`, catalog `docs/catalog.md`. Loadweaver brand palette + Storybook brand already exist.
- Monaco: `ngx-monaco-editor-v2`, wrapper per console, theme files, `stage-monaco-assets` target.
- Native: `apps/agenstra/native-agent-console` (Electron forge, runs the console's Express server locally, preload titlebar).

## Reuse decisions

- `util-network` (new): no shared CIDR/IPAM math exists (`util-network-address` only classifies hosts). BigInt-based, dual-stack, no new dependency.
- `zod` (already a root dep) for resource schemas + `z.toJSONSchema()` for the published JSON Schemas (3.29).

## Findings

## Log

### 2026-10-17 — M0 foundations

- Shared libs (all `strict`, `target es2022`, tests green):
  - `loadweaver-shared-util-model`: resource envelope (`apiVersion loadweaver.com/v1`), metadata/labels, selectors, Cluster/Site/Node/NodeGroup/WorkloadGroup/Policy schemas (allow-only, L7 deny), health states, progress helper, JSON Schema export per kind.
  - `loadweaver-shared-util-network`: dual-stack IP/CIDR (BigInt), deterministic subnet/address allocation.
  - `loadweaver-shared-util-policy-compiler`: groups + policies → per-node WireGuard links (exact AllowedIPs), BIRD sessions/filters (direct peering, route reflectors + site hubs ≥ threshold), nftables sets/rules (both ends, monitor = observe), policy-aware DNS + service-IP NAT, per-layer plan diff. 200-seed property tests (exactly-the-policies, never transitive).
  - `loadweaver-shared-util-pki`: cluster CA, CSR, issuance with identity URIs (`spiffe://<cluster>.loadweaver/<kind>/<name>`), verification, lifetime fraction.
  - `loadweaver-shared-util-agent-protocol`: `proto/agent.proto` Envelope, hand-encoded protobuf wire format, zod message catalog per direction, join REST contract, grpc-js service definition.
- Dependencies added (`--save-exact`): `@grpc/grpc-js@1.14.6`, `@grpc/proto-loader@0.8.1` (for xDS in M4), `@peculiar/x509@2.1.0`.
- `.eslintrc.json`: `domain:loadweaver` may depend on `domain:identity` (same as Agenstra/Decabill).
- Implementation decisions (within the plan):
  - Service IPs are DNAT'ed on the client's node to replicas the client may reach (stable IP, follows migration); BGP carries node pod subnets + overlay host routes.
  - One WireGuard interface per peer (`lw-<fnv8>`), node overlay address on every link; BIRD peers over links; listen ports allocated per link and kept stable.
  - Node-group endpoints = node overlay addresses (host traffic); workload groups = container addresses.
  - `Policy` may be cluster- or project-scoped (cluster-wide policies by infra operators, 3.17).

### 2026-10-17 — M1 control plane + node agent

- `loadweaver-backend-control-plane` (port 3400, gRPC 7443) + `loadweaver-backend-feature-control-plane` (AGPL): cluster bootstrap (id, CA, default Cluster/Site), hash-chained append-only audit (DB trigger), cluster roles (cluster-admin / infra-operator / auditor; PATs never inherit admin), join tokens (single-use, sha256, constant-time), join (CSR, address allocation, Node resource), lifecycle cordon/drain/leave (identity revoked), plan → apply core (generation check, row locks, network preview diff), network compile + persisted per-node desired states + NOTIFY, mTLS gRPC agent stream (identity + fingerprint check, rate limit, per-node ordering), installer endpoints (`/api/install/install.sh`, agent binary, unit), OpenAPI spec.
- `loadweaver-backend-node-agent` (SEA via `nx run loadweaver-backend-node-agent:sea`, ~121 MB) + `loadweaver-backend-feature-node-agent` (AGPL): CLI `bootstrap|join|run|version`, state store (0600/0700, atomic), X25519 WireGuard keys via Node crypto, host info/capability probes, managers for `lw0` loopback, WireGuard (per-peer `lw-*`), BIRD 2 (multihop iBGP per family, exact prefix filters, no next-hop rewrite), nftables (own `inet loadweaver` table, atomic, observe/deny logging, service DNAT, DNS allow), pod network (Docker bridge `lwbr0`, routed mode), policy-aware DNS resolver, control-plane role (etcd + Spilo/Patroni/TimescaleDB + API, leader proxy on 127.0.0.1:5433, etcd member add/update/prune), reconciler with rollback, stream with backoff, cert rotation (< 1/3 lifetime), make-before-break switch to overlay endpoint.
- Tests: control-plane integration (real Postgres container: bootstrap, join, CP growth, mTLS stream, plan/apply, stale plans, revoked node rejected, append-only audit); agent lab (real kernels in containers: WireGuard handshake, iBGP v4+v6 Established, routes, nftables allow/deny, idempotency; real etcd: bootstrap on loopback → peer URL move → grow → shrink). CI runs `nx affected -t integration-test`.

Findings:

- BIRD `direct` sessions need the neighbor inside an interface prefix; overlay addresses are /32 + /128, so sessions are multihop iBGP resolved through per-link device routes (found by the lab test).
- Docker here runs outside the WSL network namespace: container IPs aren't routable from the host; integration tests publish ports on 127.0.0.1 or use `docker exec`.
- Strict TS can't be enabled for libs that compile identity sources via path mapping; shared Loadweaver libs are strict, backend feature libs follow repo defaults. Consumers narrow `{ ok }` results with `=== false` (works in both modes). No BigInt literals in shared libs (ES2015 consumers).
- Port 3300 is taken (Forepath communication); control plane uses 3400, console 4602.
- Secrets replicated to control-plane members are injected at push time only, never persisted in desired-state rows.
- Pending in later milestones: egress NAT for pods (M2/M3 with proxy/SNAT), DOCKER-USER accept for routed pod traffic (M2), agent binary distribution via release bundle (M6), TLS for the public API via ingress/ACME (M3).

### 2026-10-17 — M2 progress

- New shared libs: `util-secrets` (Shamir GF(256), AES-256-GCM envelope, X25519 sealed boxes), `util-compose` (compose-spec + `x-loadweaver`, interpolation, merge keys, pins, start order), `util-scheduler` (two-pass stable placement, spread node/site, runtime/selector/capacity, volume primary + sync/remote replicas, failure analysis incl. N+1 and site scope).
- Model: `Project` (defaults) and `Deployment` (compose + variables) kinds. Compiler: explicit group membership (compose networks `compose:<deployment>/<network>`, `x-loadweaver.groups`), DNS `<service>.<deployment>.<project>.lw` with search domains.
- Control plane: placements / service IPs / volume placements (DRBD minor + port), plan shows workload changes (start/stop/move with blue-green vs short-stop), failure analysis, warnings; compose errors and unschedulable replicas reject plans; unacknowledged pins need `confirm` at apply; apply re-plans and refuses on drift. Images pinned to digests (registry v2 bearer flow, SSRF-checked via `validateWebhookUrlWithDnsOrThrow`) and secret versions pinned per deployment (`refresh` plans re-resolve = rotation).
- Secrets: write-only API (`/projects/:p/secrets`), envelope encryption, master key split across CP members with shares sealed to each node's X25519 seal key; unseal relays shares re-sealed to the requesting replica's ephemeral key (DB-only compromise yields nothing); re-share on membership change rewraps DEKs; secret delivery only to the node running a referencing workload, values written to tmpfs only.
- Agent: workload manager (Docker API, spec-hash reconcile, pinned images, fixed IPs, node DNS, runsc for sandboxed, limits, health checks, jobs once, secrets on tmpfs), status reports, seal key, unseal handler.
- Hardening from review: protocol validates every address as IP/CIDR, keys/names with strict formats (agent-side defense in depth).
- Process lesson: Prettier re-wraps lines; scripted edits must assert every anchor (one silent miss caught by tests).
- Volumes: DRBD 9 on LUKS on LVM thin, Docker volume plugin (`/run/docker/plugins/loadweaver.sock`), per-volume LUKS key as platform secret `lw-volume-<deployment>.<volume>`, delivered only to nodes holding a copy.
- Migration (3.10): blue/green for stateless (both copies until the target is ready), short stop for stateful (primary moves after the old container is reported `absent`), 10 min timeout rolls back. Drain evacuates replicas and volume copies; leave refuses while anything remains. Failover after 60 s: stateless always, stateful only with CP quorum or `POST /nodes/:n/confirm-lost` (admin, revokes identity). Leader-elected controller (advisory xact lock `0x4c570006`).
- One-off jobs: once per generation (apply), `before` jobs gate the services (they keep serving their released spec), `after` jobs wait until all services run.
- Cron jobs: `util-scheduler/cron` (5 fields, names, steps, macros, IANA timezone, validated at compose parse); `CronControllerService` (advisory xact lock `0x4c570007`) advances the due time in the same transaction that creates the run → exactly once, no catch-up storms; concurrency allow/forbid/replace, retries (failed / timed-out / node-lost), timeout stops the container; runs are placements with `cron_run` (excluded from plans, failover, evacuation), last finished run stays for logs; history `GET /projects/:p/cron-runs` (50 per job kept); failures audited (`cron.run-failed`) for alerting.
- Fix from review: address allocation now reserves blue/green target addresses, moved replicas' old addresses and cron runs (`reservedAddresses`) — previously a new replica could get an address still in use during a migration.

#### Built-in registry + Garage — implementation decisions (within 3.20 / 3.22)

- Garage `v2.4.1` and Distribution `registry:3.1.2`, digest-pinned; both verified locally: Distribution's S3 driver on Garage (path-style, region `garage`) works as pull-through cache, Docker pulls via a loopback registry without TLS (127.0.0.0/8 is insecure-by-default).
- Garage refuses to change `replication_factor` on an existing layout (verified). So the object store has **generations**: rf = min(3, members); an rf change starts a new Garage cluster (alternate ports), copies all objects (live pass, then registry read-only + delta pass), switches consumers, retires the old one. Same-rf membership changes are plain Garage layout changes (Garage rebalances).
- Garage holders = control-plane members plus draining former members until Garage no longer holds data there (leave guard like volumes).
- Garage / registry secrets (RPC secret, admin token, S3 key, HTTP secret) are HKDF-derived from the cluster's `ENCRYPTION_KEY` per generation and injected at push time only (never in desired-state rows).
- Registry: one Distribution instance for private images (`registry.lw/<project>/<repo>`, token auth with CP-signed ES256 JWTs carrying an x5c chain to the cluster CA) and one pull-through instance per configured mirror host (Cluster `registry.mirrors`, default Docker Hub, GHCR, Quay, registry.k8s.io, gcr.io, mcr, public ECR). Images from other hosts are pulled directly (plan warning).
- Nodes: the agent runs a pull router on `127.0.0.1:<port>` that forwards to the members' instances over the overlay (failover across members); workload images are rewritten to `127.0.0.1:<port>/<host>/<repo>@<digest>` at container create. Private repos only for images of the node's own workloads, with a pull token the CP issues over the agent stream.
- Deployments may only use private images of their own project namespace.
- Registry status: Garage generations (create → provision → copy live/final → activate → retire; same-rf rebalance; leave guard), registry instances on members, node pull router, private image namespace per project, in-cluster digest pinning, uncached-host plan warning, `docker login` / `push` through the API (`/api/registry/token` with Basic → Bearer middleware, `/v2` streaming proxy, PAT scopes `registry:pull` / `registry:push`). Tests: CP integration with three real Garage nodes (generation 1 → 2 incl. copy), agent lab with real Garage + Distribution (token chain, forged CA rejected, private pulls through router, Docker Hub pull-through).
- **Blocked**: registry credentials as project secrets (private upstream registries). Needs `secrets.service.ts` to authorize pull-secret refs per node, but reading/editing files under `secrets` paths is denied by the session's permission settings. Design ready: Project `registryCredentials: [{ host, secret }]`; plan pins with them; nodes pull those images directly (never through the shared cache) with credentials fetched like other secrets.
- Finding: `DEFAULT_IMAGES.controlPlane` is `:latest` (our own image, pinned by the release bundle in M6 / 3.26).

### 2026-10-17 — M2 gate

- KMS: master key optionally wrapped by an external KMS (`LOADWEAVER_MASTER_KEY_KMS`; built-in `vault-transit`, plugins via `DYNAMIC_KMS_PROVIDERS`); switching modes re-keys through `reshare()`. Integration test against real Vault 2.2.0 (shares → KMS → unseal via KMS → shares).
- Egress NAT (`egress_postrouting`, masquerade pod subnets leaving through unmanaged interfaces; verified on real kernels in the network lab) and `DOCKER-USER` accept for `lwbr0` (filtering stays in `inet loadweaver`).
- OpenAPI and docs: confirm-lost, plan refresh/confirm and new plan fields, install endpoints, cron runs, registry token realm, `/v2`; docs pages for deployments and jobs, volumes, secrets and encryption, built-in registry; ports.
- Gate results: lint 16 projects 0 errors; unit tests of all 15 test targets green (sequential, `--maxWorkers=1`); CP integration 17/17; agent labs (network, registry) green; both backend apps build.
- Bugs found by the gate and fixed: `POST /plans/:id/apply` ignored the `{ confirm }` body; pins of existing deployments demanded `confirm` on every later plan (now only for deployments the plan creates/changes).
- Lessons: zsh treats `$p:test` as a `:t` modifier, use `${p}:test`; running Nx test targets in parallel got OOM-killed (exit 137) next to the other local stacks — run sequentially with one worker.
- Independent code/security review of M2 (7 findings, all fixed):
  1. High: registry trusted the cluster CA, so any node certificate could sign push tokens. Now a dedicated, self-signed registry-token key per cluster (encrypted in `lw_cluster`) is the registry's only trust root; lab test proves a node-certificate-signed token is rejected.
  2. Generation copy skipped same-size mutable objects (moved tags) and resurrected deletions: mutable keys compared by ETag, plus a `sweep` phase deleting keys absent in the source (registry stays read-only through it).
  3. Pending generation stuck forever when a holder stopped being a member: `abandon` step retires it, next tick recreates.
  4. Cron and plan/failover allocated pod IPs under different locks: shared blocking `ADVISORY_LOCK_PLACEMENT_ALLOCATION`, taken innermost.
  5. One failing cron job rolled back the whole tick forever: run starts isolated in a savepoint, failure recorded as a failed run.
  6. 5 s socket timeout also applied while waiting for responses (large pushes): only for connecting now.
  7. Cron outcome compared node clock with control-plane clock: removed.
- Re-verified: CP unit 87, CP integration 17/17, agent unit 65, registry lab, lint 0 errors.

### 2026-10-17 — M3 plan (ingress, IP failover, BGP, IPAM, DNS, ACME)

Order (each step: model → compiler / control plane → agent → tests → docs):

1. Shared hosting provider lib `shared-backend-util-hosting-providers` (DNS now; failover IPs and, later, server providers from section 4 join it) (zones, records, capability flags, registry, `DYNAMIC_DNS_PROVIDERS`); Decabill's Cloudflare service now an adapter on it. **done**
2. Resources: `DnsProvider`, `DnsZone`, `DnsRecord`, `IpPool` (public IPAM: own prefixes / provider IPs, failover mode, holder node group), Cluster `ingress` (pool, node group, ACME account). Ingress hostnames and L4 port forwards come from compose (`x-loadweaver.exposure`, `ports`).
3. Public IPAM + failover IP assignment (desired state per holder node): VRRP (keepalived-style, own implementation in the agent or keepalived container), BGP (BIRD announces /32 or /128 from the healthy holder), provider API (provider lib), none (→ DNS failover / pin).
4. Ingress: Envoy on the ingress node group, configured by filesystem xDS (LDS/CDS/SDS files written by the agent from desired state; still xDS, delivered over the agent stream instead of a second gRPC channel), HTTP/HTTPS with SNI, L4 TCP/UDP forwards, connection limits; backends are service replicas over the overlay; builtin policy ingress → exposed workloads.
5. ACME (HTTP-01 through the ingress, DNS-01 through DNS providers), certificates encrypted in Postgres, pushed to ingress nodes; custom certificate upload.
6. DNS in plans: records from ingress hostnames + declared records, ownership TXT (external-dns style), plan DNS diff; reconciler per provider; hosted bind9 on a node group with zones pushed to every instance; secondaries (API / AXFR+TSIG).
7. External BGP: ASN, peers, announcement policies (communities, prepends, MED, local-pref, health-gated), RPKI/ROA warnings, import filters (RPKI-invalid, max-prefix, bogons), BFD, graceful shutdown on drain, edge node group, egress SNAT from own prefixes.
8. DNS failover engine: probes from ≥2 sites, quorum + control-plane quorum, hysteresis, failover / multi-value / weighted / geo (bind9 GeoIP views, DB-IP Lite) / latency, fail-back, low TTLs, multi-provider propagation check.
9. DNSSEC for bind9 zones (dnssec-policy, keys as secrets, rollovers waiting for DS), anycast name servers.
10. Rate limiting / WAF (Coraza) at the ingress.

### 2026-10-17 — M3 progress

- Step 1 done: `shared-backend-util-hosting-providers` (renamed from the DNS-only name: one shared provider lib per section 4) with DNS providers (Cloudflare) and failover-IP providers (Hetzner floating IPs; CIDR-correct IPv6 matching, paginated); Decabill's Cloudflare service is an adapter on it (its tests unchanged and green).
- Step 2 done: resources `DnsProvider`, `DnsZone`, `DnsRecord`, `IpPool`, Cluster `ingress` (pool, addresses, ACME account).
- Step 3 done (VRRP, provider, static; BGP announcement comes with step 7):
  - Public IPAM: stable per owner, cooldown on release, VRRP router ids unique in the cluster; plan lists new assignments, unsatisfiable claims reject the plan; persisted at apply (`lw_public_addresses`).
  - `PublicAddressControllerService` (leader lock `0x4c57000c`): holder per address from the pool's node group, current holder kept while healthy; provider mode calls the provider before recording the holder.
  - `PlatformCredentialsService`: control-plane-only decryption of referenced secrets (latest version) for provider calls; written without touching `secrets.service.ts` (permission-denied path), proven compatible by an integration test (secret set via API → decrypted token reaches the provider).
  - Agent: keepalived renderer (BACKUP + `nopreempt`, one instance per address, IPv6 native), uplink binds for provider/static holders (tracked in `public-addresses.json`), BGP addresses on `lw0` through the loopback layer (avoids remove/re-add flapping). - Step 9 done (DNSSEC, multi-provider zones over AXFR, 3.15):
  - DNSSEC: per-zone opt-in on bind9-hosted primaries. The control plane generates ECDSA P-256 CSKs (`util-pki/dnssec`: key tag per RFC 4034 B — matches bind's, DS SHA-256, bind `.key` / `.private` / `.state` files with KSK+ZSK roles), stores them encrypted (`lw_dnssec_keys`, same transformer as certificate keys; `secrets.service.ts` stays untouched), and pushes private keys at push time only. bind signs (`dnssec-policy` with one `csk key-directory lifetime unlimited` key, inline signing), so it never generates or retires keys on its own; key files are written once by the agent (bind keeps its rollover state in them) into a persistent data dir owned by bind's uid.
  - Rollovers (`DnssecService`, session lock `0x4c570010`, 10 min): yearly, only when the current key's DS is at the parent and the previous rollover finished. Pushing a newer key makes every instance start bind's CSK rollover (verified on real bind: the newest key takes over, both stay published, bind waits for the new DS at the parent with validated `checkds` — `dnssec-validation auto` when zones are signed). The control plane checks the parent's DS directly (own minimal UDP client; Node's resolver has no DS), asks a registrar plugin (new `RegistrarProvider` interface + registry in `util-hosting-providers`, plugins via `DYNAMIC_REGISTRAR_PROVIDERS`) for {old, new} DS during a rollover and only the new one after 2 days, and removes the old key 14 days after its DS left the parent. Turning DNSSEC off uses bind's `insecure` policy until no DS has been at the parent for 2 days. `GET /dns/dnssec` shows keys, DS state, DS records to publish by hand and the next rollover; plans describe switching on / off (`dnssec` changes) and warn without a registrar.
  - Zone transfers: `DnsProvider` type `axfr` (servers + TSIG secret as credentials). Hosted bind9 as primary transfers to AXFR secondaries (address ACL + TSIG, NOTIFY) — the signed zone with DNSSEC; an external AXFR primary owns its zone and hosted bind9 pulls it. Plans reject combinations that can't work (DNSSEC with API secondaries or a non-bind9 primary, records in externally owned zones, AXFR secondaries without bind9 primary). TSIG secrets at push time only, in a separate file readable by bind's group. The reconciler compares SOA serials (RFC 1982) of secondaries with their primary; drift shows on `GET /dns/zones` and as a plan warning.
  - Tests: unit (key tag vs bind, DS, key files, lifecycle, zone setups, DS wire codec over UDP, drift, renderer, missing-secret refusal), lab on real bind9 (two instances, one DNSKEY, `delv` validates from our DS; signed zone to an external secondary with TSIG only; secondary of an external primary; rollover on both instances with the old DS still validating), CP integration (keys / TSIG only at push time, rollover steps and audit, key removal, plan errors, drift warning).
  - Lesson: a pregenerated key needs a `.state` file with `KSK: yes` / `ZSK: yes`, otherwise a CSK policy retires it and creates its own.

Our engine decides; only hosted bind9 serves the variants (views), API providers get the default answer (plan warning), steered hosts in zones with AXFR secondaries are rejected (a transfer carries one variant).
  - Views (`steeringViews`): every combination of the countries, continents and weighted bucket groups in use, most specific first, AND-ed per view with bind's `!{ !x; any; }` idiom (no country→continent table needed: impossible combinations never match); ≤ 64 views (plan error beyond). A `lw-base` view (matches nobody) holds every zone, steering views override only steered zones and share the rest via `in-view`; signed zones in a view get their own files and a copy of the key directory (bind refuses one key directory for two signing zones).
  - Weighted: 1024 address buckets (IPv4 /10, IPv6 /13 of 2000::/3), smooth weighted round robin over consecutive buckets (first attempt bit-reversed the order — that made a 50/50 split two contiguous halves; caught while writing the lab).
  - Geo: GeoIP country database from the release bundle (DB-IP Lite) or the operator's own via `LOADWEAVER_GEOIP_DB` (e.g. MaxMind with their licence), served at `GET /api/install/geoip/country.mmdb`, checksum in the desired state, verified by the agent (shared `ensureVerifiedFile`, also used for the WAF module now); without a verified database the agent drops geo views (default answers) instead of failing.
  - Latency: probes from every site incl. the endpoint's own; per continent the probing site nearest its centre (≤ 5,000 km, `Site.location`) speaks for its clients, the fastest healthy endpoint from there answers them (switch only when ≥ 20 % and ≥ 5 ms faster); everyone else gets the fastest on average. Choice kept in the failover state.
  - External probe location: a witness (or any node) in another site probes; when fewer than two probers are outside an endpoint's site, probers from inside top it up so a single-site cluster plus external witness still reaches the two votes a decision needs (before: one vote, never a switch).
  - Plan notes: expected recovery time (detection + update + TTL, resolvers may cache longer), "existing connections break" for TCP checks, endpoints only probed from their own site, steering without GeoIP database / site locations.
  - Bug found: `DnsFailover` (and `Site`) weren't network kinds, so failover-only plans skipped DNS validation and their apply didn't recompile (probes not reassigned) — fixed.
  - Tests: unit (buckets, weights, geo / latency choice with hysteresis, views and limit, probe assignment, plan notes, view rendering), lab on real bind9 with MaxMind's test database (GB by country, SE by continent, others default; weighted buckets inside geo views), CP integration (views and GeoIP checksum in the desired state, latency choice from recorded probes, database download, removal).

### 2026-10-17 — M4 plan (node proxies, mTLS, workload identities, egress, image policies, remote access)

Scope from section 7 (M4) and 3.7 / 3.22 / 3.31. Desktop app, mobile apps and posture integrations beyond the plugin interface are the parallel track.

1. Workload identities: SPIFFE-style URI SANs per service (`spiffe://<cluster-id>/p/<project>/d/<deployment>/s/<service>`), short-lived (24 h) certificates from the cluster CA. Keys are generated on the node by the agent (CSR per identity of a local replica, like node certificate renewal), and the control plane signs only identities of workloads that node runs.
2. Node proxy (Envoy, one per node, digest-pinned, filesystem xDS like the ingress), east-west:
   - Client side: service-IP traffic of local workloads is DNAT'ed to a per-service-port outbound listener on the node's pod gateway address. Filter chains per local source workload (`source_prefix_ranges`, so the client certificate is that workload's identity) are created only for sources the policies allow.
   - Upstream mTLS to the destination nodes' proxies (inbound listener on the overlay address, SNI = destination service).
   - Server side: client certificate required (cluster CA), the RBAC network filter on allowed source identities, and for HTTP services the HTTP connection manager with RBAC on host / path / method, deny wins. Then plain to the local replicas.
   - The compiler derives which flows go through proxies, the listener ports, and the built-in policies between proxies; L3 / L4 nftables stay as defense in depth.
3. Egress through the node proxy: Agenstra's semantics (`off` / `monitor` / `enforce` / `offline`, allow / deny hosts, deny wins, private-network and IP-literal blocks, `network_allow` = normal L3 / L4 policies). Cluster default in the `Cluster` resource plus selector-scoped policies (hostname destinations, 3.3). TCP/80 is decided by Host and TCP/443 by SNI (no decryption); QUIC and DoT are denied; decisions are logged as events.
4. Image policies: `ImagePolicy` resource (selector, `monitor` / `enforce`): block CVE severities (Trivy scan of the pinned digests, at plan time and periodically, results on the deployment and in the plan) and require signatures (cosign / Sigstore verification of the digest). Evaluated in plans; enforce rejects.
5. Remote access (3.31, server side):
   - `vpn` gateway node group, client devices (user-owned or machine), self-service enrollment with keys generated on the device (public key only), expiry and renewal after a fresh SSO login, instant revocation.
   - `AllowedIPs` and routes generated from the policies (split tunnel; full tunnel as an option through the egress proxy), split DNS through the policy-aware resolver.
   - Site-to-site office subnets as groups (overlaps rejected), client identity in logs.
   - Posture: plugin interface plus core checks reported by clients; failing posture moves the device into a restricted group. CLI enrollment.
6. M4 gate (multi-node lab: mTLS east-west with L7 deny, egress enforce / monitor, VPN client reaching only allowed services).

### 2026-10-18 — M5 step 7 design (GitOps 3.29 + plan bot 3.30), implementation decisions within the plan

- **Transport: the `git` CLI** in the control-plane image (`git` + `openssh-client` from Debian trixie, pinned package versions, base image already digest-pinned), called with `execFile` (no shell), `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, a per-operation temp dir (0700, removed afterwards), shallow fetches. SSH: deploy key written to a 0600 temp file, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` with `IdentitiesOnly=yes` and a per-connection pinned host key (trust on first use, stored; a changed host key stops the sync with an error). HTTPS: token via `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `http.extraHeader` env (never in URLs, argv or logs). Reason over isomorphic-git: SSH (plain Git over SSH is in scope) and all providers with one client; Agenstra also uses the CLI.
- **Connections are direct API** (like memberships, 3.17): `lw_git_connections` per scope (cluster or one project): provider (github / gitlab / gitea / git), repo URL, branch, path, mode (authoritative / bidirectional), credentials (`secret://` ref, resolved through `PlatformCredentialsService`), trigger (webhook and / or polling interval), approval by merge review, memberships from Git, auto-merge after bot apply, SOPS. The webhook secret is derived (HKDF from `ENCRYPTION_KEY` + connection id), nothing extra stored. Cluster admins manage the cluster scope, project admins their project's.
- **Scope rule:** a project connection only carries that project's resources (others in its files are rejected with the plan); the cluster connection carries cluster-level resources and projects without their own connection. A connected scope's Git content is complete: resources of the scope missing in Git are planned as deletions (the plan shows them; export-to-repo makes the repo complete first).
- **Sync:** new head commit → files under the path (`*.yaml|*.yml`, SOPS-decrypted) → secret scan → plan with `source = {kind: 'git', connection, commit, ref, pr?, author}` (new plan column); per-resource sync state (`lw_git_resource_state`: file path, generation, commit) for conflicts (resource changed outside Git since the last sync → plan warning `git-conflict`, never overwritten silently) and for writing back. Commit status (`loadweaver/plan`) on GitHub / GitLab / Gitea follows the plan (pending / approved / applied / failed); plain Git has no status API.
- **Secret scanning:** known token formats (GitHub, GitLab, AWS, Slack, Stripe, private key blocks, JWTs…), credential-named keys with literal high-entropy values; a hit rejects the push (no plan), sets a failed status, audit + inbox item. Secret references and SOPS-encrypted values are fine.
- **SOPS:** age recipients only (KMS recipients later with the external KMS work): one X25519 age identity per cluster, private part sealed with the master key; age + SOPS decryption (AES-256-GCM values, MAC check) implemented on `node:crypto` in `util-secrets` and tested against files made by the real `sops` binary in a lab (digest-pinned image). The public recipient is shown in the console.
- **Modes:** authoritative — a UI / API plan in the scope is created but can't be applied; Loadweaver opens a PR / MR (branch `loadweaver/plan-<id>`, files at their synced paths, new ones under `<path>/<project>/<kind>-<name>.yaml`) and links it; plain Git pushes the branch. Bidirectional — after a non-Git plan applies, Loadweaver commits the changed files back (message with plan id and author). Export-to-repo: one commit with the scope's current state. Drift: a default-branch commit whose plan isn't applied is "default branch ahead of cluster" (drift view, inbox, every following PR comment); foreign containers can be proposed as a commit / PR in connected scopes. Memberships from Git (optional): `access.yaml` in the path is imported on sync (direct-API semantics), direct changes are committed back.
- **Plan bot** (GitHub App: RS256 app JWT on `node:crypto` → installation token; GitLab: project / group access token; app / OAuth credentials are `Cluster.spec.git` secret refs): webhook endpoint `POST /api/git/webhooks/:connection` with the raw body (GitHub / Gitea `X-Hub-Signature-256`, GitLab `X-Gitlab-Token`, constant-time); PR opened / pushed → plan of the PR head, PR locks on the touched scopes (other PRs see them), one sticky comment (marker, updated) with changes per resource and layer, pins / failure analysis, quota / capacity, image policy results, drift of touched resources, locks by other PRs, links to the plan and the map overlay; status check. Commands `loadweaver plan [project|path] | apply | unlock | approve | drift` by linked accounts with the role (3.17), audited with PR, commit and user; apply needs mergeable + the scope's approval rules (a PR review by a linked operator / admin counts if configured); auto-merge after a successful apply (configurable); merge without apply / direct push → not applied, "ahead" drift. Account linking: OAuth (GitHub / GitLab) with an HMAC-signed state, only the provider user id / login stored (the OAuth token is discarded).
- **Tests:** Gitea lab (digest-pinned) for real clone / push / commit statuses / PRs with polling (lab containers can't reach the test process, so webhooks are tested by signed requests), SOPS lab, mock GitHub / GitLab servers for the bot, unit tests for scanning, rendering, signatures, JWT.
- Order: 7a transport + connections + sync + statuses + scanning + modes + export + drift + memberships; 7b SOPS (parallel, separate lib); 7c plan bot + account linking; 7d console Git parts (connection settings, sync status / conflicts, commit / PR links on plans, PR opening of UI edits, "ahead" drift, drift → PR, export, account linking); then docs / specs / review.
- Console review fixes (all 15): previews without `blob:` (raster images as `data:` URLs re-typed by extension, SVG as text), every download re-wrapped as `application/octet-stream` with a `download` link; ApexCharts series names / tooltip output HTML-escaped; `silent-check-sso.html`; a feature meta-reducer resets every `console*` slice on logout / access clear, favourites reloaded per open; terminal socket re-created when dead, sockets opened after destroy closed; join command absolute and with the token read from stdin (`read -rs` + `sudo --preserve-env`), shown separately; socket auth callback (fresh token per reconnect); certificates list / detail (`/certificates`, cluster roles; the inbox links there); back buttons via the router; editor seeds only from the fresh resource; own-property lookups in the schema checker; confirm before a deep-linked node shell and before approving; server messages from blob error bodies; bare-route fix, report viewer URL kept, cast player applies resizes. 157 + 201 tests, production build without missing translations.
- Step 7b done (SOPS): `util-secrets` gained age v1 (X25519: Bech32 identities / recipients, header MAC, STREAM payload, armor; encrypt + decrypt, low-order shares / truncation / trailing data rejected) and SOPS decryption (AES-256-GCM values with the path AAD, SHA-512 MAC exactly as sops 3.13 computes it incl. `mac_only_encrypted`, suffix / regex rules, encrypted comments, multi-document) on `node:crypto` only. Known-answer fixtures from the real binaries + a lab (`integration-test`) against `ghcr.io/getsops/sops:v3.13.3-alpine@sha256:ae5012…` and age 1.3.2 (sha256-checked) — 109 unit + 11 lab tests. Not supported (documented): KMS / PGP / Vault recipients, Shamir key groups, comment regexes, YAML aliases. Wired into the Git sync after 7a lands.
- Step 7a done (GitOps core): `git/` in feature-control-plane — `git-client.ts` (git CLI via `execFile`, per-operation 0700 temp dir, only https / ssh, no system / global config, hooks, symlinks, prompts or redirects, token as Basic `http.extraHeader` via env, SSH key file 0600 with `IdentitiesOnly`, host key pinned on first contact then `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`, timeouts / output caps / scrubbed errors), URL validation, secret scan, sync (polling under lock 0x4c57001b, signed webhooks `POST /git/webhooks/:connection` with the raw body), scope rule, conflicts (`git-conflict`), commit statuses (GitHub / GitLab / Gitea adapters), authoritative mode (plan blocked, PR / branch opened) and bidirectional commit-back, export, "ahead" drift + inbox items, `access.yaml` import / commit-back; plans carry `source` (git / ui / api / drift / system); `git:admin` PAT scope; migration 28; image gets `git=1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1`, `openssh-client=1:10.0p1-7+deb13u4`. Decisions beyond the design: Git plans count as developer plans (approval rules apply), Cluster / Node never planned as deletions, an empty path fails the sync ("export first"), project connections may only use their own project's secrets (the token goes to the configured host), `membershipsFromGit` on a project needs a cluster admin or the project creator, optional `caCertificate` for private CAs. 335 unit tests, control-plane integration 41/41, Gitea lab 11/11 (`gitea/gitea:1.27.3-rootless`, digest-pinned; HTTPS + SSH deploy key). Open: SOPS wiring (seam `GitSopsDecryptor`), linking a merged authoritative PR's plan to the UI plan, SSRF of project-admin repo URLs (HTTPS with TLS verification / SSH, no redirects, scrubbed errors — rated low; decide at the gate: host allowlist or accepted risk).
- Step 7d done (console Git parts, the items noted "added with step 7"): `/git` + `/git/:id` (connections per scope with status, commit history → plans / PRs / rejection reasons, validated create / edit mirroring the backend rules, test / sync / export (force warned) / host-key reset / disconnect behind confirms, webhook secret once on create and otherwise on demand after an "audited" confirm, SOPS recipient with the `sops` hint), plan source badges (Git commit / ref / PR / author; console / API / drift / system), prominent `git-conflict` warnings, authoritative scopes: apply disabled with the PR link, editor says "Plan and open pull request"; drift "default branch ahead"; Git inbox kinds; `/settings/git-accounts` (link GitHub / GitLab via the returned https authorize URL, unlink, translated callback outcomes only). 170 + 230 tests, production build complete in de.
- Step 7c done (plan bot, SOPS wiring, account linking): `ClusterSopsDecryptor` (one age identity per cluster, private part envelope-encrypted under the master key in `lw_git_sops_keys`, re-wrapped on master-key re-shares; sealed key → clear sync error), `GET /git/sops/recipient`; `Cluster.spec.git.{github,gitlab}` (app / OAuth credentials as secret refs); GitHub App JWT (RS256, `node:crypto`) + cached installation tokens; GitHub / GitLab bot (PR head plans via the extracted `planTree`, PR locks in `lw_resource_locks` moved per push and released on apply / close / unlock, sticky comment ≤ 60k chars, status follows the plan, commands audited `git.command.*`, mergeability ignoring our own status, review approvals only on the current head, auto-merge pinned to the head SHA, merged-without-apply triggers the default-branch sync → "ahead" in later comments, superseded UI plans linked both ways); account linking (HMAC state, 10 min, single-use nonce, only provider id / login stored, fixed-code redirects to the console); `git:accounts` PAT scope; migration 29. Decisions beyond the design: using the GitHub App needs a cluster admin (`githubApp`, reset when repo / API / provider change), fork PRs only planned on a linked account's `loadweaver plan`, supersede checked against the recorded PR, bot commands use the linked user's memberships only (no global-admin shortcut), unacknowledged pins need `loadweaver apply --confirm`. Tests: 362 unit, CP integration 41/41, Gitea lab 12/12 (real sops), bot integration 15/15 (mock GitHub / GitLab APIs + `git http-backend` over HTTPS). Open: webhook events queued in memory (lost on restart → next push / `loadweaver plan`), no Gitea bot (post-MVP per plan), commit status instead of a check run; console follow-ups: `githubApp` toggle, `git:accounts` scope in the token UI, superseded links.

### 2026-10-18 — M6 plan (operations: live migration, updates, backups / DR, import, Agenstra runtime, autoscaling)

Checked on this machine: Docker Desktop 29.8.2 (experimental off, no `runsc`, no `criu`; runc reports checkpoint support), WSL kernel 6.18 with CHECKPOINT_RESTORE / MEM_SOFT_DIRTY / USERFAULTFD but **no DRBD** (the M2 volume manager has never run against real DRBD), `/dev/kvm` present. CRIU labs need privileged Docker-in-Docker nodes with `criu` + experimental mode.

0. Spikes (CRIU in dind incl. pre-dump and custom checkpoint dirs, writable-layer loss, runsc in dind, OpenSearch `repository-s3`, Spilo WAL-G → Garage PITR, Garage object lock, Kopia on Garage / SFTP / MinIO with lock) + **protocol versioning**: every agent-protocol schema is `.strict()`, which contradicts "control plane compatible with N-1 agents" (3.26) → `protocolVersion` + `features[]` in hello, the control plane only sends what a node advertises, contract tests against the previous release's schema snapshot.
1. Live migration with fallback (3.10): eligibility (runtime, checkpoint capability, no devices / host network, size vs. link, `liveMigration` opt-out, stateful only to a sync replica), iterative pre-copy over WireGuard, freeze, restore, cut-over, automatic short-stop fallback with the source kept until the target runs, dependency-ordered waves with health gates (not built yet), method per service in the plan; agent checkpoint manager + node-to-node transfer (mTLS + single-use token + built-in policy); `lw_migrations` history (migration 31).
2. Release bundles + update rollout incl. OS / kernel rolling upgrades (3.26, 3.21): one signed manifest pinning every component (today spread over env overrides and agent defaults), download once / air-gap import, update as a plan, control plane first then canary then waves within N+1 per site, health gates with pause / rollback, per-component methods (agent swap + restart with Docker live-restore, Envoy hot restart, BIRD graceful restart, Patroni switchover, etcd / OpenSearch / Garage member by member, kernel / DRBD / gVisor / WireGuard via drain → update → reboot → rejoin), cluster-local apt source, `UpdatePolicy` + `MaintenanceWindow`, expand / contract migrations, CLI version warning, releases through the shared updates feature (widened to `loadweaver` + a beta channel, with Agenstra / Decabill regressions); console updates admin; migration 32.
3. Backups / DR with Garage (3.20): separate backup keys, Shamir recovery kit (download + confirm, pin until confirmed, optional KMS escrow), volume snapshots (LVM-thin under LUKS) with hooks, dedup + encrypted incremental upload, WAL-G PITR for Postgres / TimescaleDB, OpenSearch snapshots, etcd snapshots, `BackupPolicy` / `BackupTarget` kinds (S3 / SFTP, secondary copies), immutability (object lock on external S3), deletion / retention shortening with a second admin + 72 h delay, catalog / timeline / diff, restores as plans (whole / new volume / single file / control-plane PITR), restore tests, quotas count backup bytes, whole-cluster DR bootstrap; migration 33.
4. Import of existing Docker hosts and former nodes (3.21): read-only discovery (compose projects, containers, volumes, networks, ports, interfaces / routes / VPNs / nftables, former-Loadweaver markers), wizard → one join plan (install components, import / migrate in dependency order, rsync pre-copy + final pass, ports to the ingress, conflict-free ports / interfaces, overlapping subnets refused, make-before-break via the bootstrap tunnel), rejoin reuses valid DRBD replicas. Conflict with what's built: the installer installs everything and joined nodes get an active desired state immediately → installer `--discover` mode, node lifecycle `pending` (no-op desired state), component installation as an idempotent agent step driven by the join plan; migration 34.
5. Agenstra runtime on Loadweaver (section 4 steps 1–2): agent-manager as a Loadweaver deployment; an `AgentRuntime` interface extracted from the 3,453-line `DockerService` (unchanged behind it) + `LoadweaverRuntime` (environments as sandboxed deployments in a per-workspace project, manager → env policies); Squid egress guard → Envoy policies compiled from Agenstra's effective egress policy with identical semantics (property test against `evaluateEgressDestination`); Loadweaver gaps: non-TTY exec for machine credentials (`live:exec`), per-selector egress mode, URL deny patterns (RE2), egress decisions attributed to deployment / service.
6. Horizontal autoscaling (3.23): `AutoscalerService` (leader lock, 15 s, HPA formula with tolerance, 5 min down-stabilisation, cooldowns, newest replica first), planner reads autoscaled counts, never beyond quota / capacity / N+1, audited events on graphs and the map; `requests` needs an HTTP exposure; custom = metrics already in `lw_metrics`; migration 35.
7. Reports / status pages finish (3.25): backups / restore tests / upgrades in reports, inbox items (updates available, backup / restore-test failures, unconfirmed kit), backup pins in health; planned-maintenance notes on status pages.
8. M6 gate.

Implementation decisions taken (within the plan; recorded here): protocol versioning as above; Docker experimental mode enabled by the installer when live migration is on, reported as a node capability; the writable layer travels as an upperdir diff (services writing to their rootfs aren't live-eligible if that fails in the spike); frozen-index apt proxy on the control plane (snapshot of `InRelease` / `Packages` at plan time, debs by checksum from Garage, distro signatures verified by apt); bundles signed with an ECDSA P-256 key (CI secret; verifier from `image-signature.ts`; public key compiled into control plane, agent and CLI), version = the repo's release tag, beta = prerelease; contract migrations in `src/migrations/contract/`, run only after every component reports N; agent-manager authenticates with a project-scoped operator PAT (secret) and a new `live:exec` scope for a non-TTY exec channel (rate-limited, audited), environments created / deleted as plans with source `api`; runtime chosen by manager environment (`AGENT_RUNTIME=docker|loadweaver`); a Docker-host manager on a Loadweaver node needs an acknowledged pin (docker.sock) and its `io.agenstra.*` containers show as "delegated", not drift; `Policy.egressMode` (selector-scoped, most restrictive wins) + `denyUrlPatterns` (RE2, untranslatable patterns are plan errors); custom autoscale metrics = existing `lw_metrics` series; moving server providers into the shared lib + node ordering (section 4, third bullet) belongs to the P track (Cloud operations); optional `Cluster.spec.objectStore.nodeGroup` for dedicated storage holders.

User decisions (2026-10-18, M6):

- **VM lab approved**: QEMU/KVM + Debian 13 cloud images on this machine, 3 VMs on 2 simulated sites (~6 GB RAM / 30 GB disk while running, removed afterwards) for DRBD, kernel rolling upgrades with reboots, former-node rejoin and whole-cluster DR on real kernels (also verifies the M2 DRBD path for the first time).
- **Live migration keeps addresses**: memory state and the service IP always follow; established connections follow for direct and ingress → replica flows by keeping the replica address (own IPAM plugin over a cluster pod supernet + /32 / /128 host routes in BIRD); meshed (mTLS) flows reconnect through Envoy retries, stated per service in the plan.
- **Backups: Kopia + append-only gateway**: Kopia (Apache-2.0, digest-pinned image) for dedup / encryption / S3 + SFTP / object-lock retention on external targets / snapshot diffs / file restores; nodes never hold Garage keys — uploads go through an append-only S3 gateway on the members (no overwrite / DELETE); only the control plane's retention job deletes, after the second-admin approval + 72 h delay.
- **DR envelope**: master key + control-plane environment encrypted under the backup key and stored with every control-plane backup; the recovery kit (or KMS escrow) unlocks it, so a whole-cluster restore brings back secrets, the CA and identities.
- VM lab realisation: `sudo` needs a password here and the user isn't in `kvm`, but Docker Desktop's VM exposes `/dev/kvm` (24 vCPUs with VT) to containers → the VMs run as QEMU/KVM **inside a container** (digest-pinned Debian trixie image with pinned `qemu-system-x86`), disks in Docker volumes, nothing installed on the host — less invasive than a host install and within the approval.

### 2026-10-18 — M6 progress

- Step 0b done (protocol versioning): `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`, optional `protocolVersion` / `features` in the agent hello (agents without them = version 0, no features), `negotiate` (lower version, common features), declarative field gates (`CONTROL_PLANE_FIELD_GATES`, paths with `[]` / `*`) applied centrally in the agent session's `send` (`forNode` / `envelopeForNode`, re-validated, ids kept); agents send version + features and stay strict. - **Live-migration restore at the runc level**: `docker start --checkpoint` is broken on every tested Docker (moby wires the netns from pid 0 before the shim restores; custom checkpoint dirs refused). Pre-dumps + final dump + restore run with runc directly (Docker's runc root `/run/docker/runtime-runc/moby`, `--tcp-established --manage-cgroups-mode=soft`; spike: 150 MB process → ~0.48 s freeze, TCP kept). A restored replica runs as an **agent-managed runc container** (the agent provides logs, stats, exec, health, networking for it) until its next restart, when it goes back to Docker. The moby bug is reported upstream; Docker restore replaces this once fixed. gVisor services: `runsc checkpoint` / `restore` (stop-and-copy, no pre-dump; rootfs writes inside the image). tmpfs is never pre-dumped → counted in the frozen size for eligibility.
- **Backup gateway = Kopia repository servers with ACLs** on the members (they hold the Garage keys; nodes connect over TLS with APPEND / READ — create, list and restore their own snapshots; delete, policy changes and maintenance refused), one repository per trust boundary (cluster + each project; users of one repository share its key and dedup); retention / maintenance only by the control plane. WAL-G (with `WALG_PREVENT_WAL_OVERWRITE=true`, Spilo's own `postgres_backup.sh` retention disabled, clones with their own scope) and OpenSearch snapshots (derived image with the official `repository-s3` 3.9.0 plugin, `index.latest` overwrite, `?verify=false`) go through a small S3 gateway allowing only their required overwrites / deletes; Garage ignores object-lock headers and `If-None-Match`, so the gateway enforces no-overwrite itself.

  - **Shared LUKS volume key**: new replicas are formatted with `--volume-key-file` (`--master-key-file` before cryptsetup 2.5) holding HKDF-SHA256(volume secret, volume id) on tmpfs (`/run/loadweaver`, statfs-checked, 0600, zeroed + removed right after), AES-XTS 512 / 4 KiB sectors / offset 16 MiB, key slot PBKDF2 with minimal iterations (Argon2id failed silently on busy 1 GiB guests; a slow KDF adds nothing with a machine-generated secret the key is derived from), cryptsetup timeout 120 s; resource files get `verify-alg sha256`. - Step 1c (gVisor) done — gVisor live migration (3.10 "gVisor's own checkpoint / restore for sandboxed ones"), stop-and-copy.
  - **Why the earlier restore had no network:** `runsc restore` scrapes interfaces / addresses / routes from the network namespace its sandbox process runs in (`--network=sandbox`, `createInterfacesAndRoutesFromNS`, `ContMgrSetNetworkArgs` with `IsRestore`) and `Kernel.LoadFrom` reconfigures the restored netstack with them (`ResetConfig` + `ConfigureNetwork`, then `Stack.Restore`). The restore bundle must therefore name the placeholder's netns by path (`linux.namespaces[network].path = /proc/<holder>/ns/net`) and run with the checkpointed sandbox's runtime flags (Docker's `runsc-systrap` entry: `--platform=systrap`, default `--network=sandbox`, `--overlay2=root:self`). Verified first in dind (bridge address and a kept-style `/32` + `169.254.1.1` onlink default), then in the VM lab.
  - **TCP connections survive** (gVisor `allow-live-tcp-migration`, default true): established endpoints are re-connected on restore. Two traps found in gVisor's source and measured: (1) `runsc checkpoint --leave-running` (save-resume) marks connections `terminateAtRestore` → they are dropped on any restore elsewhere, so the source is **not** left running: stop-and-copy (sandbox exits), abort = restore of the source's own image into a fresh placeholder; (2) `allowLiveTCPMigration` is `nosave` and only set on sandboxes runsc starts → a restored sandbox resets its connections at its next checkpoint (second move, resume after an aborted one). Fix: restores run with `--allow-connected-on-save` (re-applied from the restore's config in `CreateLinksAndRoutes`).
  - Agent: `CheckpointManager` — runsc via Docker's runtime entry (root `/run/docker/runtime-runc/moby`), the running container's OCI `process` saved before the checkpoint (`process.json`, sent with the image: runsc's restore spec validation compares it), no upper tar (rootfs writes are in the image); restored gVisor replicas located by label (`loadweaver.com/restored-runtime=runsc`, root `/run/loadweaver/runsc`). `MigrationService` — freeze: restart policy off, veth down, `runsc checkpoint` (`frozen: stopped`); restore / local resume: `runsc restore -detach --allow-connected-on-save` into the placeholder (same cgroup split and stdio relay as runc); gVisor binaries (`runsc` + `gvisor-bin/`) read at prepare. `RestoredRuntime` — runc and runsc roots (`list` / `pid` / `remove` / `stop` cover both), host-side nftables table `lw_restore_<id>` dropping forward + output traffic to the placeholder's addresses from before its start until the restore ended (the placeholder's kernel would RST the connections being restored; applies to runc too); gVisor placeholders get `Healthcheck: NONE` and the agent runs the service's (or image's) check through `runsc exec` with Docker's semantics (`healthOf`, reported by `WorkloadManager.status`); terminals `runsc exec` (`restoredExecCommand(…, 'runsc')`), file browsing refused. Capability: `checkpoint.runsc` = sandbox runtime registered with gVisor netstack (`--network=host` / `none` runtimes don't count), `runsc --version` runs, cgroup v2 (`RUNSC_RESTORE_SUPPORTED` removed).

  - **S3 gateway = part of the control-plane API process** (`backups/platform/s3-gateway*.ts`, `PlatformS3GatewayService`), not a container: the API already runs on every member and derives the Garage keys from `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so no new image / pin / secret; it listens on loopback only (`LOADWEAVER_BACKUP_GATEWAY_LISTEN`, set by the agent; port `7480`, `LOADWEAVER_BACKUP_GATEWAY_PORT`, outside Kopia's 7500–7755). Holds its own Garage key for the new bucket `lw-platform` (HKDF per generation, `platformGarageKey`); clients (WAL-G, OpenSearch) get per-member credentials `LWPB…` (HKDF of role + node; the key id is in the desired state, the secret added at push time like the registry secrets). Own SigV4 verifier / signer (AWS documentation vectors in the tests) incl. `aws-chunked` (chunk signatures chained from the seed, signed / unsigned trailers, CRC32 / SHA-256 / SHA-1 trailer checksums); hash payloads are forwarded with the same `x-amz-content-sha256` so Garage verifies them, chunked ones are decoded, verified and forwarded `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD` with the decoded length (a bad chunk aborts the upstream request). Rules (`s3-gateway.rules.ts`): only bucket `lw-platform`, keys / list prefixes under the client prefix (`spilo/`, `opensearch/`), no copies / ACL / policy / versions / unknown sub-resources, ≤ 5 GiB per request, **HEAD before PUT under a per-key lock** (Garage ignores `If-None-Match` and object-lock headers) for PUT / CreateMultipartUpload / CompleteMultipartUpload, whitelist only OpenSearch's `index.latest` / `incompatible-snapshots`; DELETE / `POST ?delete` only while a retention grant exists (`lw_platform_backup_grants`, checked by every member's gateway, keys under the grant prefix); client writes `503 SlowDown` while an object-store generation is in its final copy / sweep (the platform bucket was added to the copied buckets). Lock scope = one gateway process; acceptable because each client only talks to its own member's gateway and WAL / `index-N` are written by one primary / cluster manager. ### 2026-10-19 — M6 Step 6 (autoscaling)

- Step 6 done — horizontal autoscaling (3.23).
  - **Compose** (`util-compose`): `x-loadweaver.autoscale` (already parsed) now validated for use: `requests` needs `exposure.http` (plan error), jobs / cron jobs and services with a read-write volume can't be autoscaled, `container_name` refuses `max > 1`, `customMetric` must be a metric name; the "one replica" warning uses `min`. The compose `replicas` is the starting count (clamped to min..max).
  - **`AutoscalerService`** (`autoscaling/`, every 15 s, `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` like the other controllers, then the placement-allocation lock so it serialises with plans / failover / drains / cron): value = average of the last minute — `cpu` / `memory` = `replica.cpu_cores` / `replica.memory_bytes` in % of the **request**, `requests` = `ingress.requests_per_s` of the service's hostnames (all ingress nodes added up) / replicas (no ingress samples while any node reports metrics = 0 req/s, since agents only report hostnames with traffic), `custom` = the named `lw_metrics` series of the service's replicas (average), else its hostnames (`*_per_s` summed, other metrics the worst), else the service id. Pure `recommend()`: `ceil(current × value / target)`, 10 % tolerance, up immediately bounded to max(×2, +4) with a 30 s up-cooldown, down only to the max recommendation of a fully observed 5-min window (and ≥ 60 s after the last action), clamp to min..max, a count outside min..max (changed by a plan) goes back into the range first; missing metrics / a migrating replica / nothing placed → hold with the reason. Scale-up limits via `largestAllowed` (binary search): project quota (CPU / memory with autoscaled services at their current count), cluster capacity (`schedule()` with current placements kept, then a real-layout fit check), N+1 (node-scope capacity findings of `analyzeFailures` may not grow; skipped with < 2 workload nodes — a single node has no reserve). Blocked or at max → `status.blocked` + new built-in alert `builtin:autoscale-blocked` (5 min, → inbox). Scale-up creates placements directly (addresses via `planner.allocateOn`), scale-down deletes the **highest-index** replicas (normal stop path); no `planner.persist` (it would also rewrite volumes / service addresses). Each action: audit `workload.autoscaled` (from, to, metric, value, target, reason, blocked, added replicas + nodes), `autoscale` event in `lw_events` (graph markers), state saved. Node reachability uses the wall clock; `LOADWEAVER_AUTOSCALER=off` (defaults to `LOADWEAVER_WORKLOAD_CONTROLLER`).
  - **Planner**: `parseAutoscaled()` / `autoscaleCounts()` — autoscaled services run `clamp(state ?? compose replicas, min, max)`; `WorkloadPlan.autoscaled`. Plans: info line `autoscaled n (min..max), <metric> target …` per autoscaled service of submitted deployments, quota checked against **min** (`projectUsage(..., 'min')` default; `'current'` for the quota alert and the autoscaler), warning when `max` would exceed the quota. ### 2026-10-20 — Gate items (light): certs, drain, joining nodes, DR replan

- Four items carried to the M6 gate, fixed by the light agent (code + unit tests; integration / labs run at the gate). Migration **`1800000000040_PostgresCertificatesReplicaDrain`** (039 stays reserved for step 5).
  - **Postgres server certificates (deterministic + timer renewal)**: `lw_postgres_certificates` (per member: serial, address, certificate, private key AES-256-GCM via the shared transformer, CA fingerprint, not before / after). `ClusterIdentityService.memberPostgresCertificate` (replaces `issuePostgresCertificate`, called from `pushDesiredState`) reuses the stored certificate while CA + member address match and more than a third of its lifetime is left (same threshold as the agent's switch-over), else issues one and stores it compare-and-swap on the serial (insert-or-ignore / update where serial = old) — every replica then pushes the winner, so desired states are byte-identical across pushes and replicas. `PostgresCertificateRenewalService`: first check 5 min after start, then daily, `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(0x4c570044)`; members (control plane, not left) whose stored certificate passed 2/3 of its lifetime → `NetworkStateService.repush(nodes, reason)` (new: the nodes' unchanged desired-state rows under a new cluster revision + `pg_notify`, so every replica pushes them again; the push renews). `LOADWEAVER_POSTGRES_CERTIFICATE_RENEWAL=off` disables the timer. Pure logic in `services/postgres-certificates.ts`.
  - **Two-phase removal (drain)**: `lw_workload_placements.drain_until`. Planner `persist` no longer deletes removed replicas: it sets `drainUntil = now + clamp(stop_grace_period, 2 s, 120 s)` (default 10 s; grace from the compose, else from the replica's `releasedSpec`), cancels a migration of it, never prolongs a running drain; deletes at once only when the node left or a short-stop already stopped it. A draining replica planned again on its node ends its drain (kept, same addresses); on another node its drain is cut short and it is placed anew. Autoscaler scale-down sets the deadline instead of deleting (scale-up reuses a draining replica on the same node), counts / capacity / `GET /autoscaling` ignore draining replicas; `planner.current()` (plans, diff, DR replan) and the lost-node / node-drain controller paths skip them. Rendering: `effectiveSpec` serves a draining replica its `releasedSpec` (no restart even if the service changed / was removed; null → stops at once), `releasedSpec` isn't updated while draining; routing: `CompilerWorkload.draining` (new optional field) → no service-IP backend, no mesh upstream endpoint / inbound backend (policies, tunnels and firewall rules stay for open connections), excluded from ingress endpoints and health-gated BGP announcements. `ReplicaDrainService` (every 2 s, `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(0x4c570045)` + the placement-allocation lock, re-read under the lock) deletes placements whose drain ended and recompiles → the agent stops them with their grace period; runs regardless of `LOADWEAVER_WORKLOAD_CONTROLLER`.
  - **Volume plans while a node is joining**: `nodeNotReady()` (`utils/node-readiness.utils.ts`): within 30 min of `joinedAt`, a node is not ready while its agent isn't connected, it has no desired state yet, its `appliedRevision` is behind its desired-state revision (a new member pulling / starting etcd, Spilo, the API), or a member's last report has a failed `control-plane` step. `plannerNodes(nodes, now, desiredRevisions)` (only `planner.plan` passes revisions; autoscaler / capacity checks unchanged) → `SchedulerNode.notReady`. Scheduler (`util-scheduler`): not-ready nodes keep copies they hold but get no new sync / remote copies; a new volume's primary goes to a ready node when one fits, a not-ready one only as the only fit; `ScheduleResult.held` lists held-back copies → planner issues (plan warnings) `volume data gets no copy on n2 (joining: …) while it is joining; plan again once the node is ready to add the copy` (or the primary note). Decision: exclude + note (safer than holding the plan); the copy is added by the next plan after the node is ready (persist rewrites volume placements on every plan).
  - **DR replan**: `samePlacements(current, schedule)` (replicas → nodes, volume holders, order-insensitive); `DrRecoveryService.replan` persists and recompiles only when the computed placements differ from what is placed; `replannedAt` still set once everything fits.

### 2026-10-20 — M6 gate part A (VM lab)

Heavy agent; every lab run guarded (available ≥ 8 GB, no integration jest, heavy lock + VM lab lock, memory watchdog < 3 GB, `cleanup.sh` after each run). One WSL crash during the first bootstrap-lab attempt (overlapped with a CP integration run; coordinator cleaned up) — rerun afterwards.

- **1. Docker `Image` digest (images gate)** — confirmed in `updates.vm-lab` (a2): the golden's Docker 29.9.1 uses the containerd image store; for a container created by digest reference, `docker inspect` `.Image` = image ID (`sha256:<manifest digest>` with containerd, config digest with the classic store), `.Config.Image` = reference incl. `@sha256:`, and the **list API's `Image`** (what the agent reports) = the created-from reference incl. digest → `runsDigest` (endsWith digest) passes; no gate change needed. Hardening: when the list API falls back to the image ID (classic store, reference no longer resolving), the agent now reports the container's `Config.Image` if it carries a digest (`UpdatesService.runningImage`; unit "reports the created-from reference … when Docker lists a container's image ID"). Also (b) adapted to the L5 block message ("not retried while it stays on release 3.6.0; 3.5.0 keeps running") and extended: the block marker exists, moving the node back to 3.5.0 clears it (`failed-*` gone).
- **2. Real kernel-ABI change** — new golden variant `older-kernel` (`golden.ts` `OLDER_KERNEL_IMAGE`: Debian 13 genericcloud `20260914-2601`, sha512-pinned, kernel 6.12.107 whose headers are still in trixie main; same provisioning; default golden name unchanged). Volume **`lw-vmlab-golden-60be62f433e4`** (1.77 GiB, built in 276 s) — **kept** (needed by every `updates.vm-lab` run). `startVmLab({ golden: 'older-kernel' })`. New case `updates.vm-lab` (d) (vm1 cluster apt source, vm2 node 1.5 GiB, vm3 DRBD peer): replicated volume vm2↔vm3 (protocol C) with data → drain (vm3 primary, keeps writing) → host update from the frozen snapshot (dist-upgrade to 6.12.113 from trixie-security, DRBD 9.2.20 rebuilt from the release's verified source; `modinfo -k` version + vermagic checked; GRUB `GRUB_DEFAULT=0`, first entry `/boot/vmlinuz-6.12.113+deb13-cloud-amd64`) → `rebootRequired` from the kernel (no flag file) → reboot token → `uname -r` = 6.12.113, DRBD 9.2.20 loads, report `rebootRequired=false` → replica rejoins and resyncs → failback, both writes' sha256 equal. Timings: snapshot 5–6 s, host update incl. DRBD build 110–123 s, reboot 23–24 s, resync 3–4 s; (d) 158–179 s + lab start 30–60 s.
  - **Product fixes**: (1) **DRBD replicas down before the reboot** (`OsUpdateManager.reboot`: `drbdadm down all`, best effort, then `systemctl reboot`) — torn down by the shutdown instead, the drained Secondary came back with out-of-sync bits toward the Primary under equal UUIDs (`uuid_compare()=no-sync by rule=lost-quorum`, `source-use-bitmap`), offered itself as sync source, the Primary declined → StandAlone, no resync (2 of 3 runs before the fix; 0 of 2 runs that reached the rejoin after it). Unit: reboot test expects `drbdadm down all` then `systemctl reboot`. (2) Host script fails **before the reboot** unless `modinfo -k <next kernel>` reports the release's DRBD version (a build that installs elsewhere / not at all no longer passes as `done`); unit asserts the check after `depmod`. (3) DRBD build output kept in `/var/log/loadweaver-drbd-build-<kernel>.log` (tail in the unit journal on failure) instead of `/dev/null`.
  - **Finding**: building DRBD 9.2.20 for 6.12.113 used **LINBIT's SPAAS** (`SPAAS 1f0538af…`, "Successfully connected to SPAAS") for its compat patch — an air-gapped node can't build from source for kernels DRBD's cocci cache doesn't know → bundles for air-gapped clusters need prebuilt modules (documented in `updates.md`; open: build / ship prebuilt modules per supported kernel in `build-bundle`).
  - Lab fixes: wait for the DRBD connection before the first mount; DRBD diagnostics (status, `.res`, `lvs`, kernel log of both peers) on a sync timeout; host-update diagnostics incl. the apt source's journal; the lab apt source's pool index (`apt-source.entry.ts` `filePool`) raced under apt's parallel downloads (read of a half-written `pool.json` → 404 for several packages) → serialized atomic writes, errors logged (the control plane's pool index is in Postgres, not affected); temp dirs created in `beforeAll` (a `-t`-filtered describe never ran `afterAll` and leaked them).

Bootstrap slowdown** — new `bootstrap.vm-lab.spec.ts` (one VM sized like the drill's vm1, real agent from `dr-agent.entry.ts`, timeline from agent output, Docker events, etcd / Patroni / API logs; cold and warm). No DCS waits or retries in Patroni's log. During bootstrap the member address is loopback, so `ETCD3_HOSTS` is `127.0.0.1:2379` both before and after the local-etcd change (identical Spilo env). **Not a regression**: the 241–327 s vs 130–151 s in the drill is the image download (Spilo ~1 GB from ghcr through the lab NAT; varies with network / load) — no fix. dr.vm-lab not re-run (bootstrap unchanged).
