Gate part B (heavy) starts with the source-based suites.

### 2026-10-20 — Gate fixes (light 4): control-plane image packaging, forget-peer retry

- **CP image packaging — root cause (three layers)**: (1) the `prune-lockfile` target (`@nx/js:prune-lockfile`) **overwrote** the `package.json` / lockfile that webpack's `generatePackageJson` had produced with the project's hand-written `apps/.../package.json` (33 deps) — the executor always reads the source project's `package.json`; (2) even webpack's generated list missed `@bull-board/*` and `semver` (and drops the root-devDependency `tslib`), because Loadweaver imports the domain barrels `@forepath/shared/backend` / `@forepath/identity/backend` (→ `libs/domains/<domain>/backend/index.ts`, owned by no Nx project) → no file-level graph edges to `util-queue`, `feature-updates`, `feature-notifications`, … → Nx can't see their npm packages, while the bundle still loads them; (3) Nx's npm lockfile pruning drops edges with dist-tag specs (`satisfies('147.0.1', 'latest')` is false → keycloak-connect's optional `chromedriver: latest` missing → `npm ci` EUSAGE) and re-hoists nested packages wrongly (a nested `content-type@2` shadowed `~1.0.5` → "Missing: content-type@1.0.5"). Agenstra / Decabill hand-list all runtime modules and use `npm i` (tolerates lock drift), so they don't hit it; Loadweaver uses `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.
- **Fix (generic)**: `tools/webpack/external-runtime-dependencies.cjs` (`ExternalRuntimeDependenciesPlugin`, registered in the CP, node-agent and CLI webpack configs, runs right after Nx's `GeneratePackageJsonPlugin`): adds every webpack **external** the bundle requires that's missing from the generated `package.json`, at the installed (root-lock) version, and replaces Nx's pruned lockfile with `pruneNpmLockfile` — the closure of the deps walked with Node's lookup through the root lockfile, every kept entry **at its original path and version** (no re-hoisting; optional deps kept whatever their spec, marked `optional` if only optionally reachable; optional peers not followed; dev flags dropped). Build fails on an external that isn't installed or a lockfile inconsistency (instead of the container). `prune-lockfile` targets removed from the three Loadweaver apps (`prune` → `build` + `copy-workspace-modules` [+ `compile-migrations`]); `apps/loadweaver/cli/package.json` added (its `copy-workspace-modules` failed without one). Project `package.json`s unchanged (still the base / pins).
- **Verification**: CP `dist` `package.json` 50 deps, all 72 `require()`s of `main.js` covered, lock 752 entries (was 33 deps; root lock 4147); `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run` passes on the CP, node-agent (282 entries) and CLI (107) outputs. Image `api-container-image` (heavy lock) built: `ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-control-plane-api:latest` = `350cef761411`, 745 MB; `docker run --memory=1g` with `JWT_SECRET`: all modules load, Nest initialises every module (BullBoard, OpenSearch, queue, OTel, …) and stops at DI of `UsersAuthGuard` under the default `AUTHENTICATION_METHOD=keycloak` — identical with the old workaround image (pre-existing, labs run `users`); container removed. Workaround image `loadweaver-control-plane-api:dr-lab` (`09b6037d866e`) removed (no container / lab used it) and **re-tagged from the proper build** (`docker tag ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-control-plane-api:latest loadweaver-control-plane-api:dr-lab`, as the drill's comment documents) — labs keep using `loadweaver-control-plane-api:dr-lab`.
- Note: the node agent / CLI non-SEA `package.json` now also lists `webpack` (Nx's graph sees `require('webpack')` in their `webpack.config.cjs`); harmless (both ship as SEA, `generatePackageJson: false`, plugin inactive).
- **forget-peer retry** (second-pass review, low): `VolumeManager` keeps peers whose `drbdsetup forget-peer` failed in the pending marker (`{ adjust: false, forget: [...] }`, the adjust is done) instead of deleting it → retried on every reconcile (no second adjust) until DRBD accepts it; idempotent ("Invalid peer-node-id" = slot already gone → forgotten; a peer that holds a replica again is dropped from the list). `forgetPeerWarning()` → the reconciler's `volumes` step carries a message (`DRBD forget-peer pending, retried on the next reconcile: <volume> (node-id n: <error>)`) without failing the apply; persisted on the node (`lastReportSteps`). Reconciler `step` accepts `boolean | { changed, message }`. Docs: `features/volumes.md`.
- Unit: feature-node-agent 42 suites / **296** tests (+3: pending + warning + retry until success; already-forgotten slot / re-added peer; step warning in the reconciler); tsc (lib + spec) clean; prettier clean. Integration suites / labs not run.
- Files: `tools/webpack/external-runtime-dependencies.cjs` (new), `apps/loadweaver/{backend-control-plane,backend-node-agent,cli}/{project.json,webpack.config.cjs}`, `apps/loadweaver/cli/package.json` (new); agent `lib/volumes/{volume.manager,volumes.spec}.ts`, `lib/reconciler/reconciler.service{,.spec}.ts`; `docs/loadweaver/features/volumes.md`.
- Review of "Gate fixes (light 4)": accepted (generic webpack plugin adds every runtime `require` + prunes the root lockfile itself; Nx `prune-lockfile` removed for the three Loadweaver apps; forget-peer retried + surfaced on the node). **Found (medium, pre-existing)**: the control-plane container doesn't start with the default `AUTHENTICATION_METHOD=keycloak` (DI error in `UsersAuthGuard`) — the labs only use `users` auth → light fix next. Unverified: DRBD's error text for an already-forgotten slot ("Invalid peer-node-id") → `drbd.vm-lab` re-run in part B. Low: eslint can't parse `.cjs` webpack configs (lint config, pre-existing).

### 2026-10-20 — Gate fixes (light 5): keycloak auth wiring, air-gapped DRBD builds

- **Keycloak DI error — root cause (identity wiring, shared)**: in keycloak mode `KeycloakUserSyncModule` provides `UsersAuthGuard` (for its `UsersController`), but the guard's deps `RevokedUserTokensRepository` / `PersonalAccessTokenService` exist only in `PatAuthModule`, a _sibling_ import of the host, not imported by `KeycloakUserSyncModule` (users mode works because `UsersAuthModule` imports `PatAuthModule`). Agenstra (agent-controller) and Decabill wire it identically → same latent failure there. **Fix**: `PatAuthModule.register()` returns a `global: true` dynamic module (`libs/domains/identity/backend/feature-auth/src/lib/modules/pat-auth.module.ts`), fixing all three hosts. CP auth wiring moved to `apps/loadweaver/backend-control-plane/src/app/auth-wiring.ts` (`controlPlaneAuthImports` / `controlPlaneAuthGuards`, used by `AppModule`); `auth-wiring.spec.ts` compiles it with a fake DataSource for `keycloak`, `users`, `api-key` (keycloak reproduced the exact error before the fix). Image rebuilt (heavy lock): `ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-control-plane-api:latest` = `52ae4d9684bc`, re-tagged `loadweaver-control-plane-api:dr-lab`. One container start (keycloak mode, no DB / Valkey): all modules incl. `KeycloakConnectModule` / `JwtModule` initialised, then exit 1 after TypeORM's retries — **inconclusive** (the DB-dependent `KeycloakUserSyncModule` instantiates only after the DataSource) → gate: start the image in keycloak mode with Postgres + Valkey.
- **Air-gapped DRBD builds**: DRBD 9.2.20 looks up its compat patch in `drbd-kernel-compat/cocci_cache/<md5 of compat.h>/`, else local spatch, else SPAAS (`gen_compat_patch.sh`; `SPAAS=false` disables it). Now:
  - **Bundle build**: `util-release/scripts/drbd-compat.sh <src> <sha256> <out> [kernel…]` (in a container of the OS release / arch; default kernels = targets of the kernel metapackages: Debian `linux-image-<arch>` / `-cloud-<arch>`, Ubuntu generic / virtual + HWE) runs `make -C drbd prep SPAAS=true` per kernel and packs `cocci_cache/<md5>/{compat.h,compat.patch,kernelrelease.txt}`. `build-bundle --drbd-compat <kernel>:<arch>=<entry>` validates each entry (`inspectDrbdCompatEntry`: only those files, md5 = dir, kernel listed; requires `--drbd-source`), dedupes identical md5s, stores `artifacts/drbd/compat/<kernel>-<arch>-<md5>.tar.gz`. Manifest: `components.drbd.compat[] {kernel, arch, file, md5}` (optional, absent when empty → older manifests byte-identical; in `referencedArtifacts` → checksummed + signed). Several entries per kernel allowed (Ubuntu 22.04 HWE / 24.04 share kernel release names). Release job: QEMU + new step generating entries for debian:12/13, ubuntu:22.04/24.04 × amd64/arm64, passed as `${DRBD_COMPAT}`.
  - **Agent**: `prepareDrbd` downloads the node arch's compat entries from the cluster by checksum; host script: (1) with `upgrade`, after `apt-get update` and **before** `dist-upgrade` simulates it (`-s dist-upgrade`, `Inst linux-image-<k>`) and fails for any kernel without a prebuilt module or compat patch — "nothing was changed"; (2) build branch extracts all entries for `$KVER` into the source's cache (`tar -m`, compat.patch touched last so make uses it), builds with `SPAAS=false`; a different `compat.h` md5 on the node fails with the expected md5s named. New `lw_fail` writes `failed: <reason>` into the result file → action error `host update failed: <reason>` (was `failed line N`). Installer: builds no DRBD (only `modinfo` / `modprobe`) → no SPAAS dependency for bootstrap / join.
  - Consequence (documented): a plan-time snapshot newer than the release's kernels is refused before changes; kernels ship via bundle patch releases (or plan with the bundle's snapshot). **Open (decision for the coordinator)**: whether online clusters' plan-time snapshots should hold kernel metapackages at the release's kernels instead of failing the host step. **Finding**: `build-bundle --apt-snapshot` adds only the index JSON, not the `InRelease` / `Packages` / pool files it names, and the release job builds no snapshot → the air-gapped apt snapshot in bundles is incomplete (pre-existing, not fixed).
- **Lab spec (written, not run)** `updates.vm-lab` (d): vm1 plays the bundle build (network ok): resolves the snapshot's cloud kernel (`apt-cache depends linux-image-cloud-amd64`, ≠ 6.12.107), runs `drbd-compat.sh` for it, DRBD source + entry into the artifact store, manifest with `drbdSource` + `drbdCompat`. vm2 gets an nftables output policy drop except lo / established / vm1 / vm3; asserts `curl https://spaas.drbd.io/api/v1/hello` fails. Negative step: same release with the compat entry labelled for 6.12.107 → action `failed` with "neither a prebuilt module nor a compat patch for kernel <next>" + "nothing was changed", `/lib/modules` unchanged. Then the real update: next kernel = resolved one, build log contains `cocci_cache/<md5>/compat.patch` and no `SPAAS` / `spatch-as-a-service`; table removed before the reboot; rest of (d) unchanged.
- Unit: CP app 2 suites / 7 (+3); identity feature-auth 13 / 123; util-release 3 suites / 27 (+3, new `drbd-compat.spec.ts`); feature-node-agent 42 / 300 (+4: script asserts updated incl. `bash -n`, real-bash pre-check refusal with fake apt-get, covered kernels proceed, compat ignored without source / unsafe md5, OsUpdateManager arch-filtered compat download + reason as error); feature-control-plane updates 3 / 36. tsc (agent lib + spec incl. vm-lab, util-release lib + spec, CP app + spec) clean; eslint + prettier clean on touched files; build-bundle smoke (validation errors) ok.
- Files: identity `modules/pat-auth.module.ts`; CP `src/app/{app.module,auth-wiring,auth-wiring.spec}.ts`; util-release `src/lib/{manifest,source-manifest,drbd-compat,drbd-compat.spec}.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `scripts/{build-bundle.ts,drbd-compat.sh}`; agent `lib/updates/{host-commands,os-update.manager,updates.spec}.ts`, vm-lab `updates.vm-lab.spec.ts`; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; docs `features/updates.md` (new "DRBD without internet"), `deployment/host-requirements.md`.
- Gate must re-run: `updates.vm-lab` (all, esp. (d) with the new air-gap assertions; (c) uses DRBD compat path only if its kernel changes), CP image start in keycloak mode with Postgres/Valkey (+ any image-based labs / DR drill with the new `dr-lab` tag), Agenstra/Decabill backend unit/integration suites touching auth (PatAuthModule now global), CP integration suites (auth wiring refactor).
- Review of "Gate fixes (light 5)": accepted (`PatAuthModule.register()` global fixes keycloak-mode DI in the Loadweaver control plane and the same hidden failure in Agenstra agent-controller / Decabill; air-gapped DRBD builds via signed per-kernel compat-cache entries + `SPAAS=false`; installer never builds DRBD). **Coordinator decision (within 3.26, not a plan change)**: online clusters keep fresh apt snapshots (security auto-updates in maintenance windows must keep working, kernels included) — when no bundled compat entry / prebuilt module covers a new kernel, the agent falls back to SPAAS **only if the cluster is not air-gapped** (it reaches SPAAS); air-gapped clusters (bundle-imported, no upstream) refuse before any change, as implemented. **Gap (medium, against 3.26 air-gap capable)**: `build-bundle --apt-snapshot` packs only the index JSON, not the packages, and the release job builds no snapshot → bundle must carry the snapshot's package files (checksummed, signed) — light fix next. Gate re-runs: `updates.vm-lab` (all, new (d)), control-plane image in keycloak mode with Postgres + Valkey, CP integration suites, Agenstra / Decabill backend auth tests.

### 2026-10-20 — Gate fixes (light 6): SPAAS fallback online, bundle apt packages

- **SPAAS fallback for online clusters** (coordinator decision of light 5): air-gap is derived from existing state, no new cluster flag — a plan is **online** iff `Cluster.spec.updates.source !== 'upload'` **and** its apt snapshot was taken from upstream at plan time (`origin: 'plan'`; the bundle's snapshot after an upstream failure = air-gapped) (`drbdSpaasAllowed`, `rollout-planner.utils.ts`). Persisted as `RolloutOptions.drbdSpaas` (OpenAPI) and `StepTarget.host.spaas`; sent as `components.host.spaas` behind the new protocol feature **`drbd-spaas`** (field gate; N-1 agents never see it). Host script with `spaas` (and a source): the pre-`dist-upgrade` check no longer refuses an uncovered kernel but requires `curl https://spaas.drbd.io/api/v1/hello` to answer, else `lw_fail "… and LINBIT's SPAAS is unreachable …; nothing was changed"`; the build uses `SPAAS=true` (bundled compat entries still extracted; uncovered kernel → empty compat list; a different `compat.h` gets SPAAS' patch instead of failing). Without `spaas` everything is as in light 5 (offline, refuse before changes). Post-`depmod` `modinfo -k` release-version check before the reboot unchanged in both modes. `updates.vm-lab` (d) builds its host step without `spaas` → still the air-gapped path; no spec change needed.
- **Bundle carries the apt snapshot packages**: new `util-release/src/lib/apt-bundle.ts`: index schema `{ id, sources, files, pool[] {source, path, sha256, size} }`; `selectAptPackages` (roots = `bundleAptRoots(os, arch)`: installer + pinned host packages, cloud-host packages, kernel / headers metapackages as in `drbd-compat.sh`, DRBD build tools; plus all `Priority: required/important`; closure over Pre-Depends / Depends / Recommends, first satisfiable alternative, `Provides`; newest version via a dpkg-compatible `compareDebianVersions`, or the release pin); `buildAptBundleSnapshot` (takeSnapshot + selection per host); `collectAptBundleBlobs` (fetch by checksum: local cache dir first, else upstream; size + SHA-256 verified, mismatch fails the build; each blob once, grouped per OS); `writeAptPack` (tar, members named by SHA-256); `importAptBundlePacks` (CP: members must be index files with matching size, stored by checksum, pool rows registered; reports missing). New script `scripts/apt-snapshot.ts` (nx target `apt-snapshot`: `--host <os>/<arch>…`, writes `snapshot.json`, `blobs/`, `kernels/<os>-<arch>.txt`). `build-bundle --apt-snapshot <index> [--apt-files <blobs dir>]` now packs everything into `artifacts/apt/packages-<os>.tar`, manifest field **`aptPackages`** (optional, in `referencedArtifacts` → checksummed + signed). `serveAptFile`: a pool file already in the store by its checksum is served from there (pool row added) — never fetched upstream. `AptSnapshotService.importBundleSnapshot` validates the index with the schema and unpacks the packs. Release job: free-disk step, new step _Freeze the apt snapshot_ (debian 12/13, ubuntu 22.04/24.04 × amd64/arm64) → `${APT_SNAPSHOT}` into build-bundle; the DRBD compat step now passes the snapshot's kernels to `drbd-compat.sh` (patches match the shipped kernels). `LOADWEAVER_BUNDLE_MAX_BYTES` default 8 → 16 GiB.
  - **Decision (deviation from "list them as artifacts")**: the packages are listed in the signed index and packed into ≤ 4 per-OS pack artifacts listed in the manifest, not one manifest artifact per `.deb` — the manifest goes to every node with each release target (agent protocol cap 1 MiB) and N-1 control planes accept ≤ 512 artifacts; coverage by the signature is the same chain (manifest → pack/index SHA-256 → member SHA-256). Packs stay in the artifact store next to the unpacked blobs (≈ 2× the apt part in Garage; documented).
  - Bundle size (documented, estimate, not measured): ~0.4–1 GB packages per OS release × arch, several GB in total; uploaded in 1.9 GB parts.
- Unit: util-release 4 suites / **37** (+10: dpkg version order, stanzas, selection closure / pins / provides / missing, roots, snapshot with fake upstream, builder fetch-by-checksum with cache + dedupe + manifest `aptPackages`, tampered upstream fails, CP import + serving from bundle with upstream unreachable incl. store-hit without pool row + re-import, foreign pack member refused); feature-node-agent 42 / **303** (+3: online pre-check reachable / unreachable / covered kernel without curl, SPAAS build script, OsUpdateManager passes `host.spaas`); feature-control-plane updates 3 / **37** (+1 `drbdSpaasAllowed`); util-agent-protocol 5 (+1 skipped) / 49 (compat + field-gate tests green). tsc (util-release lib + spec + scripts, protocol lib + spec, CP lib + spec, agent lib + spec) clean; eslint + prettier clean on touched files; esbuild + arg-validation smoke of both scripts.
- Files: protocol `lib/{components,versioning}.ts`; agent `lib/updates/{host-commands,os-update.manager,updates.spec}.ts`; CP `lib/updates/{rollout.service,rollout.entity,rollout-planner.utils,rollout-planning.spec,releases.service,apt-snapshot.service,bundle.service}.ts`, `spec/openapi.yaml`; util-release `src/lib/{apt-bundle,apt-bundle.spec,apt-snapshot.core,manifest,source-manifest}.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `scripts/{build-bundle,apt-snapshot}.ts`, `project.json`; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; docs `features/updates.md` (new "Air-gapped OS updates", online SPAAS paragraph, 16 GiB), `deployment/host-requirements.md`.
- Gate must re-run: `updates.vm-lab` (all; (d) unchanged in intent — air-gapped, no `spaas`), CP integration `updates.integration` (bundle import path / apt snapshot import, rollout options), protocol compat freeze if the release freezes N-1; a real `apt-snapshot` + `build-bundle --apt-snapshot` run against the live archives (network, size, unresolved deps per OS) — not run here; optionally an online-cluster lab case (uncovered kernel built via SPAAS) — none exists.
- Review of "Gate fixes (light 6)": accepted (air-gap derived from existing state: `updates.source` ≠ `upload` and an upstream plan-time snapshot ⇒ online ⇒ SPAAS allowed, protocol feature `drbd-spaas` with field gate; bundle carries per-OS apt packs, packages bound by sha256 in the signed index — packs, not each `.deb`, are manifest artifacts because of the 1 MiB manifest cap / N-1's 512-artifact limit; the signature chain still covers every file). To verify in gate part B: a real `apt-snapshot` + `build-bundle --apt-snapshot` run for the lab OS (debian 12 amd64 — size, unresolved deps, network), `updates.integration`, all `updates.vm-lab` cases. Not lab-covered (accepted): an online cluster building an uncovered kernel via SPAAS.

  2. **Topology map stale for up to 10 s** → draining replicas (~10 s drain) were usually never shown as `draining`: the structure cache is now also keyed by a cheap fingerprint (compiled revision + placement count / last `updated_at`), refreshed at once on any change (`topology/topology.service.ts`; new `topology.service.spec.ts` 3). Docs: `topology-map.md`.
  3. **Debian 12 `wireguard-tools` pin wrong** (`1.0.20210914-1`; bookworm ships `1.0.20210914-1+b1`) → the release's `wireguard` package component would fail to install on Debian 12 hosts (`util-release/src/lib/pins.ts`).
  4. **Thin pool refused after a power cut** (the open "Check of pool … failed (status:64)" from the volume follow-ups; recurred in this gate's first `drbd.vm-lab` run, 4 cases failed): the lab's `thin_check` diagnostics showed `1 data blocks have leaked` / "data space map contains leaks" — a non-fatal error LVM's default `thin_check_options` refuses. The agent now activates and creates thin LVs with `--config 'global { thin_check_options = [ "-q", "--clear-needs-check-flag", "--ignore-non-fatal-errors" ] }'` (`VolumeManager.THIN_CHECK_CONFIG`; damaged mappings / metadata still fail). Unit: volumes spec (+1, command expectations updated). Docs: `volumes.md`. Crash / rejoin cases passed in all 4 runs after the fix (the leak didn't recur in them, so the fix is unit-proven, lab-compatible).

New `platform-backups` case: multi-object deletes through the gateway without a grant (AWS SDK body with XML-escaped keys) and with a key outside the prefix → `AccessDenied`, object still there. `network-lab` expectation updated for the kept-address `lwk*` interfaces in the egress NAT set. `registry-lab` waited only for the private registry: the pull-through mirror could still be starting → 503 (flaky) → waits for the mirror too. Explicit `--memory` added to the containers `live-lab`, `logs-lab`, `registry-lab`, `image-scan-lab` created without one. **DR drill**: the "wait for n2 member" workaround removed — the store deployment is planned right after n2 joined: plan warning, copy held back (`n2CopyHeldBackWhileJoining: true`), no rollback; once n2 runs the control plane the unchanged plan lists `{ action: 'copy', volume: 'shop/store/data', to: 'n2' }` and adds it. **forget-peer**: real DRBD 9.2.20 answers a forget-peer of an already-forgotten slot with **exit 0** (idempotent), not "Invalid peer-node-id" — the agent's retry is correct either way; `drbd.vm-lab` now asserts exit 0 / empty stderr, `VolumeManager.forgetPeer` comment corrected.

### 2026-10-20 — Secrets API project-role decision implemented

- `PUT` / `DELETE` project secrets now reuse `ProjectAccessService.caller`, `projectRole` and `atLeast(..., 'operator')`: project admins / operators and cluster admins allowed; developers / viewers / non-members denied with 403 before project lookup. Infra operators need an allowed project membership. `lw-` names remain cluster-admin only, checked in both controller and service; the internal volume-key path is limited to request-free system callers. PATs retain `secrets:write`, bounded by the owner's current effective roles. Reads unchanged; writes / deletes audit actor, project and name, never values.
- Tests: `secrets.controller.spec.ts` + `secrets.service.spec.ts` **46/46** (roles, scoped PATs / owner role, reserved names / direct-service bypass, audit without values, envelope storage); whole feature-control-plane unit suite once **698/698** (90 suites), using the repository's `jest.config.cts`, `--maxWorkers=2`. Docker integration specs run separately under `/tmp/lw-3a-lock.sh`, in-band with 14 GB available: `agenstra-runtime.integration.spec.ts` **1/1** (operator-only create / env change / delete, ordinary secret PUT / DELETE, `lw-` 403); `control-plane.integration.spec.ts` **44/44** (operator allowed, viewer / `lw-` denied, cluster-admin reserved writes). Prettier on touched files; ESLint on touched TypeScript: 0 errors, one existing integration-helper `any` warning. No containers left running; no commits.
- `ensureVolumeKey` verified read-only: `node:crypto.randomBytes(64)` (512 bits), never predictable derivation; stores the key as `lw-volume-…` in `lw_secrets`, encrypted under a fresh random 32-byte AES-256-GCM data key, itself AES-256-GCM wrapped by the cluster master key with secret / version-bound AAD. The master key is held in memory after threshold unseal from node-sealed Shamir shares, or external KMS / Vault; the generated volume-key buffer is zeroed after storage. No entropy fix needed. Runtime guide production caveat removed; secrets / access docs and OpenAPI updated. M6 remains done; P not started.
- Local container stack + users-mode email (2026-10-20, user-reported): `.start-containers.env.example` lists every setting the control plane reads; `docker-compose.yaml` passes them through and adds digest-pinned Valkey (queue) and MailHog (SMTP 1027 / UI 8027). Fixed: users-mode login with forced email 2FA returned 503 because Loadweaver never provided `IDENTITY_EMAIL_DISPATCHER` → new global `LoadweaverIdentityEmailBridgeModule` (shared email dispatcher, instance scope; also delivers signup confirmations / password resets), imported in `AppModule`, unit spec 2/2; then delivery failed with "Email template not found" because the build copied no email templates → `project.json` build assets copy the shared notification templates + Loadweaver's alert templates to `templates/`. Verified end to end on an isolated stack: register → login 401 `LOGIN_2FA_REQUIRED` → code mail in MailHog → login with code → access token.

### 2026-10-20 — P2: usage metering (3.24)

- **Decisions within the plan**:
  - **Meters** (hourly buckets per project): `cpu_core_hours` (Σ `replica.cpu_cores` samples × 10 s), `memory_gib_hours` (Σ `replica.memory_bytes` × 10 s), `storage_gib_hours` (provisioned volume size, **each volume once**, like the storage quota) **and** `storage_replica_gib_hours` (size × copies = primary + sync + remote replicas as placed) — hosters attach the one they bill; `traffic_in_gb` / `traffic_out_gb` (10⁹ B); `public_ip_hours` (assigned egress addresses of project policies, `egress/<project>/<policy>/<i>`, the same that `quota.publicIps` counts; ingress / DNS / VPN addresses are cluster-level, not metered).
  - **Traffic source**: the existing flow counters are per policy edge with hashed set names (no project attribution), so the node agent now also reports `replica.net_rx_bytes_per_s` / `replica.net_tx_bytes_per_s` from the containers' Docker network counters (delta per interval, counter reset → skipped). Includes east-west traffic (documented). Object storage not metered yet (documented).
  - **Storage of the billing record**: `lw_usage_1h` (project, meter, hour, value, `final`, `billing_subscription`) filled by the control plane every 5 min from `lw_metrics_1m` (continuous aggregate under the community license, else control-plane roll-up) and from its own allocation samples (`lw_usage_samples`, every 5 min, first replica per slot wins, 7 days). Not another continuous aggregate because billing rows must be **immutable once final** (15 min after the hour; recompute window 3 h; vanished inputs still finalized) and outlive the metric retention: **25 months**. Gaps (agent offline > 5 min, control plane down) are unmetered — in the customer's favour.
  - **Mapping project ↔ Decabill**: explicit in the Project spec, `spec.billing.decabillSubscriptionId` (cluster admins via plan / apply, GitOps-able, audited); snapshotted into each bucket while it is open, so remapping / deleting never moves billed hours. Several projects per subscription add up.
  - **API**: `GET /projects/:p/usage` (+ `/export` CSV) for project readers (`canReadProject`), `GET /usage` (+ `/export`) for any cluster role; `from` (floored, default month start) / `to` / `granularity` hour|day|month (93 / 400 / 800 days max) / `meter` / `finalOnly`, cluster-wide also `project`, `billingSubscription`; ≤ 50 000 rows + `truncated`; hourly rows carry `idempotencyKey` `loadweaver:<cluster>:<project>:<meter>:<hour>`. New PAT scope **`usage:read`** (bounded by roles). UTC buckets; day / month final when ended and all hours final.
  - **Decabill side — pull, the mechanism Decabill already has**: built-in addon module **`loadweaver-usage`** (contributor Nest module, `collectMeters`, 7 declared `loadweaver.*` meters, `sum`, price 0, interval 1 h), one catalog addon per cluster. Connection only from the catalog addon's **encrypted admin defaults** (`LOADWEAVER_API_URL` HTTPS, `LOADWEAVER_API_TOKEN` = auditor PAT with `usage:read`), never from the subscription snapshot (customers can set any declared addon config key at order time → would redirect the collector / leak the token). Window math: hours assigned by their end to `(start − 20 min, end − 20 min]` (gap-free across consecutive windows), plus 3 h lookback; one sample per final hour / project / meter with the idempotency key; an empty window records one zero sample (else due every minute); truncated / malformed answers fail (retry). Generic Decabill extension: `MeterCollectSample.idempotencyKey` → skipped when already recorded for (subscription, meter), stored in `usagePayload.idempotencyKey`, partial unique index catches races (23505 = already recorded).
  - Reports (3.25): monthly `metered` totals per meter in cluster / project reports (HTML table). Console: `/usage` (Observe group) — summary bar of totals, filter panel (project, resolution, from / to; "All projects" for cluster roles), flush table per period × project with open periods marked, client pager, CSV export; NgRx `consoleUsage`.
- **Files**: control plane `usage/{usage.constants,usage.utils,usage.service}.ts` (+ specs), `controllers/usage.controller.ts`, module / index / PAT scopes, `reports/{reports.service,report.utils}.ts`, `spec/openapi.yaml` (4 paths, `UsageReport`, `UsageMeterKey`, 5 parameters); util-model `projectSpecSchema.billing`; node agent `metrics/{metrics-parsing,metrics-collector.service}.ts` (+ spec); Decabill `contributors/loadweaver-usage/*` (+ 2 specs), `utils/contributor-nest-registration.ts`, `dto/meter-collect.types.ts`, `repositories/usage-records.repository.ts` (`existsByIdempotencyKey`), `services/meter-collect.job-handler.ts` (+ spec); console data-access `types/usage.types.ts`, `services/usage.service.ts`, `state/usage/*` (+ spec); feature-console `usage/{usage-page.component.*,usage-format.ts}` (+ specs), routes, nav, index; console xlf (33 new ids, German targets).

### 2026-10-20 — P6: desktop release pipeline (3.32)

- **Scope**: shared pipeline built and Agenstra Desktop moved onto it; Loadweaver Desktop skipped this run (user decision) — it plugs in with a `DESKTOP_APPS` entry + workflow matrix entries; mobile signing out.
- **Tool `tools/desktop-release`** (Nx `desktop-release`; `bundle` → `tmp/desktop-release/desktop-release.cjs`, `test`, `typecheck`): app registry `src/apps.ts` (product, Nx project, dist dir, Forge names, package name, download base, channels, entitlements, rpm deps, secret **names**; one shared ForePath identity). Commands: `sign-macos` (temp keychain, `@electron/osx-sign` hardened runtime + `entitlements.mac.plist`, `@electron/notarize` with App Store Connect API key, staple, `codesign --verify` / `spctl` / `stapler validate`, keychain + key files removed in `finally`), `zip-macos` (`ditto --keepParent`; no Developer ID → ad-hoc sign + warning), `sign-windows` (`signtool` from the newest Windows SDK, SHA-256 + RFC 3161 timestamp, `verify /pa`, PFX in a 0600 temp file, password flagged secret), `linux-rpm` (rpmbuild from Forge's packaged app, deb layout `/usr/lib/agenstra`, no strip, setuid `chrome-sandbox`, `~` prerelease versions — no new npm dep instead of maker-rpm, which isn't installed at root), `linux-repo` (throw-away GnuPG home, `rpmsign --addsign`, apt `pool/` + `dists/<channel>` via `apt-ftparchive`, `InRelease` + `Release.gpg`, rpm `createrepo_c` + `repomd.xml.asc`, `.sources` / `.repo` files, exported `forepath-desktop.asc`), `channels` (stable → stable + beta, prerelease → beta, never backwards; reads the live feeds, fails on anything but 200 / 404), `feed` (verifies the signed release manifest with the compiled-in keys exactly as the apps do, writes `<channel>.json`). Every signing command skips with a warning while its secret is missing. `@electron/osx-sign` 1.3.3 / `@electron/notarize` 2.5.0 are the versions already in the lockfile (transitive of Forge), declared in the tool's `package.json`, kept external in the bundle.
- **Shared logic** in `shared-shared-util-release-signing` (`desktop-update.ts`, product-agnostic): feed schema (https only, no credentials, optional trusted origin), `compareReleaseVersions` (semver precedence), `evaluateDesktopUpdate` (manifest signature / canonical / product, version = feed version, channel — stable takes stable only, a manifest claiming stable for a prerelease is refused — strictly newer, platform file exactly one), `verifyDesktopUpdateDownload`, `createDesktopUpdateFeed`, `desktopUpdateChannelsFor`.
- **Agenstra Desktop** (`apps/agenstra/native-agent-console`): `src/update/update-config.ts` (feed URLs, per-platform file patterns, channel default from the installed version, Authenticode publisher rule, NSIS-install detection, apt / dnf instructions) and `src/update/updater.ts` (Electron `net.fetch`, size-capped feed / manifest / signature, streamed download with SHA-256 + size cap, macOS: verified zip served to **Squirrel.Mac** through a one-shot `127.0.0.1` feed — Squirrel additionally enforces the Developer ID signature; Windows: Authenticode check via PowerShell `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` (signed install → same subject required), NSIS `/S --updated --force-run`, quit; Linux: package-manager hint; zip installs: download link). Checks 60 s after start + every 6 h, prompt once per version per session; "Check for updates" and the **Stable / Beta** channel in the settings dialog (⚙) and the Settings menu, stored as `updateChannel` in `config.json`. Build: `tsc` is now typecheck-only (`noEmit`), `main.js` / `preload.js` bundled by esbuild (the release-signing libs + zod need bundling; `electron` external). New `production-macos` package configuration (Forge `package` per arch, version set via node, signing / zip by the tool). New `test` target.

### 2026-10-20 — P3 fixes: admin claim, grace queue

- **One-time admin claim (first-admin takeover race)**: Decabill generates `lwc_` + 32 random bytes (base64url) per provisioning through a new optional stack hook `IntegratedStackModule.prepareProvisioningConfig` (`CloudInitDispatchService.prepareProvisioningConfig`, called in `SubscriptionService.provisionSubscriptionItem` and `BackorderService` right before `buildUserData`; entries merged into the effective config and persisted in the item's AES-256-GCM `configSnapshot` as `loadweaverAdminClaimToken` — never part of item responses). Decision: stored encrypted (not hashed) on the Decabill side so the Cluster tab can show it again until claimed; the node keeps only the SHA-256. `buildLoadweaverCloudInitConfigFromRequest` fails closed without a valid token. User-data: `(umask 077 && printf … > /var/lib/loadweaver-cloud/admin-claim-token)` → `loadweaver-agent bootstrap … --admin-claim-token-file <file>` → file removed (also on bootstrap failure); never on a command line / in the log. Node agent: `--admin-claim-token-file` (or `LOADWEAVER_ADMIN_CLAIM_TOKEN`), plain-bootstrap flag (not restore-only), `adminClaimTokenSha256` (32–256 URL-safe chars) → control-plane env `ADMIN_CLAIM_TOKEN_SHA256` only.
- **Shared identity (opt-in, defaults identical)**: `admin-claim.utils.ts` (`resolveAdminClaimConfig` — unset = off, malformed = fail closed; `adminClaimTokenMatches` SHA-256 + `timingSafeEqual`; `AdminClaimAttemptLimiter` 10 failures / 15 min per client IP, in memory). `AuthService.register(email, password, adminClaimToken?, clientKey?)`: after `DISABLE_SIGNUP`, only for the would-be first account (count 0) and only when configured → 403 / 429; afterwards never consulted (normal signup rules). `isAdminClaimRequired()`. `RegisterDto.adminClaimToken?` (optional, max 256); controller passes `req.ip`. No route throttle change (Agenstra / Decabill unaffected unless they set the env).
- **Loadweaver control plane**: public `GET /api/install/claim-status` → `{ claimRequired }` (looks up the identity `AuthService` via `ModuleRef` non-strict, so `api-key` / `keycloak` mode answer `false`; no module edits). Console: `IdentityAuthEnvironment.adminClaimStatusUrl` (new optional field; Loadweaver console sets `<restApi>/install/claim-status`); shared register form asks it and shows a required claim-token field only while `claimRequired` (status errors → hidden); `register` action / facade / effect / service carry `adminClaimToken` only when set. 4 new `featureRegister-adminClaimToken*` units (en / de) in the Loadweaver console catalogs (other apps' catalogs get them on their next extraction; the field never renders there without `adminClaimStatusUrl`).
- **Decabill Cluster tab**: `LoadweaverClusterService` also probes `/api/install/claim-status` (until claimed); DTO `adminClaim { status: pending | claimed | unknown, token }` — token only for the owning customer (never admin view) and only until claimed; on `claimRequired: false` the token is wiped from the snapshot and `loadweaverAdminClaimedAt` recorded (no further claim probes). Tab: warning alert "Claim your cluster" with token + instructions; admin view shows a pending hint. 5 new + 1 changed (`firstAccountHint`) billing-console units with German targets.
- **Expiration queue starvation**: new nullable `billing_subscriptions.teardown_not_before` (migration `1778400000000_AddSubscriptionTeardownNotBefore`), set by `cancelSubscription` for subscriptions with a Loadweaver item (`cancelEffectiveAt + LOADWEAVER_TEARDOWN_GRACE_DAYS`), cleared on resume / instant cancel. `findDueForCancellation` adds `COALESCE(teardownNotBefore, cancelEffectiveAt) <= :now` (ordering by `cancelEffectiveAt`, `take(batch)` unchanged). Why a column: the item service lives in the encrypted `configSnapshot`, so SQL can't see it. The job handler uses the stored time (computed fallback for older rows); the Cluster tab shows it too.

OpenAPI: Decabill (`RegisterDto.adminClaimToken`, register 403 / 429, `LoadweaverClusterInfo.adminClaim`), Agenstra (`RegisterDto.adminClaimToken`), Loadweaver (`/install/claim-status`).

### 2026-10-20 — P4: posture integrations (3.31, control-plane side)

- **Design**: `PosturePlugin` redesigned (M4 skeleton had `check(device)` per report): factories declare `category` (mdm / edr), config `fields` (secret flag), `defaultMatchBy`, `allowedHosts(config)` (validates + returns the only hosts it may call), plugins implement `testConnection` / `fetchDevices` / optional `enrich` (matched devices only). Registry: 6 built-ins, then `DYNAMIC_POSTURE_PLUGINS` (`registerDynamicProviders`, as KMS). **Integrations** = cluster settings in `lw_posture_integrations` (name used in conditions, type, config JSON AES-256-GCM via `createAes256GcmTransformer`, `match_by`, interval / max age, sync state); secrets write-only (API returns non-secret declared fields + `secretsSet`), audit carries field names only. Polling: coordinator `posture-sync.coordinator` (`LOADWEAVER_POSTURE_SYNC_CRON`, `*/2 * * * *`) → unit `posture-sync.unit` per due integration, job id `posture-sync.<id>.<slot>` (schedule slot / `manual-<minute>` / `device-<minute>` when a device reports new identifiers); DB claim (`sync_started_at`, 15 min expiry) makes duplicates no-ops; failures back off (interval × 2^n, ≤ 6 h), sanitized `last_error`. `PostureHttp`: HTTPS + allowed hosts only, `redirect: 'error'`, 20 s timeout, ≤ 4 attempts on 429 / 5xx with `Retry-After` (≤ 60 s), ≤ 2,000 requests / run, ≤ 25 MB / response, 10 min / run; errors carry method + host + path only. Results normalized per device in `lw_vpn_clients.integration_posture` (status compliant / non-compliant / unknown, risk low / medium / high, reasons, checkedAt, staleAt = checkedAt + maxAge, externalId, matchedBy). Matching by serial / deviceId / hostname in configured order; duplicate serials/ids → latest seen, duplicate hostnames → unknown (ambiguous). `deviceId` + new `serialNumber` pinned at the first report (was: after a plugin verdict) and unique among valid clients.
- **Conditions** (`ClientGroup.spec.posture.conditions`, parsed/validated in util-model `parsePostureCondition`, ≤ 32): `mdm.compliant`, `mdm.<integration>.compliant`, `edr.compliant`, `edr.risk <= low` (ops `== != < <= > >=`, low < medium < high, worst current risk), `edr.<integration>.risk < high`, `device.certificate.valid`, `device.certificate.expiresInDays >= N`, `device.diskEncryption|firewall|screenLock [== true|false]`, `device.osVersion|appVersion >= x`, `device.platform ==|!= <p>`. Category aggregation: ≥ 1 current compliant and none non-compliant; stale / missing → fail (fail closed). Older `plugins: [{type, require}]` rules now read the integration with that name (else type); `credentials` ignored. Evaluated on each report, after each sync, on integration delete, and by the existing 1-minute tick (staleness / expiry → fingerprint change → recompile).
- **Restricted-group flow**: unchanged enforcement path — `effectiveGroups` (now fed by report + integration + certificate facts) replaces failing groups by `restrictedGroup` in `remoteAccessInput` → `NetworkStateService.recompile()` → gateways / client routes. Every effective-group change audited `vpn.posture` (failing reasons, source report / integration); integration CRUD `posture.integration.*`, repeated failures `posture.integration.failing`. Built-in alerts `builtin:device-restricted` (info, per device with reasons) and `builtin:posture-integration-failing` (warning, ≥ 3 failures).
- **Device certificates**: util-pki `verifyDeviceCertificate` (bundle as trust anchors incl. intermediates, CA flag, validity, issuer CRL with signature check, outdated CRL fails), `verifyPossession` (ECDSA P-256/P-384 raw or DER, RSA PKCS#1 SHA-256), `caBundleIssues`. Cluster CA issues `client/<device id>` at `POST /vpn/devices/:id/certificate` (owner, interactive, CSR, valid until key expiry; latest serial stored → older superseded; device revocation revokes). Reports may carry `certificate {pem, proof {timestamp, signature over loadweaver-posture-v1:<id>:<ts>}}` (±5 min); verified at report time into `posture.certificate`. Trust settings `lw_posture_certificate_trust` (`companyCaPem`, `crlPem`, `trustClusterCa`, `requireProof`, defaults on).

### 2026-10-20 — P5: Terraform provider (3.24)

- **Projects** (generator `@forepath/code:lib … js` for both libs, config aligned to util-import: `es2022`, strict, `tslib` exact; app replicated from `loadweaver-cli`): `loadweaver-backend-util-terraform-protocol` (protocol), `loadweaver-backend-feature-terraform-provider` (provider), app `loadweaver-terraform-provider` (`apps/loadweaver/terraform-provider`: `main.ts`, webpack with `.proto` as `asset/source`, targets `build[:sea]`, `test`, `test-e2e`, `sea`, `package`). Tags `domain:loadweaver`.
- **Protocol (no Go)**: go-plugin handshake — `TF_PLUGIN_MAGIC_COOKIE` check (else the standard "This binary is a plugin" message, exit 1), `PLUGIN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` → 6 (protocol-5-only hosts refused), AutoMTLS: `PLUGIN_CLIENT_CERT` as the only accepted client cert (grpc-js `createSsl(…, checkClientCertificate)`), self-signed ECDSA P-256 server cert (`CN=localhost, O=HashiCorp`, SAN `localhost`, CA, server + client auth; `@peculiar/x509`, as util-pki), protocol line `1|6|unix|<socket>|grpc|<raw DER base64, no padding>` on stdout; unix socket in a fresh `mkdtemp` dir (`PLUGIN_UNIX_SOCKET_DIR`), loopback TCP in `PLUGIN_MIN_PORT..MAX_PORT` on Windows. gRPC services: `tfplugin6.Provider`, `plugin.GRPCStdio` (stream kept open; logs go to stderr as hclog JSON), `plugin.GRPCController/Shutdown`, `plugin.GRPCBroker` (accepted, drained), `grpc.health.v1.Health` (go-plugin's ping). SIGINT ignored (Terraform stops via `StopProvider`, which aborts waits). Official protos vendored unchanged with license headers + source note: `tfplugin6.proto` (Terraform v1.16.4, protocol 6.11), `grpc_stdio` / `grpc_controller` / `grpc_broker` (go-plugin v1.7.0), `health.proto` (grpc-proto @2eb777a). Parsed at start-up with protobufjs → hand-built grpc-js `ServiceDefinition`s (keepCase, int64 as numbers); no codegen, no proto-loader.
- **msgpack**: own subset (≈ 300 lines, nil / bool / int8-64 / float64 / str / bin / array / map / ext; every ext = unknown, written as cty's `d4 00 00`; 64-bit beyond safe range as bigint; depth limit; null-prototype maps). Reason: the only msgpack in the tree is a transitive `msgpackr` (native optional addon, unknown-ext handling needed anyway). cty layer: JSON type notation, `fromWire` / `toWire` per type (objects carry every attribute, numbers from strings / bigints), JSON `DynamicValue`s for state upgrades.
- **Deps**: none added to the root. Used: `@grpc/grpc-js` 1.14.6, `@peculiar/x509` 2.1.0, `reflect-metadata` 0.1.14 (root deps), `protobufjs` 7.5.5 (already installed via `@grpc/proto-loader` / dockerode override; imported directly, declared in the lib package.json — add it to the root dependencies exact if wanted), `archiver` 8.0.0 (packaging script, `ZipArchive`).

Drift: `ReadResource` compares the configured spec with the stored one after applying the same defaults (util-model) → configured form kept, real drift put into state. ### 2026-10-20 — P7a: fleet service (3.24 multi-cluster backend)

- **Design** (Agenstra controller ↔ agent-manager pattern): new app `loadweaver-backend-fleet` (`apps/loadweaver/backend-fleet`, port **3500**, image `ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-fleet-api`, generated with `@forepath/code:backend`, e2e project removed like siblings) + lib `loadweaver-backend-feature-fleet` (`@forepath/code:lib`, `domain:loadweaver`, `target: es2022`); both **BUSL-1.1** (Agenstra controller LICENSE text, URL loadweaver.com). Auth `api-key` / `users` / `keycloak` via shared identity, PAT catalog `fleet:read`, `fleet:relay`, `fleet:restore`, `fleet:admin`, `cloud:register`, `cloud:teardown` + identity scopes. Own Postgres + Valkey; queue `loadweaver-fleet` (coordinators every minute → health poll units with id per cluster + minute, operation step units with id per operation + step + attempt).
- **Cluster connections** (`lw_fleet_clusters`): name, endpoint (HTTPS, normalised, trailing `/api` dropped), optional PEM CA bundle, service credential (PAT of a dedicated cluster service user) encrypted with the shared `createAes256GcmTransformer` (`ENCRYPTION_KEY`), only a 4-char hint returned; `reference` (`decabill:<sub>:<item>`), `state` active / teardown / retired, `readOnlyUntil`, last health. Connection test before saving (`GET /api/cluster`: healthy / degraded / unreachable / credential-rejected, version from `X-Loadweaver-Version`). SSRF guardrails `FLEET_CLUSTER_ENDPOINT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (required in production), `…_ALLOW_INTERNAL_HOST`, `…_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` (never in production), DNS answers re-checked (cached 60 s), TLS verification only disableable outside production, no redirects.
- **Access model**: fleet admins (global admins, static API key) = admin everywhere; others need grants (`lw_fleet_grants`: viewer / operator / admin, cluster-wide or one project). Relay = method / path **allow-list** (`relay-rules.ts`, ~90 rules): viewer reads, operator plan / node / alert / backup / file-browser actions, admin cluster administration; project grants only on `projects/<p>/…` and `?project=`-filtered lists (repeated `project` refused); never relayed: secrets, the service user's personal resources (VPN devices, Git accounts, favourites, registry token), joining / installer; encoded / `..` / empty segments refused before forwarding. Sockets (`socket/fleet`, attach / emit / event / detach) for `plans` / `topology` / `logs` (viewer) and `terminals` (operator), cluster-wide grants only, one isolated remote socket per attachment (≤ 8). Read-only grace caps every role at viewer; retired clusters closed.
- **Relay**: `/api/clusters/:id/api/*` → `<endpoint>/api/*` with the service credential + `X-Loadweaver-On-Behalf-Of: fleet:<email>`, allow-listed request / response headers, streamed both ways (no body parser on relay paths), limits `FLEET_RELAY_TIMEOUT_MS` / `…_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (11 MiB) / `…_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (1 GiB); changes audited (`lw_fleet_audit_events`).
- **Fleet APIs**: `GET /fleet/cards` (overview + updates/status + pending plans + Site resources per cluster, TTL cache `FLEET_CACHE_TTL_MS`; limited card for project-only grants), `/fleet/inbox` (merged, critical / oldest first, unreachable clusters as items, links prefixed `/clusters/<id>`), `/fleet/sites` (`Site.spec.location`), `/fleet/compare?clusters=` (versions, capacity, policy drift over Policy / ImagePolicy / BackupPolicy / MaintenanceWindow / AlertRule by canonical spec hash).
- **Cross-cluster restore / clone** (`lw_fleet_operations`, `POST /operations`): access checked at creation (operator of every backup's project on A, of the target project on B, of the cloned project); steps validate → (clone: deployment copied from A, plan / apply on B) → transfer (A `GET /backups/:id/archive` streamed into B `POST /backups/imports`, nothing stored at the fleet) → `Restore` plan on B → apply (only with `apply`, B's approvals hold) → wait for `done`; idempotent per step (stored plan / import ids), waiting steps polled by the coordinator (6 h cap), cancel at the fleet. Decision within the plan: the archive is decrypted by A and re-encrypted under **B's own backup key** on import (B needs no copy of A's key); a source that is down goes through cluster DR with the recovery kit instead (documented).
- **Cluster-side changes** (control plane, with tests): `actorFromRequest` / `AuditLogService.record` add `details.onBehalfOf` from `X-Loadweaver-On-Behalf-Of` only for PATs carrying the new opt-in scope **`fleet:on-behalf-of`** (sanitised, ≤ 255 chars; actor stays the service user); new scopes `backups:export`, `backups:import`; `BackupTransferService` / `BackupTransferController`: `GET /backups/:id/archive` (project backups, operators, `kopia snapshot restore --mode=tar` to a temp file, audited `backup.exported`), `POST /backups/imports?volume=` (raw `application/x-tar`, size-capped stream, `tar` extraction of files / dirs / symlinks only, `kopia snapshot create` into the project repository as the control user, catalog row without policy, audited `backup.imported`), `POST /backups/now/all` (cluster admins, final backup of every placed volume); `KopiaCli.restoreArchive` / `snapshotDirectory` + `parseKopiaSnapshotCreate`; `LOADWEAVER_BACKUP_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` (50 GiB); `tar` 7.5.19 (existing root dep) added to the control-plane app package.json; OpenAPI (3 paths + header note).
- **Loadweaver Cloud hooks** (carried from P3): `POST /cloud/clusters` (fleet admin + `cloud:register`, with reference and initial grants), `PUT /cloud/clusters/:reference/teardown` (idempotent: state `teardown`, read-only until `readOnlyUntil`, one `final-backup` operation per teardown: platform postgres / opensearch / etcd runs (4xx = skipped), `backups/now/all`, wait, `backups/platform/copies/run`, best effort), `DELETE …/teardown` (resumed), `GET …` status; grace end → retired. **Decabill**: contributor job `fleet-teardown` on the `loadweaver` integrated stack (`LoadweaverFleetTeardownService`, own repositories, no shared-file edits beyond the contributor module): when `LOADWEAVER_FLEET_URL` (HTTPS) + `LOADWEAVER_FLEET_TOKEN` are set, every `LOADWEAVER_FLEET_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS` (15 min) it calls the teardown hook for each Loadweaver item of subscriptions in grace (pending cancel with effective date passed, pending withdrawal / instant cancel; `readOnlyUntil = teardownNotBefore`), 404 = not registered → skipped; unset = previous behaviour. ### 2026-10-21 — Follow-up fixes: Terraform provider (follow-up review lows, L8)

- **Plain HTTP refused**: new provider attribute `insecure_http` (bool, default `false`). An `http://` endpoint is an error ("Insecure endpoint"): `ValidateProviderConfig` reports it for the `endpoint` attribute (unless the flag is `true` or still unknown), `ConfigureProvider` also for a `LOADWEAVER_URL` fallback. With `insecure_http = true` it is accepted and a warning diagnostic (attribute `insecure_http`) is emitted on every configure. The e2e config sets `insecure_http = true` (fake control plane on loopback HTTP).
- **Response size cap**: `nodeHttpTransport({ maxResponseBytes })`, default `DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` = 32 MiB. A larger declared `content-length` aborts immediately, a streamed body aborts once it passes the limit. The error reads "response from <origin> exceeds the provider's limit of N bytes; aborted …" and surfaces as the resource's error diagnostic.
- **Node.js SHASUMS signature**: new `apps/loadweaver/terraform-provider/scripts/node-dist-verify.cjs` (CommonJS, injected fs / hash / extract, with `.d.cts` types). It pins the 29 Node.js release key fingerprints (`keys.list` of nodejs/release-keys @ `481637f8…`; includes historical signers so older versions verify) and fetches the public keys from that commit, so no keys are vendored and only the fingerprints are trusted. `package-provider.mjs` downloads `SHASUMS256.txt` + `.sig` fresh once per run per Node version and runs `gpg --verify --status-fd` in a throw-away 0700 GNUPGHOME. It requires exactly one `VALIDSIG` whose primary fingerprint is pinned, and no BADSIG / ERRSIG / REVKEYSIG. Hashes are used only from the verified text. Without `gpg` the script fails closed unless `--allow-unsigned-node-sums` is passed (warns; CI doesn't pass it). Cached archives are re-hashed on every use. Extracted binaries are cached under `extracted-<signed archive sha256>/` with a `.sha256` record and re-hashed on every use; a mismatch or bad record means re-extraction. The cache dir must be owned by the user and not group / world writable (created 0700). Checked by hand against v24.14.1: signed by 890C08DB… (pinned). The script itself was not run.
- **Windows loopback TCP**: `insecureTcpRefusal(env, clientCert, platform)` in handshake.ts. `servePlugin` refuses to start on win32 without `PLUGIN_CLIENT_CERT` (stderr message, returns `null`, no protocol line) unless `LOADWEAVER_TF_PLUGIN_INSECURE_TCP=1`.
- **Tests** (`--maxWorkers=2`): protocol 4 suites / 47, provider 3 / 48 (http refusal incl. env fallback + warning, size cap with declared and chunked bodies), app 2 / 10 (new `node-dist-verify.spec.ts`: pinned keys, SHASUMS parsing, gpg status check, fail-closed mode, cache-dir ownership, archive re-hash, extract-once + re-hash + tamper/re-extract with a mock fs). The app jest config skips transforming `scripts/*.cjs`. tsc (lib / spec / app) clean, prettier applied. eslint: no new findings; `scripts/*.mjs|cjs` aren't parsed by the eslint config (pre-existing). Docs: `docs/loadweaver/guides/terraform.md` (`insecure_http`, size cap, Windows debug flag, packaging signature check).
- Review of "Follow-up fixes: Terraform provider": accepted (`insecure_http` opt-in with warning, 32 MiB response cap, Node SHASUMS GPG-verified against 29 pinned release-key fingerprints with re-hashing of cached archives / binaries and a private cache dir, Windows TCP refused without `PLUGIN_CLIENT_CERT`). P gate: `test-e2e` (uses `insecure_http` against the loopback fake).

### 2026-10-21 — Follow-up fixes: fleet (security review of P7a)

- **H1 query smuggling**: new `utils/relay-query.ts` — the relay parses the raw query with `node:querystring` and the cluster's `maxKeys` (1000, Express 5 `simple` parser), refuses > 100 pairs / > 8 KiB, empty pairs, non-plain parameter names (percent-encoding, `+`, brackets, separators, `__proto__`) and a repeated `project` (400), and the client re-serialises the forwarded query from the parsed parameters (`serializeRelayQuery`). `project: 'query'` rules carry an allow-list of parameters (`plans`: project / status / limit; `backups`: project / resource / includeDeleted / limit; `backups/restores`: project), others → 400. `splitRelayUrl` now returns `{ path, rawQuery }`.
- **M1 (decision: approvals stay native)**: removed every approval / acceptance route from the allow-list (`plans/:id/approve`, `projects/:p/acceptances`, backup-deletion / platform-cutover / rollout `approve`) and added a hard deny list `NEVER_RELAYED` (secrets, `join-tokens`, `nodes/join`, `install`, `…/approve`, `approvals`, `acceptances`) checked before the rules. Inbox items got `nativeUrl` (`<endpoint><link>`, the same page in the cluster's own console) so the console links pending approvals there. Service-user docs no longer list `plans:approve`.
- **M5 (decision)**: `live/files…` (read / write) and `backups/:id/download|archive` need the **admin** grant; join-token routes removed (never relayed, any role); `fleet.md` documents what viewer / operator (≈ infra operator incl. terminals) / admin (≈ cluster admin incl. replica files / backup contents) reach.
- **L1**: `PATCH /clusters/:id` with a changed endpoint or CA requires `credential` in the same request (400 otherwise; unchanged normalised endpoint needs none); the stored credential is never probed against a new target.
- **L2**: control plane `auth/fleet-on-behalf-of-scope.interceptor.ts` (global `APP_INTERCEPTOR` in `ControlPlaneModule`): `POST /auth/tokens` / `PATCH /auth/tokens/:id` with `fleet:on-behalf-of` → 403 unless the caller has a cluster-wide role (`cluster-admin`, `infra-operator`, `auditor`; interactive global admins count as cluster-admin) — "service user" = account with a cluster-wide role, since identity has no service-account type. Checked at mint time only (a later demotion doesn't revoke the token; the label never grants anything).
- **L3**: socket relay re-checks every `FLEET_SOCKET_RECHECK_MS` (60 s, min 5 s) and immediately on in-process `FleetAccessEvents` (grant put / removed, connection changed / removed / retired, teardown started / updated / cancelled): handshake token re-validated (socket disconnected if not), each attachment re-authorised via `visibleCluster` + `authorizeSocketNamespace` (grace cap included), revoked ones closed with `detached { reason: 'access-revoked' }`. Remote sockets use the SSRF-guarded agent.
- **L4**: `createGuardedLookup` in `fleet-endpoint-security.ts` validates the resolved addresses inside the agents' `lookup` (HTTP client and sockets, `createClusterAgent`); the cached pre-check in `FleetClusterClient.target()` is gone (registration keeps its early friendly check).
- **L9**: Decabill `LoadweaverFleetTeardownService.inGrace(now, afterId, take)` orders by id and pages by keyset (500 per page) until a short page; docs: cross-cluster export out of a cluster in grace isn't possible via the fleet (viewer cap; downloads / archives are admin, operations need operator) — the final backup + external copy is the data path.
- **L11**: relay requests send `Accept-Encoding: identity`; a cluster 401 / 403 (always the service credential) → fleet **502** `cluster rejected the fleet credential` / `cluster refused the fleet credential: <reason>` with `clusterStatus` (audited for changes).
- **Files**: fleet lib `utils/{relay-query.ts (new, + spec),relay-rules.ts,relay-headers.ts,fleet-endpoint-security.ts,fleet-aggregation.utils.ts}` (+ specs), `services/{fleet-relay,fleet-cluster-client,fleet-clusters,fleet-cloud,fleet-overview}.service.ts`, `services/fleet-access-events.service.ts` (new), `gateways/fleet-relay.gateway.ts` (+ new spec), `modules/fleet.module.ts`, `dto/fleet.dto.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `spec/{openapi,asyncapi}.yaml`; control plane `auth/fleet-on-behalf-of-scope.interceptor.ts` (+ spec), `auth/loadweaver-pat.scopes.ts` (comment), `modules/control-plane.module.ts` (provider), `src/index.ts`, `spec/openapi.yaml` (info note); Decabill `contributors/loadweaver/loadweaver-fleet-teardown.service.ts` (+ spec); docs `docs/loadweaver/features/fleet.md`, `features/audit-log.md`.
- **Tests** (`--maxWorkers=2`): fleet lib 12 suites / 80 (attack reproduction: 1000 filler pairs + `project` refused, parser parity + round trip, approvals / acceptances / join tokens refused for admins, files / downloads admin-only, query allow-list, 401 / 403 → 502, accept-encoding, guarded lookup incl. rebinding answers, L1 credential re-entry, socket re-check on timer / event / invalid token, agent lookup on sockets); fleet app 2 / 5; control plane interceptor + audit-log 2 / 12; Decabill loadweaver contributors 5 / 65 (incl. > 500 paging). `tsc --noEmit` clean (fleet lib + spec + app, control-plane lib + spec, billing-manager lib + spec); ESLint 0 problems; Prettier clean. No Docker, no builds.

### 2026-10-21 — Follow-up fixes: posture, claim, import, billing

- **H2 posture identity borrowing**: no built-in plugin matches by `hostname` by default any more (Intune / Jamf / Kandji `serial, deviceId`; SentinelOne / CrowdStrike `deviceId, serial`; Defender `deviceId`); `hostname` stays opt-in per integration and adds a warning (`HOSTNAME_MATCH_WARNING`; API `PostureIntegration.warnings`, console list + form alert, 3 new xlf units en / de added by hand). Pinning (`posture-facts.pinIdentifiers`): device id (lower-case), serial (upper-case, placeholders dropped) and hostname (lower-case first label) are normalized and pinned at the first report; uniqueness checked on normalized values (fixes the case-sensitive `remote-access.service` check vs `normalizeDeviceId`); matching uses pinned values only (`deviceIdentifiers` no longer falls back to the report). Decision: a hostname another valid client holds is not pinned (no error — generic hostnames must not block reports), a later different hostname keeps the pin; device id / serial keep 409 / 400. Race: migration **`1800000000048_PosturePinnedIdentifiers`** (normalizes existing pins, keeps the newest duplicate, partial unique indexes `UQ_lw_vpn_clients_pinned_{device_id,serial,hostname}` on `posture->>…` WHERE `revoked_at IS NULL`, adds `lw_posture_integrations.require_user_match` default true, drops `hostname` from existing `match_by` unless it was the only key); `savePosture` releases pins of expired (unrevoked) clients first and maps 23505 → 409 (device id / serial) or "not pinned" (hostname). **User match** (`requireUserMatch`, factory flag `supportsUserMatch`, default on where supported): Intune `userPrincipalName` / `emailAddress`, Jamf `USER_AND_LOCATION` e-mail / UPN-style username (new section in the inventory request), Kandji `user.email`; the matched record's users must include the client owner (`ownerLabel`, e-mail, case-insensitive) → else `unknown` "the device's user doesn't match the owner of this VPN client" (no fallback to later keys). Decisions: EDR plugins don't support it (records carry only a last logged-in account name; `true` is refused with 400); machine clients are never user-matched; owners without `@` fail a required match (fail closed). Docs recommend `device.certificate.valid` together with `mdm.compliant`.
- **L5 company-CA device certs**: `usageIssues` in util-pki — keyUsage must be present with `digitalSignature`; an EKU, when present, must include `clientAuth`; no EKU = accepted on keyUsage alone (documented). Docs: CRL update latency (no fetching / OCSP; re-upload before `nextUpdate`), keep `requireProof` on.
- **M2 admin claim on members / DR + L10 posture env**: `ADMIN_CLAIM_TOKEN_SHA256`, `DYNAMIC_POSTURE_PLUGINS`, `LOADWEAVER_POSTURE_SYNC_CRON` added to `REPLICATED_CONTROL_PLANE_ENV` and `DR_ENVELOPE_ENV_KEYS`. `GET /install/claim-status` → `{ claimRequired, claimConfigured }` via new `AuthService.adminClaimStatus()` (api-key / keycloak: both false). Decabill `LoadweaverClusterService` marks claimed / wipes the token only on `claimConfigured === true && claimRequired === false`; missing / false `claimConfigured` keeps the token shown, status `unknown` (`LoadweaverProbeResult.claimConfigured`, one-field targeted edit in `loadweaver.utils.ts`).
- **L6 signup after the claim**: with `ADMIN_CLAIM_TOKEN_SHA256` configured, `register` refuses every registration after the first account with `503 Signup is disabled` (as `DISABLE_SIGNUP`); unset = unchanged (Agenstra / Decabill). Cloud docs: the claimed admin creates / invites users.
- **M3 backup import**: only plain ustar is accepted (`plainTarIssue`: gzip / zstd magic refused, `ustar` at offset 257 required, checked on the first 512 bytes before extracting; `tar.x` with `zstd: false, brotli: false`); running total of declared entry sizes against `LOADWEAVER_BACKUP_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` (413, wins over the parse error of a truncated body); modes masked to `0o777` in the filter (setuid / setgid / sticky stripped); staging in `LOADWEAVER_BACKUP_STAGING_DIR` (default OS temp; docs recommend a dedicated filesystem with a quota ≥ 2 × the cap) for export and import.
- **M4 instant cancel in the grace period**: `executeInstantCancel` refuses `pending_cancel` past `cancelEffectiveAt` with `SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELLATION_EFFECTIVE` (like resume). Withdrawal checked: not reachable in that state (`WithdrawalPolicyService` refuses `pending_cancel`) — spec asserts it.
- **L7**: addon script interpolation excludes `ADDON_SCRIPT_EXCLUDED_SNAPSHOT_KEYS` (`loadweaverAdminClaimToken`) and the module's `adminOnly` keys from both the env and the allowed placeholders.

### 2026-10-21 — P7b: console fleet views

- **Shape decision**: a **fleet mode of the existing Loadweaver console** (same app, same image, same `feature-console` / `data-access-console` libs), switched by the runtime config `mode: 'fleet'` + `fleet: { apiUrl, websocketUrl }` (`isFleetConsole`, util-configuration). Why: one codebase (every cluster view is reused as is through the relay instead of being duplicated in a second app), and the cleanest auth — the shared identity screens simply point at the fleet (`IDENTITY_AUTH_ENVIRONMENT.apiUrl = fleet.apiUrl`), relay URLs start with that base so the existing auth interceptor attaches the fleet token, the console never holds a cluster credential, PATs / user management are the fleet's. No `mode` (or `cluster`) = single-cluster console unchanged (all existing specs green without changes except the container spec's added facade stub).
- **Relay integration** (data-access): `ConsoleEndpointService` (root) resolves the REST base — control plane in cluster mode, `<fleet>/clusters/<activeId>/api` in fleet mode (`resolveConsoleRestApi` / `fleetRelayApiUrl`); `ConsoleApi.apiUrl` delegates to it, so all ~40 services go through the relay of the **active cluster** (per tab, session storage, UUID-validated). Sockets: `ConsoleSocketService.open` returns a `FleetRelaySocket` in fleet mode — an adapter with the Socket.IO client surface the live features use (`on/off/emit/disconnect/connected/active`): `attach` on every (re)connect, `attached`→`connect`, `event`→re-emitted event, emits queued until attached, `detached`→`disconnect` (cluster-side reconnect re-signals `connect` on the next event), refused attach / `relayError`→`connect_error` without retry, `detached {reason:'access-revoked'}`→disconnect + notice, no retry. `AccessService.me()` in fleet mode maps the **fleet grant** of the active cluster (`GET <fleet>/clusters/<id>`) to console roles (admin→cluster-admin, operator→infra-operator, viewer→auditor, project grants keep their role, read-only grace caps at auditor/viewer), so sidebar / guards / actions follow the grant, not the relay's service user. `fleetRelayErrorInterceptor` (util-configuration, env-only so the main bundle doesn't pull the data-access barrel; registered in `app.config`, no-op outside fleet mode / relay URLs) rewrites the fleet's own refusals into localized messages with `fleetRelay` in the body: `404 … is not relayed` → not available through the fleet, `403 needs … role / cluster-wide grant` → no permission, `403 read-only grace` → grace, `502 cluster rejected/refused the fleet credential` → broken cluster connection (no logout); cluster errors untouched. Switching clusters: `openFleetCluster` sets the endpoint, dispatches `fleetClusterSwitched` (added to the console slices' reset meta-reducer, `CONSOLE_CLUSTER_RESET_ACTIONS`; the fleet slice uses `FLEET_FEATURE_CONFIG`, reset on logout only) **before** navigating; logout leaves the active cluster; the container reloads access on every switch.
- **Routing / shell**: `fleetConsoleGuard` (canActivateChild on the shell): fleet mode → fleet / account / auth routes always, cluster views only with an active cluster (else `/fleet`), never-relayed views (`/git`, `/devices`, `/settings/git-accounts`, `/webhooks`, `/updates/announcements`) → `/fleet/unavailable?page=`; cluster mode → `/fleet…` / `/clusters…` lead to `/overview`, everything else unchanged. `fleetClusterLinkMatcher` + `fleetClusterEntryGuard`: `/clusters/<id>/<path>` (card / inbox links) activates the cluster and continues at `<path>`. Sidebar: `FLEET_NAV_GROUP` (Fleet overview, Clusters, Compare, Operations, Fleet audit — global admins) first; cluster groups only with an active cluster, minus unrelayed items, `/files` requires the admin grant (`fleetConsoleNav`); admin popover only the fleet's Users. Top bar: cluster switcher (`fpc-form-control` select: "Fleet (all clusters)" + non-retired clusters).
- **Coordinator rules followed**: approvals stay native — plan approve (with an info alert on pending plans), cross-project acceptances, backup deletion approvals, platform cut-over approve and rollout approve hidden in fleet mode; merged-inbox approvals / cross-project requests open `nativeUrl` (the cluster's own console) instead of the relay, other items show an "Open in the cluster's console" link when `nativeUrl` is set; join tokens / installer hidden on `/nodes` in fleet mode (`mayJoin`); file browser admin-only in the sidebar (backup / file downloads on other pages fall back to the "no permission" message for non-admin grants); edit modal requires the credential when endpoint or CA change (client check + message, `clusterUpdate().credentialRequired`); `access-revoked` and credential-502 handled as above; relayed query strings unchanged except the wizard's `GET /backups?limit=&project=` (own params only).
- **State** (`consoleFleet` slice + `ConsoleFleetFacade`, `FleetService`): clusters (load / register / change / delete / connection test / poll), grants (load / put / delete, reload after change), overview (cards, inbox, sites — independent loads), comparison, operations (list / create / cancel), Cloud status per reference, fleet audit (cursor paging by last `seq`), open / leave cluster. Types in `fleet.types.ts` (from the fleet OpenAPI; `nativeUrl` on inbox items).
- **Pages** (`feature-console/src/lib/fleet/`, shared UI patterns of the rework plan): **Fleet overview** (`/fleet`: summary bar, `fpc-panel` card per cluster — connection + health, badges teardown / read-only until, retired, Cloud, project access, update running; version → upgrade, sites, nodes, alerts, pending plans, inbox counts, CPU / memory bars, errors, Open + "Connection & grants"; merged inbox list; world map; refresh every 60 s), **Clusters** (table with health / latency / version / endpoint / access; check now, open, admin: register / edit modal with write-only password credential, CA textarea + remove-CA switch, test-before-save switch, "Test connection", delete confirm), **Cluster detail** (`/fleet/clusters/:id`: connection panel, Loadweaver Cloud panel with teardown / grace and the final backup's steps + progress, grants table + grant modal — email search in the fleet's identity `GET /users` or user id, project, role), **Compare** (selection in a filter panel, `?clusters=` in the URL, versions / capacity / policy-drift tables + summary bar), **Operations** (list with status, source → target, current step, progress, expandable steps, cancel confirm, filter by cluster, auto-refresh while running; wizard modal: restore / clone, source cluster + project → backups loaded through the relay with per-backup target volume, clone source, target cluster / project / deployment, mode, apply switch), **Fleet audit** (filter panel cluster / action, table with details, `fpc-pager`), **Unavailable** notice. **World map**: no map component in the repo (topology / landing pages have none) and no new dependency → `LoadweaverFleetWorldMapComponent`, an equirectangular SVG with **hand-drawn coarse continent outlines** (own `[lon, lat]` waypoints, no third-party map data, repository license), markers per located site (click opens the cluster's nodes), site list grouped by cluster, count of sites without location / empty state.

### 2026-10-22 — P gate: Linux desktop packaging

- **Build** (x64 WSL host, heavy lock, `NX_DAEMON=false`): `RELEASE_VERSION=1.2.3-beta.1 ELECTRON_FORGE_PLATFORM=linux nx run agenstra-native-agent-console:package:production-linux` → `agenstra_1.2.3~beta.1_amd64.deb` (maker-deb turns the prerelease into `~beta.1`, so the beta sorts before 1.2.3) + `native-agent-console-linux-x64-1.2.3-beta.1.zip`. esbuild bundling of `main.js` / `preload.js` worked unchanged (asar holds `main.js`, `preload.js`, `package.json`, icons, forge config). This host lacked `zip` (Forge's zip maker; ubuntu-latest has it) — used a temporary extracted `zip` binary, nothing installed. `linux-rpm` + `linux-repo` ran in one throw-away `ubuntu:24.04` container (digest-pinned, `--memory=2g`, host node mounted read-only; rpm 4.18.2, createrepo_c 0.17.3, apt 2.8.3, GnuPG 2.4.4 — the runner's versions).
- **Fixed (found by the run)**:
  - `rpmsign` failed: Ubuntu's rpm macros point `%{__gpg}` at `/usr/bin/gpg2` (not shipped), and the custom `__gpg_sign_cmd` was missing rpm's argv[0] word. Now `--define "__gpg <absolute gpg from PATH>"` (`findExecutable`) and `__gpg_sign_cmd %{__gpg} gpg --homedir …` (`tools/desktop-release/src/lib/linux.ts`).
  - **`Valid-Until` was not written**: apt-ftparchive 2.8 ignores `APT::FTPArchive::Release::Valid-Until` (it only writes the field when `…::ValidTime` is set). Now `ValidTime=2592000` (30 days; `Date` = signing time), the Date / Valid-Until overrides are gone, and `linux-repo` **fails** if a `Release` comes out without `Valid-Until` (README updated).
  - rpm payload dir was `0700`: Forge's packaged dir is created via mkdtemp and `cp -a <dir>/.` copies that mode onto `/usr/lib/agenstra` (non-root users couldn't run the app); the spec now normalises with `chmod -R u+rwX,go+rX,go-w` (setuid `chrome-sandbox` kept via `%attr`).
  - The SSR server shipped twice (in `app.asar` and as `extraResource`): `forge.config.js` ignores `/server` for the asar → asar 180 MB → 3.6 MB, deb 139 MB → 114 MB, zip 193 MB → 155 MB (the packaged app loads `process.resourcesPath/server`).
  - Absolute symlinks to the build machine in the packages (`assets/monaco/node_modules/.bin/marked -> /home/…/node_modules/…`, cpSync rewrites relative links): `tools/ci/stage-monaco-assets.mjs` skips `.bin`; the staging script is now an input of `stage-monaco-assets` in all six consoles (`project.json`), so a cached stage is invalidated.
  - Re-building into a non-clean `dist` nested `server/server` (stale copy): the native build removes `dist/apps/agenstra/native-agent-console` before assembling (`project.json`, both configurations).
  - Tests: desktop-release 5 suites / 29 (gpg path + argv[0], `ValidTime`, Release without `Valid-Until` refused + keyring removed, payload chmod). tsc lib + spec and eslint clean, prettier applied.
- **Verified**: rpm metadata (`1.2.3~beta.1-1.x86_64`, Requires, `/usr/lib/agenstra` 0755, `chrome-sandbox` 4755, no dangling symlinks). `linux-repo` with a throw-away RSA test key (temp GNUPGHOME in the container, never on disk outside it): apt `dists/{beta,stable}` with `Date` + `Valid-Until` (+30 d); `gpgv` good on `InRelease`, `Release.gpg` and both `repomd.xml.asc`; a modified `Release` refused; `rpm -K` "SIGNATURES NOT OK" before and "Header V4 RSA/SHA256 Signature … OK" after importing `forepath-desktop.asc` into a temp rpmdb (pool and both channel copies). **Debian 13** (`debian:trixie-slim` digest-pinned, `--memory=1g`): generated `.sources` (URI → file:) + key in `/usr/share/keyrings`, `apt-get update` verifies, `apt-get install agenstra` → `1.2.3~beta.1` installed, no missing shared libraries, as a normal user `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 agenstra` reports Electron 39.2.7 / app 1.2.3-beta.1 (GUI start not tried: needs a display); tampered `Packages` → Hash Sum mismatch; `Acquire::Max-ValidTime=1` → "Release file … is expired" (apt enforces the dates).
- **Feeds** (dev key from `release-integrity:generate-release-key` into a temp dir; real keys untouched): dev-signed manifest over the deb + rpm; `writeUpdateFeeds` with the dev key trusted writes `beta.json`, which the app's `parseDesktopUpdateFeed` (trusted origin) accepts; `evaluateDesktopUpdate` for 1.2.2 / beta / linux x64 → available (deb URL), for 1.2.3 → refused (downgrade). Tampered manifest, dev key against the compiled-in production keys, and a version mismatch are refused with no feed file written; the CLI `feed` refuses the dev-signed and the tampered manifest (exit 1, no output dir).
- **Only CI can verify**: macOS signing / notarization / Squirrel.Mac, Windows signtool / Authenticode / NSIS update, the real GPG secret and R2 uploads, `xvfb-run` packaging on ubuntu-latest, dnf / zypper clients against the rpm repo (only `rpm -K` + `gpgv` here).
- Cleaned up: temp keys, repos, work dir, packaging output (`dist/apps/agenstra/native-agent-console`), `tmp/desktop-release`, `tmp/release-integrity`; all containers were `--rm`. `dist/apps/agenstra/frontend-agent-console` (existed before) was rebuilt in place. No commits.
- Review of "P gate: Linux desktop packaging": accepted — deb / zip / rpm, signed apt + rpm repos, feed and a Debian 13 install from the signed repo work end to end. Six real bugs fixed: `rpmsign` gpg path / argv on Ubuntu (would have broken CI), `Valid-Until` silently not written by apt-ftparchive 2.8 (now `ValidTime` + fail-if-missing), rpm install dir 0700, SSR server shipped twice (asar 180 → 3.6 MB), build-machine symlinks from monaco `.bin`, nested `server/server` on non-clean rebuilds. Only CI: macOS / Windows signing and updates, real GPG secret, R2 uploads, dnf / zypper installs.

The packaging run was Agenstra Desktop itself (fixes already in Agenstra), and the monaco `.bin` symlink fix already covers all six consoles.
