  - `BOOT` optional fields `rootDir`, `stopSignal` (normalised `SIG*`, allow-list), `dnsServers` (IP literals), `statsIntervalSeconds`; bundled boot configs parse exactly as before.
  - `STATS` frame (type 6, guest → host, `{memTotal, memAvailable, cpuSteal, load1}` from `/proc`): the guest only sends it when `statsIntervalSeconds` is set, which the daemon only sets with `--stats-file` (so an old host never sees the type); the daemon writes it atomically (+ `updatedAt`).
  - Generic mode (`bridge-guest.cjs --root /newroot --tools /tools`): identity files on tmpfs `/run/lw-identity` bind-mounted over `<root>/etc/{hosts,hostname,resolv.conf}` (symlinked targets skipped, missing ones created empty), `sysfs` ro, **a fresh tmpfs `/dev` with the standard nodes instead of the design's devtmpfs** (devtmpfs would expose the bridge's virtio-serial port `/dev/vport*` to the workload), devpts (newinstance), shm, mqueue, tmpfs `/run` when the image's is empty; mount points that are symlinks / not directories refuse the start (125). Workload and exec sessions run through the static helper `lw-pty` (new mount + PID namespace, own `/proc`, chroot, `setgroups`/`setgid`/`setuid` from the image's `/etc/passwd` + `/etc/group` incl. supplementary groups, cwd, exec; exec sessions join the workload's namespaces via `/run/lw-workload.pid`; PTY with the `pty-helper.py` control protocol). Stop uses the image's stop signal. A boot config whose `rootDir` doesn't match the agent's `--root` is refused (125).
  - `bridge-host.cjs` subcommands: `boot-config --process-file boot-process.json [--root-dir]` (generic; the node agent's `{entrypoint, cmd, env, user, workingDir, stopSignal}`; resolver from the container's `resolv.conf` without loopback servers), `net-config --net-file net.json` (`{mac, mtu, ipv4?, ipv6?}` → MAC + `lw.*` kernel cmdline), `vm-domain --config vm.json --run-dir --out [--seed-image]` (full VM libvirt XML: UEFI OVMF / AAVMF with per-start nvram or BIOS amd64, `host-model` / `host-passthrough`, DRBD block disks virtio-blk boot first (`cache=none io=native` / `writeback io=threads`, `discard=unmap`), one tap per NIC `managed='no'` + multiqueue, seed as virtio-scsi read-only CD-ROM, serial / VNC on UNIX sockets, qemu-guest-agent channel; prints devices + taps), `relay --socket` (stdio ↔ UNIX socket, raw TTY). ## M7 W2: compose + scheduler (2026-10-23)

- **util-compose**:
  - `extensions.ts`: `x-loadweaver.runtime: z.enum(RUNTIMES)` (all four levels); new `x-loadweaver.microvm: { rootfsSize? }` (string / bytes), only with `runtime: microvm` ("microvm settings need x-loadweaver.runtime: microvm").
  - `model.ts`: `ServiceSpec.runtime: Runtime`, `microvm?: { rootfsBytes? }` (set for every `microvm` service, size absent = planner default), new `deviceAccess: { path: '/dev/kvm'; permissions: 'rw' | 'rwm' }[]` next to `devices: string[]` (host paths, kept for pins / migration eligibility).
  - `parse-compose.ts`: compose `runtime:` maps `runc` → runc, `runsc` / `runsc-systrap` → sandboxed, `runsc-kvm` → sandboxed-kvm; anything else errors "unknown runtime X, use x-loadweaver.runtime" (`runc` accepted as Docker's default; before, unknown values silently became runc); `x-loadweaver.runtime` wins, with a warning when they differ. `devices` (short `HOST[:CONTAINER][:PERMS]`, Docker's `HOST:PERMS`, long `{source,target,permissions}`): only `/dev/kvm`, same path in the container, `rw` / `rwm` (default `rwm`), no duplicates; errors "device X is not allowed (allow-list: /dev/kvm)", "… must keep its path …", "… permissions must be rw or rwm", "… listed twice", "devices need runtime runc: runtime X can't pass host devices through (/dev/kvm)". `/dev/kvm` keeps the `device access (/dev/kvm)` deployment pin and always warns "device access (/dev/kvm): the workload can run its own VMs; it is pinned for migration" (also when acknowledged). `runtime: microvm`: `network_mode: host` and `privileged` are errors, `cap_add` warns that capabilities apply inside the guest (replaces the spoofing / privileged warnings there), binds stay allowed (pinned as before).
  - `units.ts`: `parseBytes` accepts binary suffixes `Ki`/`Mi`/`Gi`/`Ti` (design's `rootfsSize: 10Gi`; also volumes / memory).
- **util-scheduler** (new `eligibility.ts`; `canRunWorkloads`, `canHoldVolumes`, `eligibleNodes`, `hasRequiredFeatures`, `missingFeaturesReason` moved there, still exported from the index):
  - Types: `SchedulerNode.runtimes: Runtime[]`, `isolation?` (per-level `{state, reasonCode?, reason?}`, for reasons only), `kvm?: { usable, optOut }` (replaces the design's `kvmDevice`; undefined = no usable KVM), `virtualMachines?` (undefined = no), `blockVolumes?` (undefined = yes if DRBD 9 + agent feature `vm-block-volumes`); `SchedulerService.runtime: Runtime`, `needsKvmDevice?`, `virtualMachine?`; `SchedulerVolume.mode?: 'filesystem' | 'block'`.
  - Eligibility funnel (lifecycle → selector → **exact level** → `/dev/kvm` → full VM → refuse-gated agent features): `runsLevel` = level in `runtimes`, KVM levels also refused when `kvm.optOut` or `kvm.usable === false` (stale capabilities); `needsKvmDevice` → `kvmUsable` (usable && !optOut); `virtualMachine` → `virtualMachines === true` && `kvmUsable`. Derived features (`isolationFeatures`): sandboxed-kvm / microvm → `isolation-ladder`, microvm services (not VMs) → `microvm`, devices → `workload-devices`, VMs → `virtual-machines`, block volumes → `vm-block-volumes`. These are **hard** rules (a placed replica on an agent without them moves), unlike `requiredFeatures` (kept replicas stay); unknown `features` count as present. Failure analysis uses the same funnel, so VMs fail over only to VM-capable nodes.
  - Block volumes: copies (primary and replicas) only on `canHoldBlockVolumes` nodes; reason "no eligible node can hold the block volumes its VM disks need (…)".
  - Reasons (`ineligibilityReason`, first empty step): "no eligible node (no active node can run workloads)", "(selector matches none of the N nodes that can run workloads)", "(runtime microvm: 0 of 5 nodes ready — node-1 E_KVM_UNAVAILABLE, node-2 disabled by node spec, …)" (per node: opt-out → "disabled by node spec", else the probe's `reasonCode ?? state`, KVM level with unusable KVM → `E_KVM_UNAVAILABLE`, else "not ready"; max 5 named, then "N more"), "(device /dev/kvm: 0 of N nodes with runtime X have usable KVM — … KVM not usable / KVM not reported / disabled by node spec)", "(virtual machines: 0 of N nodes with runtime microvm support full VMs — …)", "no eligible node has an agent with the protocol features … (needed for runtime X[, device /dev/kvm]); update the node agents". The old "no eligible node (runtime X, selector)" text is gone.
  - "At least" helpers (selectors only): `runtimeNodeLabels(runtimes)` → `runtime.loadweaver.com/<level>: ready` per ready level + `loadweaver.com/runtime: <strongest>`; `runtimeAtLeastExpression(min)` → `In` over `runtimesAtLeast(min)`. Multiple NICs need no scheduler input (addresses are the compiler's).
- **Consumer compile fix** (for W3 to finish): `workload-planning.utils.ts` `buildWorkloadSpec` emits `runtime: dockerRuntimeFamily(service.runtime)` and `isolation` only for `sandboxed-kvm` / `microvm` (hash-stable for runc / sandboxed). No other consumer needed changes.

## M7 W7: live sessions + guest exec (2026-10-23)

- **Node agent** (`feature-node-agent/src/lib/live/`):
  - New `guest-target.ts`: `MICROVM_LABEL = 'loadweaver.com/microvm'` (`bundled` | `generic`, **W6 sets it on the launcher container**; import it from here or keep the value), `VM_LABEL = 'loadweaver.com/vm'` (the VM workload label from the compiler), `guestKind(labels)` → `container | microvm-bundled | microvm-generic | vm` (launcher-labelled images via the image label `io.agenstra.microvm.protocol` count as bundled), `guestExecOptions` (microVMs: `toMicrovmExecOptions` from the shared bridge — `Cmd = [vm-exec, --user, --workdir, --pass-env NAME…, --, …]`, `User = agenstra-vmm`, env values stay in `Env`; full VMs refused "open the serial console instead"), `guestFileRoot` (generic: the bind source of the launcher's `/guest` = the replica's overlay `merged/`, no dependency on `rootfs-cache.ts` paths; bundled: `MergedDir` + `/guest`; VMs: "disks are not browsable"), `VM_CONSOLE_PATH`.
  - `live-sessions.service.ts`: terminals and machine exec go through `guestExecOptions` after the restored-replica branch; TTY resize stays Docker exec resize (vm-exec forwards it); exit codes from `exec.inspect()`. File browser root from `guestFileRoot`. New `openConsole(channel, consoleOpen)` (full VMs only, else "consoles are only available for virtual machines"): `vnc` = `docker exec <launcher> vm-console vnc` without a TTY and without the vm-exec rewrite, wired like machine exec (binary stdout → `execOutput`, relay stderr as `stream: stderr`, exit code); `serial` = a viewer of the shared serial collector (below), resize ignored, 30-minute input idle like terminals, a guest that doesn't read (> 4 MiB backlog) ends the session. `execInput` / `execClose` / `closeAll` route to console sessions; session cap (32) counts both. Session wiring factored into `run()` / `refuse()`.
  - New `serial-console.ts` (**the 1 MiB serial ring buffer lives on the node**): the VM's serial socket takes one client and drops output nobody reads, so the node keeps one collector per running VM container (`vm-console serial`, no TTY, stdout only — the relay's stderr complaints while the domain boots are not logged as console output) from the container's start (Docker `start` / `die` / `destroy` events on `loadweaver.com/managed=true` + `loadweaver.com/vm`, plus the running VMs at agent start), re-attaching with backoff (1 s doubling to 30 s, reset after 10 s attached) while the container runs. `SerialLog` keeps the last MiB; every console session gets it first ("show boot log"), then live output; all sessions share the line's input. The ring dies with the container (restart = new log). `LiveSessionsService.watchConsoles()` is called from `agent-connection.service.ts` `prepareHost` after `reset()`; `onModuleDestroy` stops the collectors.
  - `agent-connection.service.ts`: `consoleOpen` in `LIVE_MESSAGES` (needs a channel) → `live.openConsole`.
  - Deviation from the design: the serial session uses a non-TTY exec (raw bytes both ways, the guest's getty echoes); with the shared collector a TTY per viewer isn't possible and isn't needed.
- **Protocol**: `vm-consoles` → `agent: true` (versioning spec's implemented list: `isolation-ladder`, `vm-consoles`).
- **Control plane**:
  - New `gateways/consoles.gateway.ts` (Socket.IO namespace `socket/consoles`, env `LOADWEAVER_CONSOLES_WEBSOCKET_NAMESPACE`; added to `docker-compose.yaml` / `.start-containers.env.example`; registered in `control-plane.module.ts`). Deviation from the design's raw `/api/live/:session/vnc` WebSocket: a Socket.IO namespace like terminals / tunnels / exec — same handshake auth (`Authorization`, interactive users / API key, no PATs), same CORS, no Engine.IO `destroyUpgrade` conflict on the shared HTTP server, no extra ticket endpoint; noVNC takes a WebSocket-like channel object, so W8's `fpc-vnc-viewer` wraps the namespace. Events: `openConsole` {sessionId?, replica `<p>/lw-vm/<name>/0`, kind serial|vnc, cols?, rows?} → `consoleOpened` {sessionId, kind, recorded}; `consoleInput` {sessionId, data} (serial UTF-8 text, VNC binary); `consoleResize` (serial, recording only); `closeConsole`; `consoleOutput` {sessionId, data} (serial text with the boot log first, VNC binary RFB); `consoleClosed` {sessionId, exitCode, error?}; `error` {sessionId?, message}. Documented in `spec/asyncapi.yaml`.
  - Access: new `LiveAccessService.console(req, replica, kind)` — only `lw-vm` replicas, roles as terminals (`replica(…, 'exec')`: operators / admins, developers with `developerExec`), `vnc` refused when the VM's `console.graphical` is false (404 for an unknown VM). The node must advertise `vm-consoles` (`lw_nodes.protocol_features`), else "does not support VM consoles". Access re-checked every minute with the heartbeat.
  - Audit / records: `vm.console.open` / `vm.console.close` (target `virtual-machine/<p>/<name>`, details kind, replica, node, session, recorded; close: seconds, bytesIn / bytesOut, error). Sessions are rows in `lw_terminal_sessions` (target `virtual-machine/<p>/<name>/console/<kind>`), so the existing session list / heartbeat / orphan sweep / recordings retention apply. Serial recorded as asciicast when the cluster / project records terminals; VNC metadata and duration only (`recorded: false`).
  - Limits: 4 consoles per socket, 8 per user, opens 1/s per user (burst 5); input serial 256 KiB/s (burst 1 MiB), VNC 2 MiB/s (burst 8 MiB), ≤ 256 KiB per message (`maxHttpBufferSize` 512 KiB); 30-minute input idle; a client that doesn't read (socket.io backlog) ends the session; node relay stderr isn't forwarded.
  - `live-broker.ts`: `consoleOpen` in `LIVE_TO_AGENT` (session ends with `execExit` as for terminals; relayed across replicas through LISTEN / NOTIFY like every live message).
- **For W8**: open the namespace `socket/consoles` with the user's bearer token; serial tab = the existing terminal panel fed by `consoleOutput` text, sending `consoleInput` text; VNC tab = `fpc-vnc-viewer` passing noVNC a channel adapter (`binaryType = 'arraybuffer'`, `send(ArrayBuffer)` → `consoleInput` binary, `consoleOutput` binary → `onmessage({data})`, `consoleOpened` → `onopen`, `consoleClosed` / `error` → `onclose`). The design's `POST …/:name/console` ticket isn't needed; if W8 wants it as an API, it can return `{ namespace: 'socket/consoles', replica, kind }`. Session list: `GET /api/live/sessions` already lists consoles (target prefix `virtual-machine/`). Frontend env: add a `consoles` socket URL next to `tunnels` in `util-configuration` `environment.console*.ts`.
- **Tests** (unit only, `--maxWorkers=2`): node agent new `guest-target.spec.ts` (3), `serial-console.spec.ts` (4: ring, collector + replay + fan-out, re-attach / stop, start event), `live-sessions.service.spec.ts` +6 (vm-exec wrapping with TTY + resize and machine exec incl. env values not in argv, launcher-labelled images, VM exec refused, generic guest root browsing + VM refusal, serial console replay / shared input / close, VNC binary relay, consoles for VMs only) — live dir 4 suites / 28; node-agent lib 47 / 48 suites pass (the failing `workload-container.spec.ts` "exact isolation level" is W6's in-progress file). CP new `consoles.gateway.spec.ts` (4) and `live-access.service.spec.ts` (2), `live-broker.spec.ts` green; CP lib 102 / 104 suites (failures in `autoscale.utils.spec.ts` / `workload-controller.service.spec.ts` from W3's in-progress planning work; run with ts-jest diagnostics off because W3's `vm-planning.utils.ts` / `plans.service.ts` don't compile yet). util-agent-protocol: `versioning.spec.ts` fails only because W6 flipped `workload-devices` / `microvm` to `agent: true` without adding them to the spec's implemented list (W6 to add). `tsc --noEmit` clean for node-agent lib + spec and util-agent-protocol; CP lib / spec only show W3's errors. ESLint / Prettier clean on all touched files.
- **For the combined gate**: VM-lab spec (W13) for a full VM: serial collector captures UEFI / kernel boot output from container start, console replay after reconnect, two viewers sharing the line, VNC through noVNC end to end (RFB handshake through `socket/consoles`), console across a guest reboot (`vm-ctl reboot`) and container restart (new log); microVM terminals / machine exec / file browser in bundled and generic mode (TTY resize visible in the guest, exit codes, env values absent from `ps` in the launcher); a node without `vm-consoles` refused by the CP.

## M7 W4: node probes + KVM prep (2026-10-23)

- **Node agent: isolation probes** (new `host/isolation-probe.service.ts`, `IsolationProbeService`, provider in `node-agent.module.ts`): real per-level checks, no name matching. Inputs: `docker info` runtimes through `parseGvisorRuntimeArgs`; KVM facts from the shared host script (`buildGvisorHostScript({ kvmApt: false })` written to `<state>/isolation/gvisor-host.sh`, `check --json` → `parseGvisorHostReport`); `/dev/kvm` opened O_RDWR; `/proc/cpuinfo`. Levels:
  - `runc`: Docker answers + smoke `true` (no probe image: ready with `E_PROBE_IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, the gVisor levels then `probe-failed`); Docker down: every level `probe-failed` `E_DOCKER_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE`, `runtimes: []`.
  - `sandboxed` / `sandboxed-kvm`: `GVISOR_RUNTIMES.systrap|kvm.runtime` registered (`E_RUNTIME_NOT_REGISTERED`), platform systrap-or-default / `kvm` and Netstack (`E_RUNTIME_MISCONFIGURED`), smoke `dmesg` must show gVisor (`E_PROBE_RUNTIME_MISMATCH`, `E_PROBE_START_FAILED`, `E_PROBE_TIMEOUT`); KVM level additionally KVM usable (`E_KVM_UNAVAILABLE`) and not opted out (`disabled-by-admin`, `E_DISABLED_BY_ADMIN`).
  - `microvm` (static part only): KVM usable, not opted out, runc floor, `/dev/net/tun`, the release's launcher image present locally (or its cluster copy) — `E_MICROVM_IMAGE_UNSUPPORTED` while no `COMPONENT_IMAGES['microvm-launcher']` pin exists (W5 adds it; resolved by name at runtime, no code change needed), `E_PROBE_IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE` when not pulled. The boot probe microVM is W6 (M7.2).
  - Smoke containers: `docker run --rm --name lw-probe-<level>-<rand> --label loadweaver.com/probe=1 --network none --memory 64m --pids-limit 64 --runtime <rt>` with the node-shell image (pulled, or the cluster copy), 30 s; removed with `rm -f` on failure / timeout; leftovers removed before each probe; `workload.manager.ts` `foreign()` skips them (`isProbeContainer`, `PROBE_LABEL` in `managed-containers.ts`).
  - `kvm.usable` = device present + opens + CPU not `no` (deviation from the design's "module loaded + cpu yes": arm64 builds KVM in and reports cpu `unknown`). `cpuFlagsHash` = SHA-256 of the sorted first `flags` / `Features` line.
  - Scheduling: first `current()` (hello) probes; a stored result of the **same boot** (`boot_id`) answers at once while a fresh probe runs (never across a reboot, so the rollout's KVM gate sees post-reboot facts); every 6 h (`LOADWEAVER_ISOLATION_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS`, min 60 s); after host updates without reboot (`updates.service.ts`); after 3 consecutive start failures on a level (`recordStartFailure` / `recordStartSuccess` — **W6 wires them in `workload.manager.ts`**); on a new `desiredState.host.probeNonce`. Serialized; results + host settings stored in `agent-state.store.ts` (`isolation.json`). A changed result triggers `onChange` → `AgentConnectionService.refreshHello()` (make-before-break second stream to the same endpoint; the CP registry replaces the old session), so capabilities reach the CP without a heartbeat field.
  - Opt-out at runtime (`desiredState.host.kvm`, applied in `agent-connection.service.ts`): `auto → disabled` runs `gvisor-host.sh uninstall-kvm`, `disabled → auto` runs `install-kvm` (both new, see below; never downloads), then re-probes. Before the first host settings, the last applied desired state's `host.kvm` counts.
- **`host-info.service.ts`**: capabilities from the probe report — `runtimes` (ready levels), `isolation` (every level), `kvm` (facts + `usable` / `optOut`), `cpuFlagsHash`, `sandboxProbe` derived from `sandboxed` (v1 CPs); `checkpoint.runscKvm` only when `runsc-kvm` is registered (platform kvm, Netstack, binary runs, cgroup v2, level ready). The probe service is `@Optional` (falls back to its own instance; lab entries constructing `new HostInfoService(commands)` keep compiling).

- **Protocol**: `isolation-ladder` → `agent: true` (versioning spec updated: implemented features advertised, the rest not). Caveat for W10: `restored-runtime.ts` `sandboxRuntimeOf` is still platform-blind (may pick `runsc-kvm` for a systrap restore when `runsc-systrap` is missing); CP eligibility for KVM checkpoints must wait for W10's same-platform restore.

## M7 W6: microVM node side (2026-10-23)

- **`microvm/rootfs-unpack.ts`** (new): own streaming tar reader (ustar, pax incl. `SCHILY.xattr.*` / `LIBARCHIVE.xattr.*`, GNU long names, base-256 numbers, checksum; sparse / exotic types fail the layer); entry rules: paths normalised, absolute / `..` / NUL refused, parents walked with `lstat` (a path through a symlink or non-directory fails the layer), existing symlinks replaced instead of followed, files opened `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`, hardlinks only to files extracted from the same layer, char / block / FIFO dropped (counted), `.wh.<name>` → `mknod c 0 0` (a same-layer entry wins), `.wh..wh..opq` → `trusted.overlay.opaque=y`, AUFS `.wh..wh.*` skipped, ownership + modes kept (chown before chmod: setuid / setgid survive), xattrs only `security.capability` / `user.*`; media types OCI / Docker `tar`, `tar+gzip`, `tar+zstd` (Node's zlib zstd), foreign / non-distributable refused; both digests (blob, diffID) while streaming; decompressed bound `max(size × 8, 64 MiB)` capped by `LOADWEAVER_VMROOT_LAYER_MAX_BYTES` (16 GiB); `syncfs` (`sync -f`) before publish. Confinement: `loadweaver-agent unpack-layer` (internal command in `agent-cli.ts`) runs under `unshare --mount --pid --fork --kill-child`, makes mounts private, bind-mounts its staging dir onto itself and re-mounts every other mount read-only (`confinementCommands`), unpacks stdin, prints the result. `extractExportedTree` (same rules, no devices / whiteouts / xattrs) serves the scanner and the probe.
- **`microvm/rootfs-cache.ts`** (new, `RootfsCache`): layout `/var/lib/loadweaver/vmroot` (0700; `LOADWEAVER_VMROOT_DIR`): `layers/sha256/<hex>/` + marker `<hex>.json` `{digest, diffId, bytes, unpackedAt, usedAt}`, `replicas/<sha256(id)[0:24]>/` (`rw/` with `upper/` + `work/`, loop image `rw.img`), `staging/` (cleared at start). Blobs via the node's router (`127.0.0.1:<routerPort>/v2/<host>/<repo>/blobs/<digest>`, pull token added there) for private / mirrored images, else straight from the registry with the anonymous bearer flow (`registryApiHost`); `privateRepositories` now includes `microvm.guestImage`. One unpack per diffID (in-process promise + `O_EXCL` lock file), digest and diffID compared with the spec before `rename(staging → layers)`; disk check (declared × 4 + 1 GiB, GC first). Writable layer: thin LV `lw-vmrw-<key>` of `rootfsBytes` in the volume pool (ext4, `nosuid,nodev,noexec,discard`; re-activated, not re-formatted, when kept), else sparse loop image; overlay `lowerdir` (top first) `nosuid,nodev,noexec,index=off,redirect_dir=off,metacopy=off`, refused beyond one page of options (`E_MICROVM_IMAGE_UNSUPPORTED`, ~60 layers). `release` (replica deleted / recreated) unmounts, `lvremove`s, removes the dirs; a container restart keeps the layer. GC: LRU over layers neither mounted (overlay `lowerdir` in mountinfo) nor desired, cap `LOADWEAVER_VMROOT_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` (default 15 % of the fs), after every apply and hourly. **Multi-arch** (coordinator correction): `guestLayers` picks `microvm.platformLayers[<node arch>]` (`x64` → amd64, `arm64`), refuses with `E_MICROVM_IMAGE_UNSUPPORTED: the guest image has no <arch> variant (available: …)`; single-arch `layers` still accepted.
- **`microvm/guest-network.ts`** (new, `GuestNetwork`): NICs: generic = `eth0 ↔ lwtap0`, MAC `52:54:00` + sha256(workload id); full VMs = one per `vm.nics[]` (`lwtap<n>`, NIC MAC), each mapped to the container interface carrying its address. Per NIC inside the launcher netns (`nsenter -t <pid> -n`): interface takes the guest MAC, `ip tuntap … user/group 10930 [multi_queue]`, tap MTU = interface MTU, `ip addr flush`, `disable_ipv6`, ingress qdiscs, `matchall` redirect iface → tap, tap → iface only via flower `src_mac` + `src_ip` v4 / `arp_sip` + `arp_sha` / v6 / EUI-64 link-local / `::` icmpv6 (DAD), prio 99 drop; `arp_ignore=8` once. Idempotent (taps present → skip). `net.json` `{mac, mtu, ipv4?, ipv6?}` with the Docker network's MTU option (default 1500).
- **`microvm/microvm-probe.ts`** (new, `MicrovmProbe`, called by W4's `IsolationProbeService.microvm()` after the static checks): unpack-cache check (`unshare`, `setfattr`, `mkfs.ext4`, writable vmroot), then a generic launcher booting the node shell image (exported file system as guest root) on the internal probe network `loadweaver-microvm-probe` (`lwprobe0`, 192.0.2.0/29, link-local gateways added like the pod bridge): stdout + stderr in `docker logs`, `vm-exec` exit codes 0 / 3, file coherence (guest writes, host reads), `ping` of the guest IP, `docker stop` → exit 0 (workload traps TERM); 240 s; probe-labelled, always removed. The report carries `microvm { launcherDigest (image id), unpackCache, thinPool }` → `capabilities.microvm` (`host-info.service.ts`).
- **`workload-container.ts`**: took over W4's `workloadDockerRuntime` (`microvm` → `runc`); `devices` → `HostConfig.Devices` (any level; plan restricts to runc); `microvmContainerOptions`: runc, `Init: false`, `CapDrop ALL` + `MICROVM_LAUNCHER_CAPABILITIES`, `no-new-privileges`, `/dev/kvm` (+ `/dev/net/tun` generic / VM, DRBD devices `rw` for VMs), `PidsLimit 1024`, memory `memoryMiB + 384` MiB, `NanoCpus` vCPUs + 0.25, read-only rootfs + tmpfs `/tmp` 16m + shm 64m (generic / VM), `StopSignal SIGTERM`, `StopTimeout` grace + 10; generic: `tini -- launch-generic`, env `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_{MEMORY_MB,VCPUS,STOP_GRACE}`, `FORWARD_PORTS=`, `LW_MODE=generic`, mounts merged → `/guest` (rprivate), run dir → `/run/loadweaver/vm` ro + `stats/` rw, volumes / binds / tmpfs / secrets below `/guest`; bundled: image as is (own entrypoint, compose env + sizing env, `/guest`-prefixed mounts, no tap); VM: `tini -- launch-vm`. Labels per W7: `loadweaver.com/microvm=generic|bundled`, full VMs `loadweaver.com/vm=<name>` (not the microvm label). `bootProcess` (from `microvm.process`, else the spec's fields), `microvmRunDir` (`<runtime>/vm/<key>`), `launcherKindOf`.
- **`workload.manager.ts`**: `prepareMicrovm` before every start (also re-starts after a reboot): layers + overlay, run dir 0711 with `boot-process.json` 0600, `net.json`, `stats/` chowned to 10930; full VMs through two optional providers for W9 (`VM_BLOCK_DEVICES`, `VM_LAUNCH_FILES`), else refused. Further VM NICs: `docker network connect` to kept-address networks `loadweaver-kept-<fam>-nic<n>` (new `slot` in `keptNetworkName` / `ensureNetwork`) before the start. `attachGuestNetwork` after `start()`, on every running launcher per apply (covers missed events) and on Docker `start` events (stream with retry; filtered by the spec). Image policy / scan for generic microVMs on the guest image (pulled through the cluster), tracked for rescans. `remove` releases the guest root and the run dir. `recordStartFailure` / `recordStartSuccess` (W4) around create + start per level. `setDesired` + GC after every apply.
- **`pod-network.manager.ts`**: `169.254.1.1/32` and (IPv6 pod networks) `fe80::1/64 nodad` on `lwbr0`, `send_redirects=0`, every apply (`podGatewayCommands`; the command runner is optional so the lab entries still build).
- **Metrics**: `replica.guest_memory_total_bytes`, `replica.guest_memory_used_bytes`, `replica.guest_cpu_steal_ratio`, `replica.guest_load1` from `stats/stats.json` (≤ 60 s old) for generic / VM launchers; `node.vmroot_cache_bytes`, `node.vmroot_layers` (Prometheus: `loadweaver_replica_guest_…`, the design's `lw_*` names mapped to the existing scheme).
- **Image scanner**: `io.forepath.scan.nested-rootfs` (plain absolute path) → the image is created (never started, probe-labelled), exported, the nested part extracted with the unpack rules, `trivy rootfs` on it; findings merged into the image's scan.
- **Protocol**: `microvm` and `workload-devices` `agent: true` (versioning spec list updated); `workloads[].microvm.platformLayers` (`amd64` / `arm64` → layer lists, takes precedence over `layers`) + `MICROVM_ARCHITECTURES` in `messages.ts`.
- **Deviations** (justified): layer markers next to the layer dir (inside, they'd appear in the guest root); overlay mounted below the runtime tmpfs (`/run/loadweaver/vmroot/<key>/merged`) so Docker can't restart a launcher on an empty root after a reboot; generic guest MAC derived from the workload id and set on the container interface (`net.json` must exist before the start, the endpoint MAC isn't known then); decompression bound with a 64 MiB floor (×8 alone breaks small, highly compressible layers); boot probe boots the node shell's exported file system (local Docker image) instead of the unpack cache, which is checked separately; scanning the guest image keeps a Docker copy of it (scan / rescans as for containers; disk cost ≈ image size); metric names in the existing `replica.*` / `node.*` scheme.
- **Tests** (unit only, `--maxWorkers=2`): node-agent lib 53 suites / 407 (new `rootfs-unpack.spec.ts` with crafted tars, `rootfs-cache.spec.ts`, `guest-network.spec.ts`, `microvm-probe.spec.ts`, `pod-network.manager.spec.ts`; additions in workload-container, workload.manager, isolation-probe, metrics, image-scanner, kept-address, registry specs; `tarArchive` fixture in `test-fixtures.ts`), util-agent-protocol 5 / 62 (+1 skipped), control-plane lib 112 / 878. `tsc --noEmit` clean (node-agent lib + spec, util-agent-protocol lib + spec, control-plane lib, node-agent app). ESLint / Prettier clean on all touched files.

## M7 W11: Agenstra levels on Loadweaver (2026-10-23)

- **Mapping** (new `feature-agent-manager/src/lib/runtime/loadweaver/isolation-mapping.ts`, exported from the lib index): `standard` ↔ `runc`, `sandboxed` ↔ `sandboxed`, `sandboxed-kvm` ↔ `sandboxed-kvm`, `microvm` ↔ `microvm` (`LOADWEAVER_RUNTIME_FOR_LEVEL`, `toLoadweaverRuntime`, `toIsolationLevel`); unknown values throw `LoadweaverIsolationMappingError` (`BadRequestException`, body `code: E_ISOLATION_RUNTIME_FAILED`), never a fallback. Container create options: `loadweaverRuntimeForContainer` (`runc` → runc, the configured gVisor runtimes of a level incl. `-hostnet` → that level, `microvm: true` + `runc` → microvm, microvm with another runtime / unknown names → throw); updates: `loadweaverRuntimeForUpdate` (a microVM env pinned to its launcher's `runc` stays `microvm`, anything else throws; no moves into / out of a microVM). M7.0's `loadweaverRuntimeForIsolation` / `LoadweaverIsolationUnsupportedError` / KVM refusal removed. Checked before any secret / plan as before.
- **Compose** (`environment-compose.ts`): `EnvironmentSpec.runtime` = all four levels; `parseEnvironmentCompose` maps back exactly (absent → `runc`, Loadweaver's default; unknown → throws instead of the old `sandboxed` fallback). **MicroVM variant**: image = Agenstra's microVM image (the caller's `resolveMicrovmImage()`; `LoadweaverRuntime` falls back to it, never to the plain worker image, so the CP never compiles the worker as a generic guest), `x-loadweaver.runtime: microvm` → bundled mode via W3's `isBundledMicrovmImage` (image label `io.agenstra.microvm.protocol` = 1, image pinned by digest at plan time); no `cap_add` / `cap_drop` / `init` / `devices` / `privileged` (the node agent's `microvmContainerOptions` applies runc, `Init:false`, `CapDrop ALL` + launcher caps, `no-new-privileges`, `/dev/kvm`); `environment`: `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_FORWARD_PORTS=4096,6080`, `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_LOOPBACK_PORTS=''` (overrides the image's guard relay 3128); guest size as `deploy.resources.limits` (`LOADWEAVER_ENVIRONMENT_MICROVM_CPUS` default `2`, `LOADWEAVER_ENVIRONMENT_MICROVM_MEMORY` default `2g`; the node derives `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_MEMORY_MB` / `_VCPUS`, the planner adds 384 MiB / 250 m). Verified ad hoc with `parseCompose` (no issues; requests = limits 2 CPU / 2 GiB). `compose.loadweaver-runtime.yaml`: KVM / microVM switches, `AGENT_MICROVM_IMAGE`, the two size variables.
- **Deviations from the design (M7.5)**: (1) volume / secret targets stay the guest's paths (`/app`, the env file path) — W6's `workloadMounts(…, '/guest')` already prefixes every mount of a microVM replica (bundled included), a `/guest` prefix in the compose would end up at `/guest/guest/…`. (2) **No `vm-exec` wrapping in the manager**: W7's node agent rewrites every machine exec / terminal into a microVM replica (`guestKind` = launcher label or the image's protocol label → `toMicrovmExecOptions`), so `LoadweaverRuntime` / `LoadweaverClient` send plain argv (wrapping twice would run `vm-exec` inside the guest); test pins it. Live files use the node's `guestFileRoot` (only `putFilesIntoContainer` uses them, and only for guard sidecars, which don't exist on Loadweaver). (3) No explicit `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_ENTRYPOINT` / healthcheck in the compose: the image's entrypoint ENV is used as on the Docker host (custom `AGENT_MICROVM_IMAGE`s keep theirs); a compose healthcheck would be wrapped into `vm-exec` by W3's `microvmHealthcheck`, none is set (as before for all levels).
- **Probes** (`LoadweaverRuntime`): `capabilityView()` = `client.isolationCapabilities()` cached 60 s with in-flight sharing (errors not cached). `getDockerHostInfo` requires the view (CP unreachable → Agenstra's "Docker unavailable" path) and lists every level's runtimes with the shared installer's `runtimeArgs` (so `misconfiguredRuntime` passes and the levels reach their probe); `runIsolationProbe` maps `runtime ?? expectedRuntime` to the level and answers `{ ok, gvisorKernelDetected }` from the view (not ready: the CP's reason code + `Loadweaver: no schedulable node in project … runs X (state: per-node reason)`; unknown runtime → `E_RUNTIME_NOT_REGISTERED`; CP error → `E_PROBE_START_FAILED`); `runMicrovmProbe` real (the `microvm` level of the view). `IsolationCapabilitiesService` unchanged: microVM `E_KVM_UNAVAILABLE` / `E_MICROVM_IMAGE_UNSUPPORTED` → `unsupported`, other non-ready → `probe-failed` (gVisor levels the same). A ready level whose plan later fails (capacity) fails the creation with `E_ISOLATION_RUNTIME_FAILED` (agents.service's existing path; `LoadweaverApiError` isn't an `HttpException`).
- **`LoadweaverClient`**: `isolationCapabilities(selector?)` → `GET /api/projects/:p/isolation-capabilities[?selector=]`; types `LoadweaverIsolationCapabilities` / `LoadweaverIsolationLevelCapability`.
- **CP** (new `controllers/isolation-capabilities.controller.ts`, registered in `control-plane.module.ts`): `GET /api/projects/:project/isolation-capabilities?selector=key=value[,…]`, scope `resources:read` + `ProjectAccessService.assertRead` (project members incl. the manager's operator PAT; no new scope). Nodes = `toSchedulerNodes(plannerNodes(nodes, now, —, kvmOptOutNodes(Node resources)))` (W3's inputs, so derived runtime labels, KVM opt-out from the node spec, features); placement = `canRunWorkloads` ∩ selector (the model has no project node selector, so the request selector is the whole placement narrowing). Per level a synthetic service (exact level, selector, no requests) through `eligibleNodes` → `ready` with `nodes` = count; otherwise the most common per-node cause among the placement (`disabled-by-admin`/`E_DISABLED_BY_ADMIN` for opted-out KVM nodes, the node's probe state + reason code — `installation-failed` counts as `probe-failed` —, `E_KVM_UNAVAILABLE`, `E_RUNTIME_NOT_REGISTERED` for missing agent features / unreported; ties prefer `probe-failed`) and the scheduler's `ineligibilityReason` (≤ 512 chars); empty placement → `unsupported` `E_DOCKER_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE`. Response `{ project, selector, nodes, strongest, levels: {runc, sandboxed, sandboxed-kvm, microvm}, checkedAt }`. Capacity deliberately not considered. OpenAPI: path + `IsolationLevelCapability` schema (`spec/openapi.yaml`, prettier-formatted).
- **Docs**: `docs/loadweaver/guides/agenstra-on-loadweaver.md` "Nodes": four-level table, exact-level / never-downgrade, capability view (endpoint, 60 s cache, per-node reasons, admin switches, capacity caveat), microVM environments (bundled mode, launcher settings, `/guest` mounts by the node, ports, loopback relay off, guest size variables), KVM on by default, `--no-kvm` / `LOADWEAVER_KVM=disabled`, node spec `virtualization.kvm: disabled`, KVM modules with kernel updates + `kvm lost after update`, on-demand `POST /api/nodes/<node>/isolation-probe` (replaces M7.0's "not available yet" / "installer KVM off").
- **Tests** (unit only, `--maxWorkers=2`): new `isolation-mapping.spec.ts` (5), `isolation-capabilities.controller.spec.ts` (8: counts, non-schedulable nodes ignored, most common cause + per-node reason, opt-out, missing agent features, selector narrowing / empty placement, selector parsing, controller with Node-spec opt-out); `loadweaver.runtime.spec.ts` rewritten for the levels (each level created 1:1, unknown refused before storing, microVM compose, microVM defaults + size config, update keeps level / microVM stays, exec unchanged for microVMs, host facts + probes from one cached view, CP failure, `IsolationCapabilitiesService` end to end on the runtime, compose round trip incl. microVM, exact parse-back); `loadweaver-client.spec.ts` +1. Agenstra agent-manager 118 suites / 1762 (+6 skipped), agent-controller 133 / 1253, util-compose 2 / 79, CP controllers + modules 4 / 41. `tsc --noEmit` clean: agent-manager lib + spec + app, CP lib + spec + app. ESLint clean (touched files), Prettier clean.
- **For the combined gate**: `agenstra-on-loadweaver.vm-lab.spec.ts` (W13, optional): the four levels in the manager's `GET /api/isolation` against a single-node cluster (nested KVM), an environment at each level, a microVM environment's terminal / `sendCommandToContainer` / env-file read through the node's `vm-exec` rewrite, OpenCode reachable on the service address (bundled port forward), workspace volume at `/guest/app` in the launcher; `agenstra-runtime.integration` (CP) with the new endpoint; a node opted out (`--no-kvm`) reported `disabled-by-admin`. Open point: a microVM environment reserves its full guest size (limits = requests) — if that's too coarse for dense workspaces, add `deploy.resources.reservations` for CPU.
- Review of "M7 W11": accepted (1:1 level mapping throwing on unknown values, bundled microVM environments with Agenstra's image, probes from the new CP endpoint `GET /api/projects/:project/isolation-capabilities`, guide rewritten). Deviations accepted: no `vm-exec` wrapping in the manager (the node agent already rewrites execs into microVMs), compose keeps guest paths (the node agent prefixes mounts with `/guest`), image entrypoint used. **Coordinator decision**: microVM environments keep reserving their full guest memory (no safe overcommit); the CPU reservation becomes configurable (`LOADWEAVER_ENVIRONMENT_MICROVM_CPU_RESERVATION`, default = limit) — small follow-up (F2). Gate: W13 nested-KVM single-node run with all four Agenstra levels, `agenstra-runtime.integration` incl. the new endpoint, `--no-kvm` node → `disabled-by-admin`.

## M7 follow-ups F1 (2026-10-23)

- **Per-architecture microVM layers (CP)**:
  - `image-resolver.service.ts`: `inspectImage` split into `readTop` / `childFor` / `inspectManifest` (behaviour unchanged); new `inspectImageArchitectures(reader, ref, arches)` → `{ inspection, missing }`: one inspection per cluster architecture the image has (index children deduped by digest; a single-platform manifest's arch from its config), the first available one in `arches` order is the result (labels / process config) with `platformLayers` = every available arch's layers; throws when none matches. With ≤ 1 architecture it is exactly `inspectImage` (no `platformLayers`).
  - `microvm-planning.utils.ts`: `ImageInspection.platformLayers?`; `compileMicrovm` emits `microvm.platformLayers` (sorted keys) instead of `layers` when the inspection has them, else `layers` as before (single-arch clusters and stored N-1 inspections keep their spec hash; non-microVM workloads untouched). `imageArchitectures(inspection)` = `platformLayers` keys, else a VM image's arch, else the inspected platform's arch.
  - `plans.service.ts`: `workloadArches(nodes)` (every workload-node arch, amd64 first; unreported = amd64 as in `workloadArch`); `resolveDeployments` inspects microVM guest images for all of them (VMs stay single-arch artifacts on `workloadArch`) and warns `<image> has no linux/<arch> variant; its replicas avoid the <arch> nodes` (replaces the old "pinned for X" warning). When the plan pinned image inspections, the preview re-plans with them (`planner.plan(..., deploymentStates)`) and refuses unschedulable services; the apply re-plans with `entity.deploymentStates` the same way (the states are stored after the plan check).
  - Scheduler: `SchedulerNode.arch?`, `SchedulerService.architectures?`; hard eligibility stage after the selector (`runsArchitecture`; unknown node arch passes; replicas on a wrong-arch node move), reason `no eligible node (image architectures arm64: 0 of 1 node match — amd amd64)`. ## M7 W9: full VMs node side (2026-10-23)

- **Launcher wiring** (new `vm/vm-support.service.ts`, `VmSupport`; module provides W6's `VM_BLOCK_DEVICES` / `VM_LAUNCH_FILES` through it): before every start the VM's disks are promoted here in `vm.disks` order (boot disk through the image import), refused when a disk has no replica here or isn't `mode: block`; `vm.json` 0600 in the run dir from `vmLaunchConfig(spec, devices)` — validated with the launcher's own `parseVmLaunchConfig`, `guestAgent: true` always (the wire spec has no image `guestAgent`; the channel is harmless without an agent, backups fall back to crash-consistent), **one tap per NIC** `lwtap<n>` from W6's `guestNics` (final API, unchanged); then the cloud-init seed. Docker `destroy` events of VM launchers (`watch()`, called from `prepareHost`) demote the VM's disks (`<p>/lw-vm/<vm>.*`) unless a container of the replica exists or its disks were promoted < 2 min ago (a recreate's late destroy event); a still-open device (exit 11) stays primary.
- **Block volumes** (`volumes/volume.manager.ts`): `mount()` refuses `mode: block` (never `mkfs` / mounted on the host; the plugin's unmount skips them), `promoteBlock(id)` → `{ device: /dev/drbd<minor>, fresh }` (`fresh` = `initialiseIfNew` declared the never-written replicas current / force-promoted a new single replica), `demoteBlock`, `blockSizeBytes` (sysfs `/sys/block/drbdN/size`: a secondary can't be opened), `lvTags` / `setLvTags` (one `lvchange --deltag/--addtag`), `blockAssignments()`; the reconcile demotes a block volume whose primary moved elsewhere (`drbdadm secondary`, exit 11 ok). Device passthrough itself is W6's `blockDevices` → `HostConfig.Devices` `rw` (no `m`).
- **Image import** (new `vm/vm-image-import.ts`, `VmImageImporter`): on promotion of a boot disk with `initializeFrom`: LV tag `lw.init=<digest>` → done (also when the spec now pins another image: re-imaging is explicit only); no tag and **not fresh** → the disk holds data (failover / move): adopted (tag set, never overwritten); fresh or `lw.importing=<digest>` (interrupted import on this node) → import: tag `lw.importing` first (old init tags removed), layer fetched through `RegistryBlobSource` (router for private / mirrored repos; `privateRepositories` now includes `vm.image.ref`), **sha256 of the blob verified while streaming**, decompressed by magic (gzip / zstd), qcow2 by magic, **KubeVirt containerDisk** by tar header + checksum (first `/disk/*.qcow2|*.img` entry via W6's `readTar`, rest read for the digest), raw (`raw+zstd`) only for `raw` images; written sparse (1 MiB zero blocks skipped) into `/var/lib/loadweaver/vmimages/sha256/<hex>` (+ `<hex>.json`, `LOADWEAVER_VMIMAGE_DIR`), LRU GC (`LOADWEAVER_VMIMAGE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, default 15 % of the fs, holes don't count, stale staging removed), bounded by the disk size; then the launcher image in import mode (`BackupJobs.run`: `--network none`, no caps, read-only root, user 0, blob `:ro`, only `/dev/drbdN` `rw`): `qemu-img info --output=json -f <fmt>` (format matches, **no backing / data file**, virtual size ≤ DRBD device size), `qemu-img convert -n -f <fmt> -O raw -t none <blob> /dev/drbdN`; tags `lw.init=<digest>` (importing removed). In-flight sharing per digest / volume. Deviation from the design's "tag set on all replicas after the sync": peers can't tell a finished from an interrupted import, so the next primary adopts existing data at promotion instead; a primary crashing mid-import leaves a half-written disk on failover → operator re-images (`vmImageImport`), never an automatic overwrite of data. **Synchronous** in the reconcile (like image pulls): a large first import holds the workloads layer; status shows it (below).
- **cloud-init** (new `vm/cloud-init-seed.ts`, `CloudInitSeed`): `seed/` (0700) with `meta-data` (as sent), `user-data` (`#cloud-config\n` when absent: NoCloud wants both) and `network-config`: JSON parsed, `"${LW_DNS}"` in `nameservers.addresses` replaced by the pod bridge gateways (dropped when none), **`mtu` added per NIC** from the pod network's MTU option (W3 sends none); every `secret://` ref in user data substituted by token (unlisted refs refused — no literal leaks to the guest; `userDataSecret` = a user data that is just the ref works), values fetched through the `SecretBroker` for the replica, buffers zeroed; written only after `statfs` proves tmpfs (run dir under `/run/loadweaver`), files 0600 `wx`, rebuilt on every start, removed when the VM has no cloud-init; files > 1 MiB refused (as `seed-build`).
- **Power / status** (new `vm/vm-power.ts`, `VmPower`): `vmPower` → `docker exec <launcher> /usr/lib/agenstra-microvm/vm-ctl reboot|reset|shutdown` (VM must run here), `state` (virsh domstate → `running|paused|shutting-down|shut-off|crashed|suspended|unknown`), `fsfreeze` / `fsthaw` (60 s; failure = crash-consistent). `vmImageImport` (reimage): VM must not run, volume must be a disk of that replica, launcher image = the release pin (`launcherImage()`), the router serves the (unused) private repo only during the import (`RegistryRouter.withRepository`), disk demoted afterwards. Outcomes of both as `event` (source `storage`, labels `kind: virtual-machine`, `replica` / `action` / `import`, `result: running|done|failed`) — the protocol has no result message. **Protocol (agent → CP, optional)**: `workloadStatus.workloads[].vm { power?: VM_POWER_STATES, importing?: boolean }`; `VmSupport.annotate` adds the power of running launchers and a `pending` entry `vm.importing` for a boot disk being written; the CP stores it in `lw_workload_placements.status[node].vm` (`node-agents.service.ts`, entity type only, no migration). Capability `virtualMachines` = microVM level ready ∧ launcher present ∧ DRBD 9 (`host-info.service.ts`).
- **Backups** (`backups/backup.manager.ts`, block branch; `BackupJobs` gained `devices` / `user` / `readOnly`): running VM → `vm-ctl fsfreeze` right around `lvcreate` of the thin snapshot (thawed before `lvchange -ay`), `cryptsetup open --readonly` with the volume key, an **exact-size `dmsetup` linear view** (`<job>-disk`, DRBD's metadata at the LV end excluded), Kopia container with the view as its only device (`r`, no caps) `kopia snapshot create --stdin-file=<vm>.<disk>.raw /volume --json --parallel=4 … --tags=consistency:filesystem-frozen|crash < view` (redirect, not a pipe: a read error fails Kopia); report `files: 1`, `hooks: true` when frozen. Recovery removes `lw-bk-*-disk` views before closing mappings. Restore `kind: volume` of a block volume: launcher stopped (replica protected) and started again, or promoted + demoted for a stopped VM; `kopia show <root>/<vm>.<disk>.raw > /dev/drbdN` (device `rw`, peers follow through DRBD — no new LV / full resync needed); `kind: path` refused for VM disks; scratch restore tests unchanged (the disk file lands in the scratch ext4). Compression `zstd` is a repository policy (not set here).
- **CP backup scheduler** (small change, done): `volumeCandidates(placements, resources)` in `backup.utils.ts` — VM disks (`<p>/lw-vm/<vm>.<disk>`) carry the `VirtualMachine`'s labels + `loadweaver.com/vm: <vm>` as `deploymentLabels`; the scheduler loads `VirtualMachine` resources. Policies select VMs by labels (all disks together); hooks stay compose-only.

## M7 follow-ups F2 (2026-10-23)

- **Required host packages on existing nodes**: util-release `REQUIRED_HOST_PACKAGES` (= `MICROVM_HOST_PACKAGES`, `attr` / `e2fsprogs`; future host dependencies go here), rooted in `bundleAptRoots` and used by the installer (`lw_apt_install`, VM-lab `components.generated.sh` output unchanged). Node agent: `hostUpdateScript` gets `requiredPackages` (`name`, or `name=version` when the release pins one; names / versions checked against the safe patterns) — after `dist-upgrade` and the pin install, each one not `installed` per `dpkg-query` is installed with the agent's apt configuration only (the release's frozen snapshot: plan snapshot, or the bundle's on air-gapped clusters; never upstream); installed ones untouched; a package the snapshot lacks fails the step with `failed: required host packages …: not installable from the release's apt snapshot`. Runs on every host step (also without OS upgrade); drain / update / reboot rules unchanged, no reboot of its own (`rebootRequired` still kernel / flag only). `OsUpdateManager` passes the list; host facts now report the required packages' installed versions in `packages` too. CP: `componentDiff` lists missing required packages per node on host rollouts (`package:attr`, from `null` to `snapshot version`, method "installed from the cluster-local apt snapshot if missing (no reboot of its own)"); no gate / planner change. Docs: `host-requirements.md` "MicroVM packages" describes the behaviour (gap note removed).
- **Agenstra microVM CPU reservation**: `LOADWEAVER_ENVIRONMENT_MICROVM_CPU_RESERVATION` (default the CPU limit `LOADWEAVER_ENVIRONMENT_MICROVM_CPUS`; must be > 0 and ≤ the limit, else `loadweaverMicrovmSize` throws — read once in the `LoadweaverRuntime` constructor, so the manager fails at module init). Compose: `deploy.resources.reservations: { cpus: <reservation>, memory: <guest memory> }` next to the limits (memory fully reserved); `parseEnvironmentCompose` reads it back (`MicrovmEnvironmentSize.cpuReservation`; older composes without reservations → the limit). Manager compose sets it (`'2'`, comment), guide updated. **Planner check**: the CP uses reservations for capacity — util-compose `requests` = reservations, else limits; `microvmRequests` = CPU request + launcher overhead, memory = max(request, guest memory) + overhead; guest vCPUs from the limit (`microvmSizing`). No planner change needed.
- Tests (unit only): `required-host-packages.spec.ts` (rendered script with stubs: missing → installed from the snapshot, present → untouched, pinned spec, snapshot lacking a package → failed with reason, unsafe names, air-gapped bundle snapshot via `OsUpdateManager` without upgrade; `bash -n`), `apt-bundle.spec` (required packages rooted for every OS / arch), `rollout-planning.spec` (diff entries), `loadweaver.runtime.spec` (reservation emitted / parsed back, default = limit, invalid values incl. > limit refused, constructor throws). Node-agent `updates` 42, CP updates + install-script 40 + 41 (overlapping), util-release apt-bundle 14, Agenstra `runtime/loadweaver` 33 — all green; `tsc --noEmit` (lib + spec) for the four projects, eslint, prettier clean.
- Review of "M7 follow-ups F2": accepted (`REQUIRED_HOST_PACKAGES` installed from the frozen snapshot on every host step if missing, never upstream, no reboot; rollout diff lists missing packages; `LOADWEAVER_ENVIRONMENT_MICROVM_CPU_RESERVATION` validated at manager start, memory fully reserved, planner already uses reservations). Note: older agents show the packages as missing in the diff until they report them (cosmetic). Pending on the user: VM cloud-init secret refs (`secrets.service.ts` `valueForNode`) — hand-off prompt given.

## M7 W10: migration (2026-10-23)

- **CP eligibility** (`utils/migration-eligibility.utils.ts`): `MigrationMethod` + `vm-live`; `SessionRuntime` = wire `CheckpointRuntime` + `qemu` (CP only; the wire `checkpointRuntimeSchema` is unchanged); `overheadMs` keys `runc` 400 / `runsc` 2 000 / `runsc-kvm` 2 500 / `qemu` 300 (initial values, lab-measured later); `estimateFreeze(…, platform?)`: runc and qemu pre-copy (qemu + 2 MiB device state), runsc freezes the whole memory. Per level: runc → `live`; sandboxed → `stop-and-copy (gVisor)`; sandboxed-kvm → `stop-and-copy (gVisor KVM)` only when both nodes have `isolation-ladder`, `checkpoint.runscKvm` and `sandboxed-kvm` ready (`checkpointSupport(node, runtime, platform)`, reason "no gVisor KVM checkpoint support on X (restore must use the same platform)"); microvm → `chooseQemuMigration`: full VMs `vm-live (QEMU)` (both nodes `vm-migration` + `live-migration`, `host-passthrough` only between equal `cpuFlagsHash`, every disk with a sync replica on the target, freeze budget); generic microVMs `vm-live` only without filesystem volumes **and** with the S7 switch `LOADWEAVER_MICROVM_LIVE_MIGRATION=on` (default off: "virtio-fs state migration is not enabled for microVMs"); with filesystem volumes always short stop; bundled → fallback (user-mode network state); not yet inspected → fallback. New input `targetFeatures` (= `replicaAgentFeatures(service)`): a target lacking one → fallback. No cross-site licence gate exists in the eligibility code yet (nothing to reuse) — open for the BUSL split.
- **Planner** (`workload-planner.service.ts`): W3's interim `kvmLevelMigrationFallback` removed; `migrationLauncher(deployment, service, inspection)` (VM + CPU model / bundled / generic / unknown from the pinned image configs) and `targetFeatures` passed to `chooseMigrationMethod`. `vm-live` counts as a session method (`isCheckpointMethod`): addresses kept, running spec stored, `beginAttempt` runtime `qemu`.
- **CP sessions** (`utils/migration-state.utils.ts`): `SessionMethod` (`live | stop-and-copy | vm-live`); `sessionStep` for `vm-live`: prepare → precopy → (source `freeze` done, also straight from precopy) → restore → cut-over, no transfer phase; `precopyLimitMs` (`vmMaxSeconds` + 30 s) aborts a silent pre-copy. `sessionCommands` `vm-live` branch: `vmMigrationPrepare` (addresses, volumes, spec, token) → `vmMigrationStart` (downtime = freeze budget, `maxSeconds`, optional bandwidth) → `vmMigrationSwitchover` once a running pre-copy passes `vmSwitchoverAfterMs` (60 s) → nothing in freeze / restore (nodes report themselves) → `migrationCommit` both → abort target first, source per `sourceMayResume`. `sessionOptionsFromEnv` (`LOADWEAVER_VM_MIGRATION_MAX_SECONDS` 120, `…_SWITCHOVER_AFTER_MS`, `…_MAX_BANDWIDTH_BPS`). `migration-session.service.ts` sends `vm-live` sessions too; `migration-records.ts` / `workload-controller.service.ts`: session typing, `precopyLimitMs`, cut-over sets no `restored` for qemu (the target's launcher is a normal Docker container), fallback / queued `allocateOn(…, addressFamiliesOf(parsed))` (per-NIC layouts). Entities: `runtime` types widened (`qemu`); **no DB migration needed** (`lw_migrations.method` varchar(16), `runtime` varchar(8), no check constraints).
- **Node agent, QEMU live migration** (new `migration/vm-migration.service.ts`, `VmMigrationService`; `agent-connection.service.ts` routes `vmMigration*` and the commit / abort of sessions it `owns`; sessions persisted in `<state>/vm-migrations`, recovered at start with their disks held out of the reconcile):
  - target prepare: full VMs only (generic microVMs refused: S7); disks `drbdadm net-options --allow-two-primaries=yes`; marker `migration/incoming` in the run dir; `VmSupport.expectIncoming` (disks neither promoted nor image-initialised); `createReplica` on the kept addresses (extra NICs on `loadweaver-kept-<fam>-nic<n>` as before); transfer endpoint with a **relay** to the launcher's libvirt session socket (`/proc/<pid>/root/dev/shm/agenstra-microvm/vmm/run/libvirt/libvirt-sock`), disks promoted (`promoteForMigration`) on the first relay connection (the source allowed two primaries by then); input firewall for the source's WireGuard addresses; `restore` done once `vm-ctl state` = running.
  - source start: launcher running + VM spec; disks dual-primary; Docker restart policy `no` (a launcher whose domain left must never cold-boot it); `listenRelay` unix socket `migration/peer.sock` (owner 10930, 0600); `vm-ctl migrate /run/loadweaver/vm/migration/peer.sock <downtime> [MiB/s]`, `vm-ctl jobinfo` every second → `precopy` running (round = iteration, totalBytes = processed, dirty rate); over `maxSeconds` → `migrate-abort`, failed; done → `precopy` + `freeze` done (`freezeMs` = `domjobinfo --completed` total downtime). Switchover = `vm-ctl suspend`.
  - commit: source removes its launcher, demotes, ends the window; target removes the marker, `incomingDone`, ends the window (retried ≤ 2 min while the peer is still primary), committed grace. Abort: target closes the endpoint / relays, removes the launcher, demotes, ends the window; source `migrate-abort`, `resume` if paused, `resumed` = domain running, restart policy back only then, window closed once the target let go.
- **Transfer relay** (`transfer.service.ts` / `transfer-protocol.ts`): `hello { relay: true }` → `result { ok }` → raw bytes both ways (`pipeRelay`, backpressure, closed with the attempt), only on attempts opened with a `RelayTarget`; `connectRelay` / `listenRelay` on the source. Same mTLS node certificate + single-use token checks as batches.
- **DRBD** (`volume.manager.ts`): `setDualPrimary(id, allow)`, `holdDualPrimary`, `inDualPrimary`, `promoteForMigration` (only inside the window); the reconcile neither demotes nor `adjust`s a disk in the window (a pending adjust waits). `after-sb-*` unchanged (disconnect).
- **W9 hook** (`vm-support.service.ts`, targeted): `released()` skips replicas with an active migration session; incoming replicas get their DRBD device paths without promotion / import.
- **Launcher** (small additions, `apps/shared/microvm-launcher`): `launch-vm` incoming mode (marker present → no boot, polls until the domain exists; a restart while the marker exists waits again); `vm-ctl migrate | jobinfo | jobinfo-completed | migrate-abort | suspend | resume` (`virsh migrate --live --p2p --tunnelled --auto-converge --abort-on-error`, transient both ends, no storage copy). Run dir: writable `migration/` subdir bind-mounted for VM launchers (`workload-container.ts`, created 0711 in `prepareMicrovm`).
- **gVisor KVM platform parity**: `restored-runtime.ts` `sandboxRuntimeOf(runtimes, platform?)` (platform from `parseGvisorRuntimeArgs`, Netstack only, never falls back across platforms; without platform: any Netstack runtime for state / list / kill / exec), placeholder label `loadweaver.com/restored-platform` from the replica's runtime, restore with that platform's runtime; `checkpoint.manager.ts` records the source platform (runtime flags / restored label), refuses unknown platforms; `migration.service.ts` prewarms the spec's platform.
- **DNS**: `reconciler.service.ts` `keptHostRoutes` adds extra VM NICs' `hostRoutes` to the resolver clients. BIRD origination already covered every NIC's kept addresses (CP compiler `keptAddresses` per NIC, W3).
- **Protocol**: `vm-migration` → `agent: true` (versioning spec implemented list updated).
- **Tests** (unit only, `--maxWorkers=2`): CP lib 122 suites / 971 (eligibility +9 incl. per-level / VM / microVM / estimates, state +5 `vm-live`, planner isolation `migrationLauncher`); node agent 60 / 481+ (new `vm-migration.service.spec.ts` 10 with mocked virsh / docker / drbd, `migration.spec.ts` +2 real-TLS relay round trip / refusal, restored platform tests, volumes dual-primary window, vm-support migrating skip + incoming, container `migration` mount, `keptHostRoutes`); util-agent-protocol 5 / 65 (+1 skipped). `tsc --noEmit` clean: CP lib + spec + app, node-agent lib + spec + app, util-agent-protocol spec. ESLint 0 errors, Prettier applied; `bash -n` on `launch-vm` / `vm-ctl` (no shellcheck installed).
- **For the gate (VM lab, spikes)**: **S4** — libvirt tunnelled p2p between two session daemons through the relay (does a session libvirtd accept the agent's uid-0 connection on its socket via `/proc/<pid>/root`? else relay through `docker exec … setpriv` as 10930, or the QMP `migrate unix:` alternative); `virsh migrate` from the source launcher to `qemu+unix:///session?socket=…`; nvram from template on the target; seed image + taps + DRBD minors identical on both ends. **S7** — virtio-fs `--migration-mode` + bridge daemon re-attach for generic microVMs (until then CP switch off and the agent refuses). VM lab cases: VM with two NICs + 2 disks migrated under load (kept addresses per NIC, DNS + BIRD routes on the target, ARP / NA announce), freeze vs budget, forced switch-over, `maxSeconds` abort → short stop, abort before / after QEMU switch-over (source resumes / short stop, never two running guests), agent killed mid-migration on either side (relay dies → abort; recovered sessions keep the window), dual-primary window closing order (target demotes, source `net-options no` retry), `drbdadm adjust` deferred while dual-primary, `host-passthrough` between unequal CPUs → short stop, gVisor-KVM checkpoint / restore between two KVM nodes and refusal toward a systrap-only node. Measure `overheadMs.qemu` / `runsc-kvm`.

Deviations accepted: generic microVM live migration behind `LOADWEAVER_MICROVM_LIVE_MIGRATION` (default off) until spike S7 proves virtio-fs migration; no runtime cross-site licence check (BUSL is a licence term, existing live migration has none either). - **User decision (2026-10-23): generic microVMs live-migrate like other workloads** — W10's opt-in switch is removed; W10b implements `microvm-live (QEMU)`: lower layers prepared on the target, writable upper pre-copied and synced in the freeze, virtiofsd migration mode + QEMU vhost-user-fs migration, filesystem volumes switched during the freeze (never dual-mounted), bridge re-attach; fallback to short stop only when a node lacks the capability. Spike S7 validates it in the gate.

## M7 follow-ups F3b: background boot-disk import, explicit VM command fields (2026-10-23)

- **Background boot-disk import** (node agent): new `vm/boot-disk-imports.ts` (`BootDiskImports`, owned by `VmSupport`). The reconcile only decides: `VmImageImporter.prepareBootDisk` promotes and, when an import is needed, marks `lw.importing=<digest>` **before** the job is queued (an agent restart before the job ran repeats the import instead of adopting an empty disk); then a job per disk is queued and `WorkloadDeferred` thrown. `WorkloadManager.applyNow` catches `WorkloadDeferred` per replica (other workloads go on, no isolation start failure recorded; any other error still fails the apply as before). Concurrency per node `LOADWEAVER_VM_IMPORT_CONCURRENCY` (default 2, 1–16), one job per disk (later reconciles observe it; a recreate with a new spec hash keeps it). The boot disk is handled first (nothing else promoted while it is written), devices still in `vm.disks` order. Done → job dropped (disk says `lw.init`), event, `onSettled` → `WorkloadManager.reapply()` starts the launcher. Failed → event (`error`), status `failed` with the reason, retry with backoff (1 min doubling, max 30 min); before the retry the reconcile gets the reason. Cancellation via the new hook `VM_DISK_JOBS.desired(workloads)` (called every apply): replica no longer wants the disk here (VM deleted / stopped / placement moved), volume assignment gone, or `initializeFrom` digest changed → queued jobs dropped, running ones aborted (`AbortSignal` → the `qemu-img` container is killed; a shared layer download continues for the cache), disk demoted once the write stopped (not when the volume is gone). `released()` skips replicas whose import holds the disk; `vmImageImport` (reimage) is refused while the first import of that disk runs. W9 semantics kept: `lw.init` never overwritten, adopt-on-failover unchanged (a move mid-import leaves a half-written disk the next primary adopts — same as W9's mid-import crash, re-image by the operator). W10 intact: incoming replicas return their devices before any import; migrating-source skip unchanged.
- **Progress**: `BackupJobs.run` gained `signal` (kill + remove, rejects with the reason) and `progress` (stdout polled every `intervalMs`); `qemu-img convert -p`, `convertProgress` parses the last `(x/100%)`; `writeDiskFile` `onBytes` (blob bytes). Protocol `workloadStatus.workloads[].vm.importProgress { phase: queued|fetching|writing|failed, bytes?, totalBytes? }` (`vmImportProgressSchema`, `VM_IMPORT_PHASES`); `importing` kept. `VmSupport.annotate` replaces a stopped launcher's entry / adds one: `pending` + message ("writing the boot disk from the VM image (512 MiB of 2048 MiB)") + `vm.importing: true` + progress, or `failed` + reason + `importProgress.phase: failed`. CP: entity / view types, `VirtualMachineDto.status.importProgress` (nullable) + OpenAPI; phase logic unchanged (`importing` → `Importing`, `failed` → `Failed`). Events of the job: labels `kind: virtual-machine`, `replica`, `volume`, `operation: boot-disk-import`, `result: running|done|failed|cancelled` (no command fields → never folded into `lw_vm_commands`).
- **Explicit command fields**: protocol `agentEventSchema.vmCommand { type, action?, importId? }` (optional, strings bounded, unknown keys refused). Agent: every `vmPower` / `vmImageImport` outcome event carries it; failures additionally label `action` (only a valid power action; an invalid one is the reason) / `import`. - **Docs**: `docs/loadweaver/features/virtual-machines.md` boot-disk paragraph (background, progress, failure / retry, cancellation, restart) + `LOADWEAVER_VM_IMPORT_CONCURRENCY` row.

## M7 W10b: microVM live migration (2026-10-23)

- **CP eligibility** (`utils/migration-eligibility.utils.ts`): `LOADWEAVER_MICROVM_LIVE_MIGRATION` / `microvmLiveMigration` removed (no hidden flag). Generic microVMs — with or without filesystem volumes — use the existing session method `vm-live` (same phases / commands; the node tells VM and microVM apart by the spec) with the plan label **`microvm-live (QEMU)`** (full VMs keep `vm-live (QEMU)`), when both nodes have `vm-migration` + `live-migration` and the new capability **`microvmMigration`**; otherwise short stop / blue-green with `no microVM live migration on <node> (its launcher needs virtio-fs state migration: QEMU 10.0+, virtiofsd 1.13+)`. Bundled: only when the image's launcher label `io.forepath.microvm.migration` lists `bundled` (planner `migrationLauncher` → `{ kind: 'bundled', migration }`, `bundledMicrovmMigration`; the `generic,vm` inherited from the launcher base doesn't count — Agenstra's `launch` has no incoming mode, so today: fallback). Estimate: QEMU's + `microvmSyncMs` (250) + `volumeHandoverMs` (400) per filesystem volume; a microVM's tmpfs counts like memory (pre-copied), runc / runsc unchanged. Console `PlanChange.method` gains `vm-live` (pre-existing gap).
- **Capability** (node agent): launcher image labels `io.forepath.microvm.migration=generic,vm`, `…qemu-version`, `…virtiofsd-version` (Dockerfile, from the pinned package ARGs); `IsolationProbeService` reads them after the boot probe (`docker image inspect --format {{json .Config.Labels}}`) → `capabilities.microvm.migration { generic, modes, qemu, virtiofsd }` (`microvm/microvm-migration.ts`: `generic` = mode `generic` + QEMU >= 10.0 + virtiofsd >= 1.13) → `capabilities.microvmMigration` = microVM level ready && generic. Protocol: both fields optional in `nodeCapabilitiesSchema`. Smoke test checks `virtiofsd --help` lists `--migration-mode`.
- **Why QMP instead of libvirt p2p for microVMs**: the writable layer's last changes and the volume hand-over must happen after the guest stopped but **before** the virtio-fs device state reaches the target (its virtiofsd opens every path the guest knows when it loads the state). QEMU's `pause-before-switchover` gives exactly that window, but libvirt enables and continues it itself (no hook). So `vm-ctl qmp-migrate` drives QEMU through `virsh qemu-monitor-command` (caps `pause-before-switchover` + `auto-converge`, `downtime-limit`, `max-bandwidth`, `migrate unix:<peer.sock>`); `migrate-status` (query-migrate), `migrate-continue`, `migrate-cancel`, `fs-release`. Target: `launch-generic` with the marker `migration/incoming` creates the domain `--paused` with `<qemu:commandline>-incoming defer` and `migrate-incoming unix:/dev/shm/agenstra-microvm/vmm/incoming.sock`; the agent's endpoint relays to that socket (`launcherIncomingSocket`), the agent resumes the guest once query-migrate says `completed`, then the launcher starts the bridge daemon with `--resync`. All vhost-user-fs devices get `migration=internal` (`<qemu:override>`, user aliases `ua-guestroot` / `ua-lwtools` / `ua-lwvols`); every virtiofsd `--migration-mode=find-paths --migration-on-error=abort` (root also `--migration-confirm-paths`: the host file browser writes there).
- **Writable layer + tmpfs (upper-copy approach)**: **file-level iterative passes** (`microvm/guest-sync.ts`), not `thin_delta` / snapshot diffs. Reasons: (1) the target's overlay must be mounted before its launcher starts (virtiofsd chroots into `/guest` at start; a later mount isn't seen), and an overlay's upper must not change underneath a mounted overlay — so the target applies passes **through its merged directory** (whiteouts → deletions, opaque directories → lower entries removed), which a block copy can't; (2) it works for both W6 writable-layer backends (thin LV and the loop-file fallback), `thin_delta` only for thin LVs and only with metadata snapshots + LV snapshots of a mounted ext4; (3) uppers are small and the passes reuse the mTLS batch transfer; tmpfs volumes (host tmpfs in the launcher) use the same code. Pass = lstat signature (kind, mode, uid, gid, size, mtime/ctime ns, inode) vs. the target's last confirmed manifest; changed entries as a pax tar (owner, mode, mtime, `user.*` / `security.capability` via one `getfattr` per directory, hard links, FIFOs; devices / sockets skipped), deletions as the topmost removed path. Safety: the source walks with directory descriptors (`/proc/<pid>/fd/<n>/<name>`, `O_NOFOLLOW`, inode re-checked after open, a swapped entry is resent next pass); the target refuses anything below a non-directory and replaces links instead of following; peer metadata validated (`parsePassMeta`); > 500 000 entries or non-UTF-8 names fail the attempt (→ short stop). Up to 4 passes while the guest runs (until one is ≤ 8 MiB), the last one in the freeze. Lower layers: the target's `createReplica` → `prepareMicrovm` unpacks them from the registry (diffID-verified, W6) before the endpoint opens.
- **Freeze (source, `VmMigrationService.migrateMicrovm`)**: guest passes → `qmp-migrate` → poll (100 ms) until `pre-switchover` (guest stopped) → final pass `guest-final` (target applies before answering: new `RelayTarget.onBatch`) → with volumes: relay **gate** (`listenRelay` → `gate(2 GiB)` / `release()` / `held()`, new `pipeGatedRelay`: holds QEMU's last bytes, ends the remote side gracefully only after everything went out) → `migrate-continue` → `completed` (all of QEMU's state in the relay) → `fs-release` (volumes' virtiofsd ends) → per volume unmount the `/lwvol/<i>` bind (propagates into the launcher, fails while held) + `VolumeManager.releaseForMigration` (umount + strict `drbdadm secondary`) → batch `handover` (target: `takeOverForMigration` = `drbdadm primary` + mount + bind into its `/lwvol/<i>`, propagates into the running incoming launcher) → gate released → `completed` → `precopy` / `freeze` done (`freezeMs` = max(QEMU downtime, measured)). Target resumes on `completed`, reports `restore`.
- **Filesystem volumes of generic microVMs** (contract change, needed for the single-primary hand-over: the image root's virtiofsd used to hold volume files through `--announce-submounts`): no Docker volume mounts below `/guest` any more. New `microvm/guest-volumes.ts` (`GuestVolumes`): per-replica tmpfs dir `<runtime>/vmvol/<key>` bind-mounted onto itself + `--make-shared`, bound `rslave` at `/lwvol` in the launcher; each volume promoted + mounted by `VolumeManager.mount` (CP primary rule as the plugin did) and bound to `<dir>/<index>` (`remount,bind,ro` for read-only); released with the replica (unmount + secondary; never deletes through a remaining mount). `launch-generic`: a third virtiofsd for `/lwvol` (pid file for `fs-release`), tag `lwvols`; `volumes.cmdline` from the agent (`lw.vol=<index>:<hex target>:<ro|rw>`, validated) on the kernel command line; `initramfs-init-generic` mounts `lwvols` at `/lwvols` (outside the workload root) and binds each index to `/newroot<target>` (ro remount). Migration target: `WorkloadManager.expectIncoming` → directory without volumes. `VolumeManager`: `holdForMigration` / `endMigrationHold` / `inMigration` (no `adjust` meanwhile), `releaseForMigration`, `takeOverForMigration` (only inside a hold).
- **Abort**: before the hand-over → `migrate-cancel` (QEMU restarts the vCPUs; a forced switch-over's pause is resumed as before), `resumed: true`. After the volumes' virtiofsd went → `resumed: false` (can't continue there), volumes the target never confirmed are mounted again on the source (retried ≤ 2 min until the target demoted), the CP's short stop takes over. Target abort: launcher removed (its taken-over volumes unmounted + demoted, its writable layer discarded), marker, holds released. Commit: source closes the replica's live sessions (`LiveSessionsService.closeReplicaSessions` → `execExit { error: 'replica migrated to <node>' }` / `tunnelClose { reason }`), `vm-ctl destroy`, launcher + writable layer removed; target `incomingDone`. No dual-primary window and no `settle` for microVM sessions.
- **Bridge re-attach** (shared bridge lib, protocol stays 1, additive): the target's daemon connects only after the guest runs there, so the guest's port reports the disconnect (`PORT_OPEN 0`, reads return EOF); `bin/guest.ts` re-reads the port (200 ms) and, after an established session ended (`PortAttachment`), calls `GuestAgent.reattach()`: exec sessions hung up (SIGHUP), TCP streams closed, fresh `FrameConnection`, workload output on a fresh window (paused sources resumed), raw `MICROVM_RESYNC_MARKER` + `HELLO { version, running: true }`. Host daemon `--resync` (`HostDaemonOptions.resync`): skips bytes until the marker (a frame torn by the switch-over can't desync it), `HELLO { running: true }` → ready without BOOT, a protocol error → looks for the marker again; `bin/host.ts` reconnects to the guest port when no marker arrived within 10 s (forces the PORT_OPEN toggle). Workload output still in the old daemon's queue is lost (bytes, not the stream).
- **Files**: CP `utils/migration-eligibility.utils.ts`, `utils/microvm-planning.utils.ts`, `services/workload-planner.service.ts`, `utils/migration-state.utils.ts` / `utils/workload-planning.utils.ts` (doc texts); node agent `microvm/{guest-sync,guest-volumes,microvm-migration}.ts` (new), `migration/{vm-migration.service,transfer.service}.ts`, `volumes/volume.manager.ts`, `workloads/{workload-container,workload.manager}.ts`, `live/live-sessions.service.ts`, `host/{isolation-probe,host-info}.service.ts`, `node-agent.module.ts`; protocol `messages.ts` (capabilities); bridge `constants.ts`, `host-daemon.ts`, `guest-agent.ts`, `port-attachment.ts` (new), `bin/{guest,host}.ts`; launcher `launch-generic`, `vm-ctl`, `initramfs-init-generic`, `Dockerfile` (labels), `scripts/image-smoke-test.sh`; console `plans.types.ts`; docs `features/{migration,isolation-levels,virtual-machines}.md`; decision-log row in `loadweaver.md`. Not touched: F3b / W13 files, secrets, `.npmrc`, `rootfs-cache.ts` (its `replicaPaths` / layer preparation reused as is).
- **Tests** (unit only, `--maxWorkers=2`): node-agent lib 64 suites / 514 (new `guest-sync.spec.ts` 7: full / incremental / deletion / dir→file passes, opaque dirs, no link following either side, peer meta validation, getfattr parsing, tar round trip through `readTar`, launcher support labels; new `guest-volumes.spec.ts` 2; `vm-migration.service.spec.ts` +5 generic: QMP parsing, target incoming + pass through merged + hand-over + resume, source freeze ordering (final pass and gate before continue, fs-release → detach → hand-over → release), abort before / during the hand-over; `migration.spec.ts` +1 real-TLS gate + `onBatch`; volumes, workload-container (+1), workload.manager (+1), live-sessions (+1), isolation-probe, host-info); CP lib 124 / 985 (eligibility rewritten for microVMs + tmpfs estimate + no switch; planner bundled flag); util-agent-protocol 5 / 66; bridge 10 / 73 (new `reattach.spec.ts` 4). `tsc --noEmit` clean: node-agent lib + spec + app, CP lib + spec + app, protocol lib + spec, bridge lib + spec, data-access-console lib. ESLint 0 errors (one pre-existing non-null warning in `workload-planner.isolation.spec.ts`), Prettier applied; `bash -n` launch-generic / vm-ctl / launch-vm / smoke test, `sh -n` initramfs-init-generic (dash; the hex decoder checked in dash, busybox in the gate). No shellcheck installed.
- **For the gate (spike S7 + VM lab; W13 not finished, so not written into lab specs)**: S7 — QEMU 10.0.13 vhost-user-fs `migration=internal` via `<qemu:override>` accepted by libvirt 11.3; virtiofsd 1.13.2 `--migration-mode=find-paths` round trip incl. `--announce-submounts` and an overlay root; libvirt tolerating QMP-driven `migrate` / `migrate-incoming` (domain states paused / postmigrate, `virsh resume` after an incoming migration, `-incoming defer` through `<qemu:commandline>` with `create --paused`); `pause-before-switchover` reached with auto-converge; guest virtio-serial `PORT_OPEN 0` → EOF → re-attach (and the 10 s reconnect fallback); `rslave` propagation of `/lwvol/<i>` mounts into a running launcher and into the volumes virtiofsd's chroot; the unmount failing while virtiofsd still holds a volume; busybox `printf` octal decode in the initramfs. Lab cases: generic microVM (nginx / postgres image) migrated under load with writes to the writable layer during pre-copy and in the last second (content + deletions + whiteouts + opaque dirs + setuid / capabilities on the target), tmpfs volume content kept, filesystem volume hand-over (never mounted on both nodes: check `drbdadm status` roles over time), open TCP connection survives, `vm-exec` / terminal on the source ends with "replica migrated", new exec on the target, stats continue; abort before the hand-over (guest resumes on the source), abort during the hand-over (short stop, volume mounted again), agent killed mid-freeze either side; fallback toward a node with an older launcher (`microvmMigration: false`); a bundled Agenstra microVM → short stop / blue-green; measure `microvmSyncMs` / `volumeHandoverMs` and the gate's held bytes.
- Review of "M7 W10b": accepted (`microvm-live (QEMU)` driven by the source over QMP with `pause-before-switchover`, file-level writable-layer passes through the target's merged dir, volumes via a separate virtiofsd at `/lwvol` with single-primary hand-over in the freeze, abort paths, bridge re-attach with resync marker, `microvmMigration` capability from launcher labels, switch removed).
