## M7 follow-ups F5: live migration of bundled (Agenstra) microVMs (2026-10-23)

- **Bundled launcher** (`apps/shared/microvm-launcher/rootfs/usr/lib/agenstra-microvm/launch`, additive): new **migration mode** only with `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_MIGRATION=1` (set by the Loadweaver node agent, never by the agent manager; any other value refuses with 125). In it: root virtiofsd with `--migration-mode=find-paths --migration-on-error=abort --migration-confirm-paths`; domain with the `qemu` namespace, alias `ua-guestroot` and `<qemu:override>` `migration=internal`; `domain.name` written for `vm-ctl`; `/run/loadweaver/vm/migration` allowed in the mount check (without the flag such a mount still refuses the start). **Incoming mode** = migration mode + marker `/run/loadweaver/vm/migration/incoming`: `create --paused` with `-incoming defer`, QMP `migrate-incoming unix:/dev/shm/agenstra-microvm/vmm/incoming.sock` (same socket as `launch-generic`, so `launcherIncomingSocket` is reused), waits ≤ `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_INCOMING_WAIT` (3600 s) until the agent resumed the domain, then the bridge daemon with `--resync`. Without the flag the script's commands are identical (empty arrays / strings; the domain XML differs by one blank line); QEMU user networking unchanged. Rendered XML checked well-formed for all four flag combinations. `vm-ctl` comment only.
- **Labels**: launcher `Dockerfile` `io.forepath.microvm.migration="generic,vm,bundled"` (inherited by Agenstra's worker-microvm image, which keeps `launch` as entrypoint; a bundled image replacing the launcher script must override the label — noted in the Dockerfile). Smoke test greps `launch` for the migration / incoming mode. Bridge `constants.ts` doc updated.
- **CP** (`migration-eligibility.utils.ts`): bundled with `migration: true` (planner `bundledMicrovmMigration`, unchanged) now needs both nodes' new capability **`microvmBundledMigration`** (instead of `microvmMigration`, which describes the node's launcher; bundled images bring their own) + `vm-migration` / `live-migration`; plan label **`microvm-live (QEMU; guest connections reset: user-mode networking)`** (`BUNDLED_MICROVM_LIVE_LABEL`; the requested wording kept inside the existing method-label scheme). Old images: `bundled microVM: its launcher has no live migration (image built before the incoming mode; label io.forepath.microvm.migration without bundled)`; agent / level missing: `no bundled microVM live migration on <node> (agent or microVM level)`. **Fix found on the way**: generic and bundled microVM launchers boot with `host-passthrough` too, so the `cpuFlagsHash` equality check now applies to every microVM (W10b only checked full VMs with `host-passthrough`).
- **Protocol / capability**: `nodeCapabilitiesSchema.microvmBundledMigration` (optional boolean); `host-info.service.ts` reports it = microVM level ready (agents without F5 don't send it → fallback). No workload-spec change: the node decides the migration mode from the pulled image's labels (`bundledMigrationSupported` in `microvm-migration.ts`: `bundled` mode + QEMU ≥ 10.0 + virtiofsd ≥ 1.13), so older agents never see a new strict field and older bundled images keep running exactly as before.
- **Node agent, launcher options** (`workload-container.ts`): `MicrovmHostSide.bundledMigration`; bundled in migration mode get `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_MIGRATION=1`, only `<runDir>/migration` bound at `/run/loadweaver/vm/migration` (rw; nothing else of the run dir), and **filesystem volumes as agent mounts**: per volume `bind <vmvol>/<index>` → `/guest<target>`, `ReadOnly` per volume, propagation `rslave` (no Docker volume mounts; tmpfs / secrets / binds below `/guest` unchanged). `workload.manager.ts` `prepareBundled` (via `prepareMicrovm(…, image)`, image = pulled reference / `current.Image` on restarts): label check; migration mode → run dir + `migration/`, `GuestVolumes.prepareDir` + `attach` (not on an incoming target), `volumes.json`; old image as an incoming target → refused (`… has no live migration (no incoming mode)`), so a target never cold-boots a second guest. `remove` releases bundled volumes from `volumes.json` (no rootfs release).
- **Node agent, migration** (`vm-migration.service.ts`): `LauncherKind` `bundled`; every generic microVM branch is now "microVM" (`isMicrovm`), kind from the spec (`launcherKindOfSpec`). Differences for bundled: (1) **guest root** = the launcher's `/guest`: the source scans `guest/` of the launcher container's overlay upper (from `/proc/<pid>/mountinfo`, Docker's `GraphDriver.UpperDir` as fallback; no `guest/` yet = nothing to send), the target applies through `/proc/<pid>/root/guest` of its incoming launcher; both sides leave the launchers' mount points out (`guestMountPoints(inspect.Mounts)` → new `exclude` option of `scanPass` / `applyPass` in `guest-sync.ts`: no entry at / below a mount point is scanned or written, nothing holding one is deleted, replaced or emptied by an opaque dir — otherwise a pass would overwrite secrets / volume roots through their mounts). tmpfs volumes as for generic. (2) **Volume hand-over**: the image root's virtiofsd holds the volume files (and after a Docker-driven restart the launcher may bind a volume mount directly), so instead of `fs-release` the source **kills its launcher** once QEMU reported `completed` (state already in the gated relay; the restart policy is `no` since the start), then detach (`umount` + strict secondary) → hand-over → gate released; the earlier `completed` result is reused (the dead launcher can't answer). Target: `takeOverForMigration` + mount at `<vmvol>/<index>` propagates into the running incoming launcher (rslave); read-only volumes are additionally remounted `ro` inside the launcher's mount namespace (`nsenter -t <pid> -m mount -o remount,bind,ro /guest<target>`; a host remount doesn't propagate). (3) The source refuses a bundled launcher not started in migration mode (container env lacks `AGENSTRA_MICROVM_MIGRATION=1`, e.g. created before the image update) → precopy failed → CP short stop. Commit / abort / resume / bridge re-attach as W10b (an abort after the kill: `resumed: false`, volumes re-taken, short stop). `procDir` injectable (tests).
- **Networking limitation** (documented): QEMU user-mode network (slirp) state stays in the source launcher → the guest's open TCP connections are reset (forwarded OpenCode / VNC connections end with the bridge re-attach as for generic microVMs; outbound slirp connections break); processes, memory, files and the service address survive.

- **Files**: launcher `launch`, `vm-ctl` (comment), `Dockerfile`, `scripts/image-smoke-test.sh`; bridge `constants.ts` (doc); protocol `messages.ts`; CP `utils/migration-eligibility.utils.ts` (+ spec), `utils/microvm-planning.utils.ts` (doc); node agent `migration/vm-migration.service.ts` (+ spec), `microvm/guest-sync.ts` (+ spec), `microvm/microvm-migration.ts`, `workloads/workload-container.ts` (+ spec), `workloads/workload.manager.ts` (+ spec), `host/host-info.service.ts` (+ spec); docs above. Not touched: W13 files (`util-vm-lab`, lab specs), secrets, `.npmrc`, Agenstra code (behaviour on Docker hosts unchanged).

- **For the gate (S7-bundled, VM lab; not written into W13's lab specs)**: spike — QEMU 10.0.13 migrates a domain with `<interface type='user'>` (slirp vmstate) + vhost-user-fs `migration=internal` on a non-announce-submounts root virtiofsd with Docker submounts below `/guest`; the target's libvirt-generated user-net MAC vs the migrated virtio-net state; `rslave` bind of an **empty** `<vmvol>/<i>` at `/guest/app` receives the later host mount (mount onto the bind's root) inside a running launcher and inside the root virtiofsd's chroot; `nsenter` ro remount of the propagated mount; overlay upper path from `/proc/<pid>/mountinfo` with Docker 29's containerd snapshotter. Lab cases: Agenstra microVM environment on a 2-node cluster migrated under load (agent writing in `/app` and below `/guest/root`, a long-running process keeps its PID / memory, OpenCode answers on the service address afterwards, workspace volume never mounted on both nodes — `drbdadm status` over time, files changed in the last second present, secret env file untouched), plan shows `microvm-live (QEMU; guest connections reset: user-mode networking)`, an outbound guest TCP connection is reset and re-established, open `vm-exec` / terminal ends with "replica migrated", new exec on the target works; read-only volume stays read-only on the target; abort before the hand-over (guest continues on the source), abort after the kill (short stop, volume back on the source), agent killed mid-freeze on either side; fallbacks: image built on the W10b launcher (`generic,vm`) → short stop / blue-green, target agent without `microvmBundledMigration` → fallback, launcher created before the image update (no migration env) → precopy failed → short stop; a bundled microVM between nodes with different CPU flags → fallback (CPU reason); Agenstra on plain Docker (`microvm.isolation-lab.spec.ts`) unchanged. - **Boot checks** (users mode, isolated compose projects `g2boot-cp` / `g2boot-fleet` from the apps' compose files with an override: no container names, no host ports, `mem_limit` 2g / 512m / 256m / 128m, `restart: no`; the user's `loadweaver-control-plane-*` / `loadweaver-fleet-*` containers untouched; `down -v` afterwards): CP "Nest application successfully started", 59 / 59 migrations on an empty DB, `/api/health` 200, no error / warn lines, 270 MiB; fleet started, 14 migrations, `/api/health` 200, 192 MiB.
- **Fixes**:
  - **Launcher arm64 build was empty (release bug)**: the Dockerfile's `ARG QEMU_VERSION` is an environment variable of every `RUN`, and qemu-user (binfmt, the arm64 stages of the multi-arch release build) reads `QEMU_VERSION` as its `-version` option → every stage-1 `RUN` printed "qemu-aarch64 version 10.2.3" and exited 0; the image (101 MB) had no QEMU / libvirt / kernel / initramfs, the build was green. Renamed to `PKG_QEMU_VERSION` (comment: never name a build argument `QEMU_*`); the label `io.forepath.microvm.qemu-version` keeps its name and value. Smoke test now asserts the label is set and equals the installed `qemu-utils` version (caught the broken image, rc 1) and runs its container with `--memory 1g`. No other Dockerfile uses a `QEMU_*` build argument.
  - **Control plane hung on boot after the `APT_SNAPSHOT_READER` fix**: the import cycle was gone, but `InstallService` still constructor-injected the reader (`useExisting: AptSnapshotService`), and `AptSnapshotService → ArtifactStore → ObjectStoreControllerService → NetworkStateService → InstallService` closes a DI cycle — Nest waits forever (last log `UsersAuthModule dependencies initialized`, event loop idle; the old `dr-lab` image booted). `InstallService` now looks the reader up at render time via `ModuleRef.get(APT_SNAPSHOT_READER, { strict: false })` (null-safe, warning on failure unchanged). New `services/install.service.spec.ts` (Nest testing module with a reader that injects `InstallService`: compiles within 5 s and `script()` reads the snapshot; without a reader / failing reader still renders; fails with the old constructor injection) and guard **`no-injection-cycles.spec.ts`** (constructor-injection graph incl. `@Inject(TOKEN)` and `useExisting` / `useClass` aliases over the CP, fleet and node-agent libs, Tarjan SCC; parser self-check; proven to report exactly `APT_SNAPSHOT_READER, AptSnapshotService, ArtifactStore, InstallService, NetworkStateService, ObjectStoreControllerService` on the old code). `apt-snapshot-reader.ts` doc updated.
  - **CP integration specs would not type-check** (ts-jest uses `apps/loadweaver/backend-control-plane/tsconfig.spec.json`, which compiles node-agent sources pulled in by the integration specs with the base `target: es2015` and non-strict): BigInt literals in `guest-sync.ts` (TS2737) and `!probe.ok` not narrowing `MicrovmProbeResult` without `strictNullChecks` (TS2339 in `isolation-probe.service.ts`). Fixed: CP spec tsconfig `target: es2022` (as the node-agent lib), `probe.ok === false` (narrows in both modes). Would have failed the G4 CP integration run.
  - **Flaky unit test** `workload.manager.spec.ts` "defers a VM whose boot disk is being imported…" (fixed 20 ms sleep before asserting the background re-apply; failed once under parallel load) → polls up to 2 s for the third `createContainer`.
- **Files**: `apps/shared/microvm-launcher/Dockerfile`, `apps/shared/microvm-launcher/scripts/image-smoke-test.sh`, `libs/domains/loadweaver/backend/feature-control-plane/src/lib/services/install.service.ts` (+ new `install.service.spec.ts`), `…/feature-control-plane/src/lib/no-injection-cycles.spec.ts` (new), `…/feature-control-plane/src/lib/updates/apt-snapshot-reader.ts` (doc), `apps/loadweaver/backend-control-plane/tsconfig.spec.json`, `libs/domains/loadweaver/backend/feature-node-agent/src/lib/host/isolation-probe.service.ts`, `…/feature-node-agent/src/lib/workloads/workload.manager.spec.ts`, `graph/graph.json`. No commits; secrets controller / service and `.npmrc` not touched.
- **Cleanup**: boot-check stacks + volumes removed; the arm64 launcher, superseded images (first launcher build, old worker-microvm / old `dr-lab` `5ee0122e08e5`, old lab microVM image, old docs image) and the Trivy cache volume removed; kept: pinned Trivy image, golden volumes, the images in the table. `e6ba7a2deae8` (an earlier CP build) stays: a container of the user's stack uses it.
- **Open points**:
  - The user's running CP stack still uses an image without the DI fix → rebuild / recreate (`nx run loadweaver-backend-control-plane:api-container-image`, then `start-containers`); building with the `test` configuration retags `ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-control-plane-api:latest` (also done here).
  - arm64 verified only under QEMU emulation (build + smoke test); the real `release` push (`--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64`) runs in CI. The arm64 build takes ~9 min under emulation here.
  - Image builds themselves (BuildKit) run without a memory limit (not a container we start); all containers started in G2 had `--memory` / `mem_limit`.
  - Docs build: the SSR prerender logs "Failed to load navigation" (build-time fetch of `http://ng-localhost/assets/docs/navigation.json`, shared `feature-docs`, from main); the served pages render the sidebar — harmless, noted for G6.
  - Catalog staleness from main (files not touched by this branch): Agenstra console catalog lacks 13 ids used in `feature-agent-console` (e.g. `featureChat-renameChatSessionAria`), Decabill billing console lacks `featureProjectDetail-targetTime`, shared docs lacks `featureDocsLayout-brandAlt` → `extract-i18n` for those apps in G6.

Inside the Debian 13 cloud-kernel lab VMs (`-cpu host`) `/dev/kvm` exists and works: microVMs, full VMs (UEFI) and gVisor's KVM platform all run at three levels (Hyper-V → WSL → lab VM → guest). No fallback mode needed. Host MemAvailable stayed ≥ 6.9 GiB (S5 with three levels running), watchdog never fired.

- **Files changed**:

## M7 follow-up F6: guest OOM priority for the bridge agent (2026-10-24)

- **What**: from G3 open point 1 (S10). A workload filling the guest's RAM could get the bridge agent OOM-killed (largest RSS) → guest powers off, container exits 255 instead of 137. Now the always-on guest processes are protected and everything the agent spawns is a normal OOM candidate:
  - guest init (bundled `guest-init`, generic `initramfs-init-generic`): `echo -1000 >/proc/self/oom_score_adj` right before `tini` (tini + agent inherit it; PID 1 is never an OOM victim anyway); failure only logs to the console.
  - `GuestAgent.start()` sets its own `oom_score_adj` -1000 (defense in depth, also logs when it can't). Workload and exec processes are spawned through `spawnUnprotected()`: the agent sets itself to 0 right before the (synchronous) spawn and back to -1000 right after (`finally`), so the child inherits 0 at fork — no window in which the child or its own children still carry -1000 (a post-spawn `/proc/<pid>` write would race with the child's forks). Applies to both modes (generic lw-pty, bundled setpriv / pty-helper) — Agenstra's bundled images use the launcher's `guest-init` + `bridge-guest.cjs`, so one change covers both.
  - Exit code: a workload killed by the guest OOM killer dies by SIGKILL → already `128 + 9 = 137` (bundled: `exitStatus`; generic: lw-pty returns `128 + WTERMSIG`, also when the namespace init is killed). New: the agent reads `/proc/vmstat` `oom_kill` at workload start and exit and logs "guest OOM killer ended N process(es) while the workload ran (workload exit status …)" so the reason is visible in the guest log.
  - Docs: `docs/loadweaver/features/isolation-levels.md` (MicroVMs) — sizing note: guest kernel + guest tools ≈ 60 MiB, a 256 MiB microVM leaves ≈ 157 MiB for the workload; a workload filling guest memory is OOM-killed itself (exit 137), never the bridge agent.
- **Files**: `libs/domains/shared/backend/util-microvm-bridge/src/lib/{constants.ts,guest-agent.ts,bridge.spec.ts,oom-priority.spec.ts (new)}`, `apps/shared/microvm-launcher/rootfs/usr/lib/agenstra-microvm/{guest-init,initramfs-init-generic}`, `docs/loadweaver/features/isolation-levels.md`.
- **Tests**: new `oom-priority.spec.ts` (7, mocked `/proc` writes / `/proc/vmstat`): -1000 on start; workload inherits 0 and the agent is back at -1000; exec inherits 0; protection restored when the spawn throws (workload exit 127); SIGKILL → WORKLOAD_EXIT 137 + OOM log line; no log when the counter didn't move; unwritable `oom_score_adj` → logged, spawning unchanged. `bridge.spec.ts` identity expectation now includes the agent's `-1000` write. util-microvm-bridge 12 suites / **82** (+7). `tsc --noEmit` (lib + spec), ESLint, Prettier clean; `bash -n` / `sh -n` on both init scripts. No labs, no image builds.
- **G5 must verify** (after rebuilding `shared-microvm-launcher` and Agenstra's `worker-microvm` / `agenstra-isolation-lab-microvm*` images): S10 overfill (or a workload that allocates beyond the guest's MemAvailable) → **container exit 137**, guest log shows the OOM kill of the workload process and the new "guest OOM killer ended …" line, **no** "bridge agent exited" before the WORKLOAD_EXIT is reported; same for a bundled (Agenstra) microVM. Watch for: a fill that lives in tmpfs (pages owned by no process) with no adj-0 process left to kill → guest kernel panics "no killable processes" instead (the S10 spec's tmpfs fill could hit this; then fill from the workload's own RSS or keep a victim process alive). `cat /proc/<agent pid>/oom_score_adj` = -1000 and of the workload = 0 inside a running guest.

## Fix: email 2FA enforced only with SMTP (2026-10-24)

Found in G5: clusters from `loadweaver-agent bootstrap` and Loadweaver Cloud run `users` auth with forced email login 2FA (`DISABLE_FORCE_LOGIN_2FA` unset) but without SMTP, so the claimed admin gets `LOGIN_2FA_REQUIRED` (email) and no code ever arrives.

- **Decision (user, 2026-10-24)**: "No forced 2FA without SMTP". Forced email login 2FA applies only once SMTP is configured; until then login succeeds with email + password, the CP logs a warning at boot and the console shows cluster admins a warning banner. User-enabled email 2FA can't work without SMTP either → same rule (not enforced; enabling email 2FA is refused with 400). TOTP is always enforced.
- **Mechanism (opt-in, shared identity)**: `IIdentityEmailDispatcher` gets an optional `isDeliveryConfigured?(): boolean` + helper `isIdentityEmailDeliveryUnavailable(dispatcher)` (`util-auth/email-dispatcher.interface.ts`). `AuthService` (`feature-auth`) treats email 2FA as unenforceable only when the dispatcher implements it and returns false: `enforceLogin2fa`, `getTwoFactorStatus` (`forceEnabled` / `method` are the effective values), `disableEmail2fa`, `beginOrConfirmEmail2fa` (400 "Email is not configured…"); new public `isEmailLogin2faSuspended()` (forced policy on + no delivery) and `onModuleInit` warning. Agenstra / Decabill / fleet bridges don't implement the method → behaviour unchanged. Only the Loadweaver CP bridge (`loadweaver-identity-email-bridge.module.ts`) opts in: `isDeliveryConfigured: () => EmailService.isEnabled()` (`SMTP_HOST` + `SMTP_PORT`, read at start).
- **Console**: `GET /api/access/me` gains `emailLogin2faSuspended` (cluster admins only, else false; false without `users` auth — AuthService looked up via ModuleRef like `install.controller.ts`); OpenAPI `AccessMe` updated. `AccessMe.emailLogin2faSuspended?` in `data-access-console`; the console container shows a flush warning `fpc-alert` (`lwConsoleContainer-emailNotConfigured`, link `lwConsoleContainer-emailNotConfiguredLink` → https://docs.loadweaver.com/docs/console) for cluster admins; `messages.xlf` / `messages.de.xlf` updated.
- **Docs**: `docs/loadweaver/console.md` new "Email and two-factor login" section; notes in `getting-started.md` and `deployment/loadweaver-cloud.md` (step 2).
- **Files**: `libs/domains/identity/backend/util-auth/src/lib/email-dispatcher.interface.ts`, `libs/domains/identity/backend/feature-auth/src/lib/services/auth.service.ts` (+ spec), `libs/domains/loadweaver/backend/feature-control-plane/src/lib/notifications/loadweaver-identity-email-bridge.module.ts` (+ spec), `…/feature-control-plane/src/lib/controllers/access.controller.ts` (+ new `access.controller.spec.ts`), `…/feature-control-plane/spec/openapi.yaml`, `libs/domains/loadweaver/frontend/data-access-console/src/lib/types/console.types.ts`, `libs/domains/loadweaver/frontend/feature-console/src/lib/container/container.component.{ts,html,spec.ts}`, `apps/loadweaver/frontend-console/src/i18n/messages{,.de}.xlf`, docs above. Not touched: integration / VM-lab specs, secrets controller / service, `.npmrc`. No commits.
- **Tests (unit only)**: identity `auth.service.spec.ts` new block (6: non-opted dispatcher still enforces + no warning; opted + SMTP → enforced; opted + no SMTP → login without code, no email, boot warning; user-enabled email 2FA not enforced but TOTP still is; status effective + enable refused; `DISABLE_FORCE_LOGIN_2FA=true` → not suspended) — feature-auth 14 / 14 suites, 139 tests; CP bridge spec (+1) and `access.controller.spec.ts` (4); console `container.component.spec.ts` (+2 banner). `tsc` (feature-auth, CP lib + spec, feature-console lib, data-access-console lib) clean — the console / data-access spec tsconfigs show pre-existing `@angular/common/http` resolution errors in identity frontend files only; ESLint + Prettier clean on touched files.
- **VM-lab specs must change (G5/G6 re-run, not done here)**: `cloud.vm-lab.spec.ts` (~l.562–571 currently records `LOGIN_2FA_REQUIRED` / `method: 'email'` as the G5 finding) and the bootstrap lab login: with no SMTP the claimed admin's `POST /api/auth/login` must return 200 + `access_token` **without** a code; optionally assert `GET /api/access/me` → `emailLogin2faSuspended: true` for the admin and the CP log line "forced email two-factor login is NOT enforced". The `DISABLE_FORCE_LOGIN_2FA: 'true'` workarounds in `m7-cluster-agent.entry.ts` / `dr-agent.entry.ts` can stay (or be dropped). Needs the CP image rebuilt.
- **Open points**:
  1. There is no supported way yet to set SMTP on a bootstrapped / Cloud cluster: `SMTP_*` / `EMAIL_FROM` are not in `REPLICATED_CONTROL_PLANE_ENV` nor `DR_ENVELOPE_ENV_KEYS`, and `bootstrap` has no option for it. Docs say "control-plane environment"; a CLI / bootstrap option (and replication + DR) is a follow-up.
  2. The fleet service has the same problem (forced email 2FA, SMTP optional) but was deliberately left unchanged; opting in is a one-line change in `fleet-identity-email-bridge.module.ts` if wanted.
  3. `isDeliveryConfigured` reflects only "SMTP configured", not "SMTP works": a misconfigured server still enforces email 2FA (codes fail to send).

## Fix: SMTP settings for bootstrap / Cloud clusters (2026-10-24)

Closes open point 1 of "Fix: email 2FA enforced only with SMTP" for new clusters.

- **Flow** (same as the other control-plane env, e.g. `ADMIN_CLAIM_TOKEN_SHA256`): `bootstrap` flags → `JoinService.bootstrap` control-plane environment → bootstrap CP process env → `REPLICATED_CONTROL_PLANE_ENV` → `memberEnvironment` / `role.environment` pushed to every member → `controlPlaneApiSpec` spreads `role.environment` into the `lw-control-plane` container (no change needed there; API only, not Postgres) → `DR_ENVELOPE_ENV_KEYS` → `restoredEnvironment` on `bootstrap --restore`.
- **Variables** (what the CP actually reads: shared `EmailService` reads `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `EMAIL_FROM`; there is no `SMTP_SECURE` — port 465 means SMTPS; `resolve-email-company-name.ts` reads `EMAIL_COMPANY_NAME`, `_ADDRESS_LINE1`, `_POSTAL_CODE`, `_CITY`, `_COUNTRY`, `_VAT_ID`, `_EMAIL`): all 12 added to `REPLICATED_CONTROL_PLANE_ENV` and `DR_ENVELOPE_ENV_KEYS` (`SMTP_PASSWORD` in the secrets block, the rest under configuration). Pushed only over the agent stream (never persisted in desired-state rows), like `DB_PASSWORD`.
- **bootstrap**: `--smtp-host`, `--smtp-port` (default 587), `--smtp-user`, `--smtp-password-file` (else `LOADWEAVER_SMTP_PASSWORD`, never a flag value — same pattern as `--admin-claim-token-file`), `--email-from`, `--email-company-name|-address|-postal-code|-city|-country|-vat-id|-email`. `BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL_FLAGS` + `readBootstrapEmailSettings` (agent-cli), `bootstrapEmailEnvironment` (join.service) validates before anything starts: host needed once any setting is given, host name / IP, port 1–65535, user and password only together, `EMAIL_FROM` / company email address form, no control characters (header injection), password kept verbatim (file: trailing newline dropped). The flags are not restore-only; with `--restore` they are refused (`NEW_CLUSTER_ONLY_FLAGS`: the envelope keeps the settings). Usage text in `apps/loadweaver/backend-node-agent/src/cli.ts`.

  - `lw_email_settings` (one row `cluster`; migration `1800000000051_CreateEmailSettings.ts`, entity `entities/email-settings.entity.ts`): host / port / user / sender / company in clear, password envelope-encrypted with the cluster master key (`envelopeEncrypt`, AAD `email-settings/cluster`, like the SOPS identity); `revision` bumped per change. `MasterKeyService.reshare` re-wraps it (counted in `rewrapped`).
  - `email/email-settings.utils.ts` (validation = bootstrap rules: host name / IP, port 1–65535 default 587, user + password together, `from` / company email forms, country ISO-2, no control characters; env view, transport view, DR view), `email/email-settings.service.ts`, `email/email-runtime.ts` (company block holder for the statically registered notifications module), `controllers/email-settings.controller.ts`.

Applied on every replica without restart: the saving replica at once, the others by a 10 s poll on the row's `revision` (Postgres is the replicated store). While the master key is sealed, the row applies without the password (delivery counts as configured → email 2FA stays enforced; sends fail and retry) and the password is retried every poll.

  - DR: `DrEnvelopeContents.email?` (stored settings as `SMTP_*` / `EMAIL_*` incl. password, inside the sealed payload; escrow like `cluster`, the restored DB brings the row back anyway); `DrEnvelopeService` gets `EmailSettingsService` as `@Optional()`.

## Cloud email: decisions recorded (2026-10-24)

**Superseded (2026-10-27, user):** the Cloud email-service / provider design below and the Email settings API + page are dropped; SMTP via control-plane env like Agenstra / Decabill (`loadweaver.md` 3.17, 4, decision log 2026-10-27).

Plan-only (no code, no tests). Records the user's answers to the seven Loadweaver Cloud email questions (open point 4 of "Email settings API + page; Cloud relay design").

- **Decided**: (1) no own relay / MTA: clusters send directly to a **commercial EU email service** with one credential per cluster at the vendor, provisioned / rotated / revoked by Decabill via the vendor API; limits and metering via per-credential vendor features / stats. (2) **One-time enrollment token in user-data + sealed fetch** from Decabill at first start (works before the claim). (3) **Shared operator sender domain** (`noreply@mail.loadweaver.cloud`, "<cluster> via Loadweaver", DKIM / DMARC, configurable per operator); customer domains only with own SMTP. (4) **50 / hour, 500 / day per cluster**, one recipient, no attachments, raisable per plan; enforced vendor-side per credential where available, by the CP's outbound limiter (template check only there) and by Decabill revocation on abuse. (5) **Included quota + throttling**, `email.messages` reported to Decabill. (6) Existing Cloud clusters: **"Use Loadweaver email service"** button on the Email page. (7) Third-party operators: **own email-service account** in their Decabill; without it no SMTP, as today.
- **Plan**: `loadweaver.md` section 4 block rewritten ("Loadweaver email service (Cloud)" instead of "relay"), 3.17 console note adjusted, section 8 replaced by four new open questions (vendor comparison SES / Brevo / Mailjet / Scaleway TEM / Postmark / Mailgun EU with uncertain facts marked; limit enforcement without per-credential quotas; included quota size; metering source), four decision-log rows. Both `.mmd` diagrams: relay node removed, `MailVendor` node, cluster → vendor SMTP, enrollment edge to Decabill, Decabill → vendor credential provisioning / stats.
- **Follow-up answers (2026-10-24)**: (1) vendors: Decabill **email-vendor adapter interface** (create / rotate / revoke credential, set quota where supported, read stats) with three adapters the operator picks in their Decabill env: **generic SMTP** (shared operator credential; revocation hits all clusters, per-cluster stats only from the CP counter), **Mailgun EU** (per-cluster subaccount / SMTP credential, per-subaccount limits (verify)), **Amazon SES** `eu-central-1` (IAM user per cluster, sender pinned via IAM, per-cluster configuration set, quota per account only); vendor facts verified in a spike at implementation start. (2) **CP limiter + Decabill watchdog**: revoke at > 20 % over the daily limit or bounce / complaint thresholds, notify, manual re-enable; vendor account cap as backstop. (3) **1,000 messages / month** included per subscription, non-2FA mail throttled first, raisable per plan; 50 / hour and 500 / day stay. (4) Naming confirmed; existing clusters enroll via Decabill sign-in + approval → one-time code pasted on the Email page; `email.messages` from vendor per-credential stats, CP counter as fallback (always for generic SMTP).
- **Plan (follow-up)**: `loadweaver.md` section 4 block rewritten (adapters, 4-layer enforcement, quota, metering source, enrollment flow), section 8 reduced to one new open question (per-cluster isolation for generic SMTP), four decision-log rows. Both `.mmd` diagrams: `MailVendor` relabelled "Email vendor (SMTP / Mailgun / Amazon SES)", Decabill → vendor edge notes the revoke threshold.
- **Follow-up (2026-10-25)**: generic-SMTP isolation decided: optional provisioning hook for per-cluster SMTP users, else shared credential + CP counter + watchdog alerts / rotation with an explicit operator warning / checkbox in Decabill; Mailgun / SES recommended for public offerings. Section 8 has no email questions left; one decision-log row. Diagrams unchanged.
- **Implementation**: after the M7 gate, unless the user says otherwise; starts with the vendor spike (Mailgun / SES facts marked "(verify)").

- **S7 freeze analysis** (new breakdown log line: final guest pass, QEMU at completion, hand-over; QEMU's `query-migrate` at the last running poll, at the pause and at completion):
  - **Where the freeze went**: QEMU's own part (pause → `completed`) was 0.4–1.5 s in every G5 run; QEMU's throughput estimate (`ram.mbps`) tracked the relay (~120–335 Mbit/s ≈ 15–40 MB/s at the pause; bursts up to 1 Gbit/s right after the switch are socket buffers). The rest: the final guest pass 0.1–0.5 s and, for microVMs with filesystem volumes, the **hand-over ≈ 1.0–1.5 s per volume** (kill / fs-release, umount, `drbdadm secondary` → `primary`, mount; nested) — estimate assumes 400 ms.
  - **What was wrong**: the control plane passed `downtimeLimitMs = freezeBudgetMs` (3000) — QEMU alone could use the whole budget, the final pass / hand-over / resume came on top. **Fixed**: `qemuDowntimeLimitMs` = budget − `overheadMs.qemu` (300) − (microVM: `microvmSyncMs` 250 + n × `volumeHandoverMs` 400), ≥ 100 ms — the same split the eligibility estimate uses. Budget (3 s) and eligibility unchanged. Effect in the lab (same nested setup): VM freeze 3.5–4.4 s → **2.8–3.1 s**; generic microVM with 1 volume **2.0–3.0 s** (was 6.6 s in G3 S7); bundled microVM with 2 volumes 2.9–4.4 s (QEMU ≈ 1 s + hand-over ≈ 2.6–3 s).
  - Also found on the way (product): an aborted capped attempt left its speed cap on the domain (`migrate-setspeed` / QMP `max-bandwidth` persist) → the next uncapped attempt crawled at 1 MiB/s; and QEMU's own default `max-bandwidth` (128 MiB/s) applied to every microVM migration — `vm-ctl` now always sets the speed (unlimited without a cap). A forced switch-over (`vmSwitchoverAfterMs`, "forced to complete") was still cancelled by `maxSeconds` counted from the start → now its own window.
  - **Not changed (user / calibration decisions)**: `volumeHandoverMs` 400 is optimistic for this nested lab (1.0–1.5 s / volume); `overheadMs.qemu` 300 vs measured VM excess (libvirt downtime − QEMU part) 0.3–1.0 s nested; `microvmSyncMs` 250 matches (0.1–0.5 s). A bundled microVM with two volumes can exceed 3 s here. On a real host (no nesting, local NVMe, 10 GbE): QEMU's final transfer for a 0.5 GiB guest ≲ 0.2–0.4 s, DRBD demote / promote + mount ≈ 0.2–0.5 s per volume → expected freeze ≈ 1–1.5 s with two volumes; recalibrate `volumeHandoverMs` / `overheadMs.qemu` on real hardware (W10 "lab-measured later"). Eligibility for microVMs is plausible (estimate VM 2700 ms budget share, microVM 1 vol 2050 ms, 2 vols 1650 ms) — the estimate under-counts the nested hand-over only.

## Fix: registry access by project roles (2026-10-26)

**Decision (user, "project roles only")**: the registry token realm (`GET /api/registry/token`) authorizes each requested repository `<project>/<repository>` from the caller's role in that project — viewers and up pull, developers and up push; **no cluster role needed** for project repositories. Cluster admins act as project admins everywhere (pull + push on every project); auditors / infra operators keep pull on every project (they read every project, `canReadProject`), infra operators lose the old implicit push (`infra` permission). `lw-system/…` is never granted to users (nodes get it via `issueForNode`). PAT bounds unchanged: the route needs `registry:pull`, push additionally `registry:push`. Unauthorized repositories / actions are dropped from the token (standard Docker behaviour, no error). `docker login` (no scope) succeeds for anyone with ≥ 1 project membership or a cluster role (or the API key); otherwise 403 "Missing project membership". `registry:catalog:*` only for cluster roles (`issueWithCatalog`). Plan: `loadweaver.md` 3.22 bullet + decision-log row 2026-10-26; `loadweaver.mmd` not affected.

**Files**

- `libs/domains/loadweaver/backend/feature-control-plane/src/lib/registry/registry-scope.utils.ts` — `grantRegistryAccess(requested, projects, caller: AccessCaller, { push })` (project-role based), new `registryProjectActions`, `mayUseRegistry`, `requestsRegistryCatalog`.
- `.../src/lib/controllers/registry.controller.ts` — uses `ProjectAccessService.caller()` instead of `ClusterAccessService.assert(read)` / `can(infra)`; catalog token for cluster roles.
- `.../src/lib/services/registry-token.service.ts` — doc comment of `issueWithCatalog` (now also cluster-role users).
- Docs: `docs/loadweaver/features/built-in-registry.md` ("Who may push and pull" role table); OpenAPI `spec/openapi.yaml` `/registry/token` description + 403.

**Tests** (unit, `--maxWorkers=1`): `src/lib/registry/registry.spec.ts` (role matrix: viewer pull-only, developer/operator/admin push+pull, other project / non-member denied, cluster admin all, infra operator / auditor pull, `lw-system` never, PAT push narrowing, login + catalog detection) and new `src/lib/controllers/registry.controller.spec.ts` (login without scope for a member without cluster role, 403 without membership, PAT `registry:pull` vs `registry:pull`+`registry:push`, cluster-admin all + catalog, catalog refused for project-only callers). Whole CP project suite also ran once (134 suites / 1050 tests green). tsc (lib + spec), eslint, prettier clean on touched code / docs files.

**VM-lab cluster specs must change** (not edited here, `integration/**` off-limits): `m7/m7-cluster.ts` `registryPassword()` — drop the explicit `PUT /cluster/members/<me>` `cluster-admin` workaround. Instead the PAT owner needs a **developer+ project membership** in every project whose repositories the lab pushes to (`PUT /projects/<project>/members/<userId>` with `{ role: 'developer' }` or `admin`, after the project exists) — a PAT never inherits the global admin's powers and project creators are not auto-members. Pull-only users need viewer. The PAT scopes `registry:pull` + `registry:push` stay. A CP image rebuild is needed before the next lab round.

- Node agent `workloads/workload.manager.ts` — `LayerUnpackError` → per-replica failed status (no aborted reconcile); Docker 304 on start ignored; `removeUndesired` at the start of the volumes step (VM + disk removal deadlock); agent-cli `unpack-layer` reason only.

- CP `vm-image-import.service.ts` — stall watchdog for URL downloads (whole download, every phase), progress every 32 MiB; TypeORM `[rows, affected]` for `UPDATE / DELETE … RETURNING` (also `live/live-broker.ts`).

### Open points

- WAL archiving fails (retried) until the first apply makes the node a gateway member ("Backup gateway refused GET … unknown access key" in the CP log until then) — cosmetic noise.
- vmapi-r1's "no first desired state for 8 min" is fixed by a plausible cause (listener catch-up) but not reproduced; watch the next cold cluster starts.

## Fix: fleet-mode cluster actions (2026-10-26)

- **User report**: in fleet mode no option to join nodes into an opened cluster; various other cluster actions are disabled.
- **Root cause (investigation)**: not a role / timing bug — `AccessService.me()` maps the fleet grant correctly (the user is a fleet admin → `cluster-admin`; fleet logs show `GET /api/clusters/<id>/grants` 200). The missing actions were **design rules**: join tokens / installer / `nodes/join` on the relay's hard deny list `NEVER_RELAYED` for every role (P7a + security follow-up **M5**), approvals / acceptances native (**M1**), mirrored in the console (`mayJoin = mayOperate && !fleetMode`, approve / accept hidden). Plus a real **gap**: admin actions the console offers but the allow-list didn't carry (→ 404 "not available through the fleet"): backup-key escrow, DR info, platform Postgres restore start / discard, OpenSearch restore, posture integrations CRUD / test / sync + certificate trust, wallboard tokens, host import, and `GET search`.
- **User decisions (2026-10-26)**: (1) **B** — relay join tokens for cluster-wide fleet admins (reverses M5); (2) approvals through the fleet with a per-user signed identity (reverses M1, design first); (3) close the gap, deliberately excluded items hidden in fleet mode + documented.

## Decabill: SMTP for Loadweaver Cloud clusters (2026-10-27)

- **Scope** (plan section 4 "Loadweaver Cloud: transactional email", simplified 2026-10-27): Decabill's `loadweaver` contributor passes the operator's SMTP (`effectiveConfig.smtp` — plan `providerConfigDefaults` + requested config, same `host / port / user / password / from` block and resolution as `agenstra-controller` / `agenstra-manager` / `decabill-billing`; no new admin settings) to the new cluster as `bootstrap` email flags.
- **Implemented** (unit tests only): `loadweaver.utils.ts` — `resolveLoadweaverEmailSettings` (no `smtp.host` → `undefined`, no flags: cluster starts without email as before; the siblings' MailHog defaults deliberately not applied; fails closed on control characters / > 1024 chars, port outside 1–65535, user without password or vice versa — the checks `bootstrap` would otherwise fail on the node); `LoadweaverCloudInitConfig.email`; user-data adds `--smtp-host`, `--smtp-port` (only when set; bootstrap default 587), `--smtp-user`, `--smtp-password-file /var/lib/loadweaver-cloud/smtp-password`, `--email-from`. Password written exactly like the admin claim token (`(umask 077 && printf '%s' <quoted> > file)` before bootstrap, `rm -f` on failure and after success, together with the claim-token file). All bootstrap args now go through the existing `quoteShellLiteral` (`utils/cloud-init/work-dir.utils.ts`; output unchanged for the previous safe values). `--email-company-*` not rendered: the shared `smtp` block has no company fields (would need a new setting). `provider-config-schema.utils.ts`: `PRODUCT_FIELD_SERVICES.smtp` now includes `loadweaver`, so the plan editor shows the SMTP block for Loadweaver plans. Order form unchanged (the Agenstra kinds show no SMTP inputs there either; Loadweaver orders send no `smtp`, so the plan's value applies).
- **Docs**: `docs/decabill/features/server-provisioning.md` (settings table row, "Email (operator SMTP)" paragraph, cloud-init step 5), `docs/loadweaver/deployment/loadweaver-cloud.md` (first steps: SMTP from the provider if configured).
- **Files**: `libs/domains/decabill/backend/feature-billing-manager/src/lib/contributors/loadweaver/loadweaver.utils{,.spec}.ts`, `…/src/lib/utils/provider-config-schema.utils{,.spec}.ts`; docs above.
- **Tests** (`--maxWorkers=1`): `loadweaver.utils.spec` 41 (new: no SMTP → no flags; resolution incl. string port / blank host; refusals; flags quoted incl. `'` in user, password with `'"$()\`\;&|`only in the root-only file write before bootstrap, never on the command line, removed on failure + success; bash executes the write → exact bytes, and parses the flags → exact values without the password; unauthenticated SMTP → no password file / port);`provider-config-schema.utils.spec`5.`tsc --noEmit` clean (lib + spec config), ESLint 0, Prettier clean.
- **Gate (lab)**: provision a Loadweaver plan with `smtp` against MailHog / a test relay → the cluster's control-plane environment has `SMTP_*` / `EMAIL_FROM`, `/var/lib/loadweaver-cloud/smtp-password` is gone after bootstrap, email 2FA / confirmations are delivered; without `smtp` the cluster starts without email.

## UI groundwork: action buttons, title bars, search (2026-10-27)

User requests: (1) action bands use buttons like Agenstra, not links (example `/fleet/clusters`); (2) the list "title bar" consistently, but per follow-up: **single-list pages do not repeat the page title** (page header → search → list, as on Agenstra / Decabill single-list pages); a list title bar only where a page has several sections, with the search **under** it (Decabill board lanes: lane header → search); (3) search on Loadweaver list pages; (4) no `·` separators (badges / separate muted spans / list-item meta instead).

**Reference patterns (Agenstra / Decabill)**: row actions `fpc-button-group size="sm"` + icon-only `fpc-button size="sm"` (warning + pencil = edit, danger + trash = delete, secondary = everything else; documented on `fpc-list-item`); search `fpc-search-field class="border-bottom" [bordered]="false"` directly under `fpc-page-header` on single-list pages (`admin-projects-page`, `billing-list-search.ts` client filter) and under `fpc-lane-header` inside lanes on multi-list pages (`invoices`, `overview`); empty search → `fpc-empty-state icon="search"`; meta as `d-flex flex-wrap gap-3` of icon + text spans; no `·` anywhere in their templates.

**Inventory before** (Loadweaver console, 57 page / panel templates): 26 `variant="link"` buttons (16 files) + 5 anchor / `btn-link` actions in action bands; 101 `·` in templates / TS (+7 in specs); search on 7 pages (audit, files, logs, resources, search, topology, VMs). Agenstra / Decabill: single-list pages already page header + search + list; multi-list pages already lane header + search; their 16 `variant="link"` uses are row-title links in boards / dropdown triggers / form "Clear" helpers, not action bands → **no change needed** in Agenstra / Decabill.

**What changed (Loadweaver console, `libs/domains/loadweaver/frontend/feature-console/src/lib/`)**

- **Action buttons (~43 link / anchor actions → buttons)**: fleet clusters (4: poll / open secondary, edit warning, delete danger), fleet cluster detail grants (2), fleet operations cancel, fleet overview card details, access (+ access-requests, project-requests), drift (2 anchors → routerLink buttons), backups (9), backup detail (3), backup restores (2), backup keys, platform backups (2), files (5), slos (2 anchors), status pages (2 `a.btn`), topology (2), updates (3); labelled text actions in action bands turned into icon groups too (nodes / devices / wallboards revoke, posture, reports, sessions, git accounts, trusted fleets, imports open). Accessible names via `ariaLabel` + `title`, existing test ids kept. Left on purpose (10): modal / form helpers (nodes join Copy, wallboard Copy, trusted-fleets add / remove key, backup-keys add share, git modal "Show advanced"), terminal alert actions, top-bar nav chrome.
- **Title bars**: new shared `fpc-list-header` (`libs/domains/shared/frontend/ui-components/src/lib/list-header/`, lane-header chrome + `count` / `count / total`, `[fpcListHeaderActions]`; spec, story, catalog entry, export). Used only where a page has several sections: fleet overview (cluster cards next to inbox / sites; search directly under it, sticky together). Single-list pages: no second headline (removed the interim list headers from 17 pages; dropped the list-panel title that repeated the page title on wallboards and certificates). Multi-section pages with a search that belongs to one panel: search moved into that panel under its title bar (git connections, devices). Pages whose search filters several sections (sessions, policies, access, nodes, backups catalog) keep it under the page header.
- **Search (22 pages added)**: fleet clusters, fleet operations, fleet overview, access, alerts (+ silences), certificates, devices, dns records, git, imports, backups catalog, backup restores (+ tests), files (directory filter), nodes, plans, policies, reports, sessions (+ tunnels), slos, status pages (+ incidents), updates (releases / plans / windows), wallboards. Client-side over loaded rows (no list endpoint has a query param; audit / logs / fleet audit keep their server-side filters) via new `list-search.ts` (`matchesSearch`, `filterBySearch`, shared `NO_MATCHES_TITLE` / `NO_MATCHES_HINT`); every page has its no-matches empty state. Skipped: detail / form / config pages, health (tree), drift (short report sections), metrics (query page), git accounts / trusted fleets (few entries), usage (filters already).
- **`·` removed (all 101 + 7 in specs)**: templates use flex-gap span groups, icon + text meta or `fpc-badge size="sm" color="light"` (latency, version, arch / format, counts, kinds); plain-text contexts (option labels, panel / page titles, tooltips, TS-built labels in `posture-format`, `policy-format`, `plan-format`, `update-format`, `live-format`, `git-page`, `topology-page`, `fleet-world-map`, `resource-editor`) use `, `, `; `, `:` or parentheses.

**Tests**: specs updated / added per page (buttons not `.btn-link` + variant, no second headline / search right after the page header or inside the panel under its title bar, search filters rows, no-matches state, `count / total` on the fleet overview title bar); new `list-search.spec`, `list-header.component.spec`, `imports-page.component.spec`, `backup-restores-page.component.spec`. ## Workspace (map-first console) (2026-10-27)

Concept + user decisions recorded as **3.36 Workspace (map-first console)** in `loadweaver.md` (route / model, map, filters, popover / panel, action registry, editing → drafts → dry-run preview → plan, server-side shared drafts, live, scope / fleet / small screens, phases P0–P6), 4 decision-log rows, open questions in section 8 (idle-draft expiry, no locks while drafting, discarding others' drafts — implemented as recommended until decided). Both diagrams updated (console = Workspace landing, API = drafts + dry-run, live = drafts + structure changes).

### Backend: B1, B2, drafts, B3 (done)

- **B1** `planOverlay()` (`topology/topology.utils.ts`) also marks deployments' volumes, `VirtualMachine` (its `lw-vm` replica + disks `project/lw-vm/<vm>.<disk>`), `DnsRecord` (hostname from the zone's domain, `DnsZone` names looked up only when a plan touches records) and `Site`. The overlay part of `TopologyService.topology()` moved into `overlay()` and accepts proposed changes (no stored plan).
- **B2** `POST /plans { …, dryRun: true }` builds the full plan (diff, network / workload preview, failure analysis, risk, warnings) and returns it unsaved (`id: dry-run`, `dryRun: true`): no `save`, no `planCreated` event (Git PRs / notifications), no lookup. `POST /topology/preview` (scope `plans:create`) = same body → map + overlay + `plan`. `PlanSource.draft { id, title }` tags plans submitted from a draft.
- **Drafts** `drafts/` (entity `lw_drafts`, migration `1800000000053_WorkspaceDrafts`, `drafts.utils.ts` pure: op keys, patch, scope, `mayEditDraft` / `mayPlanScope`, conflicts, plan input, If-Match; `DraftsService`; `DraftsController`): `POST /drafts`, `GET /drafts?status=`, `GET /drafts/:id`, `PATCH /drafts/:id` (If-Match or `version`; 409 with the current draft), `POST /drafts/:id/preview` (dry-run + topology overlay + conflicts), `/submit` (claims the draft first, 409 on conflicts, reopens on a refused plan), `/discard`. Audited `draft.create|update|submit|discard`. Owner = fleet person / user / `api-key`. Limits 500 ops, 2 MiB, 100 open per owner. Live: `socket/plans` sends `draftsSnapshot` + `draftPatch` (by edit rights).
- **B3** `socket/topology`: `subscribe { structure: true }` → `structureChanged { version }` (also for project members; flows still cluster roles only; flows-only subscribe without a cluster role still refused). `TopologyService.structureVersion()` public.
- **Fleet relay**: `GET drafts`, `GET drafts/:id` viewer; `POST drafts`, `PATCH drafts/:id`, `POST drafts/:id/(preview|submit|discard)`, `POST topology/preview` operator (like `POST plans`); `If-Match` forwarded.
- OpenAPI: `/topology/preview`, `/drafts*`, `DraftOpInput` / `DraftOp` / `Draft` / `DraftConflict`, `CreatePlanDto.dryRun`, `PlanResponseDto.dryRun`, `PlanSource.draft`.
- Unit tests (all green, `--maxWorkers=1`): `topology.utils.spec` (B1), `topology.service.spec` (proposed overlay), `plans-dry-run.spec` (nothing stored / no events), `drafts.utils.spec`, `drafts.service.spec` (concurrency 409, sharing by project rights, fleet person owner, preview conflicts, submit conflict → rebase → plan, reopen on refused plan, discard), `gateways/topology.gateway.spec` (B3), `gateways/plans.gateway.spec` (drafts streaming), fleet `relay-rules.spec` / `relay-headers.spec`; import / injection cycle specs green.

### P5: semantic zoom / aggregation, worker layout, perf, B3 in the console (done)

- Semantic zoom: the page follows the canvas zoom (`zoomChange`) and re-instantiates only on a level change (L0 sites + border, L1 nodes / groups / addresses, L2 stacks / VMs / volumes, L3 replicas); maps with more than 1,500 drawn items start at L1. Selection, search hits (≤ 200) and the traced path stay visible at every level with their containers. Hidden children aren't created at all; their edges are bundled onto the nearest visible ancestor (counts, flow rates added).
- Stable positions: the layout is computed once over every drawn item (`allDrawn`) and the visible subset is placed from it (`workspacePositions` places a collapsed compound in the middle of its expanded area), so nothing jumps between levels. `workspaceLayout()` is self-contained (all helpers inside) and runs in a Blob web worker built from its own source (`workspace-layout.worker.ts`) for maps above 1,500 items, with a synchronous fallback (no `Worker`, worker error). Layouts are cached in memory by key and the last one per user + cluster in local storage (≤ 5,000 boxes).
- B3 in the console: `socket/topology` subscribes with `{ structure: true }` (project members too), `structureChanged` → `topologyStructureChanged` → the current map reloads quietly (`reloadTopologyOnStructureChange$`), the Workspace reloads the declared resources; the old 60 s re-poll only runs while the socket is down.
- Perf (unit level): 1,000 nodes / 10,000 replicas / 5,000 flows — model, full layout, L1 instantiation, bundling and positions within the budget; layout alone in `workspace-layout.spec`.

Remaining "not available through the fleet": `/webhooks` and `/updates/announcements` (shared features that call the cluster outside `ConsoleApi`, not through the relay) — follow-up: route their services through the relay base URL and add admin relay rules.

### Follow-up (2026-10-27): remaining fleet parity gaps closed (done)

- **Webhooks + release announcements in the fleet cluster view**: `clusterScopedApiEnvironment()` (data-access-console) gives the shared notifications / updates features an `apiUrl` that follows `ConsoleEndpointService.restApi()` on every request (control plane natively, the active cluster's relay in fleet mode); `app.config.ts` provides both through it. Relay rules (admin): `admin/webhooks` list / event types / get / deliveries / create / update / delete / test, `updates/announcements` (+ status, check). Console: `/webhooks` and `/updates/announcements` removed from the fleet-unavailable list; the announcements guard accepts the cluster-wide admin grant in fleet mode (global admin natively); the admin popover shows both with a cluster open (webhooks for cluster admins as before, announcements for the admin grant), none without a cluster.
- **Reads scoped to the person**: the cluster's `FleetIdentityInterceptor` now verifies claims on reads too (without consuming the nonce), so person-scoped reads of project grants are capped to the person (before, reads stayed the service user's — needed for the person-scoped read rules).
- **Live streams for project grants**: fleet `authorizeSocketNamespace()` allows `plans` / `topology` for project grants with `needsClaim`; the socket relay attaches only to clusters that verify the fleet and sends `auth.fleetIdentity` = a fresh signed claim (`SOCKET`, `/socket/<ns>`, audience = cluster, user + grants) on every (re)connect. Cluster: `TrustedFleetsService.evaluateSocket()` (namespace-bound, nonce consumed, no PAT-caller requirement — capping by the connecting user's own roles keeps it at most what that user has); `PlansGateway` / `TopologyGateway` verify it in the handshake (refused claim → connection refused) and use the person for `access.caller` → plans / drafts filtered to the person's projects, topology structure changes (flows stay cluster roles). No trusted fleet: the relay refuses the project-grant attach and the console keeps its periodic refresh. Logs / terminals / consoles stay cluster-wide.
- Tests: fleet `relay-rules.spec` (+webhooks / announcements rules, socket namespaces for project grants), `fleet-relay.gateway.spec` (+1: untrusted refused, verified → claim in the handshake, re-minted on reconnect), control-plane `fleet-identity.interceptor.spec` (reads verified without nonce, refused reads), `trusted-fleets.service.spec` (+1 socket claim: namespace binding, replay), `plans.gateway.spec` (+1: refused / verified handshake, caller as the person), data-access `fleet-endpoints.spec` (+1 cluster-scoped env), feature-console `global-admin.guard.spec` (new), fleet / container specs. All green; tsc (control-plane, fleet, feature-console, frontend-console app) + eslint clean.
- Gate items: fleet e2e with a project-only grant against a trusting cluster (live draft patches / plan progress / structure changes only for the person's projects; nothing of other projects), and against a non-trusting cluster (periodic refresh); webhooks and announcements pages through the fleet.

## Fix: stale 'not available through the fleet' messages (2026-10-27)

- **User report**: in a fleet-opened cluster the console still showed "Not available through the fleet: this part of the cluster is only reachable in the cluster's own console." although the feature works.
- **Sources of the message** (and what was done):
  - `fleet-relay-error.interceptor.ts` (`lwConsoleFleet-relayUnavailable`): rewrites the fleet's 404 `<VERB> <path> is not relayed` (route without a relay rule). **Kept** as the safety net. Every console request was checked against `relay-rules.ts` with an admin grant (esbuild bundle + script over every `this.url(…)` path in `data-access-console`). Everything the console loads on a page is relayed. These were still unrelayed and are offered in fleet mode, so they produced the message:
    - **Search favourites** (`GET|PUT|DELETE search/favorites…`; `POST search/recent` fails silently): the star in the palette / search page → the message in the palette. Favourites are personal to the signed-in account, which through the fleet is the service user, so they stay native (the decided "personal resources" exception). **Fixed in the console**: `loadweaver-search-results` gets `starrable` (palette + page pass `favouritesAvailable = !fleetMode`). In fleet mode there is no star and favourites are not loaded. Recents stay session-local.
    - **Access import** (`POST access/import`), **etcd snapshot download** (`GET backups/platform/etcd/etcd-<yyyymmdd>t<hhmmss>z`), **air-gapped bundle upload** (`POST updates/bundles`): not decided exceptions, so **closed the gap** with admin relay rules (cluster-wide grants only, like `access/export`, `backups/<id>/download`, release download). A bundle upload is streamed without a claim. Bundles above `FLEET_RELAY_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (default 11 MiB) get 413 from the relay.
    - Decided native items that are still refused: install script (console already uses the native URL), `nodes/join`, recovery kit (hidden in fleet mode with its own warning on `/backups/keys`), trusted fleets, VPN devices, Git accounts. These are `NEVER_RELAYED` (message "is never relayed", not shown as this text) or have their routes blocked (below).
  - `/fleet/unavailable` page (`LoadweaverFleetUnavailablePageComponent`) + `fleetConsoleGuard` / `FLEET_UNAVAILABLE_PATHS` + sidebar filter: the list already held only the decided exceptions (`/devices`, `/settings/git-accounts`, `/settings/trusted-fleets`). The page text was stale ("never relayed … joining, Git connections, approvals"). It now has a **specific reason for each page** (`fleetUnavailableReason()` in `fleet-format.ts`: VPN devices / linked Git accounts belong to the signed-in account, i.e. the fleet's service account; trusted fleets are the trust anchor). An "Open in the cluster's console" link appears only for these pages and only when the native endpoint is known. A fallback text covers anything else. A spec checks that the list contains exactly the three decided paths and that each has a reason.
  - Checked, no change: the per-page fleet notices (`lwConsoleBackupKeys-fleetNative` next to the kit actions; approvals hints `lwConsoleFleet-approvalNative` / identity panel, which only apply while the cluster doesn't verify the fleet; nodes installer hint): all describe decided or conditional exceptions precisely.

- **Follow-up (user decisions 2026-10-27)**: (1) stream the release bundle upload through the relay; (2) search favourites per fleet person. Both are recorded in `loadweaver.md` 3.24, which has two new decided bullets, updated "Relay scope" / parity bullets and 2 decision-log rows. Both `.mmd` diagrams updated (relay label).
  - **(1) Bundle upload**:
    - Fleet `relay-rules.ts`: `RelayRule.stream`, set only on `POST updates/bundles` (admin).
    - `FleetRelayService` pipes the request unbuffered and skips `FLEET_RELAY_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` and the byte-limit transform. Backpressure comes from axios piping the socket.
    - The upload has an `AbortController`: it aborts on caller `aborted` / `close` before `req.complete`, and on `FLEET_RELAY_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` (new, default 2 h, 1 min – 24 h). Cleanup runs on `res` close. `ClusterRequest.signal` is passed to axios.
    - Fleet bootstrap raises the HTTP server `requestTimeout` to the stream timeout.
    - Claim: `declaredStreamBody()` / `fleetStreamBinding()` give `bh` = `stream:<Content-Length>:<sha256 hex>` (new `FleetClaimInput.bodyBinding`). Without the header there is no claim.
    - `x-loadweaver-content-sha256` is forwarded by the relay and allowed by CORS (fleet + control plane).
    - Control plane:
      - `fleet-identity.utils.ts` adds `CONTENT_SHA256_HEADER`, `FLEET_STREAM_BOUND_ROUTES` (`POST /api/updates/bundles`), `declaredContent()`, `fleetStreamBinding()` and `expectedBodyBinding()`. `TrustedFleetsService.evaluate` uses the latter: stream binding only on stream routes without a raw body and with both headers.
      - `bundle.service.ts` gets `declaredDigestSource()`: it hashes and counts as the bytes pass, keeps the underlying stream when the tar reader stops early, and `verify()` drains the rest and compares. `importStream(…, verifyUpload)` runs `verify()` after `readBundle`, before `finishImport` (a mismatch is refused and audited).
      - `updates.controller.ts` uses it whenever the header is present (natively optional).
    - Console: `utils/sha256.ts`, an incremental SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) plus `sha256OfBlob` reading 8 MiB chunks. In fleet mode `UpdatesService.uploadBundle` computes the digest first, then sends `X-Loadweaver-Content-SHA256`. Natively there is no header.
    - OpenAPI updated (control-plane `/updates/bundles` header, fleet relay POST description).
  - **(2) Favourites per person**:
    - Fleet: `RelayRule.personal` (always `needsClaim` → verified cluster + person required). Rules `GET search/favorites`, `PUT|DELETE search/favorites/<item>`, `POST search/recent` (viewer, cluster-wide). The item is one segment; `normalizeRelayPath` accepts encoded characters only there and only `%3A` / `%2F`. Removed from the "never relayed" spec.
    - Control plane `search.service.ts`: `preferenceKey()`. Through a fleet (PAT with `fleet:on-behalf-of`), favourites / recents and the favourite flags in results use the verified person (`ProjectAccessService.caller` already maps it to `fleet:<iss>:<sub>`). Without a verified claim: reads empty, writes 403, visits ignored.
    - Console:
      - `AccessMe.fleetIdentity` (verified + person, also during the read-only grace).
      - `favouritesAvailable(fleetMode, me)` in `access-format.ts`.
      - Palette and search page show the star and load favourites when available; the page loads them via an effect once the access is known. Otherwise the star is hidden and a hint shows (`lwConsoleSearch-favouritesFleet`; new `starHint` input on `loadweaver-search-results`).
  - **i18n**: +1 unit (`lwConsoleSearch-favouritesFleet`, de target). Parity 3145 / 3145, XML parses, every `@@lwConsole…` id present.
  - **Docs**: `docs/loadweaver/features/fleet.md` (deny list without favourites, new bullets for favourites per person and the streamed bundle upload), `search-and-wallboard.md` (favourites per fleet person), `updates.md` (declared SHA-256), `console.md` (star in fleet mode).
  - **Checks**: fleet lib 16 suites / 113 tests, data-access-console 54 / 265, control-plane fleet-identity / updates / search / trusted-fleets / cycle specs and feature-console search / access / container / fleet specs all green. `tsc --noEmit` clean on the fleet lib + spec, control-plane lib + spec, fleet + control-plane apps, data-access-console and feature-console lib configs (the Angular spec configs only show the known `@angular/*` moduleResolution noise). ESLint 0, Prettier clean.
  - **Tests** (`--maxWorkers=1`, green):
    - fleet `relay-rules` (+2: favourites per person incl. encoded item / refused encodings, stream rule unique and admin-only).
    - fleet `fleet-relay.service` (+3: bundle past the size limit piped as is with the stream binding + signal; no digest → no claim, abort on disconnect; favourites 404 without a verifying cluster, forwarded with the claim and encoded path).
    - control-plane `fleet-identity.utils` (+3: declared content, binding only on stream routes, claim check incl. length mismatch), `updates-services` (+2: digest match after a partial read, mismatch / short / overlong refused), new `search-preferences.spec` (3: person used, no favourites for an unverified fleet relay, native unchanged). `trusted-fleets`, import / injection cycle specs green.
    - data-access `sha256.spec` (new, against node crypto, edge lengths / chunkings, Blob), `updates.service` (+1 fleet digest header, native none), `fleet-endpoints` (`fleetIdentity` incl. grace).

The control plane now switches it off (`server.requestTimeout = 0`; the header timeout stays) and enforces receive limits in `createRequestTimeoutMiddleware` (`feature-control-plane/src/lib/utils/request-timeout.middleware.ts`, registered in the app bootstrap):

### Fix: section sub-nav layout (user report, during P8)

- Cause: the global `.fpc-routed-outlet > router-outlet + *` rule (higher specificity than the component's `:host`) forced the section host into `flex-direction: column`, so the vertical sub-nav stacked above the page. `section/section-page.component.ts` now uses the Resources layout: `fpc-split-pane` (240–480 px like the tree, not collapsible; collapsed when the section has a single page) with the vertical `fpc-tab-group` in the start column (own scroll) and the routed page in the end column (`fpc-routed-outlet`). Width per user in the console settings (`sectionNavWidth`, shared by every section; `sectionNavWidth()` clamps, `onWidth()` stores the last size after 400 ms); phones: the start column + gutter hidden, the `<select>` above the page.
- `fpc-tab-group` (ui-components) got a generic `stretch` input (vertical only: the list fills its container instead of the fixed 14 rem rail, no own border).
- Only the section page uses a vertical tab group as side nav (object pages use horizontal tabs; Admin / Account / fleet pages have no sub-nav).
- i18n: 1 unit. Specs: `section/section-page` (+2: split layout + width store, width clamp).

### Sticky tables: root cause + fix (2026-10-28)

Debugged in the running dev console (headless Chromium via Playwright, read-only; in the test browser only, the console bundle was switched from fleet mode to the CP's dev API key from `.start-containers.env`). Per table: computed `position` of `thead th`, the first ancestor with `overflow ≠ visible`, whether it really scrolls, `getBoundingClientRect` of the head / foot before and after scrolling it.

- **Root cause 1 – lanes had no height** (all `loadweaver-lane`s): `fpc-board-lane`'s host was `flex: 0 1 auto` in `fpc-section-column`, so it was content-sized; Chromium sizes an auto-height column flexbox from its items' flex basis, and the body is `flex: 1 1 0` → **body 0 px tall** (e.g. members / sessions / backups: lane 78 px = header + search, body `clientHeight` 0, content clipped). Nothing in a lane body could scroll, so no head could stick. Fix: `fpc-board-lane :host { flex: 1 1 auto }` (Agenstra / Decabill lanes already had `h-100`; no change there).
- **Root cause 2 – `.table-responsive` wrappers** still around 11 sticky tables (audit, fleet audit, usage, git commits, backups ×2, platform backups ×2, files, fleet cluster grants, fleet ops wizard): the wrapper (`overflow-x: auto` ⇒ `overflow-y: auto`) is the table's scroll container but never scrolls vertically, so the head scrolled away with the outer area (audit: head 172 → −28 px after a 200 px scroll). Fix: wrappers dropped; audit / fleet audit / usage → `fpc-panel class="flex-grow-1" flush scroll` (the body scrolls, the **pager footer stays pinned** below it — the "tfoot" the user expected); git commits → panel `scroll` + `--fpc-panel-scroll-max-height: 28rem` (also avoids the sticky panel header and the thead both sticking at `top: 0` of the md scroller); lanes → `scrollX`; wizard modal → plain bordered box (modal body scrolls). Safety net in `styles/_tables.scss`: `.table-responsive:has(> .fpc-table--sticky-head|foot) { overflow: visible }` + a scrolling lane body holding a sticky table also scrolls sideways.
- **Root cause 3 – master-detail stacked** (`loadweaver-master-detail`, all list | detail sections at ≥ xl): the global `.fpc-routed-outlet > router-outlet + *` rule (0,1,1) beat the component's `:host` (0,1,0) and set `flex-direction: column`, so the list's `flex: 0 0 30rem` became a 480 px tall band with the detail below it. Fix: `:host(.lw-md) { flex-direction: row }`; `.fpc-md` also states `flex-direction: row`.
- `fpc-data-table` was fine: `.fpc-data-table__scroller` is the bounded scroller, head stays put (tasks, cluster contents); its pager sits outside the scroller (pinned), so no tfoot move was needed.
- Verified after the fix (scroll 200–400 px, head `top` unchanged, foot / pager bottom unchanged): audit (1400×800 and 400×760; head 172 → 172, pager 767 → 767), tasks + cluster contents data tables (rows cloned in the test DOM), injected 60-row sticky head + foot tables (with and without a `.table-responsive` wrapper) in lane bodies (sessions, members, backups) and `.fpc-md__scroll` (git, certificates): head at the body top, foot at the body bottom. Plans / plan detail: list and detail side by side at 1400, one lane at 1100. Other tables had no data in the local cluster (structure checked in the templates).
- Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean (ui-components, feature-console); jest `--maxWorkers=1` feature-console audit / usage / git / backups / files / fleet / sessions / master-detail — 20 suites / 117 tests green; ui-components board-lane / data-table / panel suites green. jsdom applies no component styles, so the layout fixes are covered by the visual checks, not specs. Catalog "Sticky tables" paragraph extended.

### Uniform table heads (2026-10-28)

User: sortable vs. non-sortable heads looked different (`fpc-data-table`'s sort `<button>`, plain `.table` heads in browser-default bold / body bg). Now one head-cell style in `ui-components/styles/_tables.scss` for every `.table > thead > tr > th` (`:where`, zero specificity): 0.875rem / 600 / 1.25rem, nowrap, middle, `--bs-tertiary-bg` via `--bs-table-bg` on `thead` (so sticky heads stay opaque tertiary); knobs `--fpc-table-head-*`. Shared `.fpc-table__sort` control (inherits font / colour / alignment, no padding / border / bg; focus-visible ring) + `.fpc-table__sort-icon` (always rendered so space is reserved; `bi-arrow-down-up` shown on hover / focus, caret while sorted; before the label in `text-end` columns). `fpc-data-table` uses it (its own `thead th` / `.fpc-data-table__sort` rules dropped; `aria-sort` stays on the `th`, none on check / more cells). Divergent overrides removed: Decabill invoices + admin-billing head rows (`small text-body-secondary`). Landing pricing / comparison matrices (Forepath, Loadweaver, Agenstra, Decabill) opt out via `.fpc-table--plain-head`. No other sortable heads exist outside `fpc-data-table`. Spec: sort control classes / reserved indicator / `aria-sort`. Verified headless on the dev server (`/activity/tasks` data-table vs `/activity/audit` plain table): identical computed head styles. Follow-ups (user): (1) head padding was still different (data-table compact 4px vs plain 8px) → shared `--fpc-table-head-padding-y/-x` (`0.5rem 0.5rem`) on `.table:not(.fpc-table--plain-head) > thead > tr > th`, regardless of `table-sm`; data-table compact rule now `> :not(caption, thead)`. A per-density head padding was tried, then dropped on user feedback: the roomier head padding applies in both densities, compact only tightens body rows. Verified headless in both densities: `/activity/tasks` and `/activity/audit` heads 8px padding / 36.5px high (first column 16px left only from `fpc-panel--flush`'s edge inset, same as its body cells). (2) Audit entry-number column (`#` / `seq`) removed from Activity › Audit and Fleet › Audit tables (colspan 6 → 5); the number moved into the expanded entry details (`#seq` before the hash / below the JSON); chain verification unchanged. Object history is a list without the number; Agenstra / Decabill audit tables have no such column. No i18n change (the `#` head had no unit). Spec: audit page has 5 heads / cells, details show `#seq`.
(3) Superseding (1): uniform cell padding per density for head / body / foot alike — `--fpc-table-cell-padding-y/-x` (normal 0.5rem, `body.fpc-density-compact` 0.25rem) on `.table:not(.fpc-table--plain-head) > :not(caption) > * > *` (beats Bootstrap / `table-sm`); the head-only padding vars and data-table's compact padding rule are gone (`fpc-data-table__table--compact` stays as a hook, row height still from `FpcDensityService`). Landing tables stay opted out; the `fpc-panel flush` 1rem first / last column inset stays (no conflict). Verified headless: normal 8px everywhere (head 36.5px), compact 4px everywhere (head 28.5px), tasks = audit; neither page has a tfoot (same selector).
(4) User revision of (3): head cells keep the roomier vertical padding in both modes — `--fpc-table-head-padding-y` (0.5rem) on `thead > tr > *`, horizontal `--fpc-table-cell-padding-x` per mode; body / foot unchanged from (3). Verified headless: head 36.5px in both modes (compact head `8px 4px`), compact body 4px all sides, tasks = audit.

### Task dock fixes (2026-10-28)

- **Root cause "tab bar vanishes on Events"**: the `fpc-tab-group` sat in the dock _body_, a `display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: auto` scroller; the tab group's host is `min-height: 0` with the default `flex-shrink: 1`, so as soon as the (long) events list overflowed, the flex algorithm shrank the tab group to **0 px** instead of scrolling (reproduced headless: tall body content → tab group height 0). Tasks was usually short, so only Events showed it. Fix: (a) Tasks / Events moved into the dock's header strip (never scrolls); (b) `fpc-dock-panel__body` is now a plain block scroller (`display: block`), so projected children can never be squeezed; header is `flex: 0 0 auto`, wraps (`flex-wrap`, `gap 0.25rem 0.5rem`), `padding 0.25rem 0.5rem`, min 2.5rem; actions `margin-left: auto`. `bodyId` is public (for `aria-controls`).
- **Toolbar**: one row — title toggle, Tasks / Events, spinner left; filter (`fpc-search-field sm`, 14rem) + "Open all" right; wraps under the triggers on phones. "Open all" = icon-only `fpc-button` (secondary sm, `bi-eye`, `ariaLabel` + `title` from `@@lwConsoleHistory-openAll`, 32×32 like the filter height), still routes to `/activity/tasks` or `/activity/audit` per view. Filter + Open all only while the dock is open.
- **Collapsed = no selection** (user follow-up): Tasks / Events are dock triggers (`btn-group-sm` buttons, not `role=tab`): `aria-pressed` only while open (`selected = open ? tab : null`), `aria-expanded` = dock open, `aria-controls` = dock body id. Collapsed: click opens directly on that view; open: other view switches, the selected one closes (the panel's chevron toggle also closes → no selection). Running count badge on Tasks (`task-dock-running`, visually-hidden "running"); no unread count on Events (the feed has no read state; events load only while open). Open / height persistence unchanged (`lw.dock`). Phones: the collapsed strip above the bottom bar _is_ the sheet trigger (both entries); the full-screen sheet body now fills the sheet (`flex: 1 1 auto; height: auto`) and the resize gutter is hidden.
- Checks: jest `--maxWorkers=1` nav/tasks (new spec: collapsed no selection + aria-expanded / aria-controls, open on Events with 40 events, repeated switching keeps triggers + filter in the header, same trigger / chevron close, Open all by aria-label / title / `bi-eye`), container, dock-panel — green; `tsc --noEmit` feature-console + ui-components clean. Headless on the dev server (1400×800, 700, 390; tall fake content injected in the test DOM): triggers at a fixed header position across 3× Tasks ↔ Events, min / max / mid resize and the phone sheet; collapsed → none pressed; keyboard Tab + Enter opens Events.
- **Follow-up (user)**: "Open all" removed (the `@@lwConsoleHistory-openAll` id stays — still used by `object-history`). Header now: left = chevron title + spinner; right = filter (open only, `margin-left: auto` in the growing header slot) directly left of the Tasks / Events group (actions slot). One row at 1400 (filter 1002–1226 px, triggers 1234–1392); at 390 title + filter on row 1, triggers wrap right-aligned to row 2 (header 72 px); collapsed strip one row. Spec asserts triggers in the actions slot, filter in the header slot, no Open all. Behaviour / ARIA / badge unchanged; jest nav/tasks + container green, tsc clean, headless 1400 + 390 re-checked.
