### Fix: activity pages runtime errors (2026-10-28)

User: `/activity/drafts` and `/activity/plans` "throw some error killing the content". Reproduced headless on the dev server (cluster mode, and fleet mode emulated in the browser: `mode: "fleet"` kept, relay calls answered from the CP with its dev key, `GET views` 403 like the user's fleet — the running fleet / CP containers answer `GET /drafts`, `GET /plans` with 200/304, relay rules for `drafts`, `drafts/:id`, `plans` (`project`, `status`, `limit`) and `plans/:id` are correct, so not an old-backend 404). Direct loads rendered; **SPA navigation** broke. Paths relative to `libs/domains/loadweaver/frontend/`.

- **Root cause 1 (both modes, all master-detail shells: plans, drafts, alerts, backups)**: entering a shell from another route (section tab Plans → Drafts, Audit → Plans, Tasks → Plans …) — `masterDetailId()` ran in the shell's constructor while the router hadn't advanced the child routes yet (`firstChild.snapshot` undefined) → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'paramMap')` in the factory → the navigation failed, the content area stayed empty and the URL on the old page. Only reloads / deep links worked. Fix `feature-console/src/lib/section/master-detail.component.ts`: `child?.snapshot?.paramMap` (null then; the shell re-reads on `NavigationEnd`).
- **Root cause 2 (fleet mode)**: `FleetRelaySocket` lacked `removeAllListeners()` — the teardown of every live feature (plans / topology / logs effects, the Workspace draft store) threw `UnsubscriptionError: socket.removeAllListeners is not a function` when leaving / switching a plan (plans list → detail re-connects the live socket). Fix `data-access-console/src/lib/sockets/fleet-relay-socket.ts`: `removeAllListeners(event?)` (= `off`).
- **Drafts in fleet mode**: the open drafts were loaded once at sign-in — at the fleet level against `clusters/none/api/drafts` (400, seen in the fleet log) and never re-read on opening / switching a cluster. `container.component.ts`: connect only with an active cluster (fleet mode); a cluster switch disconnects, clears and reconnects the draft store.
- **Graceful errors**: `WorkspaceDraftStore.loadError` (the failed open-drafts load; `error` stays the tray's last action); Activity › Drafts shows `fpc-alert` (`drafts-error`) for the shown list (open → `loadError`, submitted / discarded → the page's own load) instead of "No drafts". Plans already showed the facade error. Browser check with relay 404s (`GET drafts|plans is not relayed`): both pages show the alert "Not available through the fleet …" inside the intact page.
- Specs: `section/master-detail.spec.ts` (enter the shell from another route, list + empty / detail with id — fails without the fix with the same TypeError), `sockets/fleet-relay-socket.spec.ts` (teardown `removeAllListeners` + `disconnect`), `drafts/drafts.spec.ts` (alert instead of empty state, open + discarded), `workspace/workspace-draft.store.spec.ts` (`loadError` set / cleared).
- Browser sweep (fleet emulation + cluster mode, 1400×800): Plans ↔ Drafts ↔ Audit ↔ Tasks via tabs, plan detail lane, draft detail lane, Observe Health → Alerts, Operate Terminals / Sessions → Backups, Delivery Git / Updates / Certificates (cluster mode), unknown-id deep links of plans / drafts / alerts / backups — no page errors any more. No alerts / backups / certificates / rollouts data in the dev cluster, so their detail lanes were checked via unknown-id deep links only. Seen but not changed: `GET views` 403 in the user's fleet (saved views need a cluster that trusts the fleet's identity claim — shown inside the Views dropdown, not on the page), `git/sops/recipient` 409 (master key not unsealed — expected).
- Checks: jest `--maxWorkers=1` feature-console container / plans / drafts / section / workspace (9 suites green), data-access-console fleet-relay-socket (5); `tsc --noEmit` feature-console + data-access-console lib clean.

### Uniform control heights (2026-10-28)

User: (1) pagers — page-size select, prev / next arrows, page numbers must be one height; (2) generally, controls in a row (buttons, groups) must be uniform. Measured headless before: Activity › Audit pager arrows 28.4 px vs page-size select 32.4 px (`.pagination-sm` pads 0.25rem, `form-select-sm` uses the chrome's 0.375rem); page-header icon actions 37.6 px; plans search strip 36 vs filter toggle 40; bordered sm search 32 vs `btn-sm` 32.4; terminals picker fields 4 px off the segmented toggle / button line.

- **Shared scale** `ui-components/styles/_controls.scss` (forwarded from `styles/index.scss`): `--fpc-control-height-sm` / `-md` / `-lg` / `-header`. Comfortable = natural chrome metrics (sm 2.0234rem = `btn-sm`, md 2.5625rem, lg 3.2656rem, header 2.35rem) so non-density apps (Agenstra, Decabill, landings, docs — none use `FpcDensityService`) keep their button / input heights; `body.fpc-density-compact`: sm 1.875rem, md 2.25rem, header 2.125rem. `.btn` (raw + `fpc-button`, `.btn-group-sm/-lg`, `.input-group-sm/-lg` buttons, `fpc-tab-group` options), `.form-control` (not textarea / file / color / plaintext), `.form-select` (not multiple / size), `.input-group-text` and `.pagination .page-link` derive their block padding from the resolved tier (`--fpc-control-h`); page links are square (`min-width` = tier). `p-0` / `py-*` utilities still win. Inside `.fpc-page-header` / `.fpc-object-header__head` `--fpc-control-height-sm` = header tier (text `sm` buttons, selects match the icon-only actions); `.dropdown-menu` inside keeps sm.
- **Components**: `fpc-button` icon-only square = `var(--fpc-control-height-sm/-md/-lg)` (`xs` 1.5rem; the per-context `:host-context` page-header / object-header / dropdown overrides are gone); chip-as-control now only for a lone badge (`:has(.fpc-button__content > fpc-badge:only-child)`, badge sm tall) — a label + count badge ("Layers [2]", topology) keeps button padding (was flattened). `fpc-pager` / `fpc-pagination`: hard-coded `min-width: 2.375rem` dropped (scale handles it). `fpc-search-field`: strip = tier (`--fpc-search-field-height`), new host classes `--lg` / `--bordered` (bordered inner = tier − 2 borders). `fpc-typeahead-select`: same (always bordered). ### Postgres bootstrap with the final config (user decision 2026-10-27 evening)

Spec differences found between `bootstrap` (address 127.0.0.1, no CA, no platform backups) and the first apply: `POD_IP` (loopback → overlay), `SSL_CERTIFICATE` / `SSL_PRIVATE_KEY` (content, cluster CA), the WAL-G env (`platformBackups`). Membership itself was already out of the spec (`LOCAL_ETCD_HOSTS`).

- **POD_IP removed** from the Spilo spec: Spilo's `configure_spilo.py` only reads it under Kubernetes (`USE_KUBERNETES`); for `SPILO_PROVIDER=local` the connect address comes from the host name — it had no effect except the re-create. (Clone spec unchanged.)
- **TLS from files**: constant `SSL_CERTIFICATE_FILE` / `SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` = `/home/postgres/pgdata/tls/server.{crt,key}` (`<stateDir>/postgres/tls`, `SPILO_TLS_FILE_ENVIRONMENT`). Bootstrap: the agent creates the directory (Spilo owner), Spilo generates its self-signed pair there (it never overwrites an existing key). Later: `installSpiloTls` writes the CA's certificate (0600, Spilo owner, atomic rename) only when it changed; if Postgres wasn't (re-)started in that reconcile the agent sends SIGHUP to the postmaster (`ManagedContainers.exec` new, `POSTGRES_RELOAD_COMMAND`, best effort — Spilo's own `SSL_TEST_RELOAD` cron, on because `SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` is set, reloads within 5 min). Certificate renewals no longer re-create Postgres either. The PITR clone keeps its env-based certificate.
- **WAL-G at bootstrap**: gateway constants + HKDF credentials moved to `util-agent-protocol/src/lib/platform-backup-gateway.ts` (`gatewayAccessKeyId`, `gatewaySecret`, `gatewayPortFrom`, `memberPlatformBackups`); the CP's `platform-backups.utils.ts` / `s3-gateway.rules.ts` re-export them, `platformBackupsRole` uses `gatewayPortFrom`. `JoinService.bootstrap` passes `platformBackups: bootstrapPlatformBackups(env, nodeName)` — exactly what the CP pushes for its first node (platform backups are on by default). The bootstrap API therefore also listens on the gateway; WAL archiving fails (retried by Postgres) until the object store exists.
- **Membership changes**: nothing membership-dependent is in the Spilo spec any more; rule recorded in loadweaver.md 3.2 (future membership-dependent Patroni settings via `PATCH /config` or a rolling restart, leader last after a switchover).
- **Not changed**: etcd is still re-created once on the first apply (loopback → overlay binding; the overlay doesn't exist at bootstrap) — Patroni loses its DCS for those seconds (`retry_timeout` 10 s → a short demotion is possible); the API is re-created (TLS / gateway / log store env), stateless. DR `--restore` still starts on loopback without platform backups (re-create on its first apply as before).
- Specs: `join/bootstrap-determinism.spec.ts` (new, 3: bootstrap role vs first-apply role → same Postgres hash; 1 → 3 members + draining + witness + log store + new certificate → same hash; gateway port override), `postgres-tls.spec.ts` (file env, same hash with / without a certificate; `installSpiloTls` writes / skips / ownership), `control-plane.spec.ts` (no `POD_IP`), `control-plane-role.handover.spec.ts` (reload command, never fails), `managed-containers.spec.ts` (`exec`), CP `platform-backups.utils.spec.ts` (CP push = `memberPlatformBackups`).
- Docs: `architecture/README.md` (`postgres-tls` row). loadweaver.md: 3.2 + 3.22 bullets, decision log rows; loadweaver.mmd State node.

### Verification

- Jest (`--maxWorkers=1`): node agent `control-plane/|join/|managed-containers` 11 suites / 61; CP lib (claim-admin, platform backups, backups, push-determinism, agent-stream, no-import / no-injection cycles, identity bridge, s3-gateway, platform-dr) 14 / 122; fleet lib 16 / 114; fleet app 2 / 6; CP app 3 / 9; util-agent-protocol 5 / 66 (+1 skipped). `tsc --noEmit` clean: CP lib + spec, node agent lib + spec, util-agent-protocol, CP + fleet app + spec. ESLint: 0 errors (4 existing-style non-null warnings in a spec).

Measure "nodes applied" (was ~150 s). Watch: the one etcd re-create on the first apply (Patroni DCS gap).

## Local dev nodes (2026-10-28)

Two real nodes in the local compose cluster (`loadweaver-control-plane-*`, API :3400, gRPC :7443), site `default`, as
Docker-hosted QEMU/KVM VMs like the VM lab — but **not** lab-labelled (`org.forepath.loadweaver.dev-node`, not
`org.forepath.loadweaver.vm-lab`), so lab cleanups leave them alone.

- **Names / addresses**: `lw-devnode-N` = 10.78.1.(10+N), tap-(N−1) (switch has 8 taps): `lw-devnode-1` (10.78.1.11),
  `lw-devnode-2` (10.78.1.12) running; `lw-devnode-3` (10.78.1.13) configured, **not created yet** (see below); containers `lw-devnode-switch` (bridge + taps + NAT in its own netns, 128 MiB), `lw-devnode-1` / `-2` (QEMU, `-cpu host` = nested KVM, 2 vCPU).
  Volumes: `lw-devnode-base` (private copy of golden `lw-vmlab-golden-94b93949b154`, so pruning lab goldens doesn't
  break the overlays), `lw-devnode-{1,2}-disk` (24 GB qcow2 overlay + cloud-init seed), `lw-devnode-state` (switch
  `/lab`: ssh key, `net.sh`, agent bundle). Image `lw-devnode-qemu:local` (= the lab QEMU image, re-tagged).
- **Memory** (2026-10-30, 3.43): **4096 MiB** guest per VM (`DEVNODE_MEM_MB`, default in `common.sh`), container
  limit +700 MiB = 4.7 GiB each; a member with the full role (etcd, Spilo, OpenSearch, CP API, Garage, registry) uses
  ≈ 2.6 GiB in the guest, the container ≈ 3.8 GiB. Was 2048 MiB (≈ 1 GiB RSS each when idle, no member role). `up.sh` refuses unless MemAvailable ≥ VMs + 5 GiB (`FORCE=1` overrides). **Stop
  them (`down.sh`) before VM-lab runs** — `run-lab.sh` needs ≥ 8 GiB available.
- **Agent**: the lab cluster build `m7-cluster-agent.js` (real agent + lab reconciler: no WireGuard/firewall/BIRD/
  ingress, static overlay routes; same as the M7 cluster specs), with the lab's +3 GiB capacity reserve patched to 0.
  Installed as `lw-agent.service` (`/opt/loadweaver/lw-agent.js run`, state `/var/lib/loadweaver`), components from
  `components.generated.sh` (runc, gVisor, gVisor-KVM; microVM unsupported: launcher image not loaded).
  **Since 2026-10-30 (3.43)** the bundle is built from the current tree and runs the full member role:
  `LW_LAB_LOG_STORE=1` in `lw-agent.service` keeps the log store (the lab entry drops it otherwise), and the lab
  reconciler isolates a failing control-plane layer like the real one. Images in every VM: etcd / Spilo / Valkey /
  Garage / registry / Kopia (pinned digests, from the golden image), OpenSearch 3.9.0 (pinned, pulled in the VM), the
  local CP image `ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-control-plane-api:latest` (`docker save | docker load`).
  **Rebuild** (code changed): `node ~/.cache/forepath-vm-lab/devnodes/build-agent.js ~/.cache/forepath-vm-lab/devnodes/bin/lw-agent.js`
  (= the M7 global setup's tsc + esbuild for `m7-cluster-agent.entry.ts` only; under `/tmp/uiq/tv/serial.sh`), CP
  image via `nx run loadweaver-backend-control-plane:api-container-image`, then `bash rebuild.sh [node…]`: recreates
  the VM containers with `MEM_MB` (disks / volumes / identity kept, never create.sh's disk setup), installs the
  bundle + `LW_LAB_LOG_STORE=1`, loads the CP image, pulls OpenSearch, powers the guest off. The node's CP traffic
  is blocked in the switch while it is rebuilt, so a stopped member never connects (and is never picked as the etcd
  bootstrapper) by being rebuilt. ~5 min per node.
- **Networking**: the compose CP only knows itself as `localhost` (`LOADWEAVER_PUBLIC_URL`, `GRPC_ENDPOINTS=localhost:7443`,
  TLS name `localhost`), so each VM runs `systemd-socket-proxyd` units on 127.0.0.1 / ::1 :3400 and :7443 → gateway
  10.78.1.1, which the switch DNATs to the docker host (172.17.0.1, the CP's published ports). The CP talks to the
  nodes only over the agent stream. After a restart the agent first tries the seeded fake members' overlay addresses
  (10.93.0.1–3), so it reconnects after ≈ 70 s.
- **Joined** via `POST /api/join-tokens {"site":"default"}` (dev API key) and `lw-agent.js join --server
http://127.0.0.1:3400 --name lw-devnode-N --endpoint-host 10.78.1.1N --label env=dev`. Result: both `active`,
  `connected`, `applyStatus: applied`, not control-plane members (the seeded members ams1-vm-01 / fra1-edge-01/02
  fill the membership; if those leave, a dev node would be promoted and its member role would fail — no CP image
  loaded).
- **Scripts** (`~/.cache/forepath-vm-lab/devnodes`; the `/tmp/devnodes` copy is gone, `/tmp` is tmpfs): `create.sh`
  (one-time, idempotent; run under `/tmp/lw-3a-lock.sh`; **never for an existing node whose container was removed:
  it re-creates the disk overlay** — use `rebuild.sh`), `rebuild.sh` (see Agent), `join.sh`, `up.sh`, `down.sh`
  (guest poweroff, disks and membership kept; nodes show disconnected; also stops the switch — to stop one node
  only, power its guest off: `vm <node> <<< 'systemd-run --on-active=1s systemctl poweroff'`), `status.sh [--fix]`
  (containers, memory, `GET /nodes`, CP ↔ overlay routes), `net-cp.sh [--check]` (see CP ↔ member overlay), `remove.sh`.
- **CP ↔ member overlay** (2026-10-30, live 3.43): the compose CP talks to Garage admin and the registry on the
  members' overlay addresses (10.93.0.9–11). **`net-cp.sh`** sets it up idempotently and prints only what it changed
  (`--check`: what it would change): connects the switch to the CP container's compose network (name from
  `docker inspect loadweaver-control-plane-api`; switch = 172.22.0.6 there), keeps the switch's default route on the
  docker bridge (`via 172.17.0.1 dev eth0`; a connect / restart can move it to eth1 → no NAT, the VMs lose DNS /
  internet), routes each `lw-devnode-*` overlay IPv4 from `GET /api/nodes` via the VM address (`ip_of`) in the switch,
  and the same /32s via the switch in the CP's netns (throwaway `lw-devnode-qemu:local` container with `NET_ADMIN` in
  `container:loadweaver-control-plane-api`); stale routes via the VMs / the switch (e.g. the old hand-made
  `10.93.0.0/24`) are removed. Called by `up.sh` and `rebuild.sh`; `status.sh` runs it with `--check`,
  `status.sh --fix` repairs. **Re-run after recreating / restarting the CP container** (its netns routes go with it).
- **Leaving cleanly**: `remove.sh` = `POST /nodes/<name>/drain` → `POST /nodes/<name>/leave` (console: Nodes →
  Drain → Leave) → disable the agent → remove containers and all `org.forepath.loadweaver.dev-node` volumes. A
  recreated CP database forgets them anyway; then just `remove.sh` (API errors ignored) and `create.sh` + `join.sh`.
- **N nodes** (2026-10-28, later): `common.sh` `NODES=(lw-devnode-1 lw-devnode-2 lw-devnode-3)`; add a name to grow.
  `DEVNODES="lw-devnode-3"` limits any script to a subset; up/down/status/remove skip nodes whose container doesn't
  exist. `create.sh` and `up.sh` refuse unless MemAvailable ≥ (VMs to start) × 2748 MiB + 5 GiB (`FORCE=1`).
  Third node: `/tmp/lw-3a-lock.sh bash /tmp/devnodes/create.sh lw-devnode-3 && bash /tmp/devnodes/join.sh lw-devnode-3`.
  It was **not started**: MemAvailable was 5.9–7.5 GiB with two nodes up and other jobs running (needs ≥ 7.7 GiB).
- **Quorum tests**: the control-plane membership is the 3 seeded demo members (`ams1-vm-01`, `fra1-edge-01`,
  `fra1-edge-02`, which don't exist, always disconnected); existing members are kept while active/cordoned, so dev
  nodes are never promoted and the real CP stays the compose container (no etcd/Postgres quorum anywhere). A real
  quorum test needs dev nodes as members: (1) load the CP image into every dev node (the lab's
  `loadImages(vm, [CP_IMAGE])`, i.e. `docker save ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-control-plane-api:latest | ssh … docker load`)
  and set `LOADWEAVER_CONTROL_PLANE_IMAGE` (+ `LOADWEAVER_MICROVM_LAUNCHER_IMAGE` if wanted) in `lw-agent.service`;
  (2) remove the demo members (drain → leave, or `confirm-lost` since they're disconnected) so `computeControlPlaneMembership`
  promotes the 3 dev nodes; (3) ≈ +2.5–3 GiB guest RAM per member (etcd, Postgres, CP API; the lab gave members 3 GiB
  and drops the log store) — i.e. 3 × ~3.5 GiB containers, more than this machine has free next to the user's stacks.
  Even then the compose CP stays the API the console talks to; member CPs on the nodes form a second, node-hosted
  control plane — a cleaner quorum setup is the lab's `startCluster` (bootstrap on a dev node, the others join).

### Branched fixes B: search focus (2026-10-28)

- **Sources of the glows:** Bootstrap `.form-control:focus` (box-shadow ring + border tint) and `.btn:focus-visible` on the clear button, plus the earlier keyboard ring, which was an inset `box-shadow` in the translucent `--bs-focus-ring-color` drawn over the strip. That ring read as a glow and did not look like one outline. The marketing (hero) variant also had its own `0 0 0 .25rem` focus glow. Nothing focus-related lives in `styles/_controls.scss` (heights only), the brand chrome or app `styles.scss`, so the fix is scoped to the two components.
- **`fpc-search-field`** (`search-field.component.scss`): the wrapper and every descendant (`*`, `*:focus`, `*:focus-visible`) get `box-shadow: none !important; outline: 0 !important`. The marketing input keeps `border-color: var(--bs-border-color)` on focus. The wrapper border, including the bottom edge, never changes on focus. Mouse focus shows only the caret.
- **Keyboard focus:** one solid `2px var(--bs-primary)` outline on a wrapper `::after` (`z-index: 6`, above the focus-raised input). It shows only when `.fpc-field-kbd-focus:focus-within` is true (the origin is tracked in `focus-origin.ts`, because text inputs match `:focus-visible` on mouse focus too) or when the wrapper `:has(> clear:focus-visible)`. On a bordered strip the ring sits just outside the 1px border (`inset: -border-width`, `border-radius: inherit`). In a lane search band or list toolbar strip, which are borderless and edge-to-edge, it is drawn 2px inside so it is not clipped. The marketing container gets `border-radius: .75rem` so the ring follows the input.
- **`fpc-typeahead-select`** (`typeahead-select.component.scss`): the same rules apply to `.fpc-typeahead-select__input-group`, including the spinner and `__clear`, with the same band/toolbar variant. No TS changes were needed; the existing `keyboardFocus` signals are kept.
- Not verified yet (no build or browser run). To check: Tab vs click into the search in a lane band, a list toolbar, a form/modal, and on the landing hero, plus Tab to the clear button.

### Dropdown positioning fix (2026-10-28)

Bug: portaled `fpc-dropdown` menus (`appendTo="body"`: column chooser, Views, ⋮) often opened far to the left of their
trigger. Cause: `place()` measured the menu while it still carried its previous inline `left` (or the inline-mode
anchoring `top: 100%` / `inset-inline-end: 0` from the component CSS), so its shrink-to-fit width was under-measured and the
end-alignment math (`trigger.right - width`) plus the clamp went wrong; it anchored on the host element (which can be
stretched by layout classes) instead of the trigger button; `minWidth` was applied only after the width was read; and the
position was computed once, so late size changes (fonts, async items) never re-placed it. Fix (`ui-components/dropdown`):
measure in a neutral fixed state at the viewport origin (min-width applied first), anchor on the projected trigger's
`getBoundingClientRect()`, align start (left = trigger left) or end (right = trigger right); new default
`alignment="auto"` = `end` when the trigger is in the right half of the viewport (portaled only; inline mode unchanged,
`auto` = start there), flip above when below has less room than above, cap height + scroll when neither fits, clamp into
the viewport with 8 px margin; re-place on the next animation frame, on menu `ResizeObserver`, on scroll (capture, except
scrolling inside the menu) and resize. Portaled menus get `.fpc-dropdown__menu--portaled` (`position: fixed; inset: auto;
margin: 0; transform: none`) instead of `.dropdown-menu-end`. Column chooser / Views / object-header ⋮ already pass
`alignment="end"`. Not yet verified (no tests/builds run).

### Breadcrumb style (2026-10-28)

`fpc-breadcrumbs` / `fpc-breadcrumb-item` (shared, all apps) got a calm chip look, styled in `breadcrumbs.component.scss`
with `::ng-deep` so hand-written crumbs (`fpc-object-header`) share it: ancestors are quiet chips (small radius, 5 %
emphasis tint, `--bs-secondary-color` text; hover 10 % tint + body text, pressed / menu-open 14 %; inset 2 px
`--bs-focus-ring-color` keyboard ring because trails clip their overflow); the current item is plain semibold body text
(`aria-current="page"`, no link); separators muted (`--bs-tertiary-color`): `divider="›"` (also `>`, `»`, `chevron`)
draws a small `bi-chevron-right`, any other divider stays text (`/` path-style trails, the default). One line, row height
`--fpc-control-height-sm` (density-aware), chips slightly lower; crumbs truncate (max 16 rem / 14 rem in `sm`) with the
full name as `title` (now defaults to the label). New, backward compatible: `collapse` (default on, ≥ 3
`fpc-breadcrumb-item`s) measures on resize / label change and folds middle crumbs (root side first) into an "…" chip
(body-portaled `fpc-dropdown`, `overflowLabel` "Show hidden levels") after the first crumb; menu rows emit the item's
`selected` with a cancelable event and otherwise follow `href` / `routerLink`. Item: optional `icon` (muted kind icon),
`routerLink` + `queryParams`, and a `<button>` crumb when neither `href` nor `routerLink` is set (previously inert
text). Hand-written crumbs (object header) get the look but not the collapse — switching it to `fpc-breadcrumb-item
[routerLink]` would enable it. Stories: kind icons, collapsed, path style. Not yet verified (no tests/builds run).

### Object header uses breadcrumb items (2026-10-28)

`fpc-object-header` now renders its trail as `<fpc-breadcrumbs divider="›">` + `fpc-breadcrumb-item`s, so it gets the
"…" collapse too: linked ancestors pass `[routerLink]` / `[queryParams]` / `[title]` / `[icon]`, the last crumb is
`[active]="true"` (no link, `aria-current="page"`). Link-less ancestors deliberately stay a hand-written plain-text
`.fpc-breadcrumb-item` span (muted, no chip) instead of a component item, because the item would now render a dead
`<button>` firing `selected`; they are never collapsed. `FpcCrumb` input shape unchanged apart from a new optional
`icon`. The header's custom crumb SCSS (nowrap / truncation / link overrides) is gone; only the `min-width: 0` wrapper
remains. Spec queries `fpc-breadcrumb-item` (title on the host) and covers the link-less case; catalog row updated.
Not yet verified (no tests/builds run).

### Data table: fixed head, scrolling body (2026-10-28)

`fpc-data-table` (`libs/domains/shared/frontend/ui-components/src/lib/data-table/*`) no longer scrolls its head: a
`.fpc-data-table__grid` flex column holds [head block: column-head `<table>` + the search / actions toolbar row
(`[fpcDataTableHeadToolbar]` + `fpc-list-toolbar`), `flex: none`] → [`.fpc-data-table__scroller`: only the body
`<table>` (+ infinite sentinel, empty / no-matches state), `flex: 1 1 0%; min-height: 0; overflow: auto`] → pager
(unchanged, outside the grid). `0%` instead of `0` so auto-height hosts (`nested`, `d-block` consumers like fleet-ops
backups) don't collapse. Column alignment: both tables carry the same `<colgroup>` structure; the body keeps auto
layout and has an aria-hidden, zero-height sizer `<thead>` (head labels / sort icon / chooser width, nothing focusable)
so head texts still size the columns; a ResizeObserver (sizer cells, body table, scroller; re-attached in
`afterEveryRender` when the column set changes) copies the measured px widths into the head `<col>`s, sets the head
table width and `table-layout: fixed` (`fpc-data-table__table--measured`), and the body's vertical scrollbar width into
`--fpc-data-table-gutter` (padding on the head frame + toolbar row). Horizontal scroll: body `scroll` mirrors
`scrollLeft` to the head (`overflow: hidden`); head `scroll` (focus) and sideways `wheel` drive the body (listeners
outside Angular). A11y choice: one logical ARIA table — wrapper `role="table"` with `aria-label` / `aria-rowcount`
(moved off `<table>`), both `<table>`s `role="presentation"`, explicit `rowgroup` / `row` / `columnheader` / `cell`
roles on every section / row / cell, toolbar row = `role="row"` + `role="cell" aria-colspan`, empty state and
loading-more wrapped as row / cell; consumer `fpcDataTableFooter` rows without roles get `row` / `cell` / `rowheader`
set after render. Kept: sort buttons, select-all, column chooser (toolbar or head corner, sticky right), sticky first
column in both tables (head via `fpc-table--sticky-first` + `--sticky-head` for the corner layer), stacked cards
< 36rem (container moved from the scroller to the grid; head frame + sizer + chooser hidden), column priorities (both
tables), virtual scroll (viewport = body scroller, now without the head offset), expand rows, sticky tfoot, density,
edge insets, `--fpc-flush-bleed: 0` inside the grid. `stickyHeader` is now a no-op (still toggles the host class).
Removed: sticky-thead rules, `100cqi` toolbar-cell pinning. Spec: head-only `thead th` count, `[role="table"]`
rowcount, new structure test; catalog row + story text updated. `styles/_tables.scss` unchanged.

  `additionalFilters: { agentId }` (hits ordered by `orderItemsBySearchIds` over this agent's own runs, so foreign
  ids drop out; `total > 0` with no ids = empty page), else the fallback fetches this agent's runs (`limit=1000`)

### Loadweaver user names instead of ids (2026-10-29, user)

User: "Raw user IDs still show must be resolved the same way it is in the other applications." Closes the open
items of the data-list log (sessions / tunnels "User", plan approvals, deletion / cut-over requester + approver,
wallboard "Created by", fleet audit actor, access members, audit actor).

- **Pattern found (reused, no new one)**: Agenstra and Decabill resolve users **server-side** from the identity
  `users` table (`UserEntity` / `UsersRepository`) and return the email **next to** the id in the same DTO:
  Agenstra `createdByUserId` + `createdByEmail` (tickets), `authorEmail` (comments), `actorEmail` (ticket / page
  activity), identity `ClientUserResponseDto.userEmail` (workspace members); Decabill `userEmail` (admin projects /
  invoices / subscriptions, ids deduplicated before the lookup), `createdByEmail` (project tickets). The label is the
  **email** (the users table has no display name). No client-side users endpoint is used for this.
- **Visibility (same as the other apps)**: no extra rule beyond the record's own authz: the email is part of the
  record's response, so whoever may read the record sees it (Agenstra: any user with access to the workspace sees
  member / author / actor emails; Decabill admin lists: admins). In Loadweaver every lookup runs **after** the
  record filter (only ids of returned records are resolved; e.g. sessions filtered by project admin / auditor,
  plans by `planVisible`, deletions by scope read, members by `assertRead` / cluster role, audit by `auditScope`,
  plan socket patches only to sockets that may see the plan, fleet audit fleet-admin only).
  Fleet persons (`fleet:<iss>:<sub>`) only by a **verified** email (an unverified fleet claim is never shown as a
  name: no look-alike approvers).
- **Backend (control plane)**: new `fleet-identity/user-emails.ts`: `userEmails(manager, ids)` = one `In(...)` query on
  `UserEntity` (uuid ids, `user:<id>` prefix stripped) + one on `FleetPersonEntity` (fleet ids), never per row;
  `emailOf(map, id)`; `userIdsByEmail(manager, email)` for the audit actor filter. DTO fields added (all
  `string | null`, `null` = deleted user / not a user):
  `TerminalSessionDto.userEmail`, `TunnelDto.userEmail` (`live-records.service`); `PlanResponseDto.createdByEmail` +
  `approvals[].userEmail` (`dto/plan.dto.ts` `toPlanResponse(plan, approvals, emails)` + `planUserIds`; every
  `PlansService` response through `respond()`, list / socket snapshot / poll batched per page / poll);
  `DeletionDto.requestedByEmail / approvedByEmail` (`backups.service`); `PlatformCutoverDto.requestedByEmail /
approvedByEmail` (`platform-cutover.service`); platform status `retentionRequest.requestedByEmail /
approvedByEmail` (`platform-backups.service`); `VmCommandDto.requestedByEmail` + `powerDetail.changedByEmail`
  (`virtual-machines.service`); `WallboardTokenDto.createdByEmail` (`health/wallboard.service`);
  `ProjectMemberDto` / `ClusterMemberDto` = entity + `userEmail`, `createdByEmail` (`access/project-access.service`,
  `controllers/access.controller` return types); `AuditEntryDto.actorEmail` (only `actorType: 'user'`, not in the

### Decabill server paging (2026-10-29, user)

User: "Decabill paging should be done." Every Decabill `fpc-data-table` over a server collection that still paged on
the client (facades batch-loaded everything, see DB-2 "Open") is now `paging="server"` with replace-page facades in
the DB-1 pattern (state `total` / `page` / `pageSize` or `hasMore`, `billingPageWindow`, one request per page, batch /
accumulate actions + effects removed incl. route registrations). project-board/\* untouched (other owner).

- **Helper** `feature-billing-console/src/lib/shared/server-paging.ts` `dbServerPaging`: new `url` option (key prefix)
  → `fpcListQueryState` syncs search / page / size to the URL (`q` / `p` / `n`, prefixed per tab: `act-` / `hist-`,
  `pend-` / `hist-`, `open-` / `hist-`, `bo-`; nested / modal tables without URL); a change of a tracked filter goes
  back to page 1 (one load). Specs: filter → page 1, URL seeding. Sort stays client-side within the page, as on the
  six DB-1 lists (no list toolbar offers a server sort).
- **Lists (before → after)**
  - Admin promotions: batch-load + client → server, `total` (`GET /admin/billing/promotions?limit&offset&search`,
    already paginated). Redemptions modal (nested): batch → server, `total` (`:id/redemptions`), page 1 per opened
    promotion, other promotion starts empty. Create / bulk Deactivate reload the current page.
  - Admin customer profiles / supplier profiles: batch → server, `total` (endpoints already paginated). Bulk Recompute
    trust / Delete, create / edit / delete modals reload the current page.
  - DATEV exports: batch → server, `total`; scope tab (tenant view / unified) is a tracked filter (page 1, one
    request). Queued-export polling no longer depends on the shown page: one request per queued (scope, year)
    resolves placeholders (`resolveQueuedDatevExports`), then the current page reloads; trigger reloads the current
    page. Bulk Download changes no data (no reload).
  - Customer promotions (Active | History): batch → server, `total` (`/promotions/active`, `/promotions/redemptions`);
    only the shown tab loads; redeem reloads the current page.
  - Customer offers (Pending | History): unpaged API → server, `total`; accept / decline reload the current pages.
  - Customer invoices (Open & overdue | History): whole list → server, `hasNext` (array API with limit / offset,
    `limit + 1` like customer subscriptions); create / payment-return poll reload the current page.
  - Backorders tab (subscriptions page): batch → server, `hasNext` (`limit + 1`), `status=pending,retrying`; bulk
    Retry reloads the current page. Overview only needs the load error (count from the summary): page 1.
  - Project detail time entries (nested): batch → server, `total` (endpoint already paginated); bulk Delete / bill time
    reload the current page. Ticket time entries (project board) unchanged.
  - Admin billing invoice audit (customer + supplier, nested): one request with the service default 20 → server,
    `total` (endpoints already paginated), like the admin-offers audit table.
  - Admin subscriptions usage-meter modal, meter entries (nested): unpaged → server, `total`; create / bulk Delete
    reload the current page.
- **Endpoint changes** (authorization unchanged everywhere: same guards / roles / scopes, `ensureAdmin`, user and
  tenant scoping; paging only narrows the rows within the existing scope):
  - `GET /offers/pending`, `GET /offers/history`: optional `limit` / `offset` (ParseIntPipe, default 10 / 0, max 100)
    → `PaginatedCustomerOffersResponseDto { items, total, limit, offset }`; count + page in SQL, still per `userId` /
    tenant / status; search unchanged (search-index ids capped at 1000, then paged in SQL). Only consumer: Decabill
    offers service.
  - `GET /backorders`: limit capped at 100, new optional `status` (comma list, validated, 400 on unknown), still the
    caller's own backorders.
  - `GET /admin/billing/subscriptions/:id/meter-entries`: `limit` / `offset` (default 10 / 0, 1–100) →
    `PaginatedUsageMeterEntriesResponseDto`; repository keeps the tenant filter; openapi.yaml updated. Only consumer:
    this admin page.

### Progress as rows, freed columns (2026-10-29, user)

- **Agenstra pattern found** (`feature-agent-console/src/lib/chat/chat.component.html`, workspace / environment create + update): `fpc-progress` with `height="0.375rem"`, `[striped]` + `[animated]` while running, default primary tone; in the add / update modal footers a `small` `role="status" aria-live="polite"` block: one text line "Operation: step" left + "NN%" right (`d-flex justify-content-between mb-1`), the bar below; in table cells the bar alone under the name. No own component (inline markup); the shared updates manager (`feature-updates`) has no bar.
- **Shared component**: new `fpc-progress-row` (`ui-components/src/lib/progress-row/`, exported, catalog row, stories, spec) composing `fpc-progress`: slim 0.375rem bar, `label` (status / step text, truncates), optional `status` badge, `valueText` (default the percentage; `''` none), `state` running / success / failed / paused / idle → primary / success / danger / warning / secondary (`variant` overrides, e.g. warning for a running rollback), striped + animated only while `running`; `layout` `stacked` (Agenstra: text above the bar) or `inline` (text · bar · aside on one line from md, stacked on phones); text line is a polite live region (`live`); bar `role="progressbar"` + `aria-valuenow` / min / max / `aria-label` (`ariaLabel`, default `label`). Slots `[fpcProgressRowAside]` (time, small toggles) and default content (details below). Agenstra left as is: its usages are a bare bar in table cells (not a row) and two modal footers whose inline markup already is the pattern; swapping adds a host element and Agenstra spec churn for no visual change.
- **Plan detail** (`/activity/plans/:id`): the progress lane (`grow 0 0 420px`, lane header "Apply progress" / "Rollback progress", on every tab) is gone; the progress is a full-width row directly under the page header (`border-bottom px-3 py-2`, `layout="inline"`): step text · bar · percent · start time · "Nodes (n)" disclosure; cause ("Rolled back because") and failure lines under the bar; the per-node table (state · node · layers · error) opens under the row (`max-height 16rem`, scrolls). Bar tone: failure / failed / rollback-failed → danger, running → primary striped (rollback warning), applied → success, else neutral; aria label stays "Apply progress" / "Rollback progress". Phone lane tabs no longer carry a progress lane (`PlanLane` `progress` → `diagnostics`). Network tab: Network effect and Compiler diagnostics are two lanes side by side from md (count badge on diagnostics, empty state "No compiler diagnostics"), phone lane tabs Network effect / Compiler diagnostics. Live updates, cancel / apply / approve / discard and their gating unchanged (header actions).

### Loadweaver resource create/edit → modals (2026-10-29, user)

User: "rework Loadweaver to follow the modal-heavy UI concept that the other applications follow already … make sure resource creation becomes a modal (kinda like the order flow in Decabill and workspace creation in Agenstra) … moving the resource creation and editing over to modals could already hold huge value."

- **Concept found**:
  - _Decabill order flow_ (`subscriptions.component.html`, "Order plan" / "Change configuration") is one `fpc-modal size="xl"`. A step indicator sits on top (own `order-stepper` markup: numbered, active / complete), the body is `@switch (getActiveOrderWizardStepId())` (plan → infrastructure → configuration → **summary**) with a sticky summary sidebar. The footer has Back (`dark`) left, and Next / submit (primary) right.
  - Validation is per step: `canAdvanceOrderWizardStep()` blocks Next, and submit only on the summary step. The modal can't be closed while submitting (`closable` / `closeOnEscape` / `closeOnBackdrop` false), and on success it switches to a confirmation state with Close.
  - _Agenstra_ "Add Workspace" / "Update Workspace" (`chat.component.html`) are `fpc-modal size="lg"` forms (`fpc-form-field` + `fpc-form-control`, `ngForm` validity disables the submit, `[loading]` while saving). Editing is a second modal with the same form, pre-filled.
  - Neither app has a dirty-close confirmation. Shared parts: `fpc-modal` + `*fpcModalFooter`, `fpc-form-field` / `fpc-form-control` / `fpc-form-check`, `fpc-button(-group)`. Loadweaver's own precedent is the backup-restore modal: the shared `fpc-stepper` with `[showNavigation]="false"` and Back / Next in the modal footer. R14: footers right-aligned with [Cancel `dark`, Primary].
- **Inventory before**:
  - Create ▾ (top bar), the cluster / project header "+" and the list "+" buttons (backup policy / target, status page, maintenance window, DNS record) navigated to `/create/<kind>` (the full-page `LoadweaverCreateWizardComponent`: stepper + Form / YAML + Review + "Add to draft") or `/create` ("Other kind", the full-page `LoadweaverResourceEditorPageComponent` YAML editor).
  - Editing was the object page's **Spec tab** (the same editor page embedded: Form / YAML, compose editor, Draft vs live, problems lane, Save to draft, Plan now, Undo in draft). "Edit in draft", `e`, the status-page / maintenance-window row "Edit", the VM header "Edit" and the topology "drawn policy" link all opened `?tab=spec`.
- **Now (one resource modal, `objects/resource-modal.component.{ts,html}` + `ResourceModalService`, hosted once in the container)**:
  - Layout: `fpc-modal` xl with **Expand** to fullscreen, the shared `fpc-stepper` (footer navigation), and steps [Kind] → General → typed steps → Review.
  - The **Kind** step appears only when opened without a kind: the typed kinds as radios, every other published kind in a select.
  - **General** has name and project. The project select offers only projects the role may draft in, plus cluster-level only if allowed.
  - The typed steps come from the existing `wizardSteps()`.
  - **Review** shows a key-value summary (Change Create / Update / Rename, resource, project, target draft "Goes into"), the rename / Git-authoritative / error / "nothing changed" notes, the Draft vs live side by side (edit) or the YAML (create), and "Preview now".
  - Form | YAML at every step on one document: a Deployment's compose file has its own editor, and a problems table reveals each problem in its editor.
  - Compiler diagnostics are computed in the component (no mounted editor needed). Each issue is mapped to its step (`stepOfIssue`: metadata → General, `spec.<key>` / `missing property "<key>"` → the step owning the field, the rest → Review). They show as stepper marks and a step alert, and Review blocks on any error.
  - Footer: Form | YAML, Expand · Cancel · Back · [Plan now on Review; "Plan and open pull request" in Git-authoritative scopes] · Next / **Add to draft** (edit: **Save to draft**).
  - Draft semantics unchanged:
    - `draft.upsert(document)`; a rename also calls `draft.remove(original)`.
    - "Preview now" runs `runPreview()` and opens the tray. It defaults on for create and off for edit.
    - New and renamed resources open their object page.
    - "Plan now" calls `facade.plan({ documents, delete? })` and the modal closes once the plan opens.
  - Edit pre-fills from the draft's upsert document, else from a fresh `ResourcesService.get` (the store's `selected` isn't touched). A resource that can't be loaded shows an alert.
  - Dirty close: X, Escape, backdrop and Cancel with changes open "Discard changes?" (`fpc-confirm-dialog`, warning). Clean closes are direct, and closing is blocked while saving.
  - Enter moves on (not in textareas, the code editor, buttons, links or selects), and focus goes to the first control of each step.
  - Gating:
    - Create ▾ shows only if `mayCreateResources()` (a cluster role or developer+ in a project).
    - The header "+" shows only if the role may create there.
    - In the modal, `mayDraftResource(kind, project)` (new, shared with `mayDraft`) marks General / Review invalid and shows "Your role may not change …".
    - Edit entries keep the existing `workspaceActions()` gating.
- **Callers**:
  - The container `openCreate` and the object header "+" (cluster: choose the kind; project: a Deployment there) open the modal.
  - So do the list "+" buttons: backups `newPolicy()` / overview `newTarget()`, status pages `newPage()`, updates `newWindow()` and DNS `newRecord()`.
  - Edit opens it from `ResourcesContextService.run('edit')` (object header / ⋮ / Contents row menus / tree), the object page `e`, status pages, maintenance windows, the VM header "Edit" and the topology drawn-policy name (`editDrawn`).
- **Spec tab**: now `resources/resource-spec.component.ts`, read-only. It shows the drafted / live YAML, the "Changed in the draft" badge, a Draft vs live toggle, Undo in draft and **Edit**, which opens the modal. Edit and Undo appear only with the edit right.
- **Route decisions**:
  - `/create` and `/create/:kind` (`?project=`) stay as **deep links**: `openCreateModalGuard` opens the modal and redirects to the parent page (the project page with `?project=`, else the cluster page). This keeps the backend search action link `/create` and bookmarks working.
  - No full-page editor fallback: "Expand" (fullscreen modal, 65vh editors) covers large YAML.
  - `?tab=spec` stays as the read-only Spec tab ("Show YAML" links), and there is no edit route.
  - `console-nav` no longer lists `/create` as an active path. `createRoute()` stays for the deep-link format.
- **Shared ui-components (generic)**: `fpc-modal` has a new `guardClose` input and `closeRequest` output. With `guardClose`, a user close (X / Escape / backdrop) emits `closeRequest` instead of closing, while `open.set(false)` still closes. It's documented in `docs/catalog.md`, with a new `modal.component.spec.ts`. No data-table files were touched.
- **Other "fill and submit" forms (decision-12 leftovers)**: a read-only sweep of all Loadweaver templates found no inline record create / edit forms besides the resource editor / wizard, so nothing else was converted. Kept inline, with reasons:
  - The import page's per-row editors + Variables + build / create plan: the page is the form, and items are compared side by side with the plan lane.
  - Saved-views rename / "Save as": one-field inputs inside the views dropdown, where a modal over a menu would be heavier.
  - Not forms: the Git webhook / SOPS / platform-restore read-only fields, the topology trace and files path bar (query tools), and the filters.
- **Removed**:
  - `objects/create-wizard.component.ts`
  - `resources/resource-editor-page.component.{ts,html,spec.ts}` (the index export is now `resource-spec` + `resource-modal`)
  - `resourceEditLink` / `RESOURCE_EDIT_PARAMS`
  - i18n `lwConsoleResourceEditor-cancel` / `-newTitle` / `-noProject` / `-unsavedDraft`
- **i18n**:
  - +21 units: `lwConsoleResourceModal-*` and `lwConsoleWizard-stepKind`.
  - Changed texts: `lwConsoleShortcuts-edit` "Edit (opens the edit dialog)", `lwConsoleDraft-emptyHint` "Use Edit, Create or …", `lwConsoleCreate-other` "Other kind…".
  - en = de = 3999 units. The only remaining orphan (`lwConsoleFleetCompare-compare`) is unrelated.
- **Specs**:

### Topology: Bootstrap border colours, hover = primary border (2026-10-29, user)

- **Cause**: the graph stylesheet already used `palette.borderColor` / `palette.secondaryColor`, but `fpcReadBrandPalette` dropped the alpha of translucent tokens. Loadweaver's `--bs-border-color` is `rgba(15, 15, 17, 0.1)` (light) / `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)` (dark), so the canvas drew near-black / pure-white outlines. `--bs-secondary-color` (rgba at 0.75) came out as full body colour for the same reason.
- **Files**:
  - `libs/domains/shared/frontend/ui-components/src/lib/brand-tokens/brand-tokens.ts` (+ spec, `src/index.ts` exports): new `fpcCssColorAlpha` and `fpcCompositeColor`; `fpcReadCssColor(name, fallback, doc?, background?)` flattens a translucent value onto `background`; `fpcReadBrandPalette` now resolves `borderColor` (`--bs-border-color`) and `secondaryColor` (`--bs-secondary-color`) flattened onto `--bs-body-bg` at runtime. They are re-read on theme / brand change through the existing `fpcObserveBrandChanges`. Without a background, the old behaviour stays (alpha dropped). Monaco widget borders and line numbers, and the terminal's inactive selection, get the same calmer, correct greys.
  - `libs/domains/shared/frontend/ui-components/src/lib/graph-canvas/graph-canvas.styles.ts` (+ spec): hover (`node.fpc-hover`) only sets `border-color: primary` at the same hairline width, with no underlay halo. Selected (`node:selected`) uses the primary border at `FPC_GRAPH_STROKE.selected` (2 px vs the 1 px hairline), so it stays distinguishable from hover, with no halo. `edge:selected` uses a primary line with no underlay. `node:active, edge:active` have `overlay-opacity: 0`, as does the base `node` (no press / tap shadow). `core` has `active-bg-opacity: 0`. Plan-mark tone halos (create / update / delete) and status dots are state, not chrome, and stay as they were.
  - Keyboard focus: the canvas has no per-node keyboard focus; the container's `:focus-visible` is already a 2px primary outline (`graph-canvas.component.scss`), not a shadow, so it's unchanged.
  - Loadweaver `topology/` has no white/black literals for map elements. The only `rgba(0,0,0,.12)` is the phone inspector's bottom-sheet shadow, which is panel chrome and is unchanged.
- **Contrast**: dark mode draws an 8% white border on `#0f0f11`, which is about `#222224`. That's faint, but it's exactly what the app's panels and tables use (`--bs-border-color`), as asked. Light mode gives about `#e7e7e7`-ish on the warm body background.
- **Checks**:
  - jest ui-components (graph-canvas, brand-tokens, code-editor, terminal): 6 suites / 56 tests passed.
  - jest LW topology: 2 suites / 14 tests passed.
  - `tsc` ui-components lib: clean.
  - ngc LW strict: clean. Decabill: clean.
  - Agenstra: 2 pre-existing errors in files I didn't touch (`file-tree.component.ts` TS2352, `load-novnc-rfb.ts` unused ts-expect-error).
- **Open**: browser check pending, in light and dark: border subtlety on containers, hover with no jump, selected 2px vs hover 1px.
- **Follow-up: star layout of sites, ordered by links (2026-10-29, user)**:
  - `workspace/workspace-layout.ts` (`workspaceLayout`, the custom preset layout the topology map uses; same in the web worker): top-level items (sites, then site-less nodes / compounds) now sit in a star around the centre instead of in one row.
    - 1 item sits at the centre, 2 go left / right, and n ≥ 3 are spaced evenly on an ellipse, starting at the top and going clockwise.
    - Radius: from the largest item's diagonal plus a gap, R = d / (2·sin(π/n)). The ellipse is stretched only outwards (both semi-axes ≥ R), towards the viewport aspect, so boxes never overlap.
    - Inside each site nothing changed. Groups stay below the star; hostnames / addresses / outside peers stay in a column to the right.
  - Aspect: `topology-map.component.ts` measures the map host (width / height, in steps of 0.25, clamped to 0.5–3, default 1.6). It is part of the layout cache / localStorage key (`<key>@<aspect>`). Old stored layouts don't match the new key, so the map lays out again once.
  - There is no cluster / control-plane element in the model, so the star centre is empty and there are no centre→site spokes. A hub element would be a model change; it's left open.
  - Ring order by links instead of by name, for few crossings:
    - Edges are mapped to their top-level items and counted per pair. Greedy insertion takes the most-linked item first (name as tiebreaker) and puts each at the slot with the fewest chord crossings, then the shortest ring distance, then the earliest slot. Up to 4 relocation passes refine it.
    - The result is rotated so the first name sits at the top, with a fixed direction, so it is deterministic.
    - It only applies to 4–16 items. Above 16 the order stays by name (the cost grows with pairs²).
    - The worker now also receives the edge endpoints.
    - The cache key is still the visible ids plus aspect, so changing live flows don't reorder the map. A new link only takes effect when the visible set changes.
  - Edges: straight again, by measurement. A curved variant (`unbundled-bezier` with a per-edge bend) was built and then removed. The new order makes the samples chain, hub, pairs, 6-ring and two linked triangles crossing-free (0 segment intersections), while name order has crossings for chain and pairs. A full mesh of 4 keeps its single unavoidable crossing. The graph canvas uses `curve-style: bezier` with `control-point-step-size: 24`: single edges are straight, parallel edges between the same pair fan out as gentle arcs, and arrowheads follow the curve. Spokes would therefore be straight, if a hub is added later.
  - Specs: `workspace-layout.spec.ts` covers:
    - 1 site centred, 2 left / right;
    - n sites from the top clockwise, on one ellipse, no overlaps (including one site with 40 nodes);
    - no overlaps for 2–24 mixed sites × aspect 0.5 / 1 / 1.6 / 3;
    - the aspect stretch and determinism;
    - groups below, border items to the right;
    - a segment-intersection helper with 6 sample topologies: never more crossings than name order, 0 for the simple ones;
    - stability.

    `graph-canvas.styles.spec.ts` asserts `bezier` + step size and no `unbundled-bezier` / `taxi`. `graph-canvas.component.spec.ts` checks that parallel edges get the bezier style.

  - Checks:
    - jest ui-components (graph-canvas, brand-tokens, code-editor, terminal): 57/57.
    - jest LW topology + workspace: 11 suites / 74 tests passed.
    - `tsc` ui-components: clean.
    - ngc LW strict: clean. Decabill: clean.
    - Agenstra: only the 2 pre-existing errors (`file-tree.component.ts`, `load-novnc-rfb.ts`).
  - Open: browser check (star at different window aspects, fit-to-screen, plan halos, selection, phone inspector); optional cluster hub at the centre.

All three apps. Browser check pending (light / dark, hover on the active action).

### Fleet mode: automatic trust + cluster-only actions (2026-10-29, user)

User: "when the connection to the cluster can be verified, the trust should automatically be established … everything that is only available in the cluster console right now should either be automatically resolved in fleet mode or at least give us the option to resolve it from the UI". Plan: 3.24 "Automatic trust" / "Without the permission" / "Console, trust state" + decision log row 2026-10-29; `loadweaver.mmd` fleet edge.

- **Control plane** (`fleet-identity/`): `TrustedFleetsService.put` accepts a fleet's service user (PAT with `fleet:on-behalf-of`) after `access.assert(admin)` (+ the route's `cluster:admin` scope) and `verifySelfRegistration`: claim required, `iss` = path issuer, `role: admin`, signed by one of the keys in the body, `checkFleetClaim` (aud = own cluster id, `PUT` + URL + body hash, lifetime), existing entry only if the signing key is trusted there or `createdBy` = this service user, nonce consumed; `req.fleetIdentity` set for the audit actor. Fleet path merges keys (`mergeTrustedFleetKeys`, ≤ 3) and keeps an existing name; unchanged → no write / no audit (both paths); audit details `registeredBy: fleet`. List / delete stay native. `isTrustedFleetRegistration` — the identity interceptor skips `PUT /api/trusted-fleets/<issuer>` (service verifies). `GET /fleet-identity` adds `trustedKeys` / `trustedSince` for verified probes. PEM comparisons trim.
- **Fleet** (`feature-fleet`): `FleetTrustService` (`establish`, `syncAll`, `shouldAttemptTrust`, `trustRevoked`, `mergeRegistrationKeys`): GET `cluster` → pinned id check → probe (`already-trusted` / `unsupported`) → `PUT trusted-fleets/<issuer>` with the exact JSON bytes + `registrationClaim` (active key, subject = fleet admin or `fleet-system`); one-time token path (`GET trusted-fleets` + merge, token only as bearer of that call). Health JSON gains `identitySince`, `identityKeys`, `pinnedClusterId`, `trust` (last attempt: state, at, via, by, reason, credentialHint, keyIds) — no migration (jsonb). `FleetClustersService`: create / update (re-verified) pin the cluster id and `establishAfterVerification`; `poll` keeps pin + trust, marks `revoked` (+ audit `identity.trust-revoked`), auto-attempts once per credential + key set (failures after 15 min). `POST /clusters/:id/trust` (`fleet:admin`, `EstablishTrustDto.adminToken?`). Identity controller: `createNext` / `activate` → `syncAll` in the background. `FLEET_AUTO_TRUST` (`fleetAutoTrustEnabled`, default on). Inbox: `trust` items only when the fleet couldn't fix it (or auto off), link `/fleet/clusters/<id>`; `nativeUrl` only for approvals on untrusting clusters. Relay 403 text points to the fleet's cluster page.
- **Console**: cluster page fact **Trust** (Trusted · since …, Not trusted + reason, Establishing…, last attempt, "Establish trust…" → modal with optional one-time cluster-admin token, password field, cleared after every call); identity lane hint rewritten; inbox `trust` items open the fleet's cluster page; `/settings/trusted-fleets` notice links to the fleet's cluster page; texts without "register … in the cluster's own console" (backend messages, plan detail, search favourites, grant role hint, operations hint). i18n +29 / ~10 changed, `lwConsoleFleetCluster-approvals` removed: 4786 / 4786 en = de.
- **Inventory (cluster-console-only → resolution):** trust registration (cluster detail, identity lane, backend messages, plan detail, search / palette favourites, saved views 403, relay approval 403) → automatic + Establish trust; approvals in the inbox → through the fleet once trusted (native link only while untrusted); `/settings/trusted-fleets` → trust on the fleet's cluster page, list / remove stay native (revocation is the cluster's decision); grant role hint / operations hint → reworded. **Stay cluster-local**: recovery-kit shares (secret material of the backup key must not transit the fleet), VPN devices / linked Git accounts (personal resources of the signed-in account; through the fleet that's the service account), the installer download / node join (the new server must reach the cluster itself; join tokens already work through the fleet), legacy items created by the service user before claims (no person to count), older clusters without claim support (update the cluster).
- **Checks:** CP jest `fleet-identity/ | fleet-on-behalf | audit-log` 7 suites / 66 green (new: authorized, forbidden, claim refusals incl. other cluster / issuer / key / non-admin / replay, already trusted, rotation, no takeover, probe keys, merge; interceptor skip); fleet jest 18 suites / 135 green (new `fleet-trust.service.spec.ts`: authorized + audit, system actor, forbidden, mismatch, already trusted, rotation, one-time token not stored, unsupported, retired, poll rules incl. revoked; clusters poll auto-trust / revoked / nothing to do; inbox trust items + native links); frontend `fleet/` 3 suites / 30 green, plan-detail / search / container / backup-keys / overview + data-access backend-message / fleet green; `tsc --noEmit` CP lib + spec, fleet lib + spec, backend-fleet spec: 0; ngc LW strict 0 errors.
- **G6 (not run):** `apps/loadweaver/backend-fleet/src/integration/fleet-identity.integration.spec.ts` — native flow now runs with `FLEET_AUTO_TRUST=false`; new block "automatic trust (2026-10-29)": revoked not undone, Establish trust with the connection credential (both audits, createdBy = service user), idempotent, limited PAT forbidden + one-time token (never stored / logged), automatic on re-verification. Container rebuild (control plane + fleet) needed before.
- **Docs outside ownership:** `docs/loadweaver/features/fleet.md` (§ Approvals step 2 "Trust, natively", § Console) and `docs/loadweaver/console.md` still describe native-only registration — to update by the docs owner.

### Resource modal: close confirmation like Agenstra (2026-10-29, user)

- Agenstra pattern: `libs/domains/agenstra/frontend/feature-agent-console/src/lib/agent-modal.ts` (`swapToOverlayAgentModal` / `restoreUnderlyingAgentModal` + `AgentModalSwapState`), used in `chat.component.ts` (add-agent → isolation-downgrade confirm, plan detail, opencode config → layer file editor) and `tickets-board.component.ts` (ticket detail → delete confirm). The underlying `fpc-modal` closes (150 ms fade), the overlay (`fpc-confirm-dialog`) opens after `AGENT_MODAL_TRANSITION_MS`, the overlay's cancel / close re-opens the underlying one; its projected content stays mounted, so state survives. Agenstra-local, so not reusable; Agenstra left unchanged.
- Shared: `FpcModalSwap` + `FPC_MODAL_TRANSITION_MS` (`ui-components/src/lib/modal/modal-swap.ts`, exported, catalog `fpc-modal` row). `toOverlay(root)` hides (consumer binds `[open]="open() && !swap.suspended()"`), shows the overlay after the fade; `back(root)` closes the overlay and re-shows after the current event (the Escape that closed the confirm can't reach the reopened modal), then restores scroll offsets (`.modal`, `.modal-body`, scrolled content) and the focused control once the dialog takes its own initial focus (`focusin`, no polling); `finish()` closes for good; `reset()`. Spec `modal-swap.spec.ts` (5).
- Loadweaver `resource-modal.component.*`: `[open]="modalShown()"` (content stays mounted under `@if (isOpen())`), `requestClose()` dirty → `closeSwap.toOverlay(host)`, clean → close; confirm `(cancelled)="keepEditing()"` (Keep editing / X / Escape / backdrop) → `back()`; `discard()` → `finish()` + close (reset on the request change). Confirm is now `[danger]` (Discard = danger, Keep editing = dark Cancel; Agenstra destructive confirms use danger). Strings unchanged (no i18n change). Specs: 5 new (clean close, dirty Escape hides then confirm, one modal / backdrop, keep editing keeps step / name / focus, Escape on confirm keeps editing and re-asks, discard resets).
- Checks: ui-components jest modal 11/11 + tsc clean; LW resource-modal specs 20/20; LW strict ngc 0 errors; Agenstra ngc only the 2 known; Decabill ngc 0. Visual check not run (no :4602 server; coordinator: no own dev servers).

### Secret names list endpoint (2026-10-29)

- Route: `GET /api/projects/:project/secrets/names?q=<substring>&limit=<1..200>` (default 50), additive to the existing metadata list. Project is required and validated with the existing RFC 1123 label pattern; there is no cluster-level secret namespace. `q` is a case-insensitive literal substring, max 200 characters. Names are distinct, sorted ascending and limited in one SQL query.
- Response: `{ items: Array<{ name: string }> }`. The query selects names only; no values, ciphertext, wrapped keys, fingerprints, lengths or checksums are loaded or returned. Optional keys/versions/updatedAt/total are omitted. The store hard-deletes all versions (no soft-delete column); deleted names are excluded. No read/list audit was added, matching the existing convention.
- Permissions: exactly the existing secrets metadata read: `@RequireScopes('secrets:read')` plus `ClusterAccessService.assert(req, 'admin')`, before secret lookup. **Project membership alone does not authorize listing**, even for project admins/operators; denied callers receive 403. PATs do not inherit interactive admin JWT roles. Fleet reads use the existing global verified-claim interceptor and cluster-role cap against the service user; project grants alone cannot authorize this endpoint.
- Console API: exported `SecretsService.listNames(project: string, query: { q?: string; limit?: number } = {}): Observable<SecretNamesResponse>`, where `SecretNamesResponse = { items: { name: string }[] }`. Uses `ConsoleApi` so the current fleet relay endpoint is followed; no form wiring changed.
- Files: `libs/domains/loadweaver/backend/feature-control-plane/src/lib/controllers/secrets.controller.ts` (+ spec, request DTOs inline), `src/lib/services/secrets.service.ts` (+ spec) and `spec/openapi.yaml` under that backend lib; `libs/domains/loadweaver/frontend/data-access-console/src/lib/services/secrets.service.ts` (+ spec) and `src/index.ts` under that frontend lib.
- Verification: memory-gated Jest 30 (`--testPathPatterns`, `--maxWorkers=2`): backend secrets controller/service **2 suites / 100 tests passed**, frontend secrets service **1 suite / 5 tests passed**. Coverage includes names-only allowlisting, membership/role denials, PAT scopes, fleet caps, filtering/limit, deletion and DTO validation. Both touched libs passed memory-gated `npx tsc --noEmit --project <lib>/tsconfig.lib.json`; scoped ESLint, Prettier check, OpenAPI YAML parse and `git diff --check` passed. SQL generation is tested with real TypeORM; execution is mocked (no live database/integration rebuild).
- Deployment: the running control-plane container **needs a rebuild** for end-to-end use. Not rebuilt; no commit, stash, checkout, reset or unrelated edits performed.
- Secret-name typeahead (user's agent added the names-only endpoint): secret references = project picker + secret-name picker (`secretName` target → `SecretsService.listNames`); hint/empty texts en + de (4808 = 4808); spec allows only the names URL. Needs control-plane rebuild.

### Built-in control-plane member: plan (2026-10-29)

Plan only (phase 1, no code changed): [loadweaver.md 3.39](./loadweaver.md) "Built-in control-plane member (2026-10-29, proposed)".

- Finding: a node-less standalone control plane (compose) lacks exactly one base service, the **master-key share holder**; `MasterKeyService.seal()` throws `no control-plane member can hold a master-key share yet`, which breaks secrets, SOPS (`GET /api/git/sops/recipient` 409), provider credentials (external DNS, ACME DNS-01), backup keys / recovery kit and the DR envelope. etcd / Patroni, registry, Garage, Kopia, OpenSearch, bind9 and the data-plane roles are not embeddable or not needed (table in 3.39).
- Proposed pattern: in-process `BuiltinMemberService`, holder `@control-plane` (not a `lw_nodes` row → never schedulable), own X25519 seal key in `LOADWEAVER_BUILTIN_MEMBER_DIR` (separate volume, never in the DB / replicated env / DR envelope), `LOADWEAVER_BUILTIN_MEMBER=auto|always|off` (default `auto`: sole 1/1 → copy 1/2 → tie-breaker 2/3 → retired from 3 members), `off` forced on node-hosted member CPs; table `lw_builtin_members` (migration 055).
- Size: ~20 files (backend ~11, node agent 2, compose / Dockerfile 2, frontend ~5, 1 integration spec). Tests: unit during implementation; one integration spec in the existing Postgres harness (no VMs); smoke on the running stack after rebuild with the user's go-ahead.
- Open: 8 decisions with recommendations (end of 3.39); waiting for the user.

### Fleet trust: one consistent state, no dot separators (2026-10-29, user)

- Report: `/fleet/clusters/7680708a-…` (cluster "local") showed "Trust established · 10/29/26, 4:50 PM · marcel.menk@forepath.io" and "Not trusted" at once.
- Root cause (live data, read-only): the fleet's connection to "local" uses the cluster's API key (credential hint `…-key`), not a PAT. The registration `PUT trusted-fleets/<issuer>` with that admin key succeeded (15:24 and 15:50, audited `identity.trust-established`); the cluster's `lw_trusted_fleets` holds the fleet's issuer with the active kid `3aef3c39-…`. The probe `GET fleet-identity` through the same API key is answered `verified: false, reason: "only PATs with fleet:on-behalf-of send fleet identities"` (`TrustedFleetsService.evaluate` ignores claims from anything but a PAT with `fleet:on-behalf-of`), and the fleet maps every non-verified answer to `identity: 'untrusted'`. The page rendered the probe as "Not trusted" and the last attempt unconditionally underneath.
- What was true: the registration ("Trust established") is true: the cluster trusts the fleet's key. "Not trusted" was false; the real state is that the fleet's identities are not in effect on this connection, because the cluster ignores claims sent with an API key. Approvals, favourites and saved views don't work through the fleet as the person until the connection uses a PAT with `fleet:on-behalf-of`. Registering again changes nothing.
- Fix: one derivation `fleetTrustView(health, busy)` (`fleet-format.ts`) is the single source for the trust facts. The identity probe decides the state, and the last attempt is a past event under it. States: `trusted` (with since), `pending` (a successful attempt newer than the cluster's last answer: "Established, not confirmed by the cluster yet"), `not-in-effect` (the claims-ignored answer: "Not in effect on this connection", no "Establish trust…"), `not-trusted` (reason: a refused/failed attempt's, else the cluster's), `unsupported`, `unknown`, `establishing`. A successful attempt contradicted by a newer answer is marked superseded ("Since then: Not trusted"). Backend: `health.identityCheckedAt` is stamped by every answered identity probe (poll and the re-probe right after an establishment). An unanswered re-probe keeps the older stamp, so the console shows `pending` instead of a contradiction. The re-probe after establishment already existed.
- No "·": the trust row is now `fpc-key-value-list` rows: **Trust** (status badge tone + icon, label, muted reason + effect, action), **Trusted since** (`fpcFormatDateTime`), **Last attempt** (outcome `fpc-badge` + `fpcDate: 'datetime'` line + superseded note), **Attempted by** (user label, or muted "automatically"). Signing keys: "Active key · Oct 27, 2026" → title "Active key", Created column (`fpcDate`, priority 1, its own line on the stacked card). "Checked …" uses `fpcDate: 'datetime'` (no seconds).
- i18n (en = de): new `lwConsoleFleet-identityPending`, `lwConsoleFleet-identityNotInEffect`, `lwConsoleFleetCluster-trustAttempt`, `-trustAttemptBy`, `-trustSinceThen`; `lwConsoleFleetCluster-trustSince` "since" → "Trusted since"; no unit became unused (`-trustEstablishing` moved to `fleet-format.ts`).
- Files: `frontend/feature-console/src/lib/fleet/fleet-format.ts`, `fleet-format.spec.ts`, `fleet-cluster-detail-page.component.{ts,html}`, `fleet-pages.spec.ts`; `frontend/data-access-console/src/lib/types/fleet.types.ts`; `backend/feature-fleet/src/lib/entities/fleet-cluster.entity.ts`, `services/fleet-clusters.service.ts` (+spec), `services/fleet-trust.service.ts` (+spec); `apps/loadweaver/frontend-console/src/i18n/messages{,.de}.xlf`.
- Checks: jest fleet frontend (`fleet-format`, `fleet-pages`) 2 suites / 37 tests ✓ (new: 8 derivation cases incl. established+verified, established+stale health, superseded, revoked, forbidden, mismatch, claims ignored, establishing/unknown; 2 page cases); jest fleet backend (`fleet-trust`, `fleet-clusters` services) 2 suites / 29 tests ✓; strict LW ngc exit 0; `tsc` feature-fleet lib + spec exit 0. Screenshots `/tmp/uiq/sweep/verify2/loadweaver/fleet-trust-before.png` / `-after.png` (dev server :4602). The fleet-api container runs the published image, so `identityCheckedAt` only goes live after a rebuild. Until then the console falls back to `checkedAt`.
- Not changed (open, user decides): the connection's credential (a PAT with `fleet:on-behalf-of` would make the identities effective), and the cluster's trusted-fleets entry. The relay's 403 text for `untrusted` approvals ("establish trust") and the overview inbox still read the backend's `untrusted` for this case; the inbox shows nothing here because the last attempt succeeded.

### Built-in control-plane member: implemented + tested (2026-10-29)

Design and decisions: [loadweaver.md 3.39](./loadweaver.md) "Implemented design (decided 2026-10-29)" (standby lifecycle replaces the plan's witness lifecycle; user decisions 1–4 of 2026-10-29). Plan entry above: "Built-in control-plane member: plan (2026-10-29)".

- **Lifecycle as built**: `r` = registered real control-plane members with a seal key. `r = 0` → `@control-plane` is the active sole holder (1/1 share, unseals locally, answers `lw_unseal` relays for other replicas). `r ≥ 1` → shares / threshold on real members only, the built-in member holds no share and never answers; it keeps an in-sync **standby copy** (`lw_master_keys.builtin_standby`, whole key sealed to its public key, re-sealed on every seal / re-share, synced in place without re-key when it registers / its key changes / it is switched off). Takeover only when `r = 0` (deregistered / deleted / `left`), also after abrupt loss + restart; unreachable-but-registered members → stays sealed. Retired keys lose their standby copy. `always` = share holder too (+ standby); `off` = old 409.
- **Keystore**: dedicated volume file. The coordinator's / user's idea "use the shared file management structure" was evaluated against (a)–(d) and **rejected** (Loadweaver's `util-file-storage` default is `garage` = object-store bucket on member nodes, unavailable with 0 nodes and its credentials sit behind the master key → (d); `local` / `s3` / `garage` adapters have no file-mode control → (c); a `root + key` namespace shared with report files, isolation only by convention → (b); bucket contents travel with object-store generations / backups → (a)). Recorded in 3.39.
- **Files** (backend): `libs/domains/loadweaver/backend/feature-control-plane/src/lib/utils/builtin-member.utils.ts` (new: `BUILTIN_HOLDER`, mode parsing, key path, `builtinHolderPlan`, standby AAD); `entities/builtin-member.entity.ts` (new); `entities/master-key.entity.ts` (`MasterKeyHolder.kind/publicKey`, `MasterKeyStandby`, `builtinStandby` column); `builtin-member/builtin-member.service.ts` (new: key load / atomic generate 0600 in 0700, registration + 60 s heartbeat, mismatch guard, `sealTarget`, `canOpen` / `open`, `status`); `builtin-member/builtin-member.testing.ts` (new, in-memory TypeORM fake for specs); `services/master-key.service.ts` (holder set, seal with standby, takeover in `unseal()`, local share, `relayBuiltin`, `accept` refuses `@control-plane`, re-share compares names + built-in public key, `syncStandby`, `builtinRole`, `describe().builtinStandby`, `unsealTimeoutMs`); `controllers/cluster.controller.ts` (`controlPlane.builtin`, `controlPlane.masterKey`); `health/overview.service.ts` (`masterKeyInboxItems`, inbox kind `master-key`); `modules/control-plane.module.ts`, `src/index.ts` (wiring / exports). ### API key fleet delegation (2026-10-29, user)

- Decision (user, question "Shouldn't a normal API key (non-PAT) have the right to do everything, hence also fleet:on-behalf-of?"; offered: fleet auto-provisions a PAT (recommended) / let API keys delegate / leave it): **let API keys delegate**. Live trigger: the fleet connects to "local" with the cluster's API key, so its identities were ignored ("Not in effect on this connection").
- Control plane: `mayCarryFleetIdentity(req, scope)` = PAT with `fleet:on-behalf-of` **or** the static API key (`req.apiKeyAuthenticated`) while `LOADWEAVER_API_KEY_FLEET_DELEGATION` is on (default `on`; `off` / `false` / `0` / `no` = off). `TrustedFleetsService.evaluate` uses it; verification itself (`verifyToken` / `checkFleetClaim` / nonce in `lw_fleet_claim_nonces` / unknown issuer ignored / trusted issuer failing → 403) is unchanged and shared. Ignored reasons (probe `GET /api/fleet-identity`): PAT without the scope → `only PATs with fleet:on-behalf-of or the cluster API key send fleet identities` (switch off: the old text); API key with the switch off → `API key fleet delegation is off on this cluster (LOADWEAVER_API_KEY_FLEET_DELEGATION)`. A verified API-key probe answers `verified` (+ `trustedKeys` / `trustedSince`).
- Role cap: the access services already resolve the API key as `cluster-admin` and then cap by the claim (`ClusterAccessService.resolve`, `ProjectAccessService.caller` → `capRolesToFleetIdentity`); the static key has no scopes, so its rights = cluster admin are the cap. `assertAnnouncementsAdmin` (shared updates module, checked `isApiKeyAuth` directly) now requires the claim's admin grant when the API key carries a person.
- Acting person / two-person rules: `actorFromRequest` for the API key with a verified claim → `{ type: 'api-key', id: null, onBehalfOf, person, onBehalfOfEmail }` (creators / approvers = `fleet:<iss>:<sub>`, audit actor stays the API key). `isFleetRelayCaller` stays PAT-only, so `assertFleetApprovalIdentity` keeps refusing PAT relays without a claim and the API key without a claim is native as before. Legacy guard: `assertNotLegacyFleetItem` treats `api-key` as the credential's creator id for API-key requests with a person (items the API key created without a person stay native-only — they may be the person's own from before); platform cut-overs the same (`requestedBy = 'api-key'`). Listing / removing trusted fleets also refuses an API-key request carrying a verified person (never through a fleet). The API key's own `PUT trusted-fleets/<issuer>` (automatic trust over an API-key connection) stays the native admin path as before. Sockets (`evaluateSocket`) were already credential-agnostic: unchanged.
- Fleet / UI: no fleet backend change (the fleet always sends claims; the probe decides). `fleetTrustView`'s `CLAIMS_IGNORED` matches the new PAT reason, the switch-off reason and the old one (older clusters) → `not-in-effect`; an API-key connection with delegation on verifies → `trusted`. Backend message labels (en + de): `lwConsoleBackend-identityNotDelegating`, `lwConsoleBackend-identityApiKeyDelegationOff` (old `-identityNotPat` kept for older clusters).
- Specs: `fleet-identity.utils.spec` (switch parsing, `mayCarryFleetIdentity`, reasons, cap at the key's cluster admin, API-key legacy guard), `trusted-fleets.service.spec` (API key + valid claim → verified + person + nonce once; tampered / forged / foreign kid / expired / aud / htm / htu / bh → refused; unknown issuer → ignored; switch off → ignored, PAT unaffected; PAT without scope → new reason; probe verified; list / remove refused through a fleet person), `audit-log.service.spec` (actor api-key + onBehalfOf / email, details recorded), `cluster-access.service.spec` (API key + claim → person, role capped), `plans-fleet-approval.spec` (API key: second person approves via `fleet`, author / same verified email refused, `api-key` plans native-only); PAT paths unchanged (existing cases green). Frontend: `fleet-format.spec` (three not-in-effect reasons, API-key verified → trusted, unknown fleet stays not-trusted), `fleet-pages.spec` (new reason), `backend-message.spec`.
- Checks: jest control plane (fleet-identity, audit-log, cluster-access, plans-fleet-approval, saved-views, search-preferences, plans.gateway) 12 suites / 99 tests ✓, (backups, exec.gateway, updates) 10 / 160 ✓; jest fleet backend (fleet-trust, fleet-identity, fleet-clusters, fleet-aggregation) 6 / 45 ✓; jest frontend fleet (fleet-format, fleet-pages) 2 / 39 ✓, data-access backend-message 1 / 3 ✓; tsc control-plane lib + spec, backend-fleet app + spec ✓; strict LW ngc ✓ (0 errors); eslint changed files ✓; i18n en = de (4830 / 4830, every de unit has a target).
- Integration (G6, not run): `apps/loadweaver/backend-fleet/src/integration/fleet-identity.integration.spec.ts` — new block "API key fleet delegation": a second control plane `c` in `api-key` mode (`STATIC_API_KEY`), trusted natively with the API key, connected with it; probe verified; plan author = fleet person, author's approval 403, second person approves (`via fleet`, audit `api-key` + onBehalfOf + email); a viewer claim can't create plans; replay / forged → 403; unknown issuer → native API key (`owner = api-key`).
- Live: needs a control-plane image rebuild + container re-create (the fleet image only for the console texts); not done here (the control-plane container belongs to the built-in-member worker).
