#### Fleet sites world map (2026-10-29)

User: the map (fleet overview, Sites lane) did not fit the design and did not show the locations properly.

- **Cause (locations)**: the projection itself was consistent (outlines and markers both through `projectSite`, lon → x, inverted lat → y). The only real site, `local/default`, has `spec.location = { latitude: -90, longitude: -180 }` — the schema form's start value for numbers is the minimum (`initialValue()` in `objects/schema-form.ts`), so opening the optional `location` block saved the South Pole / date line; the marker sat half outside the bottom-left corner. Not changed here (shared form); open point: lat / lon should start empty or at 0, or the block should not pre-fill. Besides: the outlines were too coarse (no Malay peninsula, Singapore in the sea; Antarctica as a band), markers 3 px, yellow on grey.
- **Projection**: plate carrée cropped to 84° N – 60° S (`WORLD_MAP_BOUNDS`, viewBox 360 × 144, no Antarctica band); out-of-bounds coordinates clamp onto the edge, markers stay inside the frame (`clamp()`), the tooltip shows the coordinates (`formatCoordinates`, N / S / E / W localised: `lwConsoleFleetMap-north|south|east|west`).
- **Backdrop**: new hand-drawn coastlines (~1,150 waypoints from well-known coastal coordinates, no third-party data) for all continents and major islands, seas left open; adjoining outlines overlap at the Urals / Caucasus / Sinai and are stroked below / filled above, so no seams. 30° graticule. Colours from the theme (land = 10 % body colour on body bg, coast 26 %, graticule border colour), hairline frame, no shadows / gradients; light and dark.
- **Markers**: `<button>`s over the SVG (12 px, brand primary, body-bg ring, emphasis outline; focus ring), click / Enter / Space emit `siteSelected`; hover / focus shows a tooltip (`role="tooltip"`, `aria-describedby`) with site · cluster and coordinates. Sites closer than one marker at the rendered width (ResizeObserver) spread on a ring around their spot (small dot marks the true location).
- Specs: `fleet-format.spec` (projection bounds, known cities → expected positions / quadrants, graticule, waypoints in bounds, coordinates), new `fleet-world-map.component.spec` (markers, spreading narrow vs. wide, buttons, tooltip, emit); fleet specs 46/46; strict ngc clean; lint 0 errors on the touched files. #### Integrations API (3.41)

- `GET /api/integrations` → `{ env: IntegrationEnvStatus[] }` (`integrations/integrations-env.ts`, pure): `smtp` (server host:port, from, authentication on/off), `otlp` (enabled, endpoint origin), `geoip` (bundled / custom, path, active = file exists), `releases` (repository, updateCheck, cron, rollout), `postureSync` (cron, env / default), `kms` (provider or `shamir`; vault-transit: address origin, namespace, mount, key), `auth` (method; keycloak: URL, realm, client id), `plugins` (`DYNAMIC_*` module names; URLs without user info). Cluster admins only, PAT `cluster:read`. Spec asserts the serialized answer never contains secret-looking env values (SMTP password / user, OTEL credentials, VAULT_TOKEN, client secret, API key, JWT secret, npm token in a plugin URL).
- `POST /api/integrations/test` `{ kind, name }` → `{ ok, message, details?, durationMs }` (`IntegrationsService`): DnsProvider (API: `listZones` + zones using it must exist; bind9: node group exists + connected name-server node; axfr: SOA of a zone using it from every server), BackupTarget (S3: `HeadBucket` + declared object lock via `S3CopyDestination.objectLockDays`; SFTP: new `SftpCopyDestination.probe()` = connect + stat path), IpPool (`failover: provider`: `holder()` of up to 4 assigned addresses / cidr prefixes; other pools 400), SiemTarget (new `SiemForwarderService.sendTest()`: one record marked as test, cursors untouched). 10 s race, failures `200 { ok: false }`, messages sanitized (`sanitizeTestError`: error message only, resolved credential values incl. key lines, URL user info, bearer / `token=` pairs redacted, 300 chars) + `httpStatus` detail; audited `integration.test` (kind, name, ok, durationMs). Access: infra / admin for DnsProvider / BackupTarget / IpPool (PAT `cluster:read` + `cluster:nodes`), admin for SiemTarget (`cluster:read` + `cluster:admin`); role and scope before lookup. `@Throttle` 10 / min (existing throttler).
- OpenAPI (both routes + `IntegrationEnvStatus` / `IntegrationTestResult`); console data access `IntegrationsService` (`status()`, `test(kind, name)`) + `integrations.types.ts`; docs: "Testing a …" notes in dns.md, backups.md, public-addresses.md, audit-and-export.md. Specs: backend integrations service / controller / siem 85/85 incl. cycle specs, frontend 3/3; tsc + lint clean (0 errors). Fleet relay rules for the two routes: owned by the fleet agent.

#### Fleet parity for integrations (3.41)

- **Relay rules** (`feature-fleet/utils/relay-rules.ts`): Git connections are person-scoped — `GET git/connections`, `GET git/connections/<id>(/commits)` at `viewer`; create / `PATCH` / `DELETE`, `test|sync|export|host-key/reset|webhook-secret/rotate`, `GET …/webhook-secret` at `admin`; cluster-wide grants unchanged (no claim needed), project grants only with the signed identity (`needsClaim`). Certificates `PUT|DELETE certificates/<id>` moved from `admin` to `operator` (cluster-wide). Integrations hub: `GET integrations` (`admin`), `POST integrations/test` (`operator`; the cluster enforces admin for SIEM targets). Linked Git accounts as `own` rules for any grant (`ownAnyGrant`): `GET git/accounts`, `POST git/accounts/(github|gitlab)/authorize` (`consoleReturn`), `GET|DELETE git/accounts/pending/<nonce>`, `POST git/accounts/confirm`, `DELETE git/accounts/<uuid>`; the callback stays native (public URL). Header: "Git account links" removed from the never-relayed list.
- **Relay** (`fleet-relay.service.ts`): `assertConsoleReturn()` — the authorize body may only carry `returnUrl`, and only `<fleet console origin>/…/account/git-accounts` (origins: `FLEET_CONSOLE_URL`, else the explicit `CORS_ORIGIN` list, `fleetConsoleOrigins()`); the body is then bound into the claim. A cluster 403 on a request relayed with a needed claim is now passed through as the person's decision (like approvals / secrets) instead of the credential 502.
- **Control plane, Git connections**: `GitConnectionsService` already decided with `ProjectAccessService.caller()` (roles capped to the fleet identity) and audited with `actorFromRequest()` (on-behalf-of); fixed: `createdBy` and the export commit's author / message use the verified person (`actor.person`) instead of the service user.
- **Control plane, Git accounts** (`git-accounts.service.ts`): owner = the verified fleet person (`fleet:<iss>:<sub>`) when the request carries one; a fleet relay credential (PAT with `fleet:on-behalf-of`) without a person → 403; audit actor = service credential on behalf of the person. `POST …/authorize` takes `{ returnUrl? }` (`AuthorizeGitAccountDto`), accepted only with a verified fleet identity and only for an http(s) `…/account/git-accounts` page (`gitLinkReturnUrl()`); stored in the HMAC-signed OAuth state (`r`, `OAuthState.returnUrl`), the callback redirects there (`settingsUrl(result, returnUrlOf(state))`). OpenAPI updated.
- **Plan bot rule (fleet persons)**: commands / merge-review approvals of a fleet-linked account act with the roles the cluster itself grants that person id (`linkedUserRequest(fleet:…)`: no claim, so no fleet grant — today none); `GitBotService` replies with an explicit refusal ("linked to a fleet user … fleet grants only count on requests the fleet signs"). Never a remembered grant from a past claim (it could outlive a revocation at the fleet).
- **Console**: `GitService.authorizeAccount()` sends `returnUrl` (this console's `account/git-accounts` below the base href) in fleet mode; `webhookUrl()` uses the active cluster's public API in fleet mode (was the relay URL). `/account/git-accounts` no longer fleet-unavailable; offered in the account popover with a cluster open; the page shows a hint (no cluster / cluster doesn't verify the fleet) instead of loading. Git pages: `mayAdministerGitScope(me, project, fleetMode)` (project admins need `me.fleetIdentity` in fleet mode), `gitFleetIdentityGap()` hint on the list. xlf: 4 units added, `lwConsoleFleetUnavailable-gitAccounts` removed.
- Docs: fleet.md (role table, relay paragraph, linked accounts + plan bot rule, PAT scopes `git:admin` / `git:accounts` / `certificates:write`, `FLEET_CONSOLE_URL`), gitops.md, plan-bot.md, fleet openapi; `.start-containers.env.example` / docker-compose `FLEET_CONSOLE_URL`.
- Specs: relay-rules + fleet-relay (fleet suite 150/150), control plane git / fleet-identity / cycles / audit 230/230 (new `git-accounts.service.spec`, fleet block in `git-connections.service.spec`, OAuth state `returnUrl`), data-access git.service 6/6, feature-console git / git-accounts / fleet-format pass; `container.component.spec` "admin Updates item" fails on the concurrent integrations nav item (`/settings/integrations`, not this change). eslint clean on touched files, strict ngc clean. Integration specs / labs not run (on hold).

- **Overflow indicators fix** (user: "at the right the chevron doesn't vanish; clicking moves only a few pixels, not column-wise"):
  - **Cause:** the head's scroll listener wrote the head's mirrored position back into the body. That cancelled a smooth body scroll after one frame, and pulled the body back off its end when the head couldn't scroll quite as far.
  - **Fix:** the head ignores the echo of `onScroll`'s mirroring. A first version used a flag cleared on the next animation frame; the user still saw pixel-wise steps, because the head's echo event can arrive a frame later. So the echo is now recognised **by value** (`mirroredLeft`, clamped to the head's range). A real head scroll (focus into a clipped head cell) still drives the body.
  - **Column-wise paging** (`fpcScrollColumnTarget`): forwards reveals the first column cut off on the right; backwards the last one cut off on the left. Sticky first / trailing columns are covered widths, not candidates.
  - ui-components data-table + step-strip specs 54; ngc / eslint clean.
- **Follow-ups of live test 3.43 (2026-10-30)**:
  - **Agent retries failed revisions** (`stream/revision-retry.ts`, `AgentConnectionService.applyDesired`):
    - **Before:** a revision that failed or rolled back (e.g. an image briefly not pullable) stayed failed until the CP compiled a new one; an agent restart was needed.
    - **Now:** the agent applies the **same** latest desired state again after 15 s, doubling up to 5 min, jitter 75–100 %. The backoff resets on success, on a new revision and on shutdown.
    - **Serialized:** at most one retry is pending; it is scheduled only after an apply finished, and applies stay serialized by the reconciler. A retry superseded by a newer revision is not rescheduled.
    - **Reports:** a retry is reported like an apply when it applies or its status / error changed, else every 5th attempt (`RETRY_REPORT_EVERY`).
    - **Lab:** the lab agent (`m7-cluster-agent.entry.ts`) gets it too: it uses the real `AgentConnectionService` and only replaces `ReconcilerService.layers`.
    - **Not retried:** applied revisions with an isolated control-plane error (3.43). Those wait for the CP's next revision (e.g. the etcd bootstrap).
    - **Specs:** `revision-retry.spec.ts` (2) and `agent-connection.spec.ts` (+5, fake timers). The stream specs pass (16); tsc + eslint clean.
    - **Live:** bundle rebuilt (`build-agent.js`), installed on `lw-devnode-1` as `rebuild.sh` does (switch `/lab/lw-agent.js`, `/opt/loadweaver/lw-agent.js`, `systemctl restart lw-agent`; VM not recreated). The node reconnected after ≈ 2 min (overlay members first) and stayed `applied` rev 26.
  - **Dev nodes: `net-cp.sh`** makes the CP ↔ overlay routes reproducible (dev-node notes above). Applied once: it replaced the CP's `10.93.0.0/24` with /32s for 10.93.0.9–11. A second run changed nothing. A simulated break (switch default route on eth1, one route missing, a stray /24) was repaired.
    - **Verified:** from the CP container, `10.93.0.9:5000` (`REGISTRY_PRIVATE_PORT`) answers `HTTP/1.0 401 Unauthorized` (the registry). `lw-devnode-1` resolves `ghcr.io` and gets HTTPS answers.
- **Overflow indicators, verified in Chromium** (static Storybook `WideWithOverflowIndicators`, wrapper widened to 850 / 1000 px; Playwright with `~/.cache/uiq-libroot` NSS/ALSA libs). The real root causes:
  - **Head scroll events wrote stale positions back into the body.** Besides mirroring echoes, the browser clamps the head while `syncHead` rewrites its widths. Only `focusin` in the head drives the body now (wheel unchanged); the echo tracking is gone.
  - **The sticky ⋮ / actions column keeps its end padding clipped,** so `scrollWidth − clientWidth` was 8 px more than the body can ever scroll (163 of 171). The end chevron never hid. The edges now come from the content: more to the right = the last scrollable column ends past the sticky trailing cell's left edge (else the scrollport's), more to the left likewise against a sticky first column.
  - Probe: clicks 0 → 11 → 86 → 163 (column steps), the right chevron hides at the end.
  - Also fixed two pre-existing Storybook type errors (stepper description backticks, data-table drag story row type) that broke `build-storybook`.
  - Specs: data-table + step-strip 55; ngc / eslint clean.

### DB handover (3.43) (2026-10-30)

- **Trigger (live):** `lw-devnode-1` became a real member (etcd, Patroni leader, OpenSearch, object store, registry), but its API replica crash-looped with `database "loadweaver" does not exist`: the compose CP replicates `DB_DATABASE`, a fresh Spilo only has `postgres`.
- **Design implemented** (plan 3.43 "members own it, external syncs"), new folder `feature-control-plane/src/lib/database-handover/`:
  - **External vs on-node** (`databaseDeployment`): on-node when the agent sets `LOADWEAVER_CONTROL_PLANE_ON_MEMBER=true` (new, in `controlPlaneApiSpec`) or the API connects to the agent's leader proxy `127.0.0.1:5433` (older agents); `LOADWEAVER_DATABASE_HANDOVER=off` disables it on an external CP. The built-in member mode is no signal.
  - **State:** the CP's own knowledge is `database-target.json` (0600) on the state volume (`target external | members`, member overlay addresses, cluster CA, handover id, a pending audit event; no credentials: Spilo's superuser is `DB_USERNAME` / `DB_PASSWORD` of the replicated environment). Both databases carry the row `lw_database_handover` (`external` / `handover` / `members`, `external_copy` jsonb; migration `1800000000058_DatabaseHandover`), copied with the data, set to `members` on both sides before the subscription starts, then replicated. A second external replica seeing `members` adopts (file + restart).
  - **Boot step** (`prepareDatabaseTarget`, `main.ts` before TypeORM reads its settings): lifts a leftover database-level read-only freeze on the external DB; on `members` starts the in-process `MembersLeaderProxy` (`127.0.0.1:${LOADWEAVER_DATABASE_PROXY_PORT:-5433}`, Patroni `GET :8008/primary` every 2 s) and points `DB_HOST` / `DB_PORT` / `DB_SSL_*` at it (verify-full, cluster CA, `postgres.loadweaver`).
  - **Readiness:** `r ≥ 1` real members (3.39 definition) and one answers Patroni `/primary` from the CP.
  - **Handover** (`DatabaseHandoverService`, 15 s ticks, advisory lock on the external DB): leader not in recovery → drop a database a failed attempt left (adopt instead when its row says `members`) → `CREATE DATABASE … OWNER DB_USERNAME` → `wal_level = logical` through Patroni `PATCH /config` (+ `ignore_slots` for pgoutput in that DB) and `POST /restart {restart_pending}`, before the freeze, best effort → **freeze** (in-memory flag → HTTP 503 on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; `ALTER DATABASE … SET default_transaction_read_only = on`; other sessions terminated so background writers reconnect read-only) → schema by the same TypeORM migrations on the members → **copy** (`copyDatabase`: one REPEATABLE READ snapshot, cursor batches of 500 rows as `row_to_json` → `json_populate_recordset`, `session_replication_role = replica`, generated columns skipped, `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE`, sequences via `setval`, schema mismatch refused, **row counts verified**) → row `members` on both → publication + subscription (`copy_data = false`) → target file → **controlled restart** (SIGTERM; compose `restart: unless-stopped`). The audit event `control-plane.database-handover` is recorded after the restart on the members' DB (the external one was frozen). Failure: freeze lifted, half-made DB dropped, back-off 30 s doubling to 10 min.
  - **Member API replicas:** protocol `controlPlane.database: pending | ready` (feature `database-handover`, strip-gated); the external CP sends `pending` until its target is `members`; the agent's `componentsFor(role, database)` leaves out `controlPlane` (a running replica is removed), etcd / Patroni / queue / log store run.
  - **External copy:** publication `lw_external_copy` on tables with a primary key (no hypertables, no `lw_metrics*` / `lw_flows*`, no `migrations`); subscription on the external DB over all members (`target_session_attrs=read-write`, `sslmode=require`: the external server has no cluster CA), created disabled first so a failing create never empties the copy. Sync: new migrations → subscription disabled, migrations on the external copy, enabled, `REFRESH PUBLICATION`; slot lost (failover) or apply failing ≥ 10 min → drop, empty, subscribe with `copy_data = true`. State in `GET /api/cluster` → `controlPlane.database` and the row's `external_copy`. `LOADWEAVER_DATABASE_EXTERNAL_COPY=off` skips it.
  - **Read-only fallback:** the pool's pg client (`DatabaseTargetClient`, TypeORM `extra.Client`) connects to the external copy with `-c default_transaction_read_only=on` once the proxy found no primary for 45 s (at once on a start without members); writes 503 "the cluster's database members are unreachable; read-only until one is back"; 3 polls with a primary end it, connections of the other side are cut. Never promoted. Migrations are skipped while read-only; a process that started read-only restarts once the members are back.
  - **r = 0** (members removed / `left`, also while read-only): subscription dropped (`slot_name = NONE`), slot dropped if a member still answers, row `external`, target file `external`, restart; audited `control-plane.database-return`.
- **Tests:** `database-handover.utils.spec` (state machine, readiness / deployment, guard messages, fallback hysteresis, publication list, counts / schema, conninfo, copy actions), `database-target.runtime.spec` (guard middleware, pool client switch + cut, target file 0600, freeze lift, proxy-driven fallback), `database-copy.spec`, `external-copy.spec`, `database-handover.service.spec` (13: handover order, abort + back-off, copy setup failure, waits, leftover vs owned DB, adopt, return, read-only, restart after fallback start, pending audit, migrations before refresh, resync); migration 058 spec; agent `control-plane.spec` (+2); protocol specs unchanged and green. Handover specs 55, agent control-plane 45, protocol 66, related CP specs 20. tsc (app, CP lib + specs, agent, protocol) and eslint clean.
- **Docs:** `docs/loadweaver/architecture/README.md` (control plane + feature table), `features/secrets-and-encryption.md` (pointer); compose env defaults; `.diagrams/loadweaver.mmd` (`DbHandover`, parsed with mermaid).
- **Open / not done:** a long-broken subscription keeps its slot on the members (WAL retention; no `max_slot_wal_keep_size` set); no wait for the subscription to catch up before an `r = 0` return; read-only fallback data is as fresh as the subscription (during a resync it is partial); the subscription's TLS is unverified (`sslmode=require`); several external CP replicas each need their own restart (adopt covers it, one compose container is the norm); console shows `controlPlane.database` only through the API (no UI yet); i18n of the 503 texts not added.
- **CP crash loop after the handover rebuild** (user: internal server errors everywhere): two bugs.
  - **"SASL: SCRAM-SERVER-FIRST-MESSAGE: client password must be a string":** `DatabaseTargetClient` spread the pool config, and pg-pool's `password` is non-enumerable, so every connection lost it. Fixed (password carried over explicitly) + regression spec in `database-target.runtime.spec.ts`; handover specs 56.
  - **"describe is not defined":** compiled migration specs (057 / 058) in `src/migrations` were picked up by the migrations glob. User: no migration specs, ever. Removed (also the stale `dist/**/migrations/*.spec.js`).
  - Image rebuilt (`sha256:62f28227273b`), CP recreated: healthy, 0 restarts, `net-cp.sh` re-applied the routes. The handover waits for a member's Postgres leader.

### Live test 3.43: DB handover + 3 nodes (2026-10-30)

Dev stack (compose CP, `lw-devnode-1..3`, 4 GiB guests). CP image rebuilt per fix (`api-container-image`, only the API container recreated); lab agent bundle (`build-agent.js`) installed in place on every node (no VM recreation). Fleet containers stopped for Part 2 (user override: start 2 / 3 even below the headroom), restarted at the end.

**Part 1: handover on `lw-devnode-1` (only node up)**

- **Pending gate:** the crash-looping `lw-control-plane` on the node was removed; agent log "Control-plane API replica waits: the cluster's database isn't on the members yet".
- **Handover** (10:32): "copying the external database to the members (leader 10.93.0.9)" → "49046 rows in 110 tables copied and verified; switching to the members" → restart → "Control-plane database: members (through the in-process leader proxy)".
  - `lw_database_handover.state = members` on the members' DB (and the copy).
  - Audit `control-plane.database-handover` (seq 887; rows 49046, tables 110, externalCopy ok) on the members, replicated to the external copy.
  - Publication `lw_external_copy`, slot active, subscription enabled (105 tables `r`), `wal_level = logical`.
- **Member API replica:** `DB_DATABASE=loadweaver` via `127.0.0.1:5433`, `LOADWEAVER_CONTROL_PLANE_ON_MEMBER=true`, healthy (after the dev-env port fix below).
- **`GET /api/cluster` → `controlPlane.database`:** `{deployment external, location members, readOnly false, externalCopy {state ok, skipped lw_flows*, lw_metrics*}}`.
- **External copy follows:** a saved view (`POST /api/views`) insert / update reached the compose Postgres in 0.18 s / 0.16 s.
- **Console APIs:** `/cluster`, `/nodes`, `/views`, `/vm-images/catalog`, `/projects/test/incidents` 200; `/projects/test/vm-images` 200 (both Alpine tags). `GET /api/projects` has no list route (404 by design).
- **Fallback** (guest off 11:16:52):
  - writes 500 for ~45 s, then 503 "the cluster's database members are unreachable; read-only until one is back";
  - reads 200, health 200, no CP restart, `readOnly: true`.
  - Guest on: writes 200 after 36 s, no CP restart, external copy got the post-fallback write, subscription enabled, Patroni single leader (TL 4), nothing promoted.

**Part 2: 3 members**

- **Join** (11:28–11:31): `lw-devnode-2/3` were blocked from every CP (switch + node-1 nft) until the new bundle, CP image and port fix were in; then they joined etcd through `lw-devnode-1`:
  - same cluster id `0x50112f411c4071b8`, 3 started members, leader unchanged, no second bootstrap.
- **Patroni:** 1 leader + 2 replicas, but **not streaming** (see open issues: `connect_address 127.0.1.1`); the replicas follow through the WAL archive ("in archive recovery").
- **Object store** (before the fix below):
  - gen 6 rf 2 was created at 11:29:41, as soon as `lw-devnode-3` came up;
  - then gen 7 rf 3 at 11:40:31 → active 11:44:19 → gen 6 retired 11:46:19.
  - Two copies instead of one; data complete (`lw-registry` 157.8 MB / 10 objects on 3 healthy Garage nodes). The audit's `"copied": 0` is misleading.
- **Registry:** `/projects/test/vm-images` 200 throughout; member API replicas healthy on all three.
- **`/api/cluster`:** 3 members, automatic failover, database on the members, copy ok. A write reached the copy in 0.7 s.
- **HA** (`lw-devnode-3` off 12:24): 18 / 18 writes ok over 3 min, registry 200, gen 7 unchanged, etcd 2 / 3 healthy. Back on: etcd 3 / 3, Patroni replica back, same generation.
- **Leave of `lw-devnode-3`** (drain 12:31, leave accepted 13:12:18 after the fix below):
  - membership 2 with the warning "two control-plane members without a witness: …", automatic failover off;
  - etcd member removed at once (`member list` → 2);
  - gen 8 rf 2 (holders 1 / 2) created 13:08:08 → active 13:10:16, gen 7 retired;
  - registry and external copy kept working, handover state `members`.
  - Not as expected: see open issues (the left node keeps its role, `etcd_member_since` re-set instead of cleared).
- **Rejoin:** agent stopped, its `lw-*` containers removed, `/var/lib/loadweaver` moved to `/var/lib/loadweaver.left-20261030T131921` (kept). Then a fresh join token and `lw-agent.js join --server http://127.0.0.1:13400`.
  - Promoted again: 3 members, failover on.
  - etcd joined through the members: same cluster id, new member id `908a6d37…`, no bootstrap.
  - New overlay address `10.93.0.1` (re-join), so `net-cp.sh` was re-run.
  - Patroni replica created, member API replica healthy.
  - Gen 9 rf 3 created 13:43:31 (~5 min after it came up; one generation) → active 13:45:14.
  - OpenSearch: `lw-devnode-3` joined `lw-devnode-1`'s cluster (green).
- **End:** `lw-devnode-2/3` powered off (MemAvailable 5.6 GiB < 6). With 1 / 3 members etcd has no quorum, so the CP is in the read-only fallback (writes 503, reads 200), as designed. Fleet containers restarted; MemAvailable 13.8 GiB.

**Fixes (unit-tested; tsc / eslint / prettier clean)**

- **CP crashed when the members' Postgres restarted** (unhandled pg `error` event on the handover's dedicated clients):
  - `guardClientErrors()` in `database-target.boot.ts`, used by `connectExternal` and `connectMembers`;
  - spec in `database-target.runtime.spec.ts`.
- **Handover failed after the freeze** ("terminating connection due to administrator command"): it read the cluster CA through the pool whose sessions the freeze had just terminated.
  - The CA is now read before the freeze (`frozenCa`).
  - Spec in `database-handover.service.spec.ts`.
- **Members' Postgres restart for `wal_level = logical` hung for hours.** Before the handover the backup gateway (part of the gated API replica) is absent, so every `wal-push` retried ~14 min, and a shutdown waits for the archiver.
  - The agent now bind-mounts `/home/postgres/.walg.json` (`S3_MAX_RETRIES=2`) wherever WAL-G archives; Spilo's env dir has no such setting.
  - Postgres hash changes once (live: one re-create, which also ended the hung shutdown).
  - `platform-backups.ts`, `control-plane-containers.ts`, `control-plane-role.manager.ts`; specs in `platform-backups.spec.ts`.
- **Member API replica re-created on every stream switch.** The replicated environment's key order follows the sending replica's process env, so the same settings gave another hash per sender.
  - The API replica's env is now sorted (only that spec's hash).
  - Spec in `control-plane.spec.ts`.
- **Log store re-created on every etcd-peer change** (reconnects, joins, leaves). `cluster.initial_cluster_manager_nodes` is no longer in the hash.
- **Log store split into two clusters.** Joiners named all etcd peers (incl. members that had just connected), so `lw-devnode-2` + `-3` bootstrapped a second cluster while `lw-devnode-1`'s restarted.
  - Now only the etcd founder (the bootstrapper, or the sole etcd data holder) sets the initial managers; other members only join via the seed hosts.
  - `log-store.ts`; specs in `control-plane-role.etcd.spec.ts`.
- **Object store grew once per member that came up.** Growth now also waits until the set of members that are _up_ was stable for 5 min (controller-side, in memory per replica; a fresh replica only waits longer).
  - `object-store.utils.ts`, `object-store-controller.service.ts`.
- **Leave deadlock.** A draining member that keeps its seat (3 nodes) stayed an object-store member, so its data never moved and leave answered 409 forever.
  - `objectStoreMembers()` leaves out draining members.
  - Specs in `object-store.utils.spec.ts`.
- **Leader proxy cut every connection on a single missed Patroni poll.** Now only a different primary replaces the leader; longer absence is the fallback.
  - `members-leader-proxy.ts`; spec in `database-target.runtime.spec.ts`.
- **Registry listing 500 ("fetch failed")** when a member counted as connected doesn't answer, e.g. in the read-only fallback, whose `connected` flags nobody updates. It is now a 503 naming the endpoints.
  - `vm-image-catalog.service.ts` + spec.
- **`compile-migrations`** (`apps/loadweaver/backend-control-plane/project.json`) skips `*.spec.ts` (guard; the migration specs themselves were removed, user rule).

**Dev environment (not product)**

- **Compose Postgres routing:** `net-cp.sh` also routes the overlay /32s into the compose Postgres netns (the external copy subscribes to the members' :5432). It remembers the last overlay addresses (`.overlay-routes`) for CP starts before the API answers.
- **`net-cp-watch.sh` (new):** re-applies `net-cp.sh` on every start of the CP / Postgres container. The handover restarts the CP on purpose, and the netns routes don't survive; without it the CP looped "fallback start → members back → restart".
  - Run it in the background while dev nodes are up.
- **`fwd-agent-only.sh` (new):** the member API replica binds `:::3400` / `:7443`, which the VMs' loopback forwarders held.
  - Forwarders moved to 127.0.0.1 / ::1 :13400 / :17443.
  - nft DNATs only the agent's traffic (`socket cgroupv2 "system.slice/lw-agent.service"`), loaded by an `ExecStartPost` drop-in of `lw-agent.service`. A boot unit failed: nft resolves the cgroup at load time.
  - Joins use `--server http://127.0.0.1:13400`.
- **CP image on members:** `Environment=LOADWEAVER_CONTROL_PLANE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/forepath/loadweaver-control-plane-api:lw343-1` in every `lw-agent.service`. A unique tag makes the agents re-create the replicas; `:latest` keeps the old container.
- **Dev DB:** the stray, empty `lw_email_settings` table (dropped email-service design, in no migration) made the copy refuse ("schema differs"). Moved to schema `lw_stray`, not dropped.

**Open issues**

- **OpenSearch on `lw-devnode-2` still belongs to the orphaned second cluster** (`cluster_uuid _na_`). Repair: stop the agent, remove `lw-opensearch`, move `/var/lib/loadweaver/opensearch` aside, start the agent. Moving the data was refused by the permission system; left to the user.
- **Patroni replicas don't stream:** Spilo's `connect_address` is `gethostbyname(hostname)`, which is `127.0.1.1` (Debian `/etc/hosts`), so `primary_conninfo host=127.0.1.1` is the replica itself. Replication runs only via the WAL archive.
  - Needs a design: Spilo strips `PATRONI_*` env, and its generated config wins over `SPILO_CONFIGURATION`.
  - Probably real nodes too.
- **A left node keeps its role.** Its agent stays connected and heartbeating; Postgres / OpenSearch / API keep running, and Patroni still registers it through the other members' etcd endpoints. `etcd_member_since` was re-set at 13:12:25 instead of cleared (later reused).
- **`GET /nodes` `connected` is per process** (in-memory sessions): a node streaming to a member replica shows disconnected on the compose CP, while the DB flag (registry, object store) says connected.
- Writes answer 500 (not 503) in the ~45 s before the fallback starts.
- `lastError` in `controlPlane.database` stays stale after recovery.
- `discovery.seed_hosts` is still in the log store hash (restart on a membership change).
- The agent's own `PostgresLeaderProxy` also logged "leader unknown" flaps.
- The point-in-time clone spec has no WAL-G config bind.
- The compose CP and the member replicas (`lw343-1`) run the same build with every CP fix above. A later CP rebuild needs a new tag in `lw-agent.service` for the members.

### 3.43 follow-ups (2026-10-30)

Dev stack as in "Live test 3.43" (compose CP, `lw-devnode-1..3`); fleet containers stopped while the nodes started, restarted at the end.

**Live repairs (user decisions 2026-10-30)**

- **Writes back:** `lw-devnode-2/3` started (`FORCE=1 up.sh`, MemAvailable 13.4 GiB < 14.7 needed), `net-cp-watch.sh` in the background. `controlPlane.database` `readOnly: false`; `POST /api/views` 201.
- **OpenSearch on `lw-devnode-2`:** agent stopped, `lw-opensearch` removed, data moved to `/var/lib/loadweaver/opensearch.orphan-20261030T140206` (kept), agent started. It joined `lw-devnode-1`'s cluster: 3 nodes, green.

**Fixes (unit-tested; tsc / eslint / prettier clean; no migration)**

- **Patroni connect addresses** (decision in loadweaver.md 3.43): Spilo's template reads `PG_CONNECT_ADDRESS` / `RESTAPI_CONNECT_ADDRESS` via `setdefault` in `configure_spilo.py`. The agent sets both to the member's overlay address (`postgresConnectEnvironment`; none on loopback).
  - Not in the spec hash ("bootstrap with the final config" stays). A running Spilo gets them in place (`postgresConnectSyncCommand`): `/home/postgres/postgres.yml` rewritten, `POST :8008/reload`. Re-checked every 10 min, since a container restart regenerates the file.
  - `control-plane-containers.ts`, `control-plane-role.manager.ts`; specs in `control-plane.spec.ts` and `control-plane-role.handover.spec.ts`.
- **A left node keeps its role:** a left node is never compiled, and the leave closed only the session on the replica that handled it.
  - Now heartbeats / capability updates of `left` nodes record nothing: `handleHeartbeat` returns `false`, no `connected`, no `etcd_member_since`.
  - Whichever replica the agent streams to sends `leftNodeState` and then closes the session (`farewell`, in the 15 s push round or on a heartbeat). `leftNodeState` is the last state with `controlPlane.role: none`, `lifecycle: leaving` and revision + 1, so the agent removes etcd / Postgres / log store / API.
  - The leave no longer closes the local session itself.
  - `agent-stream.server.ts`, `node-agents.service.ts`, `nodes.service.ts`; specs `left-node.spec.ts`, `node-agents.etcd.spec.ts`.
- **`GET /nodes` `connected`** = local session, or a fresh heartbeat (≤ 30 s) recorded by any replica (`nodeConnectedInCluster`, also for `confirm-lost`). Spec `nodes-connected.spec.ts`.
- **Writes 503 instead of 500 before the fallback:**
  - The CP's leader proxy sets `leaderMissing` after 2 polls without a primary (≈ 4 s). The write guard then answers with the fallback's message (`MEMBERS_UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE`).
  - New `DatabaseUnavailableInterceptor` (HTTP, members target): connection errors, SQLSTATE 08xxx / 57P01–03 / 25006 → the same 503 (`isDatabaseUnavailableError`).
  - Specs in `database-handover.utils.spec.ts`, `database-target.runtime.spec.ts`, `database-unavailable.interceptor.spec.ts`.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - `lastError` is cleared after a successful `sync` step.
  - Object-store copy: the sweep counts `removed` separately (`copyBatchStart` / `afterCopyBatch`). The `generation-active` audit reports `copied` + `removed`; it used to report the sweep's count as `copied`.
  - `discovery.seed_hosts` is out of the log store hash: a running node knows the cluster from its cluster state, and a restarted one also uses the cluster-manager nodes of its last-known state. Single-node ↔ cluster still re-creates.
  - The agent's `PostgresLeaderProxy` only replaces the leader with a different primary. Misses are logged once and never drop it.
  - The point-in-time clone binds the WAL-G config like Spilo.

**Rollout**

- CP image rebuilt (`api-container-image`), tagged `:lw343-2`; agent bundle rebuilt (`build-agent.js`; previous one kept as `bin/lw-agent.js.2026-10-30-lw343-1`).
- New `rollout.sh` in the dev-node scripts: `docker load` of the tag, bundle install, `LOADWEAVER_CONTROL_PLANE_IMAGE` in `lw-agent.service`, agent restart. Run on nodes 3 → 2 → 1, then only the compose CP container recreated.
- Each agent logged "Patroni connect addresses set to <overlay> (reloaded in place)". Log store and member API replica re-created once (hash format); Postgres not.

**Found live: no replication password in the dev CP environment**

- Replicas still didn't stream after the address fix. `.start-containers.env` had empty `LOADWEAVER_POSTGRES_REPLICATION_PASSWORD` / `_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, so Spilo created `standby` / `admin` without a password.
- Repaired in the dev env (not product):
  - random values written to `.start-containers.env` (backup `.start-containers.env.bak-lw343-20261030`, gitignored);
  - `ALTER ROLE standby/admin PASSWORD` on the leader;
  - compose CP recreated.

### Derived Postgres role passwords (3.43) (2026-10-30)

Closes the product gap from "3.43 follow-ups": an external control plane without `LOADWEAVER_POSTGRES_REPLICATION_PASSWORD` / `_ADMIN_PASSWORD` gave members passwordless `standby` / `admin` roles.

- **Control plane:** `postgresRolePasswords` / `withPostgresRolePasswords` (`database-handover.utils.ts`): HKDF-SHA256 from `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, labels `loadweaver/postgres/replication` / `…/admin`, 48 hex chars. `memberEnvironment` fills only unset / empty values, so explicit env wins; added at push time only (never persisted, never logged), only for members.
- **Agent:** `syncPostgresRolePasswords` after Postgres is ensured: `POSTGRES_ROLE_PASSWORDS_COMMAND` (python in Spilo, as `postgres`, local socket) gets the passwords through the exec environment (`ManagedContainers.exec` takes `env` now), not through arguments.
  - Replica: exit 11, nothing changed (the leader's change replicates).
  - Leader: compares each role's stored SCRAM / MD5 verifier with the wanted password; on a difference `ALTER ROLE … PASSWORD '<SCRAM verifier>'` (computed in the script). The session sets `log_statement = 'none'`, `log_min_duration_statement = -1`, `log_min_error_statement = 'panic'`, `pg_stat_statements.track_utility = off`, and the script prints nothing.
  - Checked once per value (in-memory SHA-256 fingerprint), again after 10 min (leadership moves); failures retry on the next reconcile.
- A changed value is in Postgres' spec hash (`PGPASSWORD_STANDBY` / `_ADMIN`): members re-create Spilo once, which regenerates Patroni's replication credentials.
- Unit tests: derivation (stable, distinct per purpose and key, explicit wins), push-time injection (`push-determinism.spec.ts`), agent exec environment / script guards / re-check / failure (`control-plane-role.handover.spec.ts`). SCRAM verifier checked locally against the RFC 7677 vector.
- Not verified live: the dev stack has explicit values (which win). Rollout: new CP tag `:lw343-3` and agent bundle via `~/.cache/forepath-vm-lab/devnodes/rollout.sh`. Python driver (`psycopg2`, fallback `psycopg`) and socket `/var/run/postgresql` in Spilo are assumed, not probed.

### Fenced takeover (3.43) (2026-10-31)

Part A of the 2026-10-31 decision: the built-in (external) control plane takes the database over automatically when no member primary has been up for a while. Unit-tested; live test pending.

- **Takeover** (`DatabaseHandoverService`, read-only step):
  - **When:** after `LOADWEAVER_DATABASE_TAKEOVER_AFTER_MS` (default 120 000, never below the 45 s fallback; `0` / `off` = read-only as before) without any member primary. The leader proxy records `noPrimarySince`.
  - **Usable copy** (`externalCopyUnusable`): the subscription exists, every table is in `srsubstate = r`, and the replicated row says `members`. The members' last sync report (`external_copy`, replicated through the subscription itself) must have said `ok` at most `LOADWEAVER_DATABASE_TAKEOVER_MAX_LAG_MS` (5 min) before the outage. The external database must also be reachable.
  - **If not usable:** stays read-only with the reason in `controlPlane.database.takeover` / `readOnlyReason`, plus a critical inbox item.
  - **Steps:** advisory lock → a primary that came back aborts the takeover → subscription dropped (`slot_name = NONE`, the members' slot is kept) → migrations on the copy → every owned sequence moved past its column's maximum (logical replication doesn't carry sequences) → row `external` with epoch + 1, `taken_over_at` and `postgres_scope` (`<cluster>-t<epoch>`) → target file → controlled restart.
  - Audited `control-plane.database-takeover` after the restart. Critical inbox item (kind `database`) while running on the taken-over database.
- **Fencing epoch:** +1 on every takeover and handover. It lives in the target file (`epoch`, `takenOverAt`, `postgresScope`) and in the row (migration `1800000000059_DatabaseFencing`: `epoch`, `taken_over_at`, `postgres_scope`, `fences`; no spec). Upserts carry the epoch.
- **CP never switches to old data:** before a handover every member primary's data is checked (`memberDataState`).
  - Data with an older epoch is never adopted, copied into or dropped. It is fenced at the database level instead: `loadweaver.fenced_epoch` / `fenced_at` / `fenced_scope` settings, `default_transaction_read_only = on`, client sessions cut.
  - The handover runs only once exactly one current primary answers.
  - On the members' target, a second, older primary is fenced the same way.
  - The leader proxy keeps its current primary while that one answers, so a second primary isn't treated as a failover.
- **Members' role:** `controlPlane.databaseFence {epoch, takenOverAt?, scope?}` at push time. The external CP takes it from its file; member replicas read it from their database (every 30 s). Protocol feature `database-fencing` (strip gate); heartbeat `databaseFence` (fence report).
- **Agent** (`control-plane/database-fence.ts`, role manager):
  - **Probe:** python in Spilo reads the row's epoch and the fence settings, writing a JSON file in the data volume. It runs on applies (at most once per minute, or when the role's epoch changes) and every minute in between.
  - **Stale roles:** the highest epoch seen is persisted (`<state>/database-fence.json`). A role with a lower epoch (a member replica on fenced data) is not applied. Only its fence check runs.
  - **Fence:** API replica removed → rows with `created_at` / `updated_at` / `time` after the takeover exported as NDJSON per table + `manifest.json` (time series and migration bookkeeping skipped, ≤ 200 000 rows per table) → Spilo removed → export moved to `<state>/database-diverged-<time>/` → data directory **moved** to `<state>/postgres.fenced-e<dataEpoch>-<time>` (never deleted) → empty directory with a scope marker for the takeover's scope → Spilo starts empty.
  - **Why a new scope:** the old scope's etcd `initialize` key belongs to the old system id, and WAL-G would mix both timelines under one prefix.
  - **Failed export:** the rows stay in the moved-aside directory, and the report says so.
- **After the fence:** the new handover (epoch + 1) re-seeds the members, then the external copy subscribes again (existing sync).
  - Fence reports are recorded once (`recordDatabaseFence`: row `fences`, newest 20; audit `control-plane.database-fenced`; warning inbox item for a week). Not during the read-only fallback: the agent repeats its report every heartbeat.
  - Platform backups / fresh members use the takeover scope when it is newer than the last cut-over (`newerPostgresScope` in `activePostgresScope` / `activePlatformState`).
- **For the fleet (part C, coordinator request):**
  - `controlPlane.database.readOnlyReason` (members unreachable, copy not usable, takeover off, external DB unreachable, waiting) and `readOnlySince`.
  - Write refusals carry `code` in the 503 body: `read-only` from the guard and the interceptor, `freeze` during a handover freeze.
- **Console:** inbox kind `database` (label en / de), backend messages for the takeover, read-only and fence items (en / de).
- **Tests:**
  - CP: `database-takeover.spec` (timing, usability, scope, epoch comparison, fence records, inbox, SQL helpers, fence recording, scope precedence) and `database-handover.service.spec` (+7: takeover happy path, waiting / blocked / off / unreachable, primary back, fencing an old primary, several primaries / next epoch, status). Runtime / proxy / interceptor specs extended. 97 handover specs. Related specs (overview, node agents, platform, push, import cycles) are green.
  - Agent: `database-fence.spec` (decisions, probe, fence on disk, failed export, state, manager stale role / periodic fence). 84 control-plane specs.
  - Protocol 66; console `backend-message` 6.
  - tsc (CP lib + specs, app, agent lib + specs, protocol) clean; eslint and prettier clean.
- **Open:**
  - Not verified live.
  - A stale member replica's desired states (other than the control-plane role) are still applied by agents streaming to it. Its database is read-only once fenced, and it disappears when its agent fences.
  - The fence needs a running Spilo to probe: a member whose old Postgres can't start isn't fenced until it can.
  - Kept data directories / exports are never cleaned up (by design, manual).
  - The export's columns are a heuristic (`created_at` / `updated_at` / `time`).
  - Kiosk / fleet inbox don't show the `database` items.

### External copy across failovers, quiet read-only (3.43) (2026-10-31)

User decision "failover slots + keep copy" after the live finding: the takeover refused because "105 table(s) were still being copied". A Patroni failover had lost the copy's logical slot (it lived only on the old leader); the resync re-created the subscription with `copy_data`, which put every table in `i`. External DB now: subscription disabled, 105 tables `i`, data still there. Unit-tested; live test pending.

- **Failover-safe slot:**
  - The copy's slot is a Patroni permanent logical slot. `ensureFailoverSlot` reads `GET :8008/config` and patches only on a difference (`permanentSlotPatch`): `slots.<slot> = {type: logical, database, plugin: pgoutput}`, earlier `lw_external_copy_*` entries set to `null`, `postgresql.parameters.hot_standby_feedback = on`. It runs at the handover, on every sync, and right after a re-copy creates its slot. A return at r = 0 removes the entry.
  - Spilo 17 / Patroni 4 copies the slot to the replicas (one Postgres restart on each replica) and advances it there.
  - Every sync records `leader`, `slot` and `slotHolders` in `external_copy`; replicas are checked with `pg_replication_slots`. The previous values come from memory, or from the row after a restart.
  - `externalCopyAction`: the slot present on a new primary that held a copy at the last check → `ok`, no re-copy.
  - These cases still need a re-copy: slot missing; a new primary that held no copy (Patroni created the slot afresh, so changes in between would be missing); apply errors for 10 min; tables still copying after 10 min; subscription disabled with tables not `r` (the live state).
  - New actions: `enable` (a migrate step left the subscription disabled, every table in sync) and `syncing` (a refresh is still copying).
  - The leader and holders aren't updated while a re-copy is due or migrations are pending, so the decision repeats until a re-copy succeeds.
- **Re-copy that keeps the old copy** (`recopy`). Why this way: a shadow schema can't work, because logical replication maps tables by schema-qualified name. A shadow database needs every connection drained for the rename. This needs neither:
  1. The old subscription is only disabled; its tables stay `r` and readable.
  2. A new slot is created over a `replication=database` connection with `SNAPSHOT 'export'` (`createSlotWithSnapshot`) and registered with Patroni right away.
  3. `copyDatabase(…, {snapshot, tables: published, keepReadable})` imports that snapshot (`SET TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT`) and replaces the published tables in one external transaction (`DELETE` + insert). Readers and the takeover keep seeing the old rows until it commits.
  4. The old subscription is dropped (`slot_name = NONE`) and its slot dropped. The new one is created with `create_slot = false, copy_data = false`, so it streams exactly from the snapshot point.
  - On failure the new slot is dropped and deregistered, and the old copy is untouched.
- **"Complete as of":** `external_copy.completeAt` is the last `ok` sync (every table `r`), carried through `syncing` / `error` reports (`copyCompleteAt`). `copyReadiness` reads it, and `externalCopyUnusable` measures the staleness limit from it. Older reports fall back to `ok` + `checkedAt`. A disabled subscription during a re-copy counts as usable.
- **Read-only is quiet:**
  - `DatabaseTargetRuntime.writesBlocked()` covers the fallback, a freeze and a missing leader.
  - `writesPaused(job, logger)` logs `<job>: paused …` / `<job>: resumed …` once per job and debug in between.
  - Added at the start of each tick of: VM commands, Backup commands, Git sync (`kick`), Git bot, VM image imports, SIEM forwarding, Cron / Workload / Object store / Public addresses / Replica drain / DNS / DNS failover / DNSSEC / Import controllers, Autoscaler, Backups, Platform backups / copy / Cut-over / Disaster recovery, Usage sample / rollup / retention, Certificates, Postgres certificate renewal, Metrics rollup / retention, Recording retention, Orphaned live sessions, Rollouts, Update policies, Draft retention, Audit mirror, Remote access, Migration sessions, Apply sweep.
  - Not paused, because they read or have live read-only paths already: health, alerts, search, OTel, agent pushes, logs (OpenSearch).
- **Built-in member while read-only:**
  - `register()` decides from reads only: the key-mismatch guard still works, otherwise the state is `ok`. The write is deferred (`pending`), also when Postgres refuses it as read-only in a race (`isReadOnlyError`, SQLSTATE 25006).
  - The heartbeat keeps `lastSeenAt` in memory (`status()` shows the newer one) and writes the deferred registration / off mark once writable.
  - 3.39 is unchanged: the master key only uses `canOpen` (the key file) and `sealTarget` (a read). The r = 0 unseal through the built-in key works read-only (spec).
- **Tests:**
  - `database-handover.utils.spec`: failover decision, disabled / syncing, Patroni patch, completeAt.
  - `database-takeover.spec`: last complete copy.
  - `external-copy.spec`: snapshot slot, `create_slot = false`, holders, status.
  - `database-copy.spec`: snapshot + DELETE + table filter.
  - `database-handover.service.spec`, 6 new: registration + holders, failover keeps the copy, re-copy order and swap, new primary without a copy, failed re-copy repeats, enable.
  - `database-target.runtime.spec`: writesPaused.
  - New `read-only-jobs.spec` (32: every guarded job skips while paused and runs after).
  - `builtin-member.spec` (+4).
  - Handover + built-in folders: 174 tests. With the related service specs and the import / injection cycle checks: 24 suites, 263 tests.
  - tsc (CP lib + specs) clean, eslint clean (one old warning in `dns-reconciler.service.ts`), prettier clean. No migration.
- **Live test needs:**
  - CP image only (`:lw343-5`). Agent and protocol are unchanged.
  - No new env, and no manual Patroni change: the CP patches `slots` and `hot_standby_feedback` itself.
  - Expect one Postgres restart per replica while Patroni copies the slot.
  - The first sync re-copies the live external DB (disabled subscription + 105 `i`). This needs `session_replication_role`, so the external DB user must be a superuser (the compose one is).
- **Open:**
  - Holders are compared with the last check (every 15 s). A replica that lost its copy after that check (e.g. re-initialized) and then becomes primary gets a fresh slot from Patroni without a re-copy.
  - The re-copy is one transaction over all published tables: long for a large audit log.
  - Not verified live.

### Live test 3.43: takeover + fencing + fleet (2026-10-31)

Dev stack: compose CP `:lw343-5` (= `:latest`, built 12:07 UTC, no migration specs in `dist` / image), fleet recreated on its current `:latest`, both with `--env-file .start-containers.env` (CP Postgres replication / admin password hashes match the file). Agent bundle with fencing + `:lw343-5` rolled out with `rollout.sh` on nodes 3 → 2 → 1 (`FORCE=1 up.sh`, MemAvailable 15.7 GiB < 19.2 needed). No product fix needed.

- **1. Build + deploy: pass.** Start state: read-only, takeover `blocked` ("105 table(s) were still being copied").
- **2. Members back + rollout: pass.**
  - 12:11:01 "External copy: copying again (the subscription's slot is missing on the primary (lost in a failover))"; 12:11:17 slot `lw_external_copy_87774c4a86e0` registered as Patroni permanent slot; 12:11:33 "2239 rows in 105 tables copied again".
  - Patroni `GET /config`: `slots.lw_external_copy_87774c4a86e0 = {logical, loadweaver, pgoutput}`, `hot_standby_feedback: on`. Replicas restarted Postgres once (12:11:43 / 12:12:09) and hold the slot (inactive), leader active.
  - `externalCopy`: `state ok`, `failoverSlot true`, `slotHolders` all three, `completeAt` set. Subscription enabled, 105 `r`. `POST /views` 201, row on the compose Postgres within 2 s.
  - Old rows kept until commit: not observed row by row (only the logs / end state).
- **3. Switchover without re-copy: pass.** `patronictl switchover` lw-devnode-2 → 1 (12:15:57). 12:15:59 "leader is now 10.93.0.9"; report leader `10.93.0.9`, state `ok`, holders back to 3 at 12:16:31; no "copying again"; write 201 reached the copy.
- **4. Outage → takeover: pass.**
  - Guests off 12:17:12–36. Writes hung until 12:17:32+40 s, then `503 code=read-only` from 12:18:17 (second outage at 12:42:50: 503 from 12:43:33).
  - Quiet: 24 "paused" lines (one per job), 173 non-debug lines for the whole window. Built-in member `ok` (standby).
  - Read-only console data (second outage, 12:44): nodes 0 / 3 up, capacity null, `readOnly.metricsAsOf`, headline "control plane lost its quorum (0 of 3 up)", alerts `live:builtin:node-down:*` pending for all three, no capacity alerts, `/nodes` connected false.
  - Takeover 12:19:46 ("no member's Postgres was primary since 12:17:30.523Z"), restart, writable 12:20:09: `location external`, epoch 1, `takenOverAt`, `postgresScope lw-e9fb7247-t1`. Audit seq 1127 `control-plane.database-takeover` (sequences 1, copyCheckedAt 12:17:15). Critical inbox item "the built-in control plane took over …". Saved view `POST` 201.
  - Fleet DB (`lw_fleet_clusters.health.database`): 12:44:00 `readOnly true`, reason "members are unreachable"; 12:46:00 `readOnly false`, `takenOverAt` 12:45:16. After the first takeover (12:21:00) `readOnly false`, `takenOverAt` 12:19:46.
- **5. Fencing + re-seed: pass** (after the dev-env fix below).
  - CP: "Member primary 10.93.0.9 holds data of an older epoch than 1: fenced (read-only)". The first attempt failed ("cannot execute ALTER DATABASE in a read-only transaction"), the retry 15 s later worked.
  - Agents 12:23:54–58: "Postgres data of epoch 0 is older than the cluster's database (epoch 1): fencing it" → `postgres.fenced-e0-<time>` + `database-diverged-<time>` (manifest, 0 rows: nothing was written on the members after the takeover). Then "Control-plane role of database epoch 0 ignored" (stale member replicas).
  - Fresh Spilo in scope `lw-e9fb7247-t1` (new system id, TL 1). Handover 12:37:09: epoch 2, "51423 rows in 110 tables copied and verified", new slot `lw_external_copy_dcf4b7e08970` registered at once.
  - Fences recorded 12:36 (audit seq 1302 / 1310 / 1314 `control-plane.database-fenced`, `fences` with 3 entries, 3 warning inbox items). Handover audit seq 1318.
  - 12:42: external copy `ok`, `failoverSlot true`, holders all three; Patroni 1 leader + 2 streaming, lag 0; member API replicas healthy; all nodes connected, applied rev 48; write 201 reached the copy; fleet `healthy`.
- **6. End state: nodes stopped.** MemAvailable was 3.86 GiB with all three up (< 4). `down.sh` 12:42:50 used for the read-only checks above; the CP then took over again (12:45:16, epoch 3, scope `lw-e9fb7247-t3`). It now runs on the external database, so the next `up.sh` fences and re-seeds the members again (as in step 5). Fleet + CP healthy, MemAvailable 16 GiB.

**Dev environment fix (not product):** after the switch restart docker made the compose network `eth0` and the bridge `eth1`, but `net.sh` masquerades only `eth0`. VM → CP traffic left without SNAT: every agent "Stream to … closed: no answer from the control plane" for 11 min, so no member was re-seeded. `net-cp.sh` now adds `oifname <bridge dev> masquerade` to `ip lab post` when it's missing (`--check` reports it). Once it was applied, the agents reconnected and the handover ran within 2 min.

**Open issues (not blocking)**

- `lw_live_relay` cleanup (`DELETE … created_at < now() - 1 minute`) isn't paused: one `cannot execute DELETE in a read-only transaction` per minute while read-only.
- Before the fallback starts (~45 s), the LISTEN clients reconnect in a loop: 19× "Relay LISTEN: Connection terminated unexpectedly", 8× "Desired-state listener failed", plus one per job. Writes hang up to the client timeout in that window, they don't fail fast.
- Fleet relay read during the CP's takeover restart: `GET …/api/plans` 500 ("cluster unreachable: socket hang up"); 502 / 503 would fit better.
- First DB-level fence attempt fails while the old primary is still read-only (retried fine).
- `controlPlane.database.takenOverAt` stays at the last takeover after a handover, and the fleet keeps showing it.
- After the restart, the first log lines are Nest pretty-printed (colours), not JSON.
- Not verified: fleet cards / inbox / relay 503 through the fleet API (needs a signed-in user); the read-only window's fleet cards via the API.

### Fixes from the 3.43 live test (2026-10-31)

The five open issues of "Live test 3.43: takeover + fencing + fleet" (user: fix all five). Unit-tested; live test pending. No migration, no new env.

- **Live relay cleanup paused while read-only:** the `lw_live_relay` sweep (`LiveBroker`) checks `writesPaused('Live relay cleanup')` first (no more "cannot execute DELETE in a read-only transaction" per minute). Added to `read-only-jobs.spec`.
- **Fail fast before the fallback** (`MembersLeaderProxy`):
  - When `leaderMissing` starts (2 polls without a primary), the kept leader's Postgres port is probed once (TCP, 1.5 s). If it doesn't answer either, the proxy cuts its connections: running queries fail at once (503 `read-only` through `DatabaseUnavailableInterceptor`), new writes already get 503 from the guard. A leader whose Patroni was only slow keeps its connections.
  - Upstream connect timeout: 2 s while `leaderMissing`, 10 s otherwise (there was none, so a powered-off leader let pool connects hang).
  - LISTEN back-off (`utils/listen-backoff.utils.ts`, `ListenBackoff`): relay LISTEN (2 s → 30 s) and desired-state listener (5 s → 30 s). One warn on loss, retries at debug level, one line on recovery.
- **Fleet relay while a cluster restarts:** `FleetClusterClient` classifies connection failures (`clusterConnectionFailure`: refused / reset / hang-up / timeout / network / tls / aborted / other; `FleetClusterError.failure`). The relay answers 503 + `Retry-After: 10` for refused / reset / hang-up / timeout ("cluster X is not reachable: … (it may be restarting); retry in a moment"), and 502 for the rest (`code: cluster-unreachable`, `reason`). It was a 500 before. `status` stays null for these errors, so the other callers are unchanged.
- **`takenOverAt` after a handover:** the file and the row keep it, because the members' fence check still uses it as the export cutoff. The target file also records `takeoverEpoch`. `activeTakeoverAt` reports it only while the target is external and the epoch is still the takeover's; older files fall back to the epoch in the `-t<epoch>` scope. Used in `status().takenOverAt`, `takeover.state` `taken-over` and the inbox. On-node it is always null. The fleet (`clusterDatabaseFrom`) also drops it when `location` is `members`, which covers CPs up to `:lw343-5`.
- **JSON logs from the first line:** `apps/loadweaver/backend-{control-plane,fleet}/src/app-logger.ts` (`installAppLogger`, the same `CorrelationAwareConsoleLogger({ json: true, colors: false })`) is installed at the top of `main.ts`, before `prepareDatabaseTarget` / the DR tool / the lazy `bootstrap` import. `bootstrap` reuses it. Bootstrap failures are logged through it (stderr, JSON).
- **Tests:**
  - New specs: `listen-backoff.utils.spec`, `members-leader-proxy.spec` (cut / keep / probe once / connect timeouts), `fleet-cluster-client.service.spec`, and both `app-logger.spec`.
  - Extended: `live-broker.spec` (back-off), `agent-stream.listener.spec` (back-off), `read-only-jobs.spec` (relay cleanup), `database-handover.service.spec` (+1: no `takenOverAt` after handover / return), `database-handover.utils.spec` (`activeTakeoverAt`, parse), `fleet-relay.service.spec` (+2), `cluster-availability.spec` (+1).
  - CP handover / live / agent-stream / listen-backoff + import / injection cycle checks: 20 suites, 195 tests. Related CP specs (built-in member, platform backups, overview): 119. Fleet lib: 20 suites, 191 tests. App logger specs: 2.
  - tsc (CP lib + specs, fleet lib + specs, both apps + specs) clean; eslint and prettier clean on touched files.
- **Rollout:** CP image `:lw343-6` and fleet image rebuilt. Recreate both with `--env-file .start-containers.env`. Agent unchanged.
- **Open:** a slow-but-alive leader still gets the 503 window (writes refused after 2 missed Patroni polls, by design). The fence-attempt retry from the live test was not changed. Other fleet endpoints that call `client.json` (not the relay) still surface unreachable clusters with their own handling.
